definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi dirección actual es diferente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My current address is different.

definitions.note: Often used for software/app/system updates, or for updating information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una actualización del informe antes de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need an update to the report before the meeting.

definitions.note: Means “nowadays/these days” or “at the moment,” not “actually.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Actualmente vivo en Madrid, pero antes vivía en Valencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I currently live in Madrid, but before I lived in Valencia.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ando form): often used for “(is/are) acting” or “while acting/doing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está actuando en una obra de teatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is acting in a play.

definitions.note: Often used for acting in theater/film, or for how someone behaves in a situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella quiere actuar en una película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wants to act in a movie.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) preterite of "actuar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer actué en una obra de teatro en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I acted in a play at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella actuó en una película el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She acted in a movie last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella actúa en una película nueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She acts in a new movie.

definitions.note: Often used in a general sense of behaving or responding in a situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando hay un problema, él actúa rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When there is a problem, he acts quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la obra, ellos actúan muy bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the play, they act very well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Actúas muy bien en el escenario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You perform very well on stage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré acuarelas para pintar paisajes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought watercolors to paint landscapes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos un acuario con peces de colores en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have an aquarium with colorful fish in the living room.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “they showed up” or “they came in response” (e.g., to help or to an event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llamaron, acudieron de inmediato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they called, they came right away.

definitions.native: to go, to come (to a place or event)
definitions.note: Often used for going in response to a call, invitation, or need (e.g., to an appointment or to help).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a acudir a la reunión mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to go to the meeting tomorrow.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): he/she/you (formal) went/attended.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella acudió a la reunión a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She went to the meeting on time.

definitions.note: Often used with an object, especially in phrases like “acordar algo” (to agree on/arrange something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella acuerda el plan con su equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She agrees on the plan with her team.

definitions.note: Usually used reflexively as “te acuerdas (de ...)” (informal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Te acuerdas de mi nombre?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you remember my name?

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., a plan, a time, a price).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tú acuerdas la hora con el doctor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You agree on the time with the doctor.

definitions.note: Often used with an object (e.g., a price, a date) and can be followed by “con” to say who you agree with.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo acuerdo el precio con el vendedor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agree on the price with the seller.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos a un acuerdo después de hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached an agreement after talking.

definitions.note: From "acostar". Can mean either "(he/she) puts (someone) to bed" or "(he/she) lies down," depending on context (reflexive: "se acuesta").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas las noches acuesta a su hijo a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every night he puts his son to bed at nine.

definitions.native: I put to bed, I lay down
definitions.note: Commonly used reflexively as «me acuesto» = “I go to bed / I lie down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acuesto al bebé a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the baby to bed at eight.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of “acumular” (also used for “usted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El polvo se acumula en la esquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dust accumulates in the corner.

definitions.note: Past participle of "acumular"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He acumulado suficiente dinero para el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have accumulated enough money for the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acumuló mucha experiencia durante esos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He accumulated a lot of experience during those years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana estudia acupuntura y le gusta mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister studies acupuncture and she likes it a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo varias acusaciones contra el director.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were several accusations against the director.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La acusación fue muy grave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accusation was very serious.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form (used with a feminine noun or a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mujer fue acusada de robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The woman was accused of theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El acusado habló con su abogado antes del juicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The defendant spoke with his lawyer before the trial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El hombre acusado negó las acusaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The accused man denied the accusations.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle (e.g., with ser) and can also be used as an adjective or noun (“the accused/defendant”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El hombre fue acusado de robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was accused of theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía lo va a acusar de robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to accuse him of theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los periodistas acusaron al político de mentir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalists accused the politician of lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abogado acusó al sospechoso de robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer accused the suspect of theft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El delfín es un animal acuático.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dolphin is an aquatic animal.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). Used with the reflexive pronoun “te” in “acordarse de”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acuérdate de llamar a tu mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Remember to call your mom.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command, with a reflexive pronoun (te).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acuéstate temprano porque mañana tienes clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go to bed early because you have class tomorrow.

definitions.note: Common in Latin America; in Spain, "aquí" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ven acá, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, please.

definitions.note: Command (tú). "lo" = "it" (a direct object pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no puedes cambiarlo, acéptalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you can’t change it, accept it.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); it literally means “bring yourself closer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acércate, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come closer, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (ustedes); reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, acérquense a la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, come closer to the table.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted); also used reflexively as “acercarse”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, acérquese a la ventana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please come closer to the window.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La adaptación del libro al cine fue un éxito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The adaptation of the book to film was a success.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive: adaptarse (often used with “a” + noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante adaptarse a los cambios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to adapt to changes.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she adapted; it adapted; you (formal) adapted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella adaptó la historia para el teatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She adapted the story for the theater.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta solución es adecuada para el problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This solution is suitable for the problem.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estas zapatillas son adecuadas para correr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are suitable for running.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este libro es adecuado para niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is suitable for children.

definitions.note: Often used for moving to the front or progressing; also used when someone gets ahead of others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella adelanta para abrir la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She goes ahead to open the door.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “un adelantado a su época” (“ahead of his/her time”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nikola Tesla fue un adelantado a su época.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nikola Tesla was ahead of his time.

definitions.note: Often used for someone or something that is further along than expected (e.g., an advanced level).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is more advanced in math than I am.

definitions.note: Past participle of "adelantar"; often used to mean something has been scheduled earlier.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He adelantado la reunión para el lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I moved up the meeting to Monday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se adelantaron para ver mejor el desfile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They moved ahead to see the parade better.

definitions.note: Often used to encourage someone to proceed (like “go ahead”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sigue adelante y no te rindas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep going forward and don’t give up.

definitions.note: Often used to invite someone to enter or to encourage someone to continue speaking or acting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Puedo pasar? —Sí, adelante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “Can I come in?” “Yes, go ahead.”

definitions.note: Often used for money paid before the full amount is due.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave me an advance on my salary.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to lose weight before summer.

definitions.note: Often written with an accent as “además”, but here shown exactly as requested: “ademas”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Also, I want to talk to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Además, mañana podemos ir al parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Also, tomorrow we can go to the park.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs of motion (e.g., entrar, meter) to mean “(to) inside.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold; you’d better stay inside.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" (e.g., "adhiere a la pared" = sticks to the wall).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The label sticks well to the box.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" to mean joining a group, plan, or idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella se adhiere al programa de voluntariado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She joins the volunteer program.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su adicción al tabaco le afecta la salud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His addiction to tobacco affects his health.

definitions.note: Plural form (more than one).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos recursos adicionales para terminar el proyecto a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need additional resources to finish the project on time.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (e.g., “adicto a”) to say someone is addicted to something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy adicto al café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m addicted to coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un adicto al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a work addict.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; also used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son adictos al café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are addicted to coffee.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tía es muy adinerada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My aunt is very wealthy.

definitions.note: Common farewell; also said when leaving or ending a conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bueno, me voy; adios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well, I'm leaving; goodbye.

definitions.note: Feminine form (a female fortune teller).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La adivina leyó las cartas y me dio un consejo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fortune teller read the cards and gave me some advice.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command ("Guess!") or in the expression “Adivina qué” (“Guess what”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Adivina qué: mañana es mi cumpleaños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess what: tomorrow is my birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo he adivinado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have guessed it.

definitions.note: Often used for guessing an answer, what someone is thinking, or predicting something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes adivinar la respuesta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you guess the answer?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo adivinarlo sin una pista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t guess it without a clue.

definitions.note: This form can be the present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) or the formal command (usted) of “adivinar.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Guess the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Adivino que hoy va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guess it’s going to rain today.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular (yo).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guessed the answer without looking at the options.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “(he/she/you formal) guessed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella adivinó la respuesta sin ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She guessed the answer without help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bueno, me tengo que ir: adiós.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Well, I have to go: goodbye.

definitions.note: Used as a farewell (often with ¡Adiós!).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que irme; adiós.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to go; goodbye.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella administra una pequeña tienda en el barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She manages a small shop in the neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La administración del hospital cambió las reglas de visita.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La administración del dinero es importante para ahorrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Managing money is important for saving.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who manages an organization, system, or property (e.g., a website or an apartment building).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building manager lives on the ground floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella admira a su profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She admires her teacher.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for ongoing, repeated, or background actions in the past).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I admired my grandfather.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu trabajo es admirable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento mucha admiración por mi profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of admiration for my teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene muchos admiradores por su música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has many admirers because of his music.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many students admire their teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te admiro por tu valentía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I admire you for your bravery.

definitions.note: Often used for being allowed to enter a place or institution, or the process of being accepted.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission to the museum is free on Sundays.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Adolescence can be a difficult stage for some young people.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Teenagers often sleep in late on weekends.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “to where,” especially with verbs of movement. It can also appear without an accent as a relative adverb.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are you going after class?

definitions.note: Past participle (feminine singular) of "adoptar".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl was adopted when she was two years old.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My son was adopted when he was a baby.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to adopt a dog from the shelter.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They adopted a dog from the shelter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que adopte al perro del refugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you adopt the dog from the shelter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que adopten un perro del refugio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you adopt a dog from the shelter.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es la madre adoptiva del niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the child's adoptive mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esa época, adoraban a sus dioses en silencio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that time period, they worshipped their gods in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Qué perro tan adorable!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What an adorable dog!

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cachorros son adorables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The puppies are adorable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos adoran a su perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They adore their dog.

definitions.note: Often used to express strong liking or enthusiasm, not necessarily religious worship.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Adoro esta canción!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love this song!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El conocimiento adquirido en el curso me ayudó mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knowledge acquired in the course helped me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un hábito adquirido con el tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a habit acquired over time.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., acquiring skills, knowledge, property).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero adquirir más experiencia en este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to acquire more experience in this job.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “he/she/it acquired/bought” or “you (formal) acquired/bought.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa adquirió una nueva máquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company acquired a new machine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo hizo adrede para molestarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did it on purpose to annoy me.

definitions.note: Refers to border/airport customs (the authority or the checkpoint).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el aeropuerto, pasamos por la aduana sin problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the airport, we went through customs without any problems.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the government office/area where goods and travelers are inspected when entering or leaving a country.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuvimos que pasar por aduanas al llegar al aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had to go through customs when we arrived at the airport.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es una mujer adulta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is an adult woman.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es adulto y vive solo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is an adult and lives alone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta piscina, solo pueden entrar los adultos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this pool, only adults are allowed to enter.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; can refer to a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En este cine solo pueden entrar adultos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Only adults can enter this movie theater.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta piscina no se permite la entrada a adultos sin niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this pool, adults without children are not allowed to enter.

definitions.note: Plural form of “adverbio.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta oración hay dos adverbios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this sentence there are two adverbs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A pesar de la adversidad, siguieron adelante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Despite the adversity, they kept going.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico me dio una advertencia sobre el azúcar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor gave me a warning about sugar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las advertencias en la etiqueta son importantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warnings on the label are important.

definitions.note: Past participle of “advertir”; often used with “haber” (e.g., “he advertido” = “I have warned”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya te lo he advertido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already warned you.

definitions.note: Used to warn someone about a danger or consequence; commonly followed by "de" or "que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debo advertir que no toques eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must warn you not to touch that.

definitions.native: to warn him, to warn her, to warn you
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to him/her/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que advertirle que la carretera está cerrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to warn him/her/you that the road is closed.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "advertir" (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Advertí un error en el informe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I noticed an error in the report.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of “advertir”; often used to warn someone about a risk or to point something out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te advierto que la carretera está muy peligrosa hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I warn you that the road is very dangerous today.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/you (formal) warned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor nos advirtió sobre el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher warned us about the exam.

definitions.note: Used in questions (direct or indirect) to ask about a destination or direction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Adónde vas después de clase?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where are you going after class?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a llamar a la aerolínea para cambiar mi vuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to call the airline to change my flight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos al aeropuerto temprano para tomar el vuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the airport early to catch the flight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ruido afecta mi concentración.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise affects my concentration.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who is emotionally upset, or for something that has been impacted/damaged.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la noticia, ella estaba muy afectada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the news, she was very affected.

definitions.note: Past participle of "afectar"; often used with "estar" or in passive constructions ("ser").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pueblo fue afectado por la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The town was affected by the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los afectados recibirán ayuda después del accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those affected will receive help after the accident.

definitions.note: Present tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las decisiones del gobierno afectan a muchas familias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government's decisions affect many families.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cambio de horario afectará mi rutina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The schedule change will affect my routine.

definitions.note: Often used for warm feelings (care, fondness) toward a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento mucho afecto por mis abuelos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of affection for my grandparents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tormenta afectó a muchas familias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm affected many families.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él se afeita todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shaves every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me voy a afeitar antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to shave before going out.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an indirect object pronoun (-me) meaning “to shave myself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que afeitarme antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to shave myself before going out.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb: used when someone shaves themself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a afeitarse antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to shave before leaving.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: «me afeito» = “I shave (myself).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me afeito todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shave every morning.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/you formal) in the past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se afeitó antes de salir de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He shaved before leaving the house.

definitions.note: Commonly used for someone who is very interested in a sport, hobby, or activity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy aficionado al fútbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m a fan of soccer.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (e.g., “aficionado a la música”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy muy aficionado al fútbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m really into soccer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los aficionados a la música llenaron el teatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Music fans filled the theater.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis aficiones son leer y cocinar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hobbies are reading and cooking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi afición es la fotografía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My hobby is photography.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cuchilla está muy afilada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The blade is very sharp.

definitions.note: Often used for something with a cutting edge (like a knife).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cuchillo está muy afilado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knife is very sharp.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cuchillos están afilados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knives are sharp.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy afilando el cuchillo para cortar las verduras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sharpening the knife to cut the vegetables.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (he/she/you formal) of "afirmar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella afirma que no fue su culpa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She states that it wasn’t her fault.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus afirmaciones no coinciden con los hechos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His statements don't match the facts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos afirman que todo está listo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They claim that everything is ready.

definitions.note: Past tense (third-person singular) of "aflojar"; can refer to something becoming less tight or less intense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El viento aflojó por la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind let up in the afternoon.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me siento afortunada de tener buenos amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel lucky to have good friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Afortunadamente, llegamos a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fortunately, we arrived on time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy muy afortunado de tener buenos amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very lucky to have good friends.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Somos muy afortunados de tener buenos amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are very lucky to have good friends.

definitions.note: Often used for dealing with a problem, situation, or challenge (similar to “to face” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que afrontar este problema juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to face this problem together.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hace frío afuera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold outside.

definitions.note: Usually used in the phrase “a las afueras (de ...)” = “on the outskirts (of ...)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viven a las afueras de la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They live on the outskirts of the city.

definitions.native: hold on, hang on, grab on
definitions.note: Informal (tú) affirmative command; reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Aférrate a la barandilla!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold on to the railing!

definitions.note: Past tense (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando vio la pelota, se agachó para recogerla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the ball, he crouched down to pick it up.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the phrase “tener agallas” (to have guts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay que tener agallas para decir la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to have guts to tell the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pez respira por las agallas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fish breathes through its gills.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "agarrar" (also used as an informal command "grab!" depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agarra mi mano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grab my hand.

definitions.note: Past participle of "agarrar"; often used with "estar" or "tener".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo el vaso agarrado con fuerza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the glass held tightly.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” to mean “holding onto” something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños estaban agarrados de la barandilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids were holding on to the railing.

definitions.native: to grab, to seize; to hold on to
definitions.note: Common in everyday speech; can also mean “to catch” (a bus, a disease) depending on region/context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a agarrar tu mano, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to grab your hand, please.

definitions.note: Used for transportation: “agarrar el autobús/el tren”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si salimos ahora, podemos agarrar el autobús.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we leave now, we can catch the bus.

definitions.note: Colloquial in many regions; also “contraer” in more formal registers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Creo que voy a agarrar un resfriado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think I’m going to catch a cold.

definitions.native: to get hold of; to take (an opportunity/object)
definitions.note: Often implies acting quickly to take something available.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a agarrar la oportunidad cuando se presente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to seize the opportunity when it comes up.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) in the past tense (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agarraron el autobús justo a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They caught the bus just in time.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú), simple past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Agarraste las llaves antes de salir?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you grab the keys before leaving?

definitions.note: Form of "agarrar" used in the present subjunctive (e.g., "que agarre") and also as the formal (usted) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que agarre el tren a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he catches the train on time.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes) and also formal command (ustedes) of "agarrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Agarren sus mochilas y vámonos!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grab your backpacks and let's go!

definitions.native: I grab, I take hold of, I catch
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agarro el teléfono y te llamo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grab the phone and call you.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): first-person singular (“I”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agarré las llaves y salí de la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grabbed the keys and left the house.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agarró el vaso y lo puso en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He grabbed the glass and put it on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trabajo en una agencia de viajes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work at a travel agency.

definitions.note: Often refers to a planner (book/app) where you write appointments and plans.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apunté la cita en mi agenda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote the appointment down in my planner.

definitions.note: Often used for people who act on behalf of an organization (for example, police, a company, or a government).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El agente habló con nosotros en la comisaría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The agent spoke with us at the police station.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los agentes hablaron con el gerente del banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The agents spoke with the bank manager.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ruido de la calle agita al bebé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise from the street agitates the baby.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, estaba muy agitado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, he was very agitated.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ing form), used to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estaba agitando la botella antes de abrirla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was shaking the bottle before opening it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debes agitar la botella antes de abrirla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should shake the bottle before opening it.

definitions.note: Often used for stirring up emotions, conflict, or a situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa noticia vino a agitar a la gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That news came to upset (stir up) the people.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “(he/she/it) shook/stirred.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella agitó la botella antes de abrirla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She shook the bottle before opening it.

definitions.note: Often used for intense physical or emotional suffering; also commonly used for the final moments before death (“en agonía”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La familia pasó una noche de agonía en el hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The family spent a night of agony at the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi cumpleaños es en agosto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in August.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El agua se agota en verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water runs out in summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese trabajo me agota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That job exhausts me.

definitions.note: feminine form; used for a woman or a feminine noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del trabajo, estoy agotada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I’m exhausted.

definitions.note: feminine form; used with feminine nouns (e.g., entrada, localidad, camiseta)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La entrada está agotada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket is sold out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del viaje, estoy agotado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, I’m exhausted.

definitions.note: Used for things that are no longer available because all units have been sold.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El concierto está agotado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert is sold out.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective to describe a person or thing with no energy left.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del viaje, estoy agotado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, I’m exhausted.

definitions.note: Common on signs or online to say there are no more items/tickets available.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo siento, el concierto está agotado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, the concert is sold out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue un día agotador, pero lo logramos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an exhausting day, but we made it.

definitions.note: Masculine plural past participle of *agotar*. Often used with *estar* to describe people who are very tired.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del viaje, estamos agotados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, we’re exhausted.

definitions.note: Also used (masculine plural) to describe items that are no longer available; commonly with *estar*.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los boletos están agotados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tickets are sold out.

definitions.note: Used for supplies/products/resources when there are none left (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los suministros están agotados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The supplies have run out.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund; often used with "estar" to mean "to be running out (of something)" or "to be exhausting (someone/something)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos agotando el agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are running out of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tienda agotó el pan esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store ran out of bread this morning.

definitions.note: From the verb "agradar". It’s often used with an indirect object: "Me agrada" = "I like it" (literally, "It pleases me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me agrada esta canción.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this song.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used with an indirect object (e.g., "me agradaba" = "I liked it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me agradaba el café de ese lugar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked the coffee at that place.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tú): used for ongoing/repeated actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando eras niño, agradabas a todos con tu sonrisa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were a child, you pleased everyone with your smile.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El clima hoy es muy agradable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The weather today is very pleasant.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los vecinos son muy agradables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighbors are very pleasant.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object: what pleases is the subject (e.g., “Me agradan…” = “I like…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me agradan mucho estos zapatos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really like these shoes.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun when conjugated (me/te/le/nos/les): e.g., “Me agrada…” = “I like…” / “It pleases me…”. Here, the example includes the infinitive "agradar" exactly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero agradar a mis invitados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to please my guests.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object: “Le agradas” = “He/She likes you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le agradas a mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister likes you.

definitions.note: From agradar (“to be pleasing to”); often used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les): Me agrade = I like it / It pleases me.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que te agrade la comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like the food.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "agradecer" (can mean "(he/she) thanks" or "you (formal) thank").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella siempre agradece tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She always thanks you for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les agradecemos su ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We appreciate your help.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “agradecer” (can also be used for “you all” in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos agradecen tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They appreciate your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero agradecerte tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to thank you for your help.

definitions.native: to thank him, to thank her, to thank you
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (“to him/her/you” formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero agradecerle su ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to thank you for your help.

definitions.note: The pronoun “les” can also mean “to you (plural, formal)” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero agradecerles por su ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to thank them for their help.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "te" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero agradecerte tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Conditional form; often used to make polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le agradecería que me ayudara con este formulario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would appreciate it if you helped me with this form.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy muy agradecida por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very grateful for your help.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" (e.g., "estoy agradecido") and commonly followed by "por" (for).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy muy agradecido por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very grateful for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos muy agradecidos por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are very grateful for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero expresar mi agradecimiento por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to express my thanks for your help.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella agradeció la ayuda de sus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She thanked her friends for their help.

definitions.note: Includes pronouns: se = to him/her/you (formal)/them; lo = it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero agradecérselo por su ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to thank you for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer agradecí a mis amigos su ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I thanked my friends for their help.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form). Often used after expressions like “espero que…”, “quiero que…”, “no creo que…”, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me agradezcas la ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you thank me for the help.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te agradezco mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really appreciate your help.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of "agradar"; commonly used with an indirect object (e.g., "Le agrado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que te agrado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like me.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like the gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue agredido en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was assaulted on the street.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal "you" (usted) present tense of "agregar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella agrega sal a la sopa.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cheese is an extra add-on on the hamburger.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a agregar más sal a la sopa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agregó más sal a la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She added more salt to the soup.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog became aggressive when someone came near her puppies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro se vuelve agresivo cuando alguien se acerca a su comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog becomes aggressive when someone comes near his food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los perros no son agresivos si están bien entrenados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dogs aren’t aggressive if they are well trained.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La agresión ocurrió en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The assault happened on the street.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "agrio".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La salsa está agria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sauce is sour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El agricultor cultiva maíz y verduras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The farmer grows corn and vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los agricultores trabajan en el campo todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The farmers work in the countryside every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La agricultura es muy importante en esta región.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Agriculture is very important in this region.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El agua está fría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water is cold.

definitions.native: holds on, puts up with, endures
definitions.note: Commonly used to mean “hold on” (wait) or “hang in there.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aguanta un momento, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold on a moment, please.

definitions.native: putting up with, holding on, enduring
definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "aguantar"; often used with "estar" to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aguantando el dolor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m enduring the pain.

definitions.note: Commonly used for putting up with a situation or person, or for physically holding up under strain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo aguantar este calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand this heat.

definitions.native: to put up with it, to endure it, to hold it

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo aguantarlo más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't put up with it anymore.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por aguantarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for putting up with me.

definitions.native: will endure, will hold up, will put up with
definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/it/you-formal will…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé si el puente aguantará el peso del camión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know if the bridge will hold up under the weight of the truck.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú). Often used in questions like “¿Aguantas?” = “Can you handle it?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Aguantas el ruido de la calle?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you put up with the noise from the street?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que aguante el dolor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you can endure the pain.

definitions.native: I can stand it, I can take it
definitions.note: From aguantar; often used to say you can tolerate something or endure it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No aguanto este calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't stand this heat.

definitions.note: Commonly used with the sense of “to wait for” (often with «a»).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aguarda a su hermano en la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She waits for her brother at the station.

definitions.note: From the verb "aguar" (to spoil/ruin something, often by taking away the fun or good mood).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es una pena que la lluvia nos aguarde el picnic.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a shame that the rain spoils our picnic.

definitions.note: Used for “ustedes” (plural you) as a command or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, aguarden aquí un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please wait here for a moment.

definitions.note: Often refers to a traditional distilled drink in Spanish-speaking countries (type varies by region).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En Colombia, el aguardiente es muy popular en las fiestas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In Colombia, aguardiente is very popular at parties.

definitions.note: Often used in more formal writing; can also mean “awaited” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aguardó en la estación hasta que llegó el tren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He waited at the station until the train arrived.

definitions.note: Plural of "agua"; often used in set phrases like "¡Aguas!" meaning "Watch out!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las aguas del río están muy frías.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The river waters are very cold.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “agudo.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La aguja está tan aguda que pincha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The needle is so sharp that it pricks.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “agudo,” often used for sounds or voices.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene una voz aguda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a high-pitched voice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten cuidado: ese cuchillo está muy agudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful: that knife is very sharp.

definitions.note: Often used for sounds (like a voice, whistle, or scream).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escuché un sonido agudo en la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a high-pitched sound at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una aguja para coser este botón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a needle to sew this button.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito agujas para coser este botón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need needles to sew this button.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un agujero en mi calcetín.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay agujeros en la carretera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are holes in the road.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; literally “bend yourself down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agáchate detrás del sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Crouch down behind the couch.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). "lo" = "it" (masculine direct object, or neutral "that").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Agárralo y no lo sueltes!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grab it and don’t let go of it!

definitions.note: Commonly used as an informal command (tú), often as a warning (e.g., before a sudden movement or surprising news).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Agárrate, que el autobús va a arrancar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold on, the bus is about to start moving.

definitions.note: Affirmative command (ustedes). Often used like “hold on tight” / “brace yourselves.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Agárrense bien, que el autobús va muy rápido!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hold on tight, the bus is going very fast!

definitions.note: Interjection used to show realization, understanding, surprise, or a reaction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ah, ahora entiendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ah, now I understand.

definitions.note: Commonly written with an accent as «ahí», but here shown as requested: «ahi».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja la mochila ahi, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the backpack there, please.

definitions.note: Used for someone/something that has drowned or is being suffocated (e.g., by water, smoke, or food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro fue encontrado ahogado en el río.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was found drowned in the river.

definitions.note: Past participle of «ahogar». It can also be used for someone who has choked/suffocated, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño se ha ahogado en la piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child has drowned in the pool.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "ahogar"; often used with "estar" to say someone is in the process of drowning (or choking/suffocating).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Ayuda! Me estoy ahogando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help! I'm drowning.

definitions.note: Includes the reflexive pronoun “me” (“myself”). It can also mean “to choke/suffocate” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero ahogarme en la piscina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to drown in the pool.

definitions.native: to drown; to choke; to suffocate
definitions.note: Reflexive verb: the subject is the one who drowns/chokes/suffocates. Often used with "con" (e.g., "ahogarse con comida/agua/humo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a ahogarse si no sale del agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She is going to drown if he/she doesn’t get out of the water.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "ahogar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El hombre ahogó al perro en el río.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man drowned the dog in the river.

definitions.note: can also mean 'right now' or 'at the moment' depending on context
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ahora no puedo hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't talk now.

definitions.note: Past participle of «ahorcar»; often used with «haber» to form compound tenses, or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo encontraron ahorcado en el árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found him hanged in the tree.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form: “(he/she/it) hanged.” Often used figuratively in expressions like “me ahorcó la corbata” (“the tie is choking me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El prisionero ahorcó al guardia con una cuerda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoner hanged the guard with a rope.

definitions.note: Common in Mexico and some other countries; depending on context, it can mean either immediately or in a little while.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ahorita voy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella ahorra dinero para un viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She saves money for a trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo algo de dinero ahorrado para las vacaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some money saved for vacation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He ahorrado dinero para el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have saved money for the trip.

definitions.note: Gerund form; used to talk about an action in progress (often with "estar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy ahorrando para un viaje este verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m saving for a trip this summer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He adjusted the chair to be more comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy al supermercado después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the supermarket after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pájaro tiene un ala herida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird has an injured wing.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective meaning “praised” (it comes from the verb “alabar,” to praise).

definitions.note: Usually refers to a built-in cupboard in the kitchen used for storing food or dishes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got up at dawn to watch the sunrise.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bricklayer is building a brick wall.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is outside the scope of the project.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I reach it in time.
