definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy alcanzando el estante de arriba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am reaching the top shelf.

definitions.native: to reach, to catch up to
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo alcanzar la repisa de arriba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't reach the top shelf.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si caminamos rápido, alcanzaremos la cima antes de oscurecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we walk fast, we will reach the summit before it gets dark.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= her; also “it” for feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que correr para alcanzarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to run to catch her.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= it / him / you formal, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo alcanzarlo desde aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't reach it from here.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) preterite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por fin alcanzaron la cima de la montaña.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They finally reached the top of the mountain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren alcanzará la estación a las cinco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train will reach the station at five.

definitions.note: Often used to say that an amount is sufficient.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con diez euros alcanzará para el taxi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ten euros will be enough for the taxi.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Algún día alcanzaré mis metas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someday I will achieve my goals.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "alcanzar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No alcanzo la caja en el estante de arriba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't reach the box on the top shelf.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it reached.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren alcanzó la estación a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train reached the station on time.

definitions.note: Plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta ensalada lleva alcaparras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This salad has capers in it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No bebo alcohol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t drink alcohol.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tía es alcohólica y está recibiendo ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My aunt is an alcoholic and is getting help.

definitions.note: Affirmative command form with the object pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alcánzame el libro, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pass me the book, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela vive en una aldea pequeña en las montañas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother lives in a small village in the mountains.

definitions.note: Masculine plural; for a mixed group you can also use the masculine plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los aldeanos celebran la fiesta del pueblo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The villagers celebrate the town festival.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun: "me/te/le/nos/les alegra" (= "it makes me/you/him/her/us/them happy").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me alegra verte otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm happy to see you again.

definitions.native: they cheered up, they made (someone) happy
definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), third person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tus palabras me alegraron mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your words made me very happy.

definitions.native: to be happy, to be glad
definitions.note: Reflexive verb; commonly used as alegrarse de (to be glad about). Example sentence includes the infinitive form exactly as requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a alegrarse de verte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to be glad to see you.

definitions.native: will make (someone) happy, will cheer up
definitions.note: Third-person singular future: “he/she/it will make (someone) happy.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia te alegrará el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news will make your day.

definitions.native: will make (someone) happy, will cheer up
definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) future; often used with an indirect object pronoun (e.g., me, te, le, nos, les).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia les alegrarán el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news will make their day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está muy alegre hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very happy today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños cantaban alegremente en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were singing happily in the courtyard.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están alegres hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are happy today.

definitions.native: I make happy, I cheer up
definitions.note: Most often used reflexively as “me alegro” = “I’m happy/glad.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre alegro a mis amigos con mis chistes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always cheer up my friends with my jokes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alegré a mi hermana con una sorpresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cheered up my sister with a surprise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su alegría era contagiosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her joy was contagious.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia lo alegró mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news made him very happy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro se aleja de la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog moves away from the house.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa está alejada del centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is far from downtown.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" (e.g., "alejado de" = far from).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su casa está alejada del centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her house is far from downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos alejados del centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live far away from the city center.

definitions.native: to move away; to take away; to distance
definitions.note: Transitive form: alejar algo/alguien (to move/take something/someone away). (Reflexive form is alejarse, but examples here use the exact word “alejar” as requested.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a alejar la silla de la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to move the chair away from the door.

definitions.native: to move away, to get away
definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning “to move myself away” or “to get away (from something/someone).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito alejarme un poco para pensar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to get away for a bit to think.

definitions.native: to move away, to go away; to get farther away
definitions.note: Reflexive verb; used for increasing distance from someone/something (often with "de").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al verme, decidió alejarse rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw me, he decided to move away quickly.

definitions.native: to move away, to get away
definitions.note: Includes the reflexive pronoun “te” (“yourself/you”); often used as a command or with an infinitive construction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor alejarte de esa situación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better to get away from that situation.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form), often used after expressions like “es mejor que…” or with commands like “no…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor que no te alejes demasiado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better if you don’t move too far away.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), third person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro se alejó de la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog moved away from the house.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesora es alemana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is German.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (also used for mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos son alemanes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are German.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En mi clase hay tres alemanes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my class there are three Germans.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablamos en alemán, pero hoy practicamos frases alemanes en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We speak in German, but today we practice German phrases in class.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it agrees in gender and number with the noun it describes (alemán, alemana, alemanes, alemanas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesor es alemán.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is German.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to a person from Germany; for the language, Spanish usually uses “alemán” as well depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecino es alemán.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is German.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los resultados del examen son alentadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exam results are encouraging.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer alenté a mi amiga antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I encouraged my friend before the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo alergia al polen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an allergy to pollen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo alergias en la primavera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have allergies in the spring.

definitions.note: Often used invariable (same form for masculine/feminine and singular/plural) in expressions like “estar alerta” or “mantenerse alerta.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los guardias están alerta toda la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guards are on alert all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La alerta por tormenta sigue vigente esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm warning is still in effect tonight.

definitions.note: Used mainly as the name of the Greek letter (α) or to mean “the first” in a series.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La palabra empieza con la letra alfa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The word starts with the letter alpha.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aprendiendo el alfabeto en clase de español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm learning the alphabet in Spanish class.

definitions.note: Chess piece.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El alfil se mueve en diagonal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bishop moves diagonally.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La alfombra del salón es muy suave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The living room carpet is very soft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las alfombras del salón son muy suaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rugs in the living room are very soft.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy algo cansado hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m somewhat tired today.

definitions.note: Can also mean "anything" in some questions and similar contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito algo para escribir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need something to write with.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta camiseta es de algodón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This T-shirt is made of cotton.

definitions.note: An officer of the court (e.g., in charge of order in the courtroom).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El alguacil pidió silencio en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bailiff asked for silence in the courtroom.

definitions.note: refers to a person, not a thing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito hablar con alguien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to talk to someone.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "alguno"; used before a feminine singular noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes alguna pregunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any questions?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "alguno"; it agrees with a feminine noun (often one that is implied).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Hay alguna pregunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are there any questions?

definitions.note: feminine plural form; used before feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré algunas manzanas en el mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some apples at the market.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Algunas personas prefieren té en lugar de café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some people prefer tea instead of coffee.

definitions.note: Usually changes for gender/number (algún, alguna, algunos, algunas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes alguno de estos libros?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any of these books?

definitions.note: Often used in negative questions or sentences to mean “any.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes alguno?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any?

definitions.note: masculine plural form; used before masculine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Algunos estudiantes llegan temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some students arrive early.

definitions.note: masculine plural form; often used before a plural noun (e.g., “algunos libros” = “some books”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Algunos estudiantes no vinieron hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Some students didn’t come today.

definitions.note: Used before a masculine singular noun (short form of "alguno").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes algún problema?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have any problem?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: España es un aliado importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Spain is an important ally.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los aliados firmaron un acuerdo de cooperación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The allies signed a cooperation agreement.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los dos países firmaron una alianza para protegerse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two countries signed an alliance to protect themselves.

definitions.note: Commonly used to mean a wedding ring (the band).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdí mi alianza en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lost my wedding ring at the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su aliento olía a café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His breath smelled like coffee.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "dar aliento" (to encourage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tus palabras me dieron aliento antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your words encouraged me before the exam.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "alimentar" (also used for "he/she/it feeds" and "you (formal) feed").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella alimenta al bebé con una botella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feeds the baby with a bottle.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted): “I/he/she/you (formal) was/were feeding” or “used to feed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, mi abuela me alimentaba con sopa caliente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, my grandmother fed me hot soup.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about eating habits or the way someone is fed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Una buena alimentación es importante para la salud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A good diet is important for health.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "alimentar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos alimentan a los perros todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They feed the dogs every morning.

definitions.note: Gerund (used for actions in progress, like “is/are feeding”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy alimentando al bebé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am feeding the baby.

definitions.note: Often used for feeding people or animals; also used for supplying something with what it needs (e.g., a system with energy or data).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que alimentar al perro antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to feed the dog before leaving.

definitions.note: Reflexive; often used when talking about diet or nutrition (e.g., eating well/poorly).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante alimentarse bien todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to eat well every day.

definitions.note: Used as present subjunctive (él/ella/usted) or as a formal (usted) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que alimente al bebé antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you feed the baby before leaving.

definitions.note: Verb form (from “alimentar”); it can mean to feed (a person/animal) or to supply/nourish (e.g., a system or machine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cada mañana alimento a mi gato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every morning I feed my cat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos alimento y agua para vivir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need food and water to live.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used in contexts like meals, provisions, or food supplies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos comprar alimentos para la semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to buy food for the week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer alimenté al perro antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I fed the dog before leaving.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella alimentó al bebé con un biberón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She fed the baby with a bottle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta medicina alivia el dolor de cabeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This medicine relieves the headache.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aliviado porque todo salió bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m relieved because everything went well.

definitions.note: Often used for relieving pain, stress, or a problem.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este medicamento ayuda a aliviar el dolor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This medicine helps relieve the pain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta medicina aliviará el dolor en pocos minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This medicine will relieve the pain in a few minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentí un gran alivio cuando terminó el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt great relief when the exam ended.

definitions.note: Refers to a place at some distance from the speaker (often farther than “ahí”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis llaves están allá, en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My keys are over there, on the table.

definitions.note: often refers to a place farther away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejé las llaves allí, sobre la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the keys there, on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Creo que el alma es inmortal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I believe the soul is immortal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El almacenamiento en la nube es muy práctico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cloud storage is very practical.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a almacenar agua para el verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to store water for the summer.

definitions.note: Plural of "almacén".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay varios almacenes cerca de la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several stores near the station.

definitions.note: Often used for a general store or a shop that sells goods; can also refer to a warehouse depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy al almacén a comprar pan y leche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to the store to buy bread and milk.

definitions.note: Plural of "alma".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las almas de los héroes viven en las historias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heroes' souls live in the stories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré almendras para hacer galletas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought almonds to make cookies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El almirante dio órdenes a toda la flota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The admiral gave orders to the whole fleet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una almohada más blanda para dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a softer pillow to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos dos almohadas más para el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need two more pillows for the sofa.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of “almorzar” for “I”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy almorcé con mis compañeros de trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I had lunch with my coworkers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy almorzamos en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we have lunch at home.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “almorzar”; used with “estar” to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy almorzando con mis compañeros de trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having lunch with my coworkers.

definitions.native: to have lunch; to eat lunch
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre prefiero almorzar a las dos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always prefer to have lunch at two.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) in the past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer almorzaron en un restaurante cerca de la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they had lunch at a restaurant near the office.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer almorzó con sus amigos en el centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she had lunch with his/her friends downtown.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "almorzar" (to have lunch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana almuerza en casa todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister has lunch at home every day.

definitions.native: I have lunch, I eat lunch
definitions.note: Present tense (yo) form of “almorzar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre almuerzo a la una.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always have lunch at one o'clock.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a preparar el almuerzo para mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to prepare lunch for my family.

definitions.note: Often used for places to stay when traveling (e.g., hotels, hostels, apartments).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buscamos alojamiento cerca del centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for accommodation near downtown.

definitions.note: From the verb "alojar"; often used for staying somewhere (e.g., a hotel, apartment, or a host’s home).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos alojamos en un hotel cerca de la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stay at a hotel near the beach.

definitions.note: Can mean either “we rent (out)” or “we rent/hire (something)” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alquilamos un apartamento cerca de la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We rent an apartment near the beach.

definitions.note: Can mean to rent something (e.g., a car) or to rent a place (e.g., an apartment) from someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a alquilar un coche para el fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to rent a car for the weekend.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito), third person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alquilaron un coche para el fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They rented a car for the weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El alquiler de este apartamento es muy caro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rent for this apartment is very expensive.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alquilé un apartamento cerca del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I rented an apartment near work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos árboles alrededor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many trees around.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “alrededor de” to mean “around/about (approximately)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay tiendas alrededor del parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are shops around the park.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos parques en los alrededores de la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many parks in the area around the city.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like “dar el alta” or “dar de alta” (to discharge).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dieron el alta hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They discharged him/her today.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "alto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La montaña es muy alta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mountain is very high.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este medicamento es altamente efectivo.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La calle es amplia y tranquila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is wide and quiet.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos una explicación amplia del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a broad explanation of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a ampliar la cocina el año que viene.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to expand the kitchen next year.

definitions.note: Masculine singular form; for feminine use "amplia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El salón es amplio y luminoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The living room is spacious and bright.

definitions.note: Often used for abstract things like interests, knowledge, or experience.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene un amplio conocimiento de historia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has extensive knowledge of history.

definitions.note: Common in Chile and some other Latin American countries; in Spain you’ll often hear “bombilla” for this meaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se quemó la ampolleta del baño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bathroom light bulb burned out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lleva un amuleto para tener buena suerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He carries an amulet to have good luck.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), 1st person singular: “I loved.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Amé esa película desde el primer minuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I loved that movie from the first minute.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: he/she/you (formal) loved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella amó a su familia siempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She loved her family always.

definitions.note: An interjection used to show surprise or that you didn’t hear/understand; often followed by a question.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Vienes mañana? —¿An? No te escuché bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “Are you coming tomorrow?” “Huh? I didn’t hear you well.”

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who cannot read or write; can also be used figuratively to mean “uneducated” in a specific area (e.g., analfabeto digital).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo era analfabeto y no podía leer cartas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was illiterate and couldn’t read letters.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomé un analgésico para el dolor de cabeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a painkiller for my headache.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico me recetó analgésicos para el dolor de espalda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed me painkillers for my back pain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es analista de datos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a data analyst.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos analizar los resultados antes de tomar una decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to analyze the results before making a decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la renuncia, el país cayó en la anarquía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the resignation, the country fell into anarchy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis ancestros vivían en un pueblo pequeño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ancestors lived in a small town.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of "ancho".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La calle es muy ancha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is very wide.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este pasillo es muy ancho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This hallway is very wide.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to the measurement of how wide something is.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ancho de la mesa es de un metro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The width of the table is one meter.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "ancho".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos pasillos anchos para que todos puedan pasar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need wide hallways so that everyone can get through.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La anchura de la mesa es de un metro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The width of the table is one meter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La anciana vive sola, pero sus hijos la visitan cada semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elderly woman lives alone, but her children visit her every week.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used as a noun to mean “an elderly woman.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La anciana vive sola en esa casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elderly woman lives alone in that house.

definitions.note: Often used to describe people; can also be used as a noun meaning “elderly person.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo es anciano, pero camina todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is elderly, but he walks every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El anciano camina despacio por el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The elderly man walks slowly through the park.

definitions.note: Masculine plural; can refer to a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En este centro ayudan a los ancianos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this center they help elderly people.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El barco echó el ancla cerca de la costa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship dropped anchor near the coast.

definitions.note: “and” is an English word, not standard Spanish. In Spanish, the usual equivalent is “y” (or “e” before words starting with i-/hi-). If you see “and” in Spanish text, it’s typically code-switching or a borrowed English conjunction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero pan and agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want bread and water, please.

definitions.note: Common as an exclamation (especially in Spain) to show surprise or to urge someone to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Anda, date prisa!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come on, hurry up!

definitions.note: Also commonly used to mean “goes” (from andar) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano anda muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother walks very fast.

definitions.note: Often used (especially in speech) with a gerund to mean someone was doing something or going around doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andaba buscando mis llaves cuando me llamaste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was looking for my keys when you called me.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of "andar"; it can describe an ongoing past action or what someone used to do.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andaba por el parque cuando empezó a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was walking through the park when it started to rain.

definitions.note: Present tense of “andar.” Often also means “we’re going” or “we’re getting around,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andamos por el parque todas las tardes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walk through the park every afternoon.

definitions.note: Used with a gerund (e.g., "andan buscando") to express that someone has been doing something lately or is going around doing it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andan buscando un nuevo apartamento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re looking for a new apartment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis hermanos andan al colegio todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brothers walk to school every day.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of "andar"; often used with "estar" to mean "to be walking".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy andando al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m walking to work.

definitions.note: Often used more generally than English “to walk,” meaning “to go” or “to be/operate” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta andar por el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to walk around the park.

definitions.native: you walk, you go, you are
definitions.note: Present tense (tú form) of "andar"; often used to ask how someone is doing or what they’re up to.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cómo andas hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you doing today?

definitions.note: Used with andar; can be the present subjunctive (yo) or a formal command (usted), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ande más despacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you go more slowly.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “I’m going around / I’m out and about,” and also in expressions like “ando buscando…” (“I’m looking for…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy ando por el centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m walking around downtown.

definitions.note: Adjective meaning “from (or relating to) Andromeda,” the galaxy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los astrónomos observaron un cúmulo andromedano muy brillante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The astronomers observed a very bright Andromedan cluster.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of "andar" (yo form). Often used for getting around on foot or moving about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer anduve por el centro toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I walked around downtown all afternoon.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "andar" (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer anduvo por el parque durante una hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, he walked through the park for an hour.

definitions.note: Informal imperative used with vos (voseo), common in Argentina/Uruguay.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Andá a casa y descansá un rato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go home and rest for a while.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a train/metro platform.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren sale del andén 3.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train leaves from platform 3.

definitions.note: Person who receives guests (e.g., at a party or event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuestro anfitrión nos recibió con una cena deliciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our host welcomed us with a delicious dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el mercado venden anguilas frescas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the market they sell fresh eels.

definitions.note: Often refers to strong emotional anguish or worry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento mucha angustia antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of anxiety before the exam.

definitions.native: to long for, to yearn for
definitions.note: More formal/literary than "querer" or "desear".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo anhelo volver a ver a mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I long to see my family again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevo un anillo de plata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wearing a silver ring.

definitions.note: Plural of “anillo”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo dos anillos de plata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two silver rings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi amiga me anima antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friend encourages me before the exam.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used to describe an event or atmosphere (e.g., a party).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La fiesta estuvo muy animada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The party was very lively.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; can describe something (like a film or a character) that has been given movement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi película favorita es animada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My favorite movie is animated.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person, mood, place, or event with lots of energy or spirit.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ambiente estuvo muy animado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The atmosphere was very lively.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La animadora saltó y aplaudió durante el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cheerleader jumped and clapped during the game.

definitions.note: Often used for a woman who hosts or leads activities at events, parties, or on TV/radio.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La animadora presentó a los invitados y mantuvo el ambiente alegre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The host introduced the guests and kept the atmosphere cheerful.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used to describe people who are in a good mood or full of energy.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños estaban animados en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids were excited at the party.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it describes behavior or instincts that are more like an animal’s (often implying something rough or uncivilized).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su reacción fue muy animal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His reaction was very animal-like.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese animal vive en la selva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That animal lives in the jungle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta granja hay muchos animales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this farm there are many animals.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero animarte antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to encourage you before the exam.

definitions.native: to encourage her, to cheer her up
definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “la” (= her; sometimes “it” for a feminine object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a animarla porque está nerviosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to encourage her because she's nervous.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), third person singular (he/she/you formal) of "animar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El entrenador animó al equipo antes del partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coach encouraged the team before the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es nuestro aniversario de boda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is our wedding anniversary.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoche cenamos en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night we had dinner at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al anochecer, salimos a caminar por el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At nightfall, we went out for a walk in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico notó una anomalía en los resultados del análisis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor noticed an anomaly in the test results.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone left speechless by surprise or shock.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me quedé anonadado cuando vi el precio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was stunned when I saw the price.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese comportamiento es anormal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That behavior is abnormal.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "anotar" (also used for commands: "Write it down").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anota tu dirección aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write down your address here, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hice una anotación en el margen del libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a note in the margin of the book.

definitions.note: Command form (ustedes) of "anotar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anotad la dirección y el número de teléfono, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write down the address and the phone number, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a anotar tu número de teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to write down your phone number.

definitions.note: Often used in sports contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El equipo local logró anotar dos goles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The home team managed to score two goals.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) or formal command (usted) of "anotar."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que anote la dirección correcta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you write down the correct address.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoté tu número de teléfono en mi cuaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote down your phone number in my notebook.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/it noted; you (formal) noted.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anotó la dirección en su cuaderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wrote down the address in his notebook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento mucha ansia antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of anxiety before the exam.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural (ansias), often in the phrase “con ansias” (“eagerly/with anticipation”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was eagerly looking forward to the vacation.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento ansiedad antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel anxiety before the exam.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy ansiosa antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm anxious before the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esperaba ansiosamente la respuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was anxiously waiting for the answer.

definitions.note: Often used for feeling worried, uneasy, or impatient about something that will happen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy ansioso por el examen de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm anxious about tomorrow's exam.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los estudiantes están ansiosos por conocer sus notas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are eager to find out their grades.

definitions.note: Often sounds literary or formal; in everyday speech people often use "tener ganas de" or "desear" instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella ansía volver a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She longs to go back home.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts and in fixed phrases (e.g., "ante todo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ante todo, gracias por venir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First of all, thanks for coming.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anteayer fui al médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The day before yesterday I went to the doctor.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about someone’s history or prior record (e.g., criminal record) or prior information about a topic.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa revisó sus antecedentes antes de contratarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company checked his background before hiring him.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase "con antelación" (in advance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Avísame con antelación si no puedes venir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me know in advance if you can't come.

definitions.note: Usually used in the phrase “de antemano” (e.g., “Gracias de antemano”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias de antemano por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks in advance for your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La antena de la radio está rota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The radio antenna is broken.

definitions.note: Common in Latin America; in Spain, “gafas” is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito mis anteojos para leer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need my glasses to read.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis antepasados vivían en un pueblo pequeño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My ancestors lived in a small village.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la página anterior está la información que necesitas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the previous page is the information you need.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anteriormente vivía en Madrid, pero ahora vivo en Valencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I previously lived in Madrid, but now I live in Valencia.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” to mean “before” + noun/infinitive (e.g., “antes de comer”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lávate las manos antes de comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wash your hands before eating.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about something happening sooner in time, and in expressions like "antes de" or "antes que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo llegué antes que mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arrived before my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El doctor me recetó antibióticos para la infección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed antibiotics for my infection.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentí mucha anticipación antes del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt a lot of anticipation before the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa regla me parece anticuada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That rule seems outdated to me.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esas ideas son anticuadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those ideas are old-fashioned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese diseño se ve anticuado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That design looks outdated.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “antiguo”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Visitamos una iglesia antigua en el centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We visited an old church downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antiguamente, la gente escribía cartas a mano con más frecuencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Formerly, people wrote letters by hand more often.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las casas antiguas del centro son muy bonitas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The old houses downtown are very beautiful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en un barrio antiguo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in an old neighborhood.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos edificios son muy antiguos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These buildings are very old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el museo hay una antigüedad romana muy valiosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the museum there is a very valuable Roman antique.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela colecciona antigüedades.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother collects antiques.

definitions.note: Often used for sudden cravings (especially for food).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un antojo de chocolate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a craving for chocolate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encendieron una antorcha para ver en la cueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They lit a torch to see in the cave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevaban antorchas para ver en la cueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They carried torches to see in the cave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico le dio un antídoto para el veneno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor gave him an antidote for the poison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hacemos un chequeo médico anual.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We do an annual medical checkup.

definitions.note: Often refers to a school yearbook; it can also mean an annual publication.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busqué mi foto en el anuario de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked for my photo in the school yearbook.

definitions.note: Often used in formal/legal or administrative contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La anulación del vuelo nos obligó a buscar otro hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cancellation of the flight forced us to look for another hotel.

definitions.note: Past participle of "anular"; often used with "haber" (e.g., "ha sido anulado").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flight has been canceled because of the storm.
