definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They had to cancel the reservation because of the bad weather.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El nuevo horario ya ha sido anunciado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The new schedule has already been announced.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a anunciar los resultados mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to announce the results tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for promoting a product, service, or event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa va a anunciar su nuevo producto en la tele.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is going to advertise its new product on TV.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “they announced” / “you (all) announced” (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anunciaron los resultados esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They announced the results this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vi un anuncio de zapatos en internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw an ad for shoes on the internet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El director hizo un anuncio importante en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The principal made an important announcement at the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vi varios anuncios en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw several ads on the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El presidente anunció nuevas medidas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The president announced new measures.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pescador puso un gusano en el anzuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fisherman put a worm on the hook.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El análisis muestra que necesitamos más tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The analysis shows that we need more time.

definitions.note: Informal tú command with a reflexive pronoun (used to encourage someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anímate, todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cheer up, everything is going to turn out fine.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La denuncia fue anónima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report was anonymous.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Recibimos varias cartas anónimas en la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We received several anonymous letters at the office.

definitions.note: Adjective meaning someone/something whose identity is unknown or not revealed; can also refer to something done without disclosing the author.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El autor anónimo publicó el artículo en una revista científica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The anonymous author published the article in a scientific journal.

definitions.note: Also commonly used for putting out a fire/light (e.g., a candle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, apaga la luz cuando salgas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn off the light when you leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luz está apagada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is off.

definitions.note: Used for lights or devices that are not on.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las luces están apagadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lights are turned off.

definitions.note: Often used for lights or devices; can also describe something dim or dull depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El televisor está apagado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The TV is off.

definitions.note: Used as the past participle of "apagar" and often as an adjective (e.g., a device that is off).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El teléfono está apagado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is turned off.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ando): used to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy apagando la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am turning off the light.

definitions.note: Used for switching off lights, devices, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, recuerda apagar la luz cuando salgas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please remember to turn off the light when you leave.

definitions.note: Used for extinguishing a fire or flame.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los bomberos lograron apagar el fuego rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The firefighters managed to put out the fire quickly.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apagaron la luz antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They turned off the light before leaving.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted), especially with lights or devices.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apague la luz, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn off the light, please.

definitions.note: Plural command (ustedes) and also a present subjunctive form (e.g., after expressions of desire or request).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, apaguen las luces al salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn off the lights when you leave.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apagué la luz antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned off the light before leaving.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/you (formal) turned off/put out.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apagó la luz antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She turned off the light before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo un apagón y no pudimos ver la televisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a power outage and we couldn't watch TV.

definitions.note: Often refers to a piece of furniture used for storing or displaying items (e.g., dishes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pusimos los platos en el aparador del comedor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We put the plates in the dining room sideboard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este aparato no funciona bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This device isn't working well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apaga los aparatos antes de salir de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn off the devices before leaving the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El aparcamiento está lleno hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The parking lot is full today.

definitions.note: Used for parking a vehicle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a aparcar el coche aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to park the car here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aparcó el coche cerca de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She parked the car near home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato aparece de repente en la ventana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat suddenly appears in the window.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “aparecer”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces aparecen problemas de última hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes last-minute problems appear.

definitions.note: Conjugates irregularly in the preterite (yo aparecí, él/ella apareció).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De repente va a aparecer un gato en la ventana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly a cat is going to appear in the window.

definitions.native: to appear (in print/on screen); to be published; to come out
definitions.note: Often used for something that becomes visible or is released (an article, a video, a notice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi artículo va a aparecer mañana en el periódico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My article is going to appear tomorrow in the newspaper.

definitions.native: to appear (as a character/performer); to make an appearance
definitions.note: Used for being seen in a place or event, or being featured.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La actriz va a aparecer en la próxima temporada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actress is going to appear in the next season.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El nombre aparecerá en la pantalla en unos segundos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The name will appear on the screen in a few seconds.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha aparecido un problema inesperado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An unexpected problem has appeared.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "aparecer"; often used after "si" to talk about a hypothetical situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si apareciera Juan, avísame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If Juan showed up, let me know.

definitions.note: Past tense (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De repente, aparecieron dos perros en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly, two dogs appeared in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apareciste justo cuando te estaba buscando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You showed up just when I was looking for you.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form; often used for a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De repente, apareció un gato en la ventana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suddenly, a cat appeared in the window.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (can mean an ongoing past action or something that used to happen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luna aparecía entre las nubes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The moon was appearing between the clouds.

definitions.note: Often used to describe how something looks or seems, which may or may not match reality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aparenta estar cansada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She seems to be tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aparentemente, el tren llega a tiempo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apparently, the train arrives on time today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La aparición del sol cambió el ánimo de todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The appearance of the sun changed everyone’s mood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su apariencia cambió mucho después del viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her appearance changed a lot after the trip.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “las apariencias engañan” (“appearances can be deceiving”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te fíes de las apariencias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t trust appearances.

definitions.note: Can be used as a statement (he/she/it moves aside) or as an informal command (tú): “Move aside!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aparta la silla para que podamos pasar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She moves the chair aside so that we can get through.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something that is far away from other places (remote).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vive en un pueblo apartado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives in an isolated town.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco un apartamento cerca del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for an apartment near work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buscamos apartamentos cerca del centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for apartments near downtown.

definitions.native: to move aside, to set aside
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes apartar la silla para que pasen?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you move the chair aside so they can pass?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano y yo vivimos aparte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother and I live apart.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed expressions like “aparte de” (besides/aside from) or “aparte” to mean “set aside.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aparte de eso, todo está bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Aside from that, everything is fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apartó la silla para que pudiéramos pasar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He moved the chair aside so we could pass.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (e.g., “Me apasiona…”), meaning “I’m passionate about…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me apasiona la música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m passionate about music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habló apasionadamente sobre la importancia de la educación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke passionately about the importance of education.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un lector apasionado de novelas históricas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a passionate reader of historical novels.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una historia apasionante de principio a fin.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an exciting story from beginning to end.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (apelar a algo / a alguien) meaning “to appeal to” (to request, to call on, or to rely on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abogado va a apelar la sentencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer is going to appeal the sentence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi apellido es García.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My last name is García.

definitions.note: Often used to express feeling upset about something (e.g., bad news or a problem).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy apenado por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sad about what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apenas entiendo lo que dice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hardly understand what he says.

definitions.note: Used with time expressions to mean something happens immediately after something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apenas llegues, llámame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As soon as you arrive, call me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico dijo que tengo apendicitis y necesito una operación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor said I have appendicitis and I need surgery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La apertura de la tienda es a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store opening is at nine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa basura apesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That garbage stinks.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense: describes an ongoing or habitual situation in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cocina apestaba a pescado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen stank of fish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tus zapatos apestan después del entrenamiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your shoes stink after training.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Apestas a humo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You stink of smoke!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La basura está apestosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trash is stinky.

definitions.note: Often used informally and can sound insulting when describing a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Qué calcetines tan apestosos!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What stinky socks!

definitions.native: feels like, sounds good, would like
definitions.note: Used to talk about what someone feels like doing or having (often with an indirect object like “me/te/le”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Te apetece un café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you feel like a coffee?

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used for past habits/feelings like “I used to feel like...” or “I wanted to...”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes no me apetecía salir por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before, I didn’t feel like going out at night.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les) to mean “to feel like” (e.g., “me apetece…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te apetezca, podemos salir a caminar después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you feel like it, we can go for a walk after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo apetito hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have an appetite today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando vio al perro herido, se apiadó y lo llevó al veterinario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the injured dog, he took pity and took it to the vet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito apio para hacer la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need celery to make the soup.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective (also the past participle of "aplastar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche quedó aplastado después del accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car ended up crushed after the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aplastó la lata con el pie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She crushed the can with his/her foot.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): “they” form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando terminó el concierto, aplaudieron con entusiasmo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When the concert ended, they applauded enthusiastically.

definitions.native: we applauded, we clap, we clapped
definitions.note: Can mean either the preterite (past) or the present tense “we applaud/clap,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aplaudimos al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We applauded at the end of the concert.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), third-person singular (he/she/you formal) of “aplaudir.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El público aplaudió al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauded at the end of the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El público le dio un aplauso al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience gave him/her applause at the end of the concert.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al final del concierto, hubo muchos aplausos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the concert, there was a lot of applause.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El partido fue aplazado por la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The game was postponed because of the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta regla aplica a todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This rule applies to everyone.

definitions.note: Often used for software (“app”), but can also mean an application (e.g., for a job or school).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Descargué una aplicación para aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I downloaded an app to learn Spanish.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone (especially a student) who works diligently.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy aplicado y siempre hace la tarea a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very hardworking and always does his homework on time.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (to apply to) or “para” (to apply for).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a aplicar para ese trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to apply for that job.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” (apoderarse de algo) to mean taking control/possession of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los rebeldes intentaron apoderarse de la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rebels tried to take over the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su apodo es “El Tigre”.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His nickname is “The Tiger”.

definitions.note: Often used for the highest point of success, popularity, or development.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La banda llegó a su apogeo en los años noventa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The band reached its peak in the 1990s.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu aporte fue muy útil para el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your contribution was very useful for the project.

definitions.note: Commonly used in some regions; often heard as the phrase “a posta.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo hizo aposta para molestarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did it on purpose to annoy me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy apostando cinco euros a que gana el equipo rojo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m betting five euros that the red team will win.

definitions.note: Often used with "por" (to bet on something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a apostar por nuestro equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to bet on our team.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aposté cinco euros a que ganaba nuestro equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bet five euros that our team would win.

definitions.note: From the verb "apoyar". Often used for supporting a person, idea, or plan.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella apoya a su amiga en todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She supports her friend in everything.

definitions.note: Often used with "en" for what something is resting on: "apoyado en..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cartel está apoyado en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sign is leaning against the wall.

definitions.note: Can describe being supported by someone or something (literal or figurative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El proyecto está apoyado por el director.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project is supported by the director.

definitions.note: Past participle of "apoyar"; often used with "estar" to describe something being supported/leaning on something else ("apoyado en").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cartel está apoyado en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sign is leaning against the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a apoyar tu idea en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to support your idea in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes apoyar la bicicleta contra la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can lean the bike against the wall.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos me apoyaron durante el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends supported me during the exam.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “apoyar”; also used for formal commands (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me apoye en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you support me in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te apoyo en todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I support you in everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tu apoyo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for your support.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apoyé a mi amigo cuando tuvo un problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I supported my friend when he had a problem.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it supported/helped.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella apoyó a su amiga cuando lo necesitaba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She supported her friend when she needed it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aprecia mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She really appreciates your help.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (e.g., “I/he/she used to appreciate” or “was appreciating,” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo apreciaba mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really appreciated your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Apreciamos tu ayuda con el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We appreciate your help with the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos aprecian mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends really appreciate your help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero apreciar más tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to appreciate your help more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprecio mucho tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really appreciate your help.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (usted/él/ella) or affirmative command for usted ("Learn!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que usted aprenda español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to learn Spanish.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, ustedes form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que aprendan mucho este semestre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you learn a lot this semester.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú). Often used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que aprendas español conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to learn Spanish with me.

definitions.note: Also used for commands (informal): “learn!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana aprende español en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister learns Spanish at school.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (plural “you”) in Spain; present imperative (command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprended estas palabras para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learn these words for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En clase aprendemos español todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In class we learn Spanish every day.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “aprender” (used for “they” and also “you all” in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños aprenden rápido en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids learn quickly at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to learn Spanish.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it will learn) or formal you (usted) will learn.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aprenderá español este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will learn Spanish this year.

definitions.note: Future tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprenderán español rápidamente si practican todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will learn Spanish quickly if they practice every day.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprenderás mucho si practicas todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will learn a lot if you practice every day.

definitions.note: First-person singular, simple future (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprenderé español este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will learn Spanish this year.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendes rápido cuando practicas todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You learn quickly when you practice every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He aprendido mucho este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have learned a lot this year.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "aprender"; used for actions in progress (often with "estar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aprendiendo español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am learning Spanish.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form of “aprender”; often used in “si” (if) clauses and in wishes/hypotheticals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo aprendiera español, viajaría más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I learned Spanish, I would travel more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendieron español en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They learned Spanish at school.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer aprendimos mucho en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we learned a lot in class.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Dónde aprendiste español?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where did you learn Spanish?

definitions.note: Often used as an interjection to call people’s attention, like “Attention!” or “Listen up!”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito tu atención por un momento.

definitions.native: to attend to, to take care of

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to attend to the customers now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La enfermera atendió al paciente de inmediato.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.note: Often used for accidents involving a car, bike, etc., hitting a person or animal.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team captain spoke with the referee.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of "comprar"; often used with "estar" to talk about an action in progress
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy comprando pan para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am buying bread for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero comprar un libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to buy a book.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "comprar"; often used in hypothetical or dependent clauses (e.g., after "si").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo comprara un coche, viajaría más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I bought a car, I would travel more.

definitions.note: Simple future (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana compraremos comida para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will buy food for the party.

definitions.native: to buy (something) for him, her, you (formal)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to/for him, to/for her, or to/for you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a comprarle un regalo a mi mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to buy my mom a gift.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached ("it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a comprarlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to buy it tomorrow.

definitions.note: This form includes the indirect object pronoun “me” (“for me/to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes comprarme un café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you buy me a coffee?

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): “they bought” / “you all bought” (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer compraron pan y leche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they bought bread and milk.

definitions.note: Reflexive form of "comprar"; it often implies buying something for yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a comprarse un coche nuevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to buy myself a new car.

definitions.note: Direct-object pronoun + indirect-object pronoun attached to the infinitive: comprar + te.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero comprarte un regalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to buy you a gift.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal "you" (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana comprará un coche nuevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will buy a new car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana compraré pan y leche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will buy bread and milk.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo lo compraría, pero no tengo dinero ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would buy it, but I don’t have money right now.

definitions.note: Plural form of “compra.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hice las compras esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did the shopping this morning.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense of “comprar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué compras en el supermercado?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you buy at the supermarket?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), tú form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Compraste pan para el desayuno?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you buy bread for breakfast?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) of "comprar"; also the formal command (usted) "buy".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que yo compre pan hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I buy bread today.

definitions.note: Usually the formal command (usted) form: “(you) understand.” It can also be present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, comprenda mi situación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please understand my situation.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (also used for formal “you”: usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella comprende la lección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She understands the lesson.

definitions.note: Used to talk about what something contains or covers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El precio comprende el desayuno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The price includes breakfast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No comprendemos la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t understand the question.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “comprender”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos no comprenden la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They don’t understand the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo comprender por qué está tan enojado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't understand why he is so angry.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprenderlo antes de tomar una decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to understand it before making a decision.

definitions.note: Future tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo comprenderás cuando seas mayor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will understand it when you are older.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Comprendes la pregunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you understand the question?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Has comprendido la pregunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you understood the question?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) understood.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finalmente comprendió la lección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Finally, he understood the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No comprendo la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand the question.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "comprender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por fin comprendí la lección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I finally understood the lesson.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu explicación fue clara y comprensible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your explanation was clear and understandable.

definitions.note: Describes a person who is sympathetic and shows understanding toward others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesor es muy comprensivo cuando alguien llega tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is very understanding when someone arrives late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tu comprensión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your understanding.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "comprar"; also used as the negative informal command "don’t buy".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que compres pan hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you buy bread today.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "comprar" ("I buy").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro pan todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy bread every day.

definitions.note: Past participle of "comprobar"; often used as an adjective meaning something has been confirmed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El billete ya está comprobado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket has already been checked.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “comprobar” (often used with “estar” to mean “is/are checking”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy comprobando la información antes de enviarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m checking the information before sending it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a comprobar si la puerta está cerrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to check if the door is closed.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “-lo” = “it” (referring to a masculine or neutral thing/idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes de enviar el correo, voy a comprobarlo otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before sending the email, I’m going to check it again.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprobé el horario del tren antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the train schedule before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El técnico comprobó la conexión antes de irse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The technician checked the connection before leaving.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" + infinitive ("comprometerte a hacer algo" = commit yourself to doing something). It looks like English "compromise" but usually means "commit" or "pledge" in this form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que comprometerte a estudiar un poco cada día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to commit yourself to studying a little every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está muy comprometida con su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very committed to her work.

definitions.note: In the sense of being engaged to be married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está comprometida y se casa en junio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is engaged and is getting married in June.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to talk about being committed/engaged in a cause or responsibility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está muy comprometido con su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very committed to his work.

definitions.note: Used (often with "estar") to mean engaged to be married. Note: the form changes with gender/number (e.g., comprometida, comprometidos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María está comprometido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María is engaged.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos comprometidos con el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are committed to the project.

definitions.note: Used to talk about being engaged to be married.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos están comprometidos y se casan en junio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are engaged and they’re getting married in June.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: «se comprometió» = “(he/she) committed (himself/herself) / promised.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se comprometió a estudiar todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He committed to studying every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El error comprometió la seguridad del sistema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mistake compromised the system’s security.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un compromiso con mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a commitment to my family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo ir porque tengo otros compromisos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't go because I have other commitments.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comprueba tu correo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check your email, please.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with the object pronoun “lo” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no estás seguro, compruébalo en internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you’re not sure, check it on the internet.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular: “I bought.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer compré pan en la panadería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I bought bread at the bakery.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), third person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella compró pan esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She bought bread this morning.

definitions.note: Often refers to a gate that controls the flow of water (e.g., in a canal or dam).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La compuerta del canal está cerrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The canal gate is closed.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something formed from several parts (e.g., a “palabra compuesta” = a compound word).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La palabra "paraguas" es una palabra compuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The word "paraguas" is a compound word.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El informe está compuesto de tres partes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report is made up of three parts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene un comportamiento compulsivo con las compras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has compulsive behavior with shopping.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "componer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El compositor compuso una canción nueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The composer composed a new song.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un computador para hacer la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a computer to do my homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi computadora está en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My computer is on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas computadoras en la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many computers in the office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la oficina hay muchos computadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the office there are many computers.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); reflexive form: “behave yourself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compórtate en la escuela, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Behave at school, please.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos intereses comunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have common interests.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las comunicaciones en la ciudad mejoraron después de la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communications in the city improved after the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La comunicación es clave en un buen equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communication is key in a good team.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “comunicar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos se comunican por correo electrónico todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They communicate by email every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comunicar esta información al equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to communicate this information to the team.

definitions.native: to communicate with someone, to get in touch
definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “me” (= “to me / with me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes comunicarme la información por correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can send me the information by email.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb: often used for communicating with someone (e.g., “to get in touch”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comunicarse con mi profesora por correo electrónico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to communicate with my teacher by email.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta comunidad es muy acogedora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This community is very welcoming.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El comunismo fue muy influyente en la política del siglo XX.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Communism was very influential in 20th-century politics.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo era comunista en su juventud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a communist in his youth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo era comunista cuando era joven.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather was a communist when he was young.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el siglo XX, muchos comunistas fueron perseguidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the 20th century, many communists were persecuted.

definitions.note: Often used to describe things related to the local community or shared by a group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este centro comunitario ofrece clases gratis los fines de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This community center offers free classes on weekends.

definitions.note: Often refers to the Christian sacrament (especially First Communion).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi prima hizo la comunión el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousin had her First Communion last year.

definitions.note: Used with vos (voseo): affirmative imperative (command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comé despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat slowly, please.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (informal plural “you” in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿A qué hora coméis hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time do you eat today?

definitions.note: Infinitive with attached pronouns: me + lo. Often implies eating it up / eating it myself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a comérmelo todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to eat it all up.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), 1st person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer comí una manzana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ate an apple.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, comía cereal todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to eat cereal every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un error común.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a common mistake.

definitions.note: Used in the expression “el bien común” (the common good).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debemos pensar en el bien común.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must think about the common good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comúnmente llego a casa a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually get home at six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy con mi hermano al parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the park with my brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es difícil concebir una vida sin internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to imagine a life without the internet.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., permissions or requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acceso concedido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Access granted.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jefe le concedió un día libre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss granted him a day off.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito concentración para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need concentration to study.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used to describe a person’s attention or focus, or something made more intense/strong.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está muy concentrada en su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very focused on her work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy concentrado en la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m focused on the task.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito concentrar mi atención en el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to concentrate my attention on the exam.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with "me" ("myself"); used when talking about concentrating (e.g., "I need to concentrate").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito concentrarme en mi trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to concentrate on my work.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; typically used with a reflexive pronoun (me/te/se/nos/os/se).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito concentrarse para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to concentrate to study.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “te” (“yourself/you”), as in “concentrate (yourself)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas concentrarte en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to concentrate in class.

definitions.note: This form matches the verb "concentrar" (not "conocer").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me concentro mejor cuando estoy en silencio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I concentrate better when I’m in silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entiendo el concepto de la gravedad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't understand the concept of gravity.

definitions.note: Plural of “concepto”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendimos nuevos conceptos en la clase de ciencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We learned new concepts in science class.

definitions.note: Usually refers to seashells.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontré conchas en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found shells on the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo la conciencia tranquila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a clear conscience.

definitions.note: Used to say something is relevant to someone or something (often with "a").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esto no me concierne.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This doesn’t concern me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos al concierto esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We're going to the concert tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este verano hay muchos conciertos en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This summer there are many concerts in the park.

definitions.note: Past participle of "concluir"; often used with "estar" to mean something is finished.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El informe está concluido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report is finished.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a concluir la reunión a las cinco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to conclude the meeting at five.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al final del informe, escribimos las conclusiones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the end of the report, we wrote the conclusions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi conclusión es que necesitamos más tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My conclusion is that we need more time.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La reunión concluyó a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The meeting concluded at six.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos una idea concreta para empezar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a specific idea to get started.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a woman in a long-term relationship with a man without being married to him.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la novela, el rey vivía con su concubina en el palacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the novel, the king lived with his concubine in the palace.

definitions.note: Used to say something is in agreement or consistent with something else (often with "con" or "en").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su historia no concuerda con los hechos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His story doesn’t match the facts.

definitions.note: Often used for competitions with an evaluation or selection process (e.g., talent contests, job openings, grants).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana ganó un concurso de fotografía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister won a photography contest.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Concéntrate en tu trabajo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Focus on your work, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi familia vive en un condado rural.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My family lives in a rural county.

definitions.note: A male noble title; feminine is "condesa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El conde vive en un castillo antiguo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The count lives in an old castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez dictó una condena de cinco años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge handed down a five-year prison sentence.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mujer fue condenada por el juez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The woman was condemned by the judge.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sin agua, la planta está condenada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without water, the plant is doomed.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts to mean “convicted” or “sentenced.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El hombre fue condenado a diez años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was sentenced to ten years in prison.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (e.g., being sentenced to prison).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue condenado a diez años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was sentenced to ten years in prison.

definitions.note: Can be used more generally to mean strongly criticized or doomed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El edificio fue condenado por ser peligroso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was condemned for being dangerous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los prisioneros fueron condenados a varios años de cárcel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The prisoners were sentenced to several years in prison.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): refers to a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los jueces condenaron al acusado a cinco años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judges sentenced the defendant to five years in prison.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/it/you formal) of “condenar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez lo condenó a cinco años de prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge sentenced him to five years in prison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La condesa vive en un castillo antiguo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The countess lives in an old castle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Acepto las condiciones del contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I accept the conditions of the contract.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una condición médica que requiere tratamiento.
