definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to know me before judging me.

definitions.note: Often used when meeting someone for the first time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres conocerme mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to meet me tomorrow?

definitions.native: to meet each other, to get to know each other
definitions.note: Reflexive form with "nos" (we/each other).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queremos conocernos mejor antes de mudarnos juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to get to know each other better before moving in together.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive; often used for meeting someone for the first time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue un placer conocerse en persona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a pleasure to meet each other in person.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive; used for people being familiar with each other.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante conocerse bien antes de casarse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to know each other well before getting married.

definitions.native: to meet you, to know you
definitions.note: Infinitive of "conocer" with the object pronoun "te" (you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me alegro de conocerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm happy to meet you.

definitions.note: Future tense (3rd person singular): “he/she/it will…”, “you (formal) will…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana conocerá a mis padres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will meet my parents.

definitions.native: you will know, you will meet
definitions.note: Future tense (tú). Often used for becoming familiar with a place/person or meeting someone for the first time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana conocerás a mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will meet my family.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense of "conocer"; often used for knowing people/places or being familiar with something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Conoces a mi hermana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you know my sister?

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used for a person, place, or thing that is well-known or familiar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es una cantante muy conocida en España.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a very well-known singer in Spain.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; often used as an adjective (e.g., describing a woman or a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es una actriz conocida en toda España.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a well-known actress throughout Spain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un lugar muy conocido en la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a very well-known place in the city.

definitions.note: Past participle of "conocer"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese lugar ha sido conocido por su comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That place has been known for its food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un conocido me recomendó este restaurante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An acquaintance recommended this restaurant to me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son lugares conocidos para mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are places that are known to me.

definitions.note: Refers to people you know, but not close friends.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a la fiesta con mis conocidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the party with my acquaintances.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “conocer”; often used after expressions like “si…” (if) or “quería que…” (wanted that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si conociera a tu hermano, lo saludaría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I met your brother, I would say hi to him.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (tú). Often used after expressions like “si…” or “ojalá…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ojalá conocieras mejor a tus vecinos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wish you knew your neighbors better.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (tú). Can be used when “conocer” means meeting someone for the first time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si conocieras a mi profesor, te gustaría mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you met my teacher, you would really like him.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person plural: “they” (or “you all” in some regions) did the action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conocieron a mis padres en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They met my parents at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene mucho conocimiento sobre la historia de España.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has a lot of knowledge about the history of Spain.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used to talk about someone’s knowledge or expertise in a subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas conocimientos básicos de informática para este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need basic computer knowledge for this job.

definitions.native: we met, we got to know
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "conocer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer conocimos a tus amigos en el café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we met your friends at the café.

definitions.note: Preterite tense (informal singular “tú”): used for a completed past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Conociste a mi hermana ayer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you meet my sister yesterday?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (nosotros/nosotras); often used after expressions like “quería que…”, “era importante que…”, or in “si…” clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era importante que conociéramos bien las reglas antes de empezar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was important that we knew the rules well before we started.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of “conocer”; often used for meeting someone for the first time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella conoció a su esposo en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She met her husband at university.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (informal plural “you” in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Conocéis a mi hermano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you all know my brother?

definitions.native: I met, I got to know
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "conocer" (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer conocí a tu hermana en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I met your sister at the party.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense: often means “used to know” or “was knowing” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, conocía a muchas personas en el barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I knew (used to know) many people in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing/repeated past situations or background description).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando éramos niños, conocíamos a todos los vecinos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we knew all the neighbors.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all/formal you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando eran niños, conocían a todos en el barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they were kids, they knew everyone in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando vivías en Madrid, conocías a mucha gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you lived in Madrid, you knew a lot of people.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “conocer” (also used for the formal command “(you) meet/know”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que usted conozca a mi familia pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you meet my family soon.

definitions.native: let's get to know, let's meet
definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros) of “conocer”; often used to make suggestions with “que” (e.g., “Que conozcamos…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor que conozcamos a tus padres antes de la boda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better that we meet your parents before the wedding.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes/ellos/ellas) of "conocer"; often used after phrases like "espero que", "quiero que", or "para que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que conozcan a mi familia pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you (all) meet my family soon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form) of "conocer"; often used after expressions like "espero que" or "dudo que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que conozcas a mi hermana mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you meet my sister tomorrow.

definitions.note: used for knowing people and for being familiar with places or things
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conozco bien a Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know Ana well.

definitions.note: Common in Latin America and informal speech; it introduces a consequence (similar to “así que”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me contestó, conque me fui a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She didn’t answer me, so I went home.

definitions.note: Past participle of "conquistar"; it can also be used as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El país fue conquistado hace muchos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country was conquered many years ago.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los romanos conquistaron gran parte de Europa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Romans conquered a large part of Europe.

definitions.note: Often used for winning someone’s affection or support.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiere conquistar a sus clientes con buen servicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She wants to win over his/her customers with good service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo la consciencia tranquila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a clear conscience.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of being aware of something (e.g., social or environmental awareness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más consciencia sobre el cambio climático.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more awareness about climate change.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” to mean “aware of.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soy consciente de mis errores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am aware of my mistakes.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Somos conscientes del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are aware of the problem.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su decisión tuvo una consecuencia importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His decision had an important consequence.

definitions.note: Plural form of "consecuencia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus decisiones tuvieron consecuencias graves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His decisions had serious consequences.

definitions.note: Past participle of "conseguir"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he conseguido").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He conseguido un trabajo nuevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a new job.

definitions.note: Usually means “we succeeded in getting/doing something.” It can also be the present tense “we get/we manage,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conseguimos entradas para el concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We got tickets for the concert.

definitions.note: Often implies achieving something after effort (like “manage to”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por fin voy a conseguir entradas para el concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m finally going to get tickets for the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo conseguir entender este problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t manage to understand this problem.

definitions.native: we will get, we will manage
definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros) future tense of "conseguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si trabajamos juntos, conseguiremos una solución pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we work together, we will find a solution soon.

definitions.note: "lo" is an attached object pronoun meaning “it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a conseguirlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to get it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive of “conseguir” with the attached pronoun “me” (“for me/to me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes conseguirme dos entradas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you get me two tickets?

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun "te" (= you). Often means getting something for you.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a conseguirte un trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to get you a job.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal you (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si estudia más, conseguirá mejores notas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you study more, you will get better grades.

definitions.native: you will get, you will obtain, you will achieve
definitions.note: Future tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si sigues practicando, conseguirás buenos resultados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you keep practicing, you will get good results.

definitions.native: I will get, I will obtain
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conseguiré un trabajo mejor este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will get a better job this year.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “conseguir”; often used for hypothetical situations or polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuviera más tiempo, conseguiría un segundo trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more time, I would get a second job.

definitions.native: you got, you obtained, you managed (to)
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular "you" (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Conseguiste las entradas para el concierto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you get the tickets for the concert?

definitions.native: I got, I managed to get
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form meaning a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conseguí las entradas para el concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got the tickets for the concert.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "conseguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes conseguía entradas gratis para los conciertos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before, I used to get free tickets for concerts.

definitions.note: Often used for a professional or official role (for example, a school counselor or an advisor on a council).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El consejero me dio un buen consejo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The advisor gave me good advice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un consejo para mi entrevista de trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some advice for my job interview.

definitions.note: Plural form of "consejo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis padres siempre me dan buenos consejos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents always give me good advice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegaron a un consenso después de hablar un rato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They reached a consensus after talking for a while.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos tu consentimiento para usar tus datos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need your consent to use your data.

definitions.note: Often refers to the person who looks after an apartment building or is stationed at the entrance to help residents and visitors.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El conserje del edificio recibe los paquetes por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building caretaker receives the packages in the morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella conserva las fotos en una caja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She keeps the photos in a box.

definitions.note: Often used for political views, but can also describe a cautious/traditional approach in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos son muy conservadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are very conservative.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos son muy conservadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are very conservative.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes conservar esta carta para siempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can keep this letter forever.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a school for music (and sometimes other performing arts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana estudia piano en el conservatorio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister studies piano at the conservatory.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions of desire/necessity) or as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que conserve esta carta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to keep this letter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella considera cambiar de trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She considers changing jobs.

definitions.native: considered, used to consider, was considering
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), often used for ongoing/repeated actions or background context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes consideraba mudarme a otra ciudad, pero cambié de idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before, I used to consider moving to another city, but I changed my mind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo un aumento considerable en los precios este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a considerable increase in prices this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tu consideración.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for your consideration.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es considerada una experta en el tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is considered an expert on the topic.

definitions.note: Past participle of “considerar”. Often used with “ser/estar” to form the passive voice or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es considerada una experta en el tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is considered an expert on the topic.

definitions.note: Describes a person’s behavior; can also mean “respected/esteemed” in some contexts, but that sense is not as common for beginners.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy considerado con los demás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very considerate toward others.

definitions.note: Often used with "ser" to mean "is considered".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es considerado un experto en el tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is considered an expert on the topic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consideramos que es una buena idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We consider that it’s a good idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consideran que es una buena idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They think it’s a good idea.

definitions.note: Gerund form; often used to mean “given that” or “taking into account that”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Considerando el tráfico, salimos más temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Considering the traffic, we left earlier.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a considerar tu propuesta antes de decidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to consider your proposal before deciding.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form ("-ra") of "considerar"; often used after expressions like "quería que" or in "si" clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que considerara mi propuesta antes de decidir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted you to consider my proposal before deciding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Considero que esta idea es importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think this idea is important.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consideré varias opciones antes de decidirme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I considered several options before deciding.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María consideró la oferta y decidió aceptarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María considered the offer and decided to accept it.

definitions.note: Command (tú) form with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no te gusta este plan, considéralo otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t like this plan, consider it again.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "conseguir" (also used for formal commands: "you (formal) get/obtain...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que consiga el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you get the job.

definitions.note: First-person plural present subjunctive of “conseguir”; often used after “que” or to make a suggestion (e.g., “Que consigamos…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ojalá consigamos entradas para el concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hopefully we can get tickets for the concert.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que consigan trabajo pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they get a job soon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form) of "conseguir"; often used after expressions of desire, doubt, or requests (e.g., "Espero que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que consigas el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you get the job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No consigo entender esta lección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t manage to understand this lesson.

definitions.native: with himself / with herself / with itself / with yourself / with themselves
definitions.note: Reflexive prepositional pronoun meaning “with oneself”; it’s used for 3rd person (él/ella/usted/ellos/ellas/ustedes) and for the formal imperative (e.g., “Llévese…”). It corresponds to “con + sí” → “consigo.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre lleva su cuaderno consigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She always carries his/her notebook with him/her.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “conseguir” (also used for the informal command “(you) get/obtain”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre consigue lo que quiere.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always gets what he wants.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form) of "conseguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Consigues el pan en la panadería de la esquina?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you get the bread at the bakery on the corner?

definitions.note: Often used with an infinitive: "consigues + infinitive".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Consigues terminar el trabajo hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you manage to finish the work today?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consiguieron entradas para el concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They got tickets for the concert.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "conseguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por fin consiguió el trabajo que quería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He finally got the job he wanted.

definitions.note: Used with "en" to say what something is made up of or based on ("consiste en").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El trabajo consiste en ayudar a los clientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The job consists of helping customers.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing or habitual past descriptions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La receta consistía en tres ingredientes básicos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The recipe consisted of three basic ingredients.

definitions.note: Often refers to a video game console.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me compré una consola nueva para jugar con mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new console to play with my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Intenté consolar a mi amiga después de la noticia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tried to comfort my friend after the news.

definitions.native: to comfort her, to console her
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a llamarla para consolarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to call her to comfort her.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por consolarme cuando estaba triste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for comforting me when I was sad.

definitions.note: Formal; often used in official or legal contexts (e.g., royal or political).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La reina llegó al acto con su consorte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The queen arrived at the event with her spouse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía investiga una conspiración para robar información.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating a conspiracy to steal information.

definitions.native: it is stated, it is recorded
definitions.note: Common in formal contexts, often used in the phrase “consta que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Consta que la reunión empieza a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is stated that the meeting starts at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su apoyo fue constante durante todo el año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His support was constant throughout the whole year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bebé llora constantemente por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby cries constantly at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoche vimos varias constelaciones en el cielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night we saw several constellations in the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa constelación se ve mejor en invierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That constellation is easier to see in winter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia causó consternación en toda la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news caused dismay throughout the whole city.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone shocked and upset by bad news or an unexpected situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se quedó consternado al escuchar la noticia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was dismayed when he heard the news.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a country's basic laws; it can also mean a person's physical constitution.
