definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él cruzó la calle cuando el semáforo se puso en verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He crossed the street when the traffic light turned green.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cráneo protege el cerebro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The skull protects the brain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cráter del volcán estaba lleno de ceniza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The volcano’s crater was full of ash.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) or polite request.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Créame, no fue mi intención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Believe me, it wasn’t my intention.

definitions.note: Often used for payment by credit card or for borrowing money (a loan).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo suficiente dinero, así que lo pago a crédito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have enough money, so I'll pay for it on credit.

definitions.note: Command (tú): used to tell someone to believe you.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Créeme, no fue mi intención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Believe me, it wasn’t my intention.

definitions.note: Often used for raising children or animals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cría a sus hijos con mucho amor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She raises her children with a lot of love.

definitions.note: Often used for animals (and sometimes people) to mean their young; also used for something that is bred or raised.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cría del gato es muy pequeña.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat’s offspring is very small.

definitions.note: Plural form of "cría"; often used for animals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las crías de la gata duermen todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat’s babies sleep all day.

definitions.note: Plural form of "crimen".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los crímenes ocurrieron anoche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crimes happened last night.

definitions.note: Colloquial (especially in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese crío siempre hace muchas preguntas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That kid always asks a lot of questions.

definitions.note: the sport; also used for the insect in some contexts
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los domingos jugamos al críquet en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Sundays we play cricket in the park.

definitions.note: Often used for feedback or evaluation; can be positive or negative depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La crítica del profesor me ayudó a mejorar mi ensayo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher's criticism helped me improve my essay.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación es crítica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is critical.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El escritor recibió muchas críticas por su nuevo libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The writer received many criticisms for his new book.

definitions.note: Can mean “important” (a critical moment) or “inclined to criticize” (a critical person), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un momento crítico para el equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a critical moment for the team.

definitions.note: Often refers to a person who evaluates art, films, books, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El crítico escribió una reseña del libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The critic wrote a review of the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un cuaderno para tomar apuntes en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a notebook to take notes in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar cuadernos para la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy notebooks for school.

definitions.note: Commonly used in Latin America to refer to a block on a street.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La farmacia está a dos cuadras de aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pharmacy is two blocks from here.

definitions.note: Place where horses are kept.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El caballo duerme en la cuadra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The horse sleeps in the stable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese horario no me cuadra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That schedule doesn’t work for me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu historia no cuadra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your story doesn’t add up.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mesa es cuadrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is square.

definitions.note: In many Spanish-speaking places, this refers to city blocks as a unit of distance (how far you walk).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tienda está a dos cuadras de aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store is two blocks from here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese cuadro es muy bonito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That painting is very pretty.

definitions.note: Often used for a square shape (like on a page or screen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dibuja un cuadro en la hoja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Draw a square on the sheet of paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay cuadros en las paredes del museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are pictures on the walls of the museum.

definitions.note: Relative pronoun used without an accent («cual»). The accented form «cuál» is used in direct/indirect questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro cual me prestaste es muy interesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book which you lent me is very interesting.

definitions.note: Relative pronoun/determiner used without accent as “cual” (e.g., “el cual / la cual / los cuales / las cuales”). The accented form “cuál” is used in questions/exclamations, but this entry is for the unaccented “cual”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro cual me recomendaste ya está agotado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book which you recommended to me is already sold out.

definitions.note: Plural form of "cuál"; used in questions or indirect questions. Note: in standard Spanish it normally appears as "cuáles" with an accent in questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dime cuales prefieres, los rojos o los azules.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me which ones you prefer, the red ones or the blue ones.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus mejores cualidades son la paciencia y la honestidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their best qualities are patience and honesty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos a alguien cualificado para este puesto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need someone qualified for this position.

definitions.note: Used before a singular noun (e.g., "cualquier día").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes elegir cualquier libro de la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can choose any book from the table.

definitions.note: Refers to a person (not a specific one).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cualquiera puede aprender español con práctica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Anyone can learn Spanish with practice.

definitions.note: Refers to a thing or choice; often used in phrases like “cualquier cosa”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Elige cualquiera de estos libros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Choose any of these books.

definitions.note: Usually written with an accent as “cuán” in standard Spanish; often used in questions/exclamations before an adjective or adverb (somewhat literary/formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sabes cuan difícil fue tomar esa decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t know how difficult it was to make that decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te llamo cuando llegue a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll call you when I get home.

definitions.note: Unaccented form. Used as a relative/interrogative determiner in indirect questions/relative clauses; feminine singular agreeing with a feminine singular noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé cuanta agua queda en el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know how much water is left in the glass.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form (interrogative/exclamatory). Used with feminine plural nouns; in questions/exclamations it often carries an accent in formal writing: "cuántas".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿cuantas personas vienen a la fiesta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many people are coming to the party?

definitions.note: Used in questions or exclamations; feminine plural form, used with feminine nouns. Written with an accent as «cuántas» in questions/exclamations, but this entry uses the exact form «cuantas» as requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé cuantas personas vienen a la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know how many people are coming to the party.

definitions.note: Often written with an accent (cuánto) in direct or indirect questions/exclamations: ¿Cuánto cuesta? / No sé cuánto cuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Come cuanto quieras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Eat as much as you want.

definitions.note: Relative pronoun/adverb used in comparisons or with verbs like querer, poder, saber. It can also appear as *cuanto* (not interrogative/exclamatory).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te ayudaré cuanto pueda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll help you as much as I can.

definitions.note: Usually unaccented in relative uses (e.g., “as much as / whatever”). For the direct question “how much?”, Spanish normally uses the accented form “¿cuánto?”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te ayudaré cuanto pueda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll help you as much as I can.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a comparison, often in the pattern “tanto… cuanto…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te llamaré tantas veces cuanto sea necesario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you as many times as necessary.

definitions.note: Used in the expression “en cuanto” to mean “as soon as / once”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En cuanto llegues, llámame.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As soon as you arrive, call me.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (without accent); often appears in indirect questions or as a relative determiner meaning “as many as / however many,” and it can also be a misspelling of «cuántos».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé cuantos hermanos tienes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know how many brothers you have.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (without accent). Common in informal writing/texting or when accents are omitted; in standard Spanish it is «cuántos». Used in questions and exclamations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿cuantos libros tienes?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many books do you have?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo cuarenta años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am forty years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estuve en cuarentena durante una semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was in quarantine for a week.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella vive en la cuarta casa de la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lives in the fourth house on the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los soldados volvieron al cuartel después del entrenamiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldiers returned to the barracks after training.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es el cuarto día de clases.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is the fourth day of classes.

definitions.note: Often used to mean a bedroom in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi cuarto está al final del pasillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My room is at the end of the hallway.

definitions.note: Used in fractions or as an ordinal in some contexts (e.g., “un cuarto” = a quarter).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero un cuarto de pizza, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a quarter of a pizza, please.

definitions.note: Used as an ordinal (“fourth”) or a fraction (“one quarter”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me comí un cuarto de la pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate a quarter of the pizza.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa tiene tres cuartos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house has three rooms.

definitions.note: Often used for money as “a quarter” (a fourth of a dollar) or for a fourth part of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solo tengo dos cuartos en el bolsillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only have two quarters in my pocket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo cuatro hermanos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have four siblings.

definitions.note: Often used for a cleaning bucket or a small container; in some regions it can also mean "ice bucket" (for drinks).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llena la cubeta con agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fill the bucket with water, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon la cubierta en la olla, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the lid on the pot, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hace frío; trae una cubierta para la cama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold; bring a blanket for the bed.

definitions.note: In this meaning, it’s common in contexts like boats (deck) or buildings (roof).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Subimos a la cubierta del barco para ver el mar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went up to the ship’s deck to see the sea.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mesa está cubierta de polvo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is covered with dust.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las cubiertas de los libros están mojadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book covers are wet.

definitions.note: Common in some Spanish-speaking regions (especially in Latin America) to mean car tires.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que cambiar las cubiertas del coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to change the car tires.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las mesas están cubiertas con manteles blancos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tables are covered with white tablecloths.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está cubierto de nieve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is covered with snow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El suelo está cubierto de nieve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ground is covered with snow.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural to refer to knives, forks, and spoons.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más cubiertos para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more cutlery for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los platos están cubiertos con papel aluminio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plates are covered with aluminum foil.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cubo tiene seis caras iguales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cube has six equal faces.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llena el cubo con agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fill the bucket with water, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cubos de hielo están en el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ice cubes are in the glass.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “cubrir” (used after expressions of doubt, desire, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que el seguro cubra los gastos médicos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the insurance covers the medical expenses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La manta cubre la cama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The blanket covers the bed.

definitions.note: Present tense form used with ellos/ellas/ustedes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos cubren los muebles con sábanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They cover the furniture with sheets.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of “cubrir.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy cubriendo la mesa con un mantel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am covering the table with a tablecloth.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos cubrieron la mesa con un mantel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They covered the table with a tablecloth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a cubrir la mesa con un mantel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to cover the table with a tablecloth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana cubrirá el suelo con una manta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow it will cover the floor with a blanket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana cubrirán la piscina para el invierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will cover the pool for the winter.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "cubrir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La nieve cubrió las montañas durante la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The snow covered the mountains during the night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo cubro la mesa con un mantel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cover the table with a tablecloth.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mantel cubría toda la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tablecloth was covering the whole table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay una cucaracha en la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a cockroach in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay cucarachas en la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are cockroaches in the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una cuchara para la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a spoon for the soup.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the amount held by a spoon (often a tablespoon).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Añade una cucharada de azúcar al café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Add a tablespoonful of sugar to the coffee.

definitions.note: Often refers to the blade of a knife, razor, or tool.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten cuidado: la cuchilla está muy afilada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful: the blade is very sharp.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un cuchillo para cortar el pan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a knife to cut the bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más cuchillos para cortar las verduras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more knives to cut the vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abrigo cuelga detrás de la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coat hangs behind the door.

definitions.note: Present tense (they/you all hang).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las llaves cuelgan en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The keys hang on the wall.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (also used for formal commands: “cuelgue”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cuelgue el teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you hang up the phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duele el cuello.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neck hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En invierno, los cuellos de los abrigos me irritan la piel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, the collars of coats irritate my skin.

definitions.note: Usually a small to medium, fairly deep bowl.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse la sopa en un cuenco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the soup in a bowl.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cuenta las monedas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She counts the coins.

definitions.note: Used with a direct object like a story, joke, or secret (e.g., “cuenta una historia”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo cuenta historias interesantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather tells interesting stories.

definitions.note: Often used for bank accounts, user accounts, or a restaurant bill ("la cuenta").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me traes la cuenta, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring me the bill, please?

definitions.note: From the verb "contar"; it can mean "to count" (numbers) or "to tell" (a story).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos cuentan hasta diez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They count to ten.

definitions.native: they have (an amount), they add up to
definitions.note: Often used with "con" to mean "to have/possess" (e.g., "cuentan con").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuentan con tres habitaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have three bedrooms.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuántas personas cuentas en la foto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How many people do you count in the photo?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre cuentas historias muy graciosas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always tell very funny stories.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo cuentas en dos bancos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have accounts in two banks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito pagar las cuentas hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to pay the bills today.

definitions.note: Formal command form (usted): can mean “count” (numbers) or “tell” (a story/information), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuente hasta diez, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Count to ten, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuenten hasta diez antes de responder.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Count to ten before you answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuenten lo que pasó en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell what happened at the meeting.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "contar" (also used for informal command: "no cuentes...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me cuentes la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you tell me the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te cuento lo que pasó ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll tell you what happened yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuento hasta diez y vuelvo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I count to ten and I’ll be back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela me contó un cuento antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother told me a story before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Plural of "cuento".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustan los cuentos antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like stories before going to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una cuerda para atar la caja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a rope to tie the box.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos cuerdas para atar las cajas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need ropes to tie the boxes.

definitions.note: Often used with the verb "estar" to mean someone is thinking clearly (not crazy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la discusión, ya estoy más cuerdo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the argument, I'm more clear-headed now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El toro tiene un cuerno muy grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bull has a very big horn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El toro tiene cuernos grandes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bull has big horns.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los zapatos son de cuero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shoes are made of leather.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duele el cuerpo después de correr.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My body hurts after running.

definitions.note: Plural of "cuerpo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el museo hay cuerpos humanos en las esculturas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the museum there are human bodies in the sculptures.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un cuervo está en el árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A crow is in the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos cuervos sobrevolando el campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw ravens flying over the countryside.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present of "costar" (to cost).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este libro cuesta diez euros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book costs ten euros.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object (often "me/te/le/nos/les"): "me cuesta" = "it’s hard for me" / "I have a hard time."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me cuesta hablar en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard for me to speak in public.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa está en la cuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is on the hillside.

definitions.note: Used to talk about price. With indirect object pronouns: "Me cuestan..." = "They cost me..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos zapatos cuestan cincuenta dólares.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes cost fifty dollars.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "costar" (also used after "aunque", "a menos que", etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aunque cueste mucho, lo voy a comprar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even if it costs a lot, I'm going to buy it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que completar un cuestionario para la clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to fill out a questionnaire for class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que resolver estas cuestiones antes de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to solve these issues before tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa es una cuestión importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is an important issue.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay una cueva cerca de la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a cave near the beach.

definitions.note: Plural of "cueva".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Exploramos las cuevas cerca del pueblo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We explored the caves near the town.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "cuidar" (also used as the "usted" command: "Take care of...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cuida a su abuela todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She takes care of her grandmother every day.

definitions.native: was taking care of, used to take care of
definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando mi abuela estaba enferma, yo la cuidaba todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When my grandmother was sick, I took care of her every day.

definitions.note: Command form used with vosotros (you all) in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuidad a los niños esta tarde, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take care of the kids this afternoon, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Cuidado! Hay un coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Watch out! There’s a car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tu cuidado cuando estaba enfermo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your care when I was sick.

definitions.note: Often used as a warning (especially in "¡Cuidado!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Cuidado! El suelo está mojado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Careful! The floor is wet.

definitions.note: Past participle of "cuidar"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He cuidado a mi hermana toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have taken care of my sister all afternoon.

definitions.note: Often refers to someone who looks after a person (e.g., a child or an elderly person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cuidador ayuda a mi abuelo todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The caregiver helps my grandfather every day.

definitions.note: Plural of "cuidado"; often used in phrases like "tener cuidados" (to take care) or "con cuidados" (with care).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por tus cuidados durante mi enfermedad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thank you for your care during my illness.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es muy cuidadosa con los detalles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very careful with details.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lee las instrucciones cuidadosamente antes de empezar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Read the instructions carefully before you start.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who pays attention to details or avoids mistakes/accidents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sé cuidadoso cuando cruces la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful when you cross the street.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los conductores son muy cuidadosos en esta carretera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drivers are very careful on this road.

definitions.native: we take care of, we look after
definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/nosotras).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuidamos a los niños mientras sus padres trabajan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We take care of the children while their parents work.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "cuidar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos cuidan a sus abuelos los fines de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They take care of their grandparents on the weekends.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "cuidar"; used to talk about an ongoing action ("while taking care of...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy cuidando a mi hermano esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking care of my brother this afternoon.

definitions.native: to take care of, to look after
definitions.note: Often used with "de" (cuidar de + person/thing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que cuidar de mi hermano esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take care of my brother this afternoon.

definitions.native: took care of, would take care of
definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used after phrases like “quería que…” or “si…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que ella cuidara a los niños esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted her to take care of the kids this afternoon.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (tú); often used after “si” (if) or in past-tense subordinate clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si cuidaras a tu hermana, tus padres estarían más tranquilos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you took care of your sister, your parents would be calmer.

definitions.native: we will take care of, we will look after
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuidaremos a tu perro mientras estás de viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will take care of your dog while you are traveling.

definitions.note: This is the infinitive "cuidar" with the direct object pronoun "la" attached ("her").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que cuidarla esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take care of her tonight.

definitions.native: to take care of him, to look after him/it
definitions.note: "-lo" is a direct object pronoun meaning "him" or "it" (masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito cuidarlo esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to take care of him this afternoon.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “me” (“myself”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito cuidarme más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to take better care of myself.

definitions.native: to take care of us, to look after us
definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun “nos” (us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que cuidarnos más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to take better care of ourselves.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive; often refers to self-care or being careful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante cuidarse para mantenerse sano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to take care of oneself to stay healthy.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “te” attached (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero cuidarte cuando estés enfermo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to take care of you when you’re sick.

definitions.native: will take care of, will look after
definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal "you" (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cuidará a los niños esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will take care of the children tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuidaré a tu perro este fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will take care of your dog this weekend.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypothetical situations or polite offers).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo cuidaría a tu perro este fin de semana si lo necesitas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would take care of your dog this weekend if you need it.

definitions.note: Present tense: "you" (informal, singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuidas a tu hermano esta tarde?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you taking care of your brother this afternoon?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) or formal command (usted) of "cuidar."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cuide bien a su hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you take good care of your sister.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands with ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que cuiden a su abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's important that you take care of your grandmother.

definitions.native: you take care (of), you look after
definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú). Often used after expressions like "Espero que..." or "Quiero que...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cuides a tu hermana esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you take care of your sister tonight.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of “cuidar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo cuido a mi hermana después de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take care of my sister after school.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer cuidé a mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I took care of my sister.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it took care of; you (formal) took care of.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cuidó a su hermano pequeño toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took care of her little brother all afternoon.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it looked after; you (formal) looked after.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abuelo cuidó a los niños mientras yo trabajaba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grandpa looked after the kids while I was working.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “culo”. Informal; can be affectionate, teasing, or vulgar depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bebé tiene un culito muy gracioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby has a very funny little butt.

definitions.note: Vulgar/informal word.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Siéntate en el culo y deja de quejarte!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit on your butt and stop complaining!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No fue mi culpa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It wasn’t my fault.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento mucha culpa por lo que dije.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of guilt about what I said.

definitions.note: From the verb «culpar». It can also be used as an informal command (tú): «¡Culpa a...!» = “Blame ...!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él siempre culpa a los demás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always blames others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sintió mucha culpabilidad después de mentir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt a lot of guilt after lying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él se siente culpable por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels guilty about what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía ya encontró al culpable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police already found the culprit.

definitions.note: Past participle of "culpar"; often used in passive constructions with "ser".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue culpado por el accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was blamed for the accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debes culpar a otros por tus errores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn't blame others for your mistakes.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun “me” is attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes culparme por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't blame me for what happened.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Culparon al árbitro por la derrota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They blamed the referee for the loss.

definitions.note: Direct-object pronoun "te" is attached to the verb (common with infinitives).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero culparte por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to blame you for what happened.

definitions.note: Usually used with an object or with “a” to say who you blame.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No culpas a tu hermano por todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t blame your brother for everything.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "culpar"; often used after expressions like "Espero que..." or "No quiero que..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero que me culpes por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want you to blame me for what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te culpo por lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't blame you for what happened.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/it blamed; also used with usted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jefe culpó a Marta por el error.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss blamed Marta for the mistake.

definitions.note: Present tense form of «cultivar» (also used for the formal command «you grow/cultivate»).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela cultiva tomates en su jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandma grows tomatoes in her garden.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "cultivar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta granja cultivan tomates y pimientos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this farm they grow tomatoes and peppers.

definitions.note: Often used for growing plants/crops; also used figuratively for developing a quality or relationship (e.g., ‘cultivar la paciencia’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos van a cultivar tomates en su jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are going to grow tomatoes in their garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cultivo tomates en mi jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I grow tomatoes in my garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cultivos necesitan agua y sol para crecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Crops need water and sun to grow.

definitions.note: Often used for a religious service, especially in Protestant churches (e.g., el culto del domingo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos al culto el domingo por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to the worship service on Sunday morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cultura de este país es muy diversa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The culture of this country is very diverse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La diversidad cultural es muy importante en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cultural diversity is very important in this city.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchas diferencias culturales entre los dos países.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many cultural differences between the two countries.

definitions.note: Plural of “cultura”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta ciudad conviven muchas culturas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city, many cultures live together.

definitions.note: Often used for the top of a mountain; it can also mean the highest point of something in a more general sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos a la cumbre después de tres horas de caminata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached the summit after three hours of hiking.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “cumplir”. Often used after expressions of desire, necessity, or doubt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cumpla su promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he keeps his promise.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "cumplir"; often used after expressions like "espero que", "quiero que", "es importante que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que cumplas tu promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you keep your promise.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "cumplir"; it can mean either "he/she/it" or "you" (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumple todas sus promesas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He keeps all his promises.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es mi cumpleaños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is my birthday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumplen con todos los requisitos para el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They meet all the requirements for the job.

definitions.note: Often used with promises, duties, or goals (e.g., “promesa cumplida”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La promesa está cumplida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The promise has been kept.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por el cumplido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for the compliment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He cumplido mi promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have fulfilled my promise.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ing form) of "cumplir"; used to talk about an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy cumpliendo mi promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fulfilling my promise.

definitions.note: Preterite tense. Can mean “they” (ellas/ellos) or formal “you plural” (ustedes), depending on the region/context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumplieron la promesa que me hicieron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fulfilled the promise they made me.

definitions.note: Often used with obligations, promises, or requirements (e.g., cumplir una promesa, cumplir con la ley).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que cumplir mi promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to fulfill my promise.

definitions.native: to turn (an age), to have (a birthday)
definitions.note: Used to say someone reaches an age (e.g., cumplir 18 años).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana voy a cumplir 18 años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I’m going to turn 18.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense of “cumplir” (he/she/it will).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cumplirá su promesa mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will fulfill her promise tomorrow.

definitions.native: I will do, I will fulfill
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumpliré mi promesa mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will keep my promise tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular preterite (simple past) of "cumplir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella cumplió 18 años ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She turned 18 yesterday.

definitions.note: Often used for fulfilling a duty/promise or meeting a requirement or goal (e.g., “cumplo 18 años” = “I turn 18”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy cumplo con mi trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I do my job (I fulfill my work duties).

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cumplí mi promesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I kept my promise.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bebé duerme en la cuna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby sleeps in the crib.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche se salió de la carretera y cayó en la cuneta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car went off the road and fell into the ditch.

definitions.note: Plural of "cuota"; often used for regular payments (e.g., a monthly fee or an installment payment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pago las cuotas del préstamo cada mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pay the loan installments every month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo varios cupones de descuento para el supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have several discount coupons for the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No existe una cura para ese virus todavía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There isn't a cure for that virus yet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico cura la herida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor heals the wound.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de una semana, la herida ya está curada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After a week, the wound is already healed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del tratamiento, ya estoy curado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the treatment, I’m already cured.

definitions.note: Often used for foods like cheese, ham, or sausage that have been cured/aged.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré queso curado para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought aged cheese for dinner.

definitions.note: Past participle of “curar”; often used with “estar” to describe a healed wound or cured illness. Must agree in gender/number in normal usage, but this example keeps the exact form “curado”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El paciente ya está curado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient is already cured.

definitions.note: Often used for curing illnesses or healing wounds; also used for healing emotionally or in the sense of recovering.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico dice que esta medicina puede curar la infección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor says that this medicine can cure the infection.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) future tense of “curar” (to heal/cure).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico curará la herida con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor will heal the wound carefully.

definitions.note: Common in Spain to mean “(parish) priests.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el pueblo, los curas conocen a todo el mundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the town, the priests know everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hay curas milagrosas para esa enfermedad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are no miracle cures for that illness.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es muy curiosa y siempre hace preguntas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very curious and always asks questions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo curiosidad por saber qué pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m curious to know what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy curioso por saber qué pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm curious to know what happened.

definitions.note: Can be used negatively to describe someone who asks too many questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas tan curioso; es un asunto privado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be so nosy; it's a private matter.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están curiosos por saber qué hay en la caja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are curious to know what’s in the box.

definitions.note: In Spanish it’s commonly used for the spice blend or a curry dish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a preparar pollo al curry para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to make curry chicken for dinner.

definitions.note: Often written as “currículum vitae” or abbreviated “CV” in Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a actualizar mi currículum antes de la entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to update my résumé before the interview.

definitions.note: Used for things (or people) that seem affected or in bad taste, often overly sentimental.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa decoración es muy cursi.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That decoration is very tacky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tomando un curso de español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking a Spanish course.

definitions.note: Plural of "curso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este semestre estoy tomando tres cursos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This semester I’m taking three courses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carretera tiene una curva peligrosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road has a dangerous curve.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carretera tiene muchas curvas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road has many curves.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it cured/healed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico curó la herida rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor healed the wound quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy cenamos cuscús con verduras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re having couscous with vegetables for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used for a protective case for an object (like a phone, instrument, or glasses).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una custodia para mi teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a case for my phone.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “cuyo”; used to express possession (“whose”) and agrees with the thing possessed (not the owner).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conocí a una chica cuya hermana vive en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met a girl whose sister lives in Madrid.

definitions.note: Means “whose” in relative clauses and agrees with the noun it refers to (cuyo, cuya, cuyos, cuyas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Conocí al chico cuyo padre es médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I met the boy whose father is a doctor.

definitions.note: Used in questions (direct or indirect). It agrees in number: cuál (singular), cuáles (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuál prefieres?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which one do you prefer?

definitions.note: Plural form of "cuál"; used in questions and indirect questions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuáles son tus libros favoritos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which are your favorite books?

definitions.note: Formal or literary; often used before an adjective or adverb (e.g., “cuán importante”, “cuán rápido”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sabes cuán importante eres para mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t know how important you are to me.

definitions.note: Used in direct or indirect questions and exclamations; it has an accent mark (cuándo).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How much does this book cost?

definitions.native: tell him, tell her, tell them

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi cuñado vive en Madrid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito hacer algunos cálculos antes de comprar el coche.

definitions.note: feminine form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The night is warm.

definitions.note: Often used for weather, temperature, or a friendly/affectionate atmosphere.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The days here are warm in summer.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) meaning “be quiet.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please be quiet for a moment.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down, everything is going to turn out fine.

definitions.note: Used to address multiple people (ustedes) and includes the reflexive "se".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Cálmense, por favor!

definitions.note: Formal command (usted); reflexive with “se.”

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay cámaras de seguridad en la entrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are security cameras at the entrance.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with a reflexive pronoun; used to tell someone to change their clothes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold; change your clothes before going out.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather had cancer, but now he is better.

definitions.native: sing to us, sing us (a song)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sing us a song, please.

definitions.note: Plural form of "cántaro".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They filled the pitchers with water from the well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomo una cápsula cada mañana.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo metieron en la cárcel por robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put him in prison for robbery.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cásate conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marry me.

definitions.note: Often refers to the outer covering of a fruit/vegetable (peel) or an egg/nut (shell).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tira la cáscara del plátano a la basura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throw the banana peel in the trash.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or written contexts; in everyday speech, "famoso/a" is very common too.

definitions.note: Plural of “célula”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El microscopio muestra las células con claridad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The microscope shows the cells clearly.

definitions.note: Often used for the “cent” part of the euro (céntimo de euro).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only need ten cents.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The grass in the park is very green.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos un cóctel antes de la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a cocktail before dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need the code to open the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito los códigos para entrar al edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need the codes to enter the building.

definitions.native: pick it up, grab it, take it
definitions.note: Informal (tú) command with the object pronoun “lo” (“it”). In some countries (especially parts of Latin America), “coger” can be vulgar; “tomar” is often used instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cógelo del suelo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pick it up from the floor, please.

definitions.note: Also means “cholera” (a disease), but that meaning is less common in everyday conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sintió una cólera enorme cuando vio la mentira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt enormous anger when he saw the lie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustan los cómics de superhéroes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like superhero comics.

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations. It has an accent to distinguish it from "como" (without accent).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you?

definitions.note: used in questions and exclamations

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you today?

definitions.note: Common in casual speech (especially in Latin America) to agree, encourage someone, or tell them to continue.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the book to María, please.

definitions.note: Very common informal expression used to encourage someone or tell them to start/continue.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Estás listo? ¡Dale!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you ready? Go ahead!

definitions.note: Command form (tú) used with an indirect object pronoun (les = “to them”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give them the keys now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buenas tardes, damas y caballeros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te damos las gracias por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Can mean “they give” (ellos/ellas/ustedes) or “you all give” (vosotros, Spain).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They always give good advice.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m giving a class now.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give us a minute, please.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dance is an important part of culture.

definitions.note: Used with the pronoun “os” (you all); common in Spain (vosotros form).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give each other a hug.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a dar mi palabra.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana daremos una respuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will give an answer.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., "te", "les") to say who receives it.

definitions.native: to give (to him, to her, to you [formal], to it)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to give them a gift tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive of “dar” with the attached indirect object pronoun “me” (“to me”).

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “nos” (= to us).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb meaning to give oneself something (often a break, time, permission, etc.).

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun + indirect object pronoun attached to the infinitive: dar + te.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero darte un regalo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give you a gift.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it will give); also used for formal "you" (usted) in the future tense.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will give me the book tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “dar”; used to talk about what someone would give in a hypothetical situation.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they had more money, they would give more to charity.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present indicative form of "dar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me das tu número, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You give me your number, please.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) of "dar". Often used with a pronoun: "date" = "give yourself" (e.g., allow yourself, treat yourself).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give yourself a break.

definitions.note: Plural of "dato".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need more data to make a decision.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "dañar" (he/she/it damages).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The phone is damaged.
