definitions.native: to tell it to him, to tell it to her
definitions.note: Infinitive of “decir” with pronouns: “se” = to him/her/you (formal), and “lo” = it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que decírselo a María.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tell it to María.

definitions.native: to tell you it, to tell it to you
definitions.note: Includes the pronouns “te” (to you, informal singular) + “lo” (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que decírtelo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to tell it to you today.

definitions.note: Vos form (used in voseo, e.g., in Argentina and other regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué decís eso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you say that?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella dedica mucho tiempo a su familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dedicates a lot of time to her family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su dedicación al trabajo es admirable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His dedication to work is admirable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero dedicar este libro a mis padres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to dedicate this book to my parents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito dedicar más tiempo a estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to devote more time to studying.

definitions.note: Reflexive form: "me" = "myself".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a dedicarme a estudiar este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to dedicate myself to studying this year.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿A qué le dedicas más tiempo: al trabajo o a la familia?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you devote more time to: work or family?

definitions.note: Often refers to the short text written at the beginning of a book or on a gift (e.g., “To Ana, with love”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro tiene una dedicatoria para mi abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book has a dedication for my grandmother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te dedico esta canción.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dedicate this song to you.

definitions.note: Often used with "a" to mean devoting time/effort to something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dedico mucho tiempo a estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I devote a lot of time to studying.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “he/she/you (formal) dedicated.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella le dedicó la canción a su madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She dedicated the song to her mother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me corté el dedo con un cuchillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cut my finger with a knife.

definitions.note: Plural of "dedo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duelen los dedos después de escribir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My fingers hurt after writing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este producto tiene un defecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product has a defect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El producto tiene varios defectos, pero funciona bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The product has several defects, but it works well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El producto llegó defectuoso y lo devolvimos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The product arrived defective, and we returned it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debemos defender nuestros derechos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We must defend our rights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que defenderme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to defend myself.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que defenderse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to defend myself.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está defendiendo a su hermana en la discusión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is defending his sister in the argument.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella defendió a su hermano en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She defended her brother at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La defensa del equipo fue excelente hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team's defense was excellent today.

definitions.note: Often used in sports; also used in the phrase “a la defensiva” (“on the defensive”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuestro equipo tiene una defensiva muy fuerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team has a very strong defense.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los defensores del parque organizaron una reunión para proteger los árboles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The park’s defenders organized a meeting to protect the trees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella defiende a su hermano en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She defends her brother at school.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué defiendes esa idea?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you defend that idea?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo defiendo a mi hermana en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I defend my sister at school.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más definiciones para estas palabras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more definitions for these words.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una definición clara de esta palabra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a clear definition of this word.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante definir tus objetivos antes de empezar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to define your goals before starting.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta es la versión definitiva del informe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the final version of the report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Definitivamente quiero ir al cine contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I definitely want to go to the movies with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta es la versión definitivo del informe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the definitive/final version of the report.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El árbol tiene un tronco deforme por el viento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tree has a misshapen trunk because of the wind.

definitions.note: present tense form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi madre me deja usar su computadora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother lets me use her computer.

definitions.note: informal singular command
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja tu chaqueta en la silla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave your jacket on the chair.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, dejaba mi bicicleta en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to leave my bike in the yard.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (used for ongoing, repeated, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando salíamos de casa, siempre dejaban la puerta abierta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we left the house, they always left the door open.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros (you all, informal) commands in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejad las mochilas aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the backpacks here, please.

definitions.note: Plural informal command (vosotros) + direct object pronoun “la” (her/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejadla en paz, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave her alone, please.

definitions.note: Affirmative vosotros command + indirect object pronoun "le" (to him). In many regions, "vosotros" is mainly used in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejadle hablar en paz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let him speak in peace.

definitions.note: Plural (vosotros) affirmative command + direct object pronoun “lo”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejadlo en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Plural informal command (vosotros) + object pronoun “me” (“to/for me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejadme en paz, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave me alone, please.

definitions.note: Past participle of “dejar”; often used with “haber” (e.g., “he dejado…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He dejado las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often written with an accent: “déjalo”. Used to tell someone to stop holding/doing something or to leave something as it is.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, dejalo en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please leave it on the table.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command. It’s usually written with an accent: “déjame”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejame en paz, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave me alone, please.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/nosotras).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejamos las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We leave the keys on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos dejan las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "dejar"; often used with "estar" to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy dejando las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m leaving the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often used with a place or object; also used to mean 'to let/allow' in other contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a dejar las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often followed by an infinitive (dejar + infinitive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis padres no me van a dejar salir por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents aren’t going to let me go out at night.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted form) of “dejar”; also used as the usted command for “dejar” in reported/indirect commands.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que él dejara el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted him to leave his job.

definitions.note: This is a past subjunctive form of “dejar” (often used after expressions like “quería que…” or “era importante que…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que dejaran de hablar durante la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted them to stop talking during the movie.

definitions.native: (if you) left, (if you) were to leave
definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used after "si" to talk about hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si dejaras el trabajo, tendrías más tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you left your job, you would have more time.

definitions.native: we will leave, we will let, we will allow
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejaremos las maletas en el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will leave the suitcases in the car.

definitions.note: The "-la" at the end means "her" (direct object pronoun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que dejarla en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to leave her at home.

definitions.native: to leave them, to let them
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “las” = “them” (feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a dejarlas aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to leave them here.

definitions.note: "-le" is an indirect object pronoun meaning "to him," "to her," or "to you" (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a dejarle un mensaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to leave him/her (formal you) a message.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it” or sometimes “him”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo dejarlo aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't leave it here.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “los” (“them,” usually masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a dejarlos aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to leave them here.

definitions.native: to leave me, to let me
definitions.note: Object pronoun "me" = "me" is attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes dejarme en paz?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you leave me alone?

definitions.note: Object pronoun "nos" can mean "us" or "ourselves" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes dejarnos en paz, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you leave us alone, please?

definitions.native: they left, they let, they allowed
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejaron las llaves en la mesa y se fueron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They left the keys on the table and left.

definitions.native: to let oneself; to allow oneself
definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive of "dejar"; often used with another infinitive ("dejarse + infinitive") or in set phrases like "dejarse llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante dejarse ayudar cuando uno lo necesita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to let yourself be helped when you need it.

definitions.native: to allow oneself to be influenced/led ("dejarse llevar")
definitions.note: Common idiomatic use: "dejarse llevar" = to let oneself go/just go with the flow.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En vacaciones, me gusta dejarse llevar y no planear tanto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On vacation, I like to go with the flow and not plan so much.

definitions.native: to let oneself be seen/noticeable; to show (as in "dejarse ver")
definitions.note: Often used with perception verbs: "dejarse ver" = to make an appearance / to be seen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la tormenta, el sol empezó a dejarse ver.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the sun started to show itself.

definitions.native: to leave you, to let you
definitions.note: Direct object pronoun "te" = "you" (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero dejarte solo en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to leave you alone at home.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) future tense of “dejar” (to leave, to let).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana dejará las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) future tense of “dejar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana dejarán el coche en el garaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will leave the car in the garage.

definitions.native: you will leave, you will let
definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense of “dejar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me dejarás tu libro mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you lend me your book tomorrow?

definitions.native: I will leave, I will let
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te dejaré un mensaje después de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will leave you a message after the meeting.

definitions.native: would leave, would let, would allow
definitions.note: Conditional form of “dejar.” Often used for polite requests or hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo no lo dejaría entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wouldn’t let him in.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (they/you all formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuvieran tiempo, dejarían a los niños en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they had time, they would leave the kids at home.

definitions.native: you would leave, you would let
definitions.note: Conditional form ("would").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me dejarías tu bolígrafo un momento?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you let me have your pen for a moment?

definitions.note: Informal (tú) present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué dejas la puerta abierta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you leave the door open?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used in sentences like “if (someone) left/let …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me dejase en paz, estaría más tranquilo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he left me alone, I’d be calmer.

definitions.native: you left, you let, you allowed
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "dejar" for "tú".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejaste las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted) or in the present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No lo deje aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t leave it here, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive used as a “let’s …” (nosotros) command/suggestion.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejemos esto para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s leave this for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes) or formal command (ustedes) of "dejar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejen las maletas aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave the suitcases here, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of "dejar"; also used in negative commands (tú): "no dejes" = "don’t leave/let".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no dejes las llaves aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t leave the keys here.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of "dejar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejo las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I leave the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Informal command form used with "vos" (common in Argentina/Uruguay).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejá eso aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave that here, please.

definitions.native: I left, I stopped (doing), I let
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) preterite form of “dejar” (past action).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejé las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, used with "vosotros" (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no dejéis la puerta abierta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don't leave the door open.

definitions.native: let's leave it, let's stop it
definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros) affirmative command (imperative) with the object pronoun “lo” = “it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya es tarde; dejémoslo para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's already late; let's leave it for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “dejar” (he/she/you-formal left; it left).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejó las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She left the keys on the table.

definitions.note: contraction of de + el
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Salimos del cine a las diez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We left the movie theater at ten.

definitions.note: Often used as “delante de” + noun/pronoun (“in front of”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está delante de la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is in front of the house.

definitions.note: Often used for the front part/side of something (like a building, car, or clothing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La delantera de la casa tiene un jardín pequeño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The front of the house has a small garden.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective; also commonly used in sports to refer to a forward (female) or the forward line.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevo una mochila en la parte delantera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I carry a backpack on the front part.

definitions.note: Past participle of “delatar” (“to report/turn in,” often to authorities).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ladrón fue delatado por un vecino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was reported by a neighbor.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) reported someone; it often implies betraying someone’s trust.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lo delató a la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reported him to the police.

definitions.note: Commonly used as a formal command (usted). It’s often written with an accent: «déle».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dele el dinero a María.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the money to María.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La delegación llegó a la conferencia esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delegation arrived at the conference this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los delegados votaron a favor de la propuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delegates voted in favor of the proposal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos delfines cerca de la costa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw dolphins near the coast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos un delfín cerca de la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a dolphin near the beach.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es delgada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is thin.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las ramas delgadas se rompieron con el viento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thin branches broke in the wind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy delgado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very thin.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo hizo deliberadamente para llamar la atención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did it deliberately to get attention.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue un gesto deliberado para llamar la atención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a deliberate gesture to get attention.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación es delicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is delicate.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trató el tema con delicadeza para no herir a nadie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She handled the topic with delicacy so as not to hurt anyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten cuidado con ese vaso; es muy delicado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful with that glass; it’s very delicate.

definitions.note: Often used for people or topics that require tact or can be easily upset.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un tema delicado, así que hablemos con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a sensitive topic, so let’s talk calmly.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sopa está deliciosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is delicious.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las galletas son deliciosas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cookies are delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este pastel está delicioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is delicious.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos tacos están deliciosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These tacos are delicious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La delincuencia ha aumentado en este barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Crime has increased in this neighborhood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó al delincuente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the criminal.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó a los delincuentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the criminals.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El robo es un delito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Robbery is a crime.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía investiga varios delitos en el barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are investigating several crimes in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts; in legal contexts it can also mean a lawsuit/claim.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La demanda de electricidad aumenta en verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The demand for electricity increases in the summer.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts (to take someone to court).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa va a demandar al proveedor por incumplimiento de contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is going to sue the supplier for breach of contract.

definitions.note: Often used with people or organizations as the direct object.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa va a demandarlos por incumplimiento de contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is going to sue them for breach of contract.

definitions.native: to demand them, to require them
definitions.note: Can mean “to require” (for example, time, effort, or resources).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El proyecto va a demandarlos pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The project is going to require them soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Demandaron una explicación inmediata.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They demanded an immediate explanation.

definitions.note: Legal context: to file a lawsuit against someone.
