definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wished her brother good luck.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El desfile empezó a las cinco de la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The parade started at five in the afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una desgracia perder el vuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a misfortune to miss the flight.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a woman or a feminine noun; it can also be used as an insult depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pobre gata estaba sola y desgraciada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poor cat was alone and miserable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desgraciadamente, no puedo ir a la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Unfortunately, I can't go to the party.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult (“bastard/jerk”), but it can also mean “poor wretch” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Pobre desgraciado, lo perdió todo en el incendio!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Poor wretch, he lost everything in the fire!

definitions.note: Can be used as a strong insult in some contexts (like “bastard” or “jerk”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pobre hombre está desgraciado desde que perdió su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The poor man has been miserable since he lost his job.

definitions.note: Plural noun; often used to express pity or contempt, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayudaron a los desgraciados que se quedaron sin casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They helped the poor wretches who were left without a home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, la familia vivió muchas desgracias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the family went through many misfortunes.

definitions.note: Often used for undoing something that was done (like an action, a mistake, or a knot).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a deshacer el nudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to undo the knot.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like “deshacerse de” + noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito deshacerme de estas cajas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to get rid of these boxes.

definitions.note: Commonly used with "de" ("deshacerme de algo" = "get rid of something").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero deshacerme de esta ropa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get rid of these old clothes.

definitions.note: Commonly used with “de” + noun: “deshacernos de algo”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que deshacernos de esta ropa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get rid of these old clothes.

definitions.note: Commonly used with “de”: deshacerse de algo = to get rid of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero deshacerse de esta ropa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get rid of these old clothes.

definitions.note: Commonly used with "de" ("deshacerte de algo" = "get rid of something").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que deshacerte de esas cosas viejas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to get rid of those old things.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); used with reflexive pronoun “te.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deshazte de esa ropa vieja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get rid of those old clothes.

definitions.note: Past participle of "deshacer"; often used as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El nudo ya está deshecho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The knot is already undone.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), 1st person singular: “I undid.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deshice el nudo con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I undid the knot carefully.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of “deshacer” for “he/she/it” or “you” (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María deshizo el nudo con paciencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María undid the knot patiently.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La calle estaba desierta por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street was deserted at night.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it describes a place with no people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pueblo está desierto por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The town is deserted at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El desierto es muy caluroso durante el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The desert is very hot during the day.

definitions.note: Past participle/adjective of "designar"; must agree in gender/number (designado/a/os/as).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él fue designado para liderar el equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was appointed to lead the team.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to describe how someone feels.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy desilusionado con los resultados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m disillusioned with the results.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” + infinitive: “desistir de hacer algo” = “to stop/give up doing something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No voy a desistir de aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm not going to give up learning Spanish.

definitions.note: Gerund form with reflexive “se”; it often means moving smoothly along a surface (or unintentionally slipping).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño bajó la colina deslizándose sobre el césped.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy went down the hill sliding on the grass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vestido es deslumbrante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dress is dazzling.

definitions.native: to dismantle; to take apart; to tear down
definitions.note: Often used for taking apart structures, systems, or organizations (e.g., a machine, an operation, a network).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía va a desmantelar la red criminal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to dismantle the criminal network.

definitions.native: to dismantle it, to take it apart
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a desmantelarlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to dismantle it tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana desmaya cuando ve sangre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister faints when she sees blood.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective meaning someone is unconscious.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegué, él estaba desmayado en el suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, he was passed out on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pude sentirme mareado, pero no llegué a desmayar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt dizzy, but I didn’t end up fainting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me asusté tanto que desmayé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got so scared that I fainted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se desmayó en el autobús, pero ya está mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She fainted on the bus, but she’s better now.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está desnuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is naked.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las personas entraron desnudas al lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The people went into the lake naked.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bebé está desnudo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is naked.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños corren desnudos por la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids run naked on the beach.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) did it.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El enfermero desnudó al paciente para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurse undressed the patient for the exam.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hace calor; desnúdate y ponte algo más cómodo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hot; get undressed and put on something more comfortable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está desocupada y está buscando trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is unemployed and is looking for work.

definitions.note: Often used for a room, seat, or space that is not being used.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La silla está desocupada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chair is unoccupied.

definitions.note: Often used (especially in Latin America) to talk about not having a job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano está desocupado desde enero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother has been unemployed since January.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar desodorante en la farmacia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy deodorant at the pharmacy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay mucho desorden en tu habitación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a lot of mess in your room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi cuarto está desordenado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My room is messy.

definitions.note: Often used for someone who is lost or not sure where they are.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy desorientado y no sé dónde estoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m disoriented and I don’t know where I am.

definitions.note: Often refers to a private office, like a lawyer’s or doctor’s office, or an office/room in a home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abogado me espera en su despacho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lawyer is waiting for me in his office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habla despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak slowly, please.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "despacio"; often used to sound extra soft or careful (like "nice and slow").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habla despacito, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak slowly, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La despedida fue muy emotiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The farewell was very emotional.

definitions.note: Plural form of “despedida.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo muchas despedidas en el aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many goodbyes at the airport.

definitions.note: Often used about losing a job.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Juan está despedido desde la semana pasada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Juan has been fired since last week.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about losing a job (being fired).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He sido despedido de mi trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been fired from my job.

definitions.note: Past participle of "despedir" in the sense of saying goodbye.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya nos hemos despedido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have already said goodbye.

definitions.note: Can mean either saying goodbye (despedirse) or dismissing/firing someone (despedir), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos despedimos al final de la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We said goodbye at the end of the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despedimos a dos empleados la semana pasada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fired two employees last week.

definitions.note: Often used for ending someone's employment.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa decidió despedir a veinte empleados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company decided to fire twenty employees.

definitions.native: to say goodbye (to), to see off
definitions.note: Used when you part from someone or when you accompany someone as they leave.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fuimos a la estación para despedir a Marta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We went to the station to say goodbye to Marta.

definitions.native: to fire him, to dismiss him
definitions.note: Refers to ending his employment; “-lo” means “him.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a despedirlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to fire him tomorrow.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an object pronoun: “despedir + me” = “say goodbye (to others) / take my leave.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que despedirme, ya es tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to say goodbye; it’s already late.

definitions.native: say goodbye (to each other), say goodbye
definitions.note: Reflexive form with "nos" (we/us): to say goodbye to each other or to say goodbye (for us to leave).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes de irnos, tenemos que despedirnos de todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before we leave, we have to say goodbye to everyone.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; commonly used with “de” (e.g., “despedirse de alguien” = to say goodbye to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante despedirse antes de irse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to say goodbye before leaving.

definitions.note: This form includes the object pronoun “te” (you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero despedirte antes de irme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to say goodbye to you before I leave.

definitions.note: This form is 1st person singular, simple past (pretérito). It can mean saying goodbye (despedirse) or firing someone (despedir a alguien); context decides.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer me despedí de mis amigos en el aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I said goodbye to my friends at the airport.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: "despedí a + person".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despedí a un empleado por llegar tarde todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fired an employee for arriving late every day.

definitions.note: Used for planes/rockets and also for things like stickers or tape coming unstuck (in that case, often "despegarse").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El avión va a despegar en diez minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane is going to take off in ten minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El avión despegará a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane will take off at eight.

definitions.note: Often used for aircraft; also used more generally for the start of rapid growth or improvement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El despegue del avión fue puntual.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane's takeoff was on time.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form; used for planes/rockets, or for starting suddenly (e.g., a career).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El avión despegó a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane took off at eight.

definitions.note: Often used for clear weather/sky, or for a space that is not cluttered or blocked.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tarde está despejada y hace sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The afternoon is clear and it’s sunny.

definitions.note: Often used about the sky/weather; can also mean a person’s mind is clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy el cielo está despejado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today the sky is clear.

definitions.note: Used for removing objects to free up space (e.g., clearing a table, a room).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, despejar la mesa después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please clear the table after dinner.

definitions.note: Used when clouds/fog dissipate and the sky clears.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la tormenta, el cielo empezó a despejar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the sky began to clear up.

definitions.note: Used meaning to resolve or dispel uncertainty (often: despejar una duda).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito despejar una duda antes de firmar el contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to clear up a doubt before signing the contract.

definitions.note: Used as a command to more than one person (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, despejen la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please clear the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La despensa está llena de arroz y pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pantry is full of rice and pasta.

definitions.note: Often used for wasting time, money, food, or opportunities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero desperdiciar mi tiempo en eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to waste my time on that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un desperdicio de comida tirar tanto pan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a waste of food to throw away so much bread.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya he despertado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already woken up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse el despertador a las seis para levantarme temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I set the alarm clock for six to get up early.

definitions.native: we wake up, we wake (someone) up
definitions.note: Can mean either “we wake up” (reflexive: despertarse) or “we wake (someone) up” (non-reflexive: despertar), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos despertamos temprano para ir al aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We wake up early to go to the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy despertando y todavía tengo sueño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m waking up and I’m still sleepy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El despertar fue temprano hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wake-up was early today.

definitions.note: Often used as "despertarse" when the subject wakes up (reflexive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suelo despertar a las siete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually wake up at seven.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero despertar al bebé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to wake the baby up.

definitions.native: woke up, were to wake up
definitions.note: Often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., after "si" meaning "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me despertara temprano, tendría más tiempo para desayunar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I woke up early, I would have more time for breakfast.

definitions.native: to wake him up, to wake it up
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “lo” (“him” or “it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a despertarlo a las siete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to wake him up at seven.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “me” (= me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que despertarme a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to wake me up at six.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), they/you all (Spain) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se despertaron temprano para tomar el tren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They woke up early to catch the train.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive; used for waking up from sleep.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Suelo despertarse a las siete todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually wake up at seven every day.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “te” (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a despertarte a las siete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to wake you up at seven.

definitions.note: Can also be used reflexively with “te” (“yourself/you”), meaning “to wake up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito despertarte temprano para ir al aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need you to wake up early to go to the airport.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) future tense of “despertar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana se despertará temprano para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he will wake up early for the exam.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) for “tú” (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te despertaste muy temprano hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You woke up very early today.

definitions.note: First-person singular, simple past (pretérito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me desperté temprano para ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I woke up early to go to work.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) in the past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se despertó temprano para ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He woke up early to go to work.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La jefa fue despiadada con los empleados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss was ruthless with the employees.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "despedir"; used after expressions like "es posible que", "quiero que", etc. "Ustedes" is Latin America; "vosotros" is Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es posible que despidan a dos empleados esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s possible that they will fire two employees this week.

definitions.note: From the verb "despedir"; can also mean "says goodbye" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa despide a diez empleados este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company fires ten employees this month.

definitions.note: From the verb "despedir"; can also mean "fires" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella se despide de sus amigos en la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She says goodbye to her friends at the door.

definitions.native: they fired, they said goodbye to
definitions.note: Can mean “they fired (someone)” or “they said goodbye / sent off (someone),” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Juan lo despidieron ayer de la empresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fired Juan from the company yesterday.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): “he/she/it said goodbye.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se despidió de sus amigos antes de irse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She said goodbye to his/her friends before leaving.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): “he/she/it fired (someone).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa despidió a dos empleados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company fired two employees.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo despido mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll fire him tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está despierta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is awake.

definitions.note: It can mean “(he/she/it) wakes up” (present) or an informal command “wake up!” (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María se despierta temprano todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María wakes up early every day.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está despierta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is awake.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú), present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿A qué hora te despiertas normalmente?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time do you usually wake up?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands with “usted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que usted se despierte temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you wake up early.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "despertar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que despiertes temprano mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you wake up early tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy despierto desde las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been awake since six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me despierto a las siete todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wake up at seven every day.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están despiertos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are awake.

definitions.note: Often describes someone who is a bit forgetful or not paying attention.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy muy despistado hoy; se me olvidaron las llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm very absent-minded today; I forgot my keys.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with the pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despiértame a las siete, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wake me up at seven, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (él/ella/usted): it describes something/someone collapsing or falling suddenly.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El techo se desplomó durante la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The roof collapsed during the storm.

definitions.note: Past participle of “despojar”; often used with “ser/estar” or in passive constructions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue despojado de sus pertenencias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was stripped of his belongings.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of “despreciar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él desprecia a sus compañeros de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He despises his classmates.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (could mean an ongoing past action or a habitual past action: “was …-ing” / “used to …”). Often confused with English “depreciate,” but it means “to despise.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era joven, despreciaba la comida picante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was young, I despised spicy food.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su actitud fue despreciable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His attitude was despicable.

definitions.native: we despise, we look down on
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No despreciamos a nadie por su origen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t look down on anyone because of their background.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muchas personas desprecian a los demás sin conocerlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many people despise others without knowing them.

definitions.native: to despise, to look down on
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debes despreciar a las personas por su acento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn't look down on people because of their accent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo desprecio las mentiras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I despise lies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sintió desprecio por la mentira.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt contempt for the lie.

definitions.note: Often written with an accent as “después” in standard Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos vemos despues de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you after class.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" + noun/infinitive: "después de" = "after".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Primero cenamos y después fuimos a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First we had dinner and afterward we went home.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; reflexive: “say goodbye (to someone).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Despídete de tus amigos antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Say goodbye to your friends before you leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese color destaca mucho en la pared blanca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That color stands out a lot on the white wall.

definitions.note: Past participle of "desterrar"; often used with "ser/estar" (e.g., "fue desterrado" = "was exiled").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El escritor fue desterrado por el gobierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The writer was exiled by the government.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta sala está destinada a reuniones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This room is intended for meetings.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (e.g., “destinado a”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este dinero está destinado a la educación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This money is intended for education.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos fondos están destinados a la educación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These funds are intended for education.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuál es tu destino final?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your final destination?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cree que el destino le tenía preparada una sorpresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He believes fate had a surprise in store for him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un destornillador para apretar este tornillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a screwdriver to tighten this screw.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas destreza para tocar el piano bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need skill to play the piano well.

definitions.note: Often used both literally (physically ruined) and figuratively (very upset or exhausted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del terremoto, la ciudad quedó destrozada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the earthquake, the city was left destroyed.

definitions.note: Often used informally to mean “exhausted” or “heartbroken,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, el coche quedó destrozado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the car was wrecked.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective to describe something badly damaged or ruined; can also describe a person feeling emotionally devastated.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, el coche quedó destrozado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the car was wrecked.

definitions.note: Plural masculine adjective; often used figuratively to mean emotionally very upset or exhausted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la tormenta, los árboles quedaron destrozados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the storm, the trees were left destroyed.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "destrozar"; often used with "estar" to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están destrozando la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are destroying the house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro destrozó el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog destroyed the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La destrucción del puente causó muchos problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The destruction of the bridge caused many problems.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (agrees with a feminine noun, often used with ser/estar or as an adjective)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ciudad quedó destruida después del terremoto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city was left destroyed after the earthquake.

definitions.note: feminine plural past participle; often used with "ser" for the passive voice or with "estar" to describe a state
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las casas fueron destruidas por el huracán.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The houses were destroyed by the hurricane.

definitions.note: Used as an adjective; often after estar/ser.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El puente está destruido después de la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bridge is destroyed after the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El puente fue destruido por la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bridge was destroyed by the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El fuego puede destruir la casa en minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire can destroy the house in minutes.

definitions.note: Includes the attached direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que destruirlo antes de que sea demasiado tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to destroy it before it's too late.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué destruiste mi cuaderno?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you destroy my notebook?

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (and also as the formal command for usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no destruya el documento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t destroy the document.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El fuego destruye la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire destroys the house.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Destruyeron el puente durante la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They destroyed the bridge during the storm.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of “destruir” (to destroy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El incendio destruyó la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fire destroyed the house.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person singular: “I destroyed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sin querer, destruí el archivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By accident, I destroyed the file.

definitions.note: Past participle of "destruir" (often used as an adjective).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El edificio quedó destruído después del incendio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building was left destroyed after the fire.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luz se desvanece al amanecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light fades at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La música se desvaneció poco a poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music faded little by little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La falta de experiencia es una desventaja en este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lack of experience is a disadvantage in this job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía ha desviado el tráfico por la obra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have diverted traffic because of the construction work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche se desvió para evitar al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car swerved to avoid the dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardamos las cajas viejas en el desván.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We keep the old boxes in the attic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por las obras, tenemos que tomar un desvío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Because of the construction, we have to take a detour.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una explicación detallada del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a detailed explanation of the problem.

definitions.native: in detail, in a detailed way
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La doctora explicó el tratamiento detalladamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor explained the treatment in detail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El informe está muy detallado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report is very detailed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entiendo este detalle del contrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand this detail of the contract.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito más detalles sobre el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need more details about the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La detective encontró una pista importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The detective found an important clue.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los detectives investigan el caso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The detectives are investigating the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía hizo una detención en el centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police made an arrest downtown.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros) future of “detener.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos detendremos aquí para descansar un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will stop here to rest a little.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future (he/she/it will stop).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El policía detendrá el coche en la esquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer will stop the car at the corner.

definitions.note: Future tense (yo). Often means stopping someone/something (including yourself), or stopping in order to do something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me detendré en la tienda después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will stop at the store after work.

definitions.note: Often used for stopping a process, movement, or activity (more formal than “parar”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El policía va a detener el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer is going to stop the car.

definitions.note: Used when the police take someone into custody.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía decidió detener al sospechoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police decided to arrest the suspect.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“her” or “it,” feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que detenerla antes de que cruce la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to stop her before she crosses the street.

definitions.native: to stop him, her, it, you (formal)
definitions.note: “le” refers to an indirect object (often ‘him/her/you formal’, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a detenerle un momento para hacerle una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to stop you for a moment to ask you a question.

definitions.note: Often used with police/legal context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía va a detenerle por robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to arrest him for robbery.

definitions.native: to stop him, to stop it
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“him/it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que detenerlo antes de que cruce la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to stop him before he crosses the street.

definitions.native: to detain him, to arrest him
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“him”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía va a detenerlo esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to arrest him tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito detenerlos antes de que crucen la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to stop them before they cross the street.

definitions.native: to detain them, to arrest them
definitions.note: Often used with police or legal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía va a detenerlos esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to arrest them tonight.

definitions.note: Object pronoun “me” can mean “me” or “myself,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes detenerme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't stop me.

definitions.note: Object pronoun “nos” = “us” attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía quiere detenernos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police want to detain us.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; used when a person/thing stops (intransitive: ‘to stop oneself’).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche va a detenerse en el semáforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is going to stop at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Object pronoun attached: te = "you" (informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que detenerte antes de que digas algo de lo que te arrepientas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to stop you before you say something you’ll regret.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) and formal command (usted) of "detener".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señor, detenga el coche aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, stop the car here, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive used with "nosotros" (often to make a suggestion/command: “let’s …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Detengamos el coche aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s stop the car here.

definitions.note: Command form used with ustedes (formal or plural “you”); also used in negative commands with ustedes (e.g., “no detengan”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Detengan el coche, por favor!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop the car, please!

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of «detener», often used after expressions like «quiero que», «es mejor que», or «no» (negative command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te detengas aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t stop here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leí el contrato detenidamente antes de firmarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read the contract carefully before signing it.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person who has been detained by the police.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sospechoso está detenido en la comisaría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suspect is detained at the police station.

definitions.note: Can describe something that is not moving or has been brought to a halt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está detenido en el semáforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is stopped at the traffic light.

definitions.note: Often used with estar to describe something that is not moving or has come to a halt.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren está detenido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is stopped.

definitions.note: Commonly used for someone being held by the police (e.g., “fue detenido”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sospechoso fue detenido por la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The suspect was detained by the police.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) affirmative command; it’s used to tell one person to stop.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Detente ahora mismo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop right now!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jurado determina el veredicto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jury determines the verdict.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su determinación le ayudó a terminar el proyecto a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His determination helped him finish the project on time.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es una persona determinada y no se rinde fácilmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is a determined person and doesn’t give up easily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy determinado a aprender español este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m determined to learn Spanish this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El resultado ya está determinado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The result is already determined.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “a certain/specific” person or thing (sometimes not named).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco un libro determinado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for a certain/specific book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez va a determinar la sentencia mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge is going to determine the sentence tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él detesta levantarse temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He hates getting up early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Detesto levantarme temprano los lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hate getting up early on Mondays.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía detiene al sospechoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police detain the suspect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La detonación se oyó a varios kilómetros de distancia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The detonation was heard several kilometers away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía encontró un detonador cerca del explosivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found a detonator near the explosive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía encontró detonadores en el almacén.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found detonators in the warehouse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato está detrás del sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is behind the couch.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me detuve en la esquina para mirar el mapa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stopped at the corner to look at the map.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), third-person plural (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía los detuvieron en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested them on the street.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "detener" for "we".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Detuvimos el coche en la esquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stopped the car at the corner.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular of “detener”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía lo detuvo en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police stopped him on the street.

definitions.note: Used as a command to one person (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Detén el coche aquí, por favor!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop the car here, please!

definitions.note: Often used in police/security contexts; command to one person (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Detén a ese hombre ahora!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Detain that man now!

definitions.note: formal command (usted)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señor, deténgase un momento, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, stop for a moment, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una deuda con el banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a debt with the bank.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchas deudas y necesito ahorrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many debts and I need to save money.

definitions.note: Often used to describe how someone feels emotionally after something bad happens.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy devastado por la noticia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m devastated by the news.

definitions.note: Often used for strong religious faith or dedication to a person, cause, or activity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella siente mucha devoción por su familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She feels a lot of devotion toward her family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te voy a devolver el libro mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to return the book to you tomorrow.

definitions.native: to return (something) to him, to return (something) to her
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun "le" (to him/her/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a devolverle el libro a Ana mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to return the book to Ana tomorrow.

definitions.note: "lo" = "it" (masculine singular direct object pronoun); attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a devolverlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to return it tomorrow.

definitions.native: to return you (something), to give you back (something)
definitions.note: This form includes the indirect object pronoun “te” (“to you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a devolverte el libro mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to return the book to you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Future tense (él/ella/usted). Often used for returning an item or giving something back to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana te devolverá el libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will give you back the book.

definitions.native: I will return (it), I will give back
definitions.note: Simple future, first person singular (yo). Often used with a direct object (e.g., devolveré el libro).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te devolveré el dinero mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will give you the money back tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted form) of "devolver"; often used after "si" (if) or in reported requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me devolviera el libro hoy, podría terminar la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you returned the book to me today, I could finish the homework.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me devolvió el libro ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He returned the book to me yesterday.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer devolví el libro a la biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I returned the book to the library.

definitions.note: Often used both literally (food) and figuratively (e.g., emotions or time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pastel ya está devorado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cake is already eaten up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He devuelto el libro a la biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have returned the book to the library.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) or formal command (usted) of "devolver".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, devuelva el libro a la biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please return the book to the library.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command) form used with ustedes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que me devuelvan el libro mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to return the book to me tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “devolver”; used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es posible que…”, or in negative commands with “tú” (e.g., “no devuelvas…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que me devuelvas el libro mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to return the book to me tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cliente devuelve el producto porque está roto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The customer returns the product because it’s broken.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) present tense of “devolver”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te devuelvo el libro mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll return the book to you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). The “-le” means “to him/her/you (formal).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devuélvele el libro a Marta, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the book back to Marta, please.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with the pronoun “lo” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no es tuyo, devuélvelo ahora mismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it isn't yours, return it right now.

definitions.native: give me back, return to me
definitions.note: Command form meaning “return it to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Devuélveme el libro, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me back the book, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer di un regalo a mi amiga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I gave a gift to my friend.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "dar" (to give), not from "decir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer di un regalo a mi mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I gave my mom a gift.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela tiene diabetes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother has diabetes.

definitions.note: Often used in insults or strong expressions (e.g., "¡Diablos!").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dicen que el diablo vive en el infierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They say the devil lives in hell.
