definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero dártelo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to give it to you tomorrow.

definitions.native: give it to him, give it to her, give it to you (formal)
definitions.note: Command (tú) with attached pronouns: se + lo. "Se" can mean "to him," "to her," or "to you" (formal) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dáselo a Marta, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give it to Marta, please.

definitions.note: Used for the present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) and also as the formal command (usted) of “dar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me dé una respuesta hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you give me an answer today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la enfermedad, se siente débil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the illness, he feels weak.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del viaje, están débiles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the trip, they are weak.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viví en Madrid durante una década.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lived in Madrid for a decade.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He vivido aquí durante décadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have lived here for decades.

definitions.note: Often used as an ordinal number (e.g., “el décimo piso” = “the tenth floor”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivo en el décimo piso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live on the tenth floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El país tiene un déficit grande este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country has a large deficit this year.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with a direct object pronoun attached (la = “her/it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjala en paz, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave her alone, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with an indirect object pronoun; can refer to “him” or “her” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjale hablar un momento, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let him/her speak for a moment, please.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with an attached object pronoun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjalo en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Command (tú) form with the pronoun “los” (“them”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjalos aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave them here, please.

definitions.note: Used to ask someone to allow you to do something or to stop interfering; informal "me" object pronoun attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjame hablar, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me speak, please.

definitions.note: Command (tú): “Leave it to me.” Often used when offering to take care of something for someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te preocupes, déjamelo a mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry, leave it to me.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) meaning “leave us…” or “let us…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, déjanos en paz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, leave us alone.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). Often used in expressions like “déjate de…” = “stop … / cut it out.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjate ayudar, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let yourself be helped, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) meaning “leave it/let it,” referring to “it” (lo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjelo en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) of “dejar” used with the object pronoun “me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjeme ayudarle con las bolsas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let me help you with the bags.

definitions.note: Command (ustedes) + attached direct object pronoun. Depending on context, -la can mean “it” (feminine noun) or “her.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjenla en paz, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave her alone, please.

definitions.note: Command (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjenlo aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave it here, please.

definitions.note: Command form used with ustedes (you all / formal you). Often used to mean “leave me alone.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjenme en paz, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave me alone, please.

definitions.note: Formal/plural command (ustedes) with the object pronoun “nos” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déjennos entrar, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let us in, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted/ustedes) with an attached indirect object pronoun: “nos” = “us.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, déjenos entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please let us come in.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) of “dar” with the pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Déme su pasaporte, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me your passport, please.

definitions.note: Command form used with "nos" (like "démonos un descanso" = "let's give ourselves a break").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Démonos un descanso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's give ourselves a break.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of "dar" for "yo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer le dí el libro a mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I gave the book to my sister.

definitions.note: From the verb “dar” (not “decir”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dí el libro a Ana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave Ana the book.

definitions.note: This noun is masculine despite ending in -a.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es un día bonito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is a beautiful day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trabajo cinco días a la semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work five days a week.

definitions.native: tell him, tell her, tell you (formal)
definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with an indirect object pronoun (-le).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, dígale que llego tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell him/her that I’m arriving late.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with an indirect object pronoun (-les).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, dígales que la reunión empieza a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell them that the meeting starts at nine.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with the object pronoun "lo" (= it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si sabe la verdad, dígalo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you know the truth, say it now.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted); also used to get someone's attention (“Excuse me?” / “Yes?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dígame la verdad, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me the truth, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted): “Tell me it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, dígamelo otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell me again.

definitions.note: Affirmative command (ustedes) with an indirect object pronoun (le).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, díganle la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell him/her/them the truth.

definitions.note: Formal command to more than one person (ustedes); also used with ustedes in many Latin American countries.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, díganme la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, tell me the truth.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) of "decir"; also used as the polite "you" form with "nos" (us).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, díganos la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell us the truth.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted); includes both direct and indirect object pronouns ("se" + "lo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, dígaselo al jefe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please tell it to the boss.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command meaning “tell it to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dímelo ahora, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me now, please.

definitions.note: Command form meaning “tell it to us.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dínoslo ahora, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell it to us now, please.

definitions.native: tell it to him, tell it to her, tell it to them
definitions.note: Command (tú): «di» + indirect object «se» (to him/her/them) + direct object «lo» (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Díselo ahora mismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell it to him/her/them right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro es muy dócil y aprende rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is very docile and learns quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este libro cuesta diez dólares.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book costs ten dollars.

definitions.note: Plural form of “dólar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo veinte dólares en efectivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have twenty dollars in cash.

definitions.note: used in questions and exclamations; written with an accent mark
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Dónde está el baño?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where is the bathroom?

definitions.note: Used instead of "y" before words that start with the "i" sound (e.g., i-, hi-).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero té e infusiones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want tea and herbal infusions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La palabra «elefante» empieza con e.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The word "elephant" starts with E.

definitions.note: Somewhat formal; common synonym: “borracho”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estaba ebrio y no podía caminar bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was drunk and couldn’t walk well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El agua llegó a ebullición en pocos minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The water reached boiling in a few minutes.

definitions.note: Often used with "la basura" to mean "throws away" (e.g., "echa la basura"). It can also be the informal (tú) command form: "¡Echa!" = "Throw!"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella echa la basura todas las noches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She throws out the trash every night.

definitions.native: was throwing, was putting, was pouring
definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "echar" (used for ongoing or repeated past actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, echaba la pelota muy lejos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I used to throw the ball very far.

definitions.native: was kicking out, was firing, was sending away
definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "echar" (often used with people: "echar a alguien" = to kick someone out).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El dueño del bar echaba a los clientes que gritaban.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bar owner used to kick out the customers who shouted.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to describe a person or animal in a lying-down position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La perra está echada en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is lying down on the sofa.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person or animal resting in a horizontal position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro está echado en la alfombra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is lying down on the carpet.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" to describe someone/something in a lying-down position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro está echado en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is lying down on the sofa.

definitions.note: Also commonly used in set phrases like “echar de menos” (to miss) or “echar una mano” (to help).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echamos la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We throw the ball to the dog.

definitions.native: they throw, they pour, they put
definitions.note: From the verb "echar"; often used with liquids ("pour") or to mean "put/throw" something somewhere depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos echan la leche en el café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They pour the milk into the coffee.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of "echar"; often used with "estar" to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy echando agua en el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m pouring water into the glass.

definitions.note: Very common verb with many meanings depending on context (e.g., “echar de menos” = “to miss”), but the basic meaning is “to throw.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tires la basura al suelo; mejor, por favor, echa la basura en el cubo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t throw the trash on the ground; instead, please throw the trash in the bin.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (tú); often used after "si" (if) for hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si echaras la carta al buzón, llegaría mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you dropped the letter in the mailbox, it would arrive tomorrow.

definitions.native: we will throw, we will put, we will pour
definitions.note: Often used very broadly in Spanish (e.g., echar = to throw, to put/add, or to pour depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echaremos azúcar al café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will put sugar in the coffee.

definitions.native: to pour on (it), to put on (it)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (“to him/her/it/you formal”), often used with “a + noun” (e.g., echarle agua a la planta).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a echarle agua a la planta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to pour water on the plant.

definitions.native: to throw it away, to throw it out
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it” or sometimes “him”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a echarlo a la basura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to throw it in the trash.

definitions.native: to fire me, to kick me out
definitions.note: Infinitive of "echar" with the object pronoun "me" attached (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a echarme del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to fire me from my job.

definitions.note: Often used with “la basura” (the trash) or similar things you discard.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echaron la basura después de la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They threw away the trash after the party.

definitions.native: to throw you out, to kick you out
definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “te” = “you” (informal singular). Often used with “de” (e.g., “echarte de…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a echarte del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to fire you from your job.

definitions.native: will throw, will put, will pour
definitions.note: Simple future (él/ella/usted) of "echar"; exact meaning depends on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echará la sal en la sopa al final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will put the salt in the soup at the end.

definitions.note: Future tense (they/you all). Often used in everyday Spanish in phrases like “echar (algo) en” = to put (something) in.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echarán las llaves en la caja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will put the keys in the box.

definitions.native: I will throw, I will toss
definitions.note: Future tense (yo). Often used in expressions like "echar una mano" (to lend a hand) or "echar de menos" (to miss), but the core meaning is "to throw/toss".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echaré la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will throw the ball to the dog.

definitions.native: would throw, would put, would pour
definitions.note: Conditional form of "echar". Often used for placing/adding something (like adding salt) or pouring (like pouring water).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo le echaría más sal a la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would add more salt to the soup.

definitions.native: you throw, you put, you add
definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense of “echar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Echas sal a la sopa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you add salt to the soup?

definitions.native: you threw, you poured, you put (in), you kicked out
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): informal singular “you” (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué echaste la leche en el café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you pour the milk into the coffee?

definitions.note: Form of “echar” used with the present subjunctive (e.g., after “que”) or as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que eche la basura hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you throw out the trash today.

definitions.native: let’s throw, let’s put, let’s add
definitions.note: First-person plural present subjunctive of "echar"; often used as a suggestion with "que" ("Que echemos...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Que echemos sal al agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s add salt to the water.

definitions.note: Often used in expressions like “echar la basura” (to throw away/take out the trash).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que echen la basura hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they take out the trash today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “echar” (used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es posible que…”, “para que…”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que eches la carta al buzón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to put the letter in the mailbox.

definitions.note: From the verb "echar"; this form is also commonly used as "I add/put" in some contexts (e.g., echar sal = add salt).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echo la pelota a mi hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I throw the ball to my brother.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “de hecho” = “in fact / actually.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De hecho, no tengo tiempo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In fact, I don’t have time today.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular of “echar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eché la carta al buzón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw the letter into the mailbox.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it threw.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Echó la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She threw the ball to the dog.

definitions.note: Often used with things like salt, sugar, or ingredients.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le echó sal a la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She added salt to the soup.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana habrá un eclipse solar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there will be a solar eclipse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El eco de su voz llenó la cueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The echo of his voice filled the cave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La economía del país está mejorando este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country's economy is improving this year.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación económica del país es complicada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country's economic situation is complicated.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco una opción económica para viajar este fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for an affordable option to travel this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Económicamente, este año ha sido difícil para mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Economically, this year has been difficult for my family.

definitions.note: Can describe something low-priced or something that saves money/resources.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este hotel es muy económico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This hotel is very cheap.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; also used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos zapatos son muy económicos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are very affordable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ecuador divide la Tierra en dos hemisferios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The equator divides the Earth into two hemispheres.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuál es tu edad?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is your age?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las edades de mis hijos son 6 y 9.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My children's ages are 6 and 9.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta es la edición de 2024.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the 2024 edition.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about editing a text, video, or photos.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La edición del video tomó muchas horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The editing of the video took many hours.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese edificio es muy alto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That building is very tall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta calle hay muchos edificios altos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this street there are many tall buildings.

definitions.note: Often refers to a magazine/newspaper editor or a film/book editor (not just a text editor program).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El editor revisó el artículo antes de publicarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The editor reviewed the article before publishing it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La educación es importante para el futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Education is important for the future.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es muy educada con todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very polite with everyone.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of “educar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella fue educada en una escuela pública.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was educated in a public school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habló educadamente con la profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He spoke politely with the teacher.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él es muy educado con sus profesores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very polite with his teachers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy educado y le encanta aprender.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very educated and he loves learning.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone’s manners (how they behave), not their level of schooling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño es muy educado con los invitados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boy is very polite with the guests.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos eran muy educados y leían mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents were very educated and read a lot.

definitions.note: In everyday Spanish, this meaning is very common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños son educados y siempre dicen “por favor”.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are polite and always say “please.”

definitions.note: Often used for raising/bringing up children (teaching behavior and values) as well as formal education.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante educar a los niños con respeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to raise children with respect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este programa es muy educativo para los niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This program is very educational for children.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos una solución efectiva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need an effective solution.

definitions.note: Often used to confirm that something is true (like “yes, indeed”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Efectivamente, la tienda está cerrada hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Indeed, the store is closed today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este método es muy efectivo para aprender vocabulario.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This method is very effective for learning vocabulary.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the phrase “en efectivo” (in cash).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedo pagar en efectivo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can I pay in cash?

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “en efectivo” = “in cash.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo pagué en efectivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I paid for it in cash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese medicamento tiene un efecto rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That medicine has a fast effect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los efectos de esta medicina son rápidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The effects of this medicine are fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este tratamiento es eficaz para el dolor de cabeza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This treatment is effective for headaches.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La eficiencia del nuevo motor reduce el consumo de gasolina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The efficiency of the new engine reduces gasoline consumption.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este método es muy eficiente.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no descansas, tu dolor de cabeza empeorará.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you don’t rest, your headache will get worse.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación empeoró después de la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation got worse after the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El emperador vivía en un gran palacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The emperor lived in a big palace.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La emperatriz saludó al pueblo desde el balcón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The empress greeted the people from the balcony.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), describing an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegué, la clase empezaba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, the class was starting.

definitions.note: Affirmative command (vosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Empezad ahora, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Start now, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He empezado a leer este libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have started reading this book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Empezamos la clase a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We start class at eight.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "empezar"; often used with "estar" to mean "to be starting."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy empezando un nuevo trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m starting a new job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a empezar ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to start now.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form (imperfect subjunctive) of “empezar”, often used in “si…” (if…) sentences and after certain expressions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo empezara hoy, terminaría mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I started today, I would finish tomorrow.

definitions.native: we will start, we will begin
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana empezaremos el proyecto a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will start the project at nine.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) simple past (preterite) of "empezar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Empezaron la clase a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They started the class at eight.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (future tense) of "empezar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La clase empezará a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The class will start at eight.

definitions.native: I will start, I will begin
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana empezaré un nuevo trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will start a new job.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) simple past (pretérito) of “empezar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Empezaste a estudiar muy temprano hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You started studying very early today.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/you formal) in the past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La clase empezó a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The class started at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puso mucho empeño en su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He put a lot of effort into his work.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "empezar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que empiece la reunión pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the meeting starts soon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "empezar"; used after expressions like "quiero que" or to give commands to a group ("ustedes").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que empiecen la tarea ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to start the homework now.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "empezar"; used after expressions like "quiero que", "es importante que", etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que empieces ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to start now.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (also used with usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La clase empieza a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The class starts at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las clases empiezan a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Classes start at eight.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Empiezas a trabajar a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You start working at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy empiezo un nuevo trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I start a new job.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carretera está muy empinada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The road is very steep.

definitions.note: From the verb "emplear"; often used with "emplear" = "to use" (a method/tool) or "to employ" (a person).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella emplea una computadora para trabajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She uses a computer to work.

definitions.note: Feminine form; can also mean a female worker/employee (often in a shop or office).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empleada de la tienda me ayudó a encontrar mi talla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store employee helped me find my size.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El empleado llegó temprano al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employee arrived early to work.

definitions.note: Masculine plural; can also refer to a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los empleados llegan a las nueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The employees arrive at nine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy buscando empleo desde hace dos meses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been looking for a job for two months.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos empleos disponibles en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many jobs available in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana trabaja en una empresa de tecnología.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister works at a technology company.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tío es empresario y tiene dos restaurantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a businessman and he has two restaurants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las empresas necesitan buenos empleados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Companies need good employees.

definitions.note: Also used as a command ("Push!") with tú.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella empuja el carrito del bebé.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She pushes the baby's stroller.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a empujar la puerta, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to push the door, please.

definitions.native: to shove; to give a push (more forceful than a gentle push)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me empujes; si necesitas pasar, dímelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t shove me; if you need to get by, tell me.

definitions.native: to propel; to move (something) forward by pushing
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para mover el coche averiado, vamos a empujar entre todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To move the broken-down car, we’re going to push together.

definitions.note: Often used for physical pushing or for figurative “drive/momentum” (e.g., in sports or projects).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El equipo jugó con mucho empuje en la segunda parte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team played with a lot of drive in the second half.

definitions.note: Used with ustedes/ellos/ellas (present subjunctive) and also as an ustedes command (imperative).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Empujen la puerta, por favor!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Push the door, please!

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él empujó la puerta para abrirla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pushed the door to open it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me dio un empujón y casi me caigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me a shove and I almost fell.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivo en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in Madrid.

definitions.native: falls in love (with), makes (someone) fall in love
definitions.note: Present tense form of "enamorar"; often used with "de" (e.g., "se enamora de...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enamora de él muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She falls in love with him very quickly.

definitions.note: feminine form (used with a female subject)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enamorada de ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in love with you.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigas están enamoradas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are in love.

definitions.note: Often used with “estar” or “estar enamorado de” to say you’re in love (with someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enamorado de ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in love with you.

definitions.note: Often used with estar + de (e.g., “estar enamorado de alguien” = “to be in love with someone”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enamorado de ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in love with you.

definitions.note: Plural adjective; commonly used to describe a couple (e.g., “los enamorados”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos están enamorados desde hace dos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been in love for two years.

definitions.note: Present tense; can also mean “we make (someone) fall in love.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos enamoramos en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fell in love in college.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “me” (“myself/me”), used with infinitives, gerunds, and commands (e.g., “quiero enamorarme…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero enamorarme otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to fall in love again.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enamoraron en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They fell in love in college.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive; used as “enamorarse de” someone/something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es fácil enamorarse de ella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s easy to fall in love with her.

definitions.native: to make you fall in love
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “te” (= you). Often used with “de” (e.g., enamorarte de algo/alguien).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enamorarte de esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to make you fall in love with this city.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “enamorar”; also used for formal commands (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que te enamore la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you fall in love with the city.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enamoré de mi mejor amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fell in love with my best friend.

definitions.native: fell in love (with), made someone fall in love
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/it fell in love; or he/she made someone fall in love.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enamoró de ella en el verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He fell in love with her in the summer.

definitions.note: Can refer to a person of short stature or a dwarf in stories/fantasy; it can be offensive if used to describe a real person, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el cuento, el enano vive en una casa pequeña.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story, the dwarf lives in a small house.

definitions.note: Plural form of "enano".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el cuento, los enanos viven en el bosque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the story, the dwarfs live in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta pieza encaja perfectamente aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This piece fits perfectly here.

definitions.note: Present tense, 3rd person plural (they) of "encajar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las piezas del rompecabezas encajan perfectamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The puzzle pieces fit together perfectly.

definitions.note: Often used for something fitting physically (like a piece in a space) or fitting well with something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta pieza necesita encajar aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This piece needs to fit here.

definitions.note: Used when something matches someone’s needs, taste, or schedule.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese horario no me deja encajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That schedule doesn’t let me fit it in / doesn’t work for me.

definitions.note: Often used for boats/ships running aground, but it can also be used more generally for getting stuck.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El barco encalló cerca de la costa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boat ran aground near the coast.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (me/te/le) to mean “(something) is loved/liked by (someone)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encanta esta canción.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love this song.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often means “used to love/like” or describes an ongoing feeling in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De niño, me encantaba leer antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As a child, I loved reading before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Often used in the sense of “to love/like something a lot” (e.g., a place, an activity, a movie).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A los niños les encantaban los cuentos antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children loved bedtime stories.

definitions.note: Often used (by a woman) as a polite way to say “nice to meet you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —Hola, soy Laura. —Encantada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —Hi, I’m Laura. —Nice to meet you.

definitions.note: Commonly used after introductions: “Encantado” (male speaker) / “Encantada” (female speaker).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hola, soy Carlos. Encantado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hi, I’m Carlos. Pleased to meet you.

definitions.note: Often used in greetings: “Encantado de conocerte/conocerle” = “Nice to meet you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encantado de conocerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Nice to meet you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un pueblo encantador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's a charming town.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La guía es muy encantadora y nos ayuda mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide is very charming and helps us a lot.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; agrees with a masculine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los anfitriones fueron muy encantadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hosts were very charming.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like “encantado/a(s) de…” (e.g., when meeting someone or being happy about something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos encantados de conocerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re delighted to meet you.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les): “Me encantan…” = “I love…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encantan los helados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love ice cream.

definitions.native: to enchant; to delight; to love (something, in the sense of really liking it)
definitions.note: Commonly used in the construction "(A alguien) le encanta + [noun/infinitive]" (e.g., "Me encanta...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta canción suele encantar a todo el mundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This song usually delights everyone.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., "te encantará" = "you’ll love it").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te encantará este libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’ll love this book.

definitions.note: Conditional form; often used to express a polite desire (similar to “I’d love to…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encantaría ir al cine contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’d love to go to the movies with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su encanto es irresistible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her charm is irresistible.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les) to mean “(something) delighted (someone)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Marta le encantó la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Marta loved the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El periodista fue encarcelado por protestar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist was imprisoned for protesting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El periodista fue encarcelado por decir la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist was imprisoned for telling the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mamá encarga una pizza para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mom orders a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” (encargado de…) to say what someone is responsible for.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El encargado de la tienda llega a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The person in charge of the store arrives at eight.

definitions.note: Often used with “de”: “estar encargado de …” = “to be in charge of …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy encargado de cerrar la tienda hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m in charge of closing the store today.

definitions.note: Past participle of “encargar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Juan fue encargado de organizar la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Juan was tasked with organizing the meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with "encargar" meaning to place an order for something (e.g., food, products).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encargamos una pizza para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "encargarse de" = to be in charge of / to take care of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos encargamos de la limpieza después de la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are in charge of the cleaning after the party.

definitions.native: we will take care of, we will handle
definitions.note: Often followed by “de” + noun/infinitive (e.g., “encargarse de”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos encargaremos de la comida para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will take care of the food for the party.

definitions.native: to take care of, to be in charge of
definitions.note: Often used with “de” (encargarme de + noun/verb) to say what you will take care of.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encargarme de la comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take care of the food.

definitions.native: to take care of, to be in charge of
definitions.note: Often used with "de" to say what someone takes care of: "encargarse de algo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo importante es encargarse de los detalles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The important thing is to take care of the details.

definitions.native: will take care of, will be in charge of
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella se encargará del proyecto mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will take care of the project tomorrow.

definitions.native: I will take care of, I will arrange
definitions.note: First person singular (yo), future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo me encargaré de llamar al médico mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will take care of calling the doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for ordering food or requesting something to be made or delivered.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encargo una pizza para esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I order a pizza for tonight.

definitions.note: Often used for a task or request someone asks you to do (e.g., an errand).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un encargo para ti: compra pan, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an errand for you: buy bread, please.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after ‘espero que…’) or as the formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que encargue la comida hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you order the food today.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer encargué una pizza para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I ordered a pizza for dinner.

definitions.note: Past tense (he/she/you-formal) of “encargar”; often used for placing an order or commissioning work.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi mamá encargó una pizza para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mom ordered a pizza for dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes un encendedor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a lighter?

definitions.note: Used for switching on devices (lights, TV, etc.) or lighting a fire/candle.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encender la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to turn on the light.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun “lo” = “it” (masculine singular object, or a generic “it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encenderlo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to turn it on now.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used to agree with a feminine noun (e.g., la luz).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luz está encendida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The light is on.

definitions.note: Feminine plural; often used for lights or candles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las velas están encendidas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The candles are lit.

definitions.note: Often used for devices/lights; can also mean “lit” (on fire).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El televisor está encendido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The TV is turned on.

definitions.note: Past participle of "encender"; often used with "haber" to form the perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He encendido la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have turned on the light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encendió la luz del pasillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She turned on the hallway light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encendí la luz porque estaba oscuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I turned on the light because it was dark.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person or animal kept inside or confined.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro está encerrado en la habitación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is locked in the room.

definitions.note: Past participle often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro está encerrado en la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is locked in the house.

definitions.native: to lock up, to shut in
definitions.note: Often used for locking something/someone inside a place, or keeping something closed in an enclosed space.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encerrar al perro en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to lock the dog in the yard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía lo encerró en una celda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police locked him up in a cell.

definitions.note: Most commonly refers to an electrical plug or the place you plug something in.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hay enchufes cerca de la cama.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are no outlets near the bed.

definitions.note: plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la biblioteca hay muchas enciclopedias antiguas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the library there are many old encyclopedias.

definitions.note: Used for formal commands (usted) and for the present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, encienda la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn on the light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, enciende la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please turn on the light.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "encender" (they/you all turn on).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la noche, encienden las luces de la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night, they turn on the street lights.

definitions.note: Present tense of "encerrar"; often used for locking someone/something inside a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El guardia encierra al perro en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guard locks the dog in the yard.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" ("encima de") to mean "on top of / over".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro está encima de la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book is on top of the table.

definitions.native: in addition, on top of that
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy llegué tarde y encima olvidé las llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I arrived late and on top of that I forgot the keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejé las llaves en la encimera de la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I left the keys on the kitchen countertop.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al oír el ruido, encogió los hombros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he heard the noise, he shrugged his shoulders.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted). Often used for ongoing or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre encontraba mis llaves en el mismo cajón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always used to find my keys in the same drawer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (third person plural). Often used for ongoing or habitual past actions, or to set the scene in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños encontraban conchas en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were finding shells on the beach.

definitions.note: Past participle of "encontrar"; commonly used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he encontrado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He encontrado mis llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have found my keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los documentos fueron encontrados en la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were found in the office.

definitions.note: Present tense (“we find”) or preterite (“we found”), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Finalmente encontramos el hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We finally found the hotel.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of “encontrar”; often used with “estar” to talk about something happening right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy encontrando las llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am finding the keys.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo encontrar mis llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't find my keys.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form; often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., after "si" = "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo encontrara, te llamaría de inmediato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I found it, I would call you right away.

definitions.note: Used in hypothetical or uncertain situations (imperfect subjunctive), often after “si” (if).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si ellos encontraran el libro, me llamarían.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they found the book, they would call me.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (tú). Often used after “si” to mean “if you found / if you were to find.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si encontraras mis llaves, me ayudarías mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you found my keys, you would help me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana encontraremos una solución.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will find a solution.

definitions.native: to find her, to find it
definitions.note: Direct object pronoun "la" can mean "her" or "it" (feminine object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encontrarla mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to find her tomorrow.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun "las" = "them" (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encontrarlas después de la clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to find them after class.

definitions.native: to find him, to find her
definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “le” (= him/her). In some regions (especially Spain), “le” can be used for a male direct object (where other regions often use “lo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encontrarle en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to find him in the park.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun "lo" (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encontrarlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to find it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun attached: "los" = "them" (masculine plural or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a encontrarlos mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to find them tomorrow.

definitions.native: to meet (up with), to find myself
definitions.note: Reflexive form (me). Often used for arranging to meet someone: “encontrarme con…” = “to meet up with…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedé en encontrarme con Ana a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I agreed to meet up with Ana at six.

definitions.native: to meet up, to find ourselves
definitions.note: Reflexive form with "nos" (we/us). Often used as "to meet up" when talking about people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Podemos encontrarnos en la cafetería a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We can meet up at the café at six.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) preterite.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontraron las llaves debajo del sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found the keys under the couch.

definitions.native: to be; to be located; to find oneself
definitions.note: Reflexive verb used to express location or someone/something’s state/condition. Must appear as the infinitive "encontrarse" when cited in isolation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante encontrarse bien antes de viajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to be (to feel) well before traveling.

definitions.native: to find you, to meet up with you
definitions.note: Includes the reflexive pronoun “te” (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero encontrarte mañana después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to meet up with you tomorrow after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrará la respuesta en el libro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find the answer in the book.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana encontrarán la solución.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will find the solution.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontrarás las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will find the keys on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te encontraré mañana en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will find you tomorrow in the park.

definitions.note: Conditional ("would" form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si buscara un poco más, lo encontraría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I looked a little more, I would find it.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Encontraste las llaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you find the keys?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros); often used for suggestions or after expressions like “espero que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontremos una solución juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s find a solution together.

definitions.native: we might find, we might meet
definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (nosotros); used in hypotheticals, wishes, or after certain past expressions (e.g., "quería que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si encontráramos las llaves, podríamos irnos ya.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we found the keys, we could leave now.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontré mis llaves en la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found my keys in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 3rd person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella encontró sus llaves en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She found her keys on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una operación encubierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a covert operation.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) present tense of “encontrar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella encuentra sus llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She finds her keys on the table.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “encontrar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos encuentran las llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They find the keys on the table.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Dónde encuentras las llaves?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Where do you find the keys?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) or formal command (usted) of "encontrar."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que encuentre las llaves pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you find the keys soon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used as an imperative for “you all” in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que encuentren las llaves pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you find the keys soon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form) of "encontrar"; often used after expressions like "quiero que", "espero que", "cuando", etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que encuentres tus llaves pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you find your keys soon.

definitions.note: Often means “find” (an object). It can also mean “meet” in the sense of “run into” someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre encuentro mis llaves en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always find my keys on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos un encuentro mañana por la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a meeting tomorrow afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El encuentro con el perro fue inesperado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The encounter with the dog was unexpected.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos encuentros todos los lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have meetings every Monday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa hizo una encuesta para conocer la opinión de los clientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company did a survey to learn the customers' opinion.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with the object pronoun "lo" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encuéntralo antes de que empiece la clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Find it before class starts.

definitions.note: Affirmative tú command + object pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te pierdes, encuéntrame en la entrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you get lost, find me at the entrance.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command form; often used with de + noun (encárgate de...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encárgate de la cena esta noche, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take care of dinner tonight, please.

definitions.note: Feminine form; refers to a woman or female opponent/adversary.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es mi enemiga en el juego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is my enemy in the game.

definitions.note: Noun meaning a person, group, or force that is opposed or hostile.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El enemigo cruzó la frontera al amanecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The enemy crossed the border at dawn.

definitions.note: Adjective meaning hostile or belonging to the enemy; it must agree in gender/number (enemigo/enemiga/enemigos/enemigas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ejército entró en territorio enemigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army entered enemy territory.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi enemigo vive en la casa de al lado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My enemy lives in the house next door.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; as an adjective it agrees with a masculine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienen planes enemigos contra nosotros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have hostile plans against us.

definitions.note: plural form of "enemigo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero tener enemigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to have enemies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo energía hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have energy today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi cumpleaños es en enero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My birthday is in January.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "enfadar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ruido me enfada mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise annoys me a lot.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enfadada contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m angry with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enfadado porque llegaste tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m angry because you arrived late.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (can also be used for a mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están enfadados porque llegaste tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are angry because you arrived late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre logras enfadar a tu hermano con tus bromas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You always manage to annoy your brother with your jokes.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive ("-ra" form), often used in conditional sentences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No creí que eso te enfadara tanto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't think that would annoy you so much.

definitions.native: to get angry, to get upset
definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive; often used for becoming angry (rather than making someone else angry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es fácil enfadarse cuando hay mucho tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s easy to get angry when there’s a lot of traffic.

definitions.native: you get angry, you get upset
definitions.note: Present tense (tú). Often used with “no te…” as a gentle warning or reassurance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te enfades conmigo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t get mad at me, please.

definitions.note: Often used for being upset or annoyed (a “fit of anger” or “being mad”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su enfado duró todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His anger lasted all day.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "enfadar" (él/ella/usted). Depending on context, it can be intransitive (got angry) or transitive (made someone angry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enfadó cuando escuchó la noticia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got angry when he heard the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor enfatizó la importancia de estudiar todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher emphasized the importance of studying every day.

definitions.note: Can be used for someone becoming ill (present tense, he/she/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana enferma a menudo en invierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister gets sick often in winter.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está enferma hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is sick today.

definitions.note: Past participle of "enfermar"; often used with "haber" (e.g., "he enfermado") or with "estar" in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He enfermado y no puedo ir a trabajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve gotten sick and I can’t go to work.

definitions.native: to get sick; to make (someone) sick
definitions.note: Uses the infinitive enfermar; can be intransitive (to fall ill) or transitive (to make someone ill).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedo enfermar fácilmente en invierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can get sick easily in winter.

definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning “to get sick (myself).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero enfermarme antes del viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to get sick before the trip.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis hermanas están enfermas hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sisters are sick today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una enfermedad y necesito descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an illness and I need to rest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En invierno, hay más enfermedades respiratorias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In winter, there are more respiratory illnesses.

definitions.note: female nurse
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi madre es enfermera en un hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother is a nurse in a hospital.

definitions.note: feminine plural form (female nurses or mixed group when using feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las enfermeras trabajan en el hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The nurses work at the hospital.

definitions.note: Refers to a male nurse; the feminine form is “enfermera”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El enfermero trabaja en el hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The (male) nurse works at the hospital.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana estudia enfermería en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister studies nursing at the university.

definitions.note: Often used for the medical room or clinic inside a school, workplace, or institution.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ve a la enfermería si no te sientes bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go to the infirmary if you don’t feel well.

definitions.note: Often used with the verb "estar" to describe someone who is unwell.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enfermo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sick today.

definitions.note: Often used for a man; for a woman, you’ll usually hear “enferma.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El enfermo necesita descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sick person needs to rest.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used for a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están enfermos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are sick.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el hospital hay muchos enfermos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many sick people in the hospital.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also refer to a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los enfermos esperan al médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sick patients are waiting for the doctor.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she got sick.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enfermó después de comer mariscos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She got sick after eating seafood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos un enfoque diferente para resolver el problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a different approach to solve the problem.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “enfrentar” (he/she/it faces; you formal face).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella enfrenta muchos retos en su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She faces many challenges at her job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He enfrentado muchos problemas este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have faced many problems this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enfrentamos muchos retos este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We face many challenges this year.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they/you plural) present tense
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos enfrentan muchos problemas cada día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They face many problems every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enfrentando un problema difícil en el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am facing a difficult problem at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que enfrentar el problema ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to face the problem now.

definitions.native: we will face, we will confront
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana enfrentaremos un nuevo desafío en el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will face a new challenge at work.

definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning “to face/confront (something) myself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que enfrentarme a mis miedos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to face my fears.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used with "a" (enfrentarse a algo/a alguien).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es difícil enfrentarse a la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to face the truth.

definitions.native: to confront you, to face you
