definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “-te” (= you, informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero enfrentarte en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to confront you in public.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana enfrentarán un examen difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will face a difficult exam.

definitions.note: Often used with "de": "enfrente de" = "in front of / across from".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La farmacia está enfrente del banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The pharmacy is across from the bank.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular: “he/she/it faced.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella enfrentó muchos desafíos el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She faced many challenges last year.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “enfriar”; used with estar to form the progressive (e.g., “está enfriando”) or to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sopa se está enfriando en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup is cooling down on the table.

definitions.note: Can be used transitively (cool something) or reflexively/intransitively (cool down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enfriar la sopa antes de servirla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to cool the soup before serving it.

definitions.note: Future tense (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con la lluvia, el aire se enfriará por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With the rain, the air will cool down at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sopa se enfría rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup cools down quickly.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands: usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que el café se enfríe pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the coffee cools down soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enfureció cuando escuchó la noticia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She got furious when she heard the news.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” to mean “hooked/addicted to” something (e.g., “enganchado a una serie”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enganchado a esta serie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m hooked on this show.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él engaña a la gente para conseguir dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He deceives people to get money.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle/adjective of “engañar”; used with “estar/ser” or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me siento engañada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel deceived.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me siento engañado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel deceived.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense: “they” (or “you” plural in Spain) deceive/trick.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces nos engañan con promesas falsas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes they deceive us with false promises.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ing form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está engañando a sus amigos con esa historia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is deceiving his friends with that story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero engañar a nadie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to deceive anyone.

definitions.native: to deceive me, to trick me
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “me” (“me”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes engañarme; sé la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't deceive me; I know the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me engañaron con una oferta falsa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tricked me with a fake offer.

definitions.native: to trick you, to deceive you
definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “te” (“you”) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero engañarte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to trick you.

definitions.native: you deceive, you trick, you lie to
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me engañas; sé la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re not deceiving me; I know the truth.

definitions.native: you tricked, you deceived, you cheated (on)
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me engañaste y ahora no confío en ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You deceived me, and now I don't trust you.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like "espero que...") or as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no me engañe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don't deceive me.

definitions.note: Used with tú (informal “you”), often in the present subjunctive or as a negative command (e.g., “No me engañes.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me engañes; dime la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t deceive me; tell me the truth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su historia era un engaño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His story was a deception.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las apariencias pueden ser engañosas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Appearances can be misleading.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El anuncio es engañoso y no dice toda la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ad is misleading and doesn’t tell the whole truth.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te engañé y lo siento mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tricked you, and I'm very sorry.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) tricked/deceived.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me engañó con una excusa y nunca volvió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tricked me with an excuse and never came back.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pobreza engendra violencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Poverty creates violence.

definitions.note: Past participle of "engordar"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he engordado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He engordado cinco kilos este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I've gained five kilos this year.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "engordar"; often used with "estar" to talk about an ongoing change.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Últimamente, estoy engordando un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lately, I'm gaining a little weight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desde que dejé de correr, empecé a engordar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since I stopped running, I started to gain weight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desde que ganó el premio, está muy engreído.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Since he won the award, he’s very conceited.

definitions.note: Used to congratulate someone (often for good news or an achievement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Enhorabuena por tu nuevo trabajo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Congratulations on your new job!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su desaparición sigue siendo un enigma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His disappearance is still a mystery.

definitions.note: Often used for a swarm of bees or other insects; can also be used metaphorically for a crowd.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos un enjambre de abejas cerca del árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a swarm of bees near the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los animales estaban enjaulados en el zoológico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The animals were caged in the zoo.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular: “he/she/it rinsed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enjuagó los platos después de lavarlos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She rinsed the dishes after washing them.

definitions.note: Commonly used for a web link or hyperlink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te envío el enlace por correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending you the link by email.

definitions.note: Often used for a connection between things or people (more general than an internet link).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un enlace directo entre el centro y el aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a direct connection between downtown and the airport.

definitions.native: to drive crazy, to make (someone) go crazy
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia lo hizo enloquecer de rabia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news made him go crazy with rage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si sigues sin dormir, vas a enloquecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you keep not sleeping, you're going to go crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando perdió el trabajo, enloqueció por completo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he lost his job, he went completely crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enmarqué la foto de mi familia y la colgué en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I framed my family photo and hung it on the wall.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “enojar” (also commonly: “gets (someone) angry”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese ruido me enoja mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise annoys me a lot.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está enojada conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is angry with me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enojado contigo porque llegaste tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m angry with you because you arrived late.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese comentario puede enojar a cualquiera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That comment can make anyone angry.

definitions.native: to anger; to provoke anger (in someone)
definitions.note: As a pronominal verb (enojarse) it means “to get angry,” but this entry is for enojar.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero enojar a mi jefe con esa decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to anger my boss with that decision.

definitions.native: to get angry, to become upset
definitions.note: Reflexive verb; used for the act of becoming angry/upset.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enojarse si sigues gritando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to get angry if you keep shouting.

definitions.note: Usually used with a reflexive pronoun (e.g., "te enojes" = "you get angry").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no te enojes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t get angry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enojo cuando llegas tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get angry when you arrive late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su enojo duró todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His anger lasted all day.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "enojar" for he/she/it/you (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enojó conmigo porque llegué tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got angry with me because I arrived late.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les): “Me enorgullece...” = “It makes me proud...”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enorgullece tu esfuerzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your effort makes me proud.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El edificio es enorme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building is huge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me ayudaste enormemente con la mudanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You helped me enormously with the move.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los perros son enormes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dogs are huge.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/it tangled; also used with a formal “you” (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cable se enredó en la silla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cable got tangled up in the chair.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a pedir una ensalada para el almuerzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to order a salad for lunch.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "ensayar"; often used with "estar" to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos ensayando la obra para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re rehearsing the play for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for practicing a performance (a play, concert, speech, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que ensayar la obra antes del estreno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to rehearse the play before the premiere.

definitions.note: Used for trying a method, plan, or idea.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a ensayar una nueva receta este fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to try out a new recipe this weekend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que escribir un ensayo para la clase de historia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to write an essay for history class.

definitions.note: Used especially for theater, music, or dance practice before a performance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ensayo empieza a las seis y termina a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rehearsal starts at six and ends at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los ensayos empiezan a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rehearsals start at six.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que entregar tres ensayos esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to turn in three essays this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy para allá enseguida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going there right away.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella enseña español en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She teaches Spanish at school.

definitions.note: Also used as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señor, enseña la lección otra vez, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, teach the lesson again, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela me enseñaba a cocinar cuando era niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother used to teach me to cook when I was a child.

definitions.note: Past participle of “enseñar”; used with “haber” (e.g., “he enseñado”) or as an adjective (e.g., “está enseñado”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya he enseñado la lección de hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have already taught today’s lesson.

definitions.note: From "enseñar"; can also mean "we show" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enseñamos español a los niños los lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We teach Spanish to the children on Mondays.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "enseñar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta escuela, enseñan matemáticas y ciencias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At this school, they teach math and science.

definitions.note: present participle/gerund of "enseñar"; often used with "estar" to describe an ongoing action
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enseñando español a mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am teaching Spanish to my sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La enseñanza de español en esta escuela es muy buena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teaching of Spanish at this school is very good.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (me/te/le/nos/les) + a + infinitive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi padre me va a enseñar a nadar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father is going to teach me to swim.

definitions.native: to show (someone how to do something)
definitions.note: Common in the pattern enseñar + a + infinitive or enseñar + cómo + verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me puedes enseñar cómo se hace esto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you show me how this is done?

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (yo/él/ella/usted). Often used in "if" clauses (si...) or after expressions that trigger the subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo enseñara español, trabajaría en una escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I taught Spanish, I would work at a school.

definitions.native: to teach him, to teach her, to teach you (formal)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun "le" (to him/her/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enseñarle a mi hermana cómo usar la aplicación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to teach my sister how to use the app.

definitions.native: to teach them, to show them
definitions.note: The ending “-les” means “to them” (indirect object).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enseñarles español a mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to teach my friends Spanish.

definitions.note: Infinitive + indirect object pronoun "me" (to me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes enseñarme cómo se hace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you teach me how it’s done?

definitions.native: to teach us, to show us
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes enseñarnos cómo se hace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you teach us how it’s done?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural (they/you all taught).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Les enseñaron a los niños a leer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They taught the children to read.

definitions.native: to teach you, to show you
definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “te” attached (“to you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero enseñarte a cocinar pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to teach you how to cook pasta.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal "you" (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La profesora enseñará español mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher will teach Spanish tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te enseñaré a cocinar una tortilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will teach you how to cook an omelet.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me enseñas a cocinar esta receta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you teach me how to cook this recipe?

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of "enseñar" (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enseñaste a cocinar pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You taught me to cook pasta.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”) or as a formal (usted) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me enseñe español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you teach me Spanish.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal (usted) command meaning “show.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, enseñe su pasaporte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please show your passport.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "enseñar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me enseñes cómo hacerlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you teach me how to do it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te enseño a cocinar pasta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I teach you how to cook pasta.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer enseñé español a mi amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I taught Spanish to my friend.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/you formal) in the past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor nos enseñó a leer en español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher taught us to read in Spanish.

definitions.native: to dirty; to soil; to make dirty
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No vayas a ensuciar el piso con los zapatos mojados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t dirty the floor with wet shoes.

definitions.note: Affirmative tú command + indirect object pronoun (le = to him/her/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enséñale a tu hermano cómo se hace.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Teach your brother how it’s done.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with the object pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enséñame cómo se hace, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Show me how it’s done, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted): “Teach/Show me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, enséñeme cómo llegar a la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please show me how to get to the station.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entendemos la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t understand the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito entender esta pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to understand this question.

definitions.native: understand him, understand her, understand you
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (often meaning “him/her/you (formal)”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo entenderle cuando habla tan rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't understand him when he speaks so fast.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo entenderlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t understand it.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “te” (informal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero entenderte mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to understand you better.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal you (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo entenderá cuando sea mayor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He'll understand it when he's older.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo explicas despacio, entenderán la idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you explain it slowly, they will understand the idea.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo entenderás cuando seas mayor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will understand it when you are older.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), simple future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo entenderé cuando me lo expliques con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll understand it when you explain it to me calmly.

definitions.note: Conditional form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo lo entendería si me lo explicaras con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would understand it if you explained it to me calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me escucharas con calma, entenderías lo que quiero decir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you listened to me calmly, you would understand what I mean.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “got it/OK” (e.g., “¿Entendido?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todo está entendido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is understood.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todo está entendido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything is understood.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "entender"; often used with "estar" to express an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy entendiendo mejor la lección hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am understanding the lesson better today.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted form) of “entender”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo entendiera la pregunta, podría responderla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I understood the question, I could answer it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entendieron la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They didn't understand the question.

definitions.note: Often refers to understanding in the sense of comprehension or mutual agreement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos a un entendimiento después de hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We reached an understanding after talking.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): used for a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Entendiste la tarea?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you understand the assignment?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella entendió la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She understood the question.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entendí la explicación al final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I understood the explanation in the end.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (I/he/she/you formal) of “entender”; often implies an ongoing or habitual understanding in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, no entendía las instrucciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I didn’t understand the instructions.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all understood; also used for ongoing or habitual past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Antes, no entendían las instrucciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Before, they didn’t understand the instructions.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object and "de" (e.g., "me entera de..." = "informs me about...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella me entera de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She informs me about the meeting.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me comí la pizza entera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate the whole pizza.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" (e.g., "estar enterado de...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enterado de la reunión de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m aware of tomorrow’s meeting.

definitions.note: Often used with estar/quedar (e.g., “estar enterado de…” = “to be aware of…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enterado de la noticia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m aware of the news.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enteramente de acuerdo contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I completely agree with you.

definitions.note: Commonly used with the reflexive form: “nos enteramos (de...)” = “we find out (about...)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos enteramos de la noticia ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found out about the news yesterday.

definitions.note: Most commonly used as the pronominal verb “enterarse (de)” meaning “to find out / to hear about.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enterar a mi jefe de lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to inform my boss about what happened.

definitions.native: to find out, to learn (about something)
definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive form of “enterarse”; commonly used with “de” and often after another verb (e.g., “quiero enterarme de algo”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero enterarme de la noticia hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to find out about the news today.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” (enteraron a alguien de algo). More commonly you’ll see the reflexive form “enterarse” meaning “to find out.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me enteraron de la noticia ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They told me about the news yesterday.

definitions.note: Usually used with "de": "enterarse de algo" = "to find out about something".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enterarse de la noticia esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am going to find out about the news this morning.

definitions.note: Often used as “enterarse (de)” meaning “to find out (about).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se enterará de la noticia mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She will find out about the news tomorrow.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me comí dos manzanas enteras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate two whole apples.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object (e.g., “enteraste a alguien de algo” = you informed someone about something). Not to be confused with English “enter.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enteraste a tu jefe del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You informed your boss about the problem.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (who you inform) and sometimes with “de” to introduce what they are informed about.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que entere a su jefe de los cambios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you inform your boss about the changes.

definitions.native: I find out, I hear about
definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive form: me entero (enterarse).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me entero de la noticia por mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I find out about the news from my sister.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me comí el pastel entero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ate the whole cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vaso llegó entero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass arrived intact.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Comimos dos pescados enteros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ate two whole fish.

definitions.note: Used in math (whole number).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los números enteros no tienen decimales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Integers don’t have decimals.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ciudad quedó casi enterrada bajo la arena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city ended up almost buried under the sand.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontraron la caja enterrada en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They found the box buried in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tesoro estaba enterrado en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasure was buried in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tesoro está enterrado cerca del río.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasure is buried near the river.

definitions.note: Adjective, masculine plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los tesoros estaban enterrados bajo la arena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The treasures were buried under the sand.

definitions.native: we bury, we bury (something), we bury (someone)
definitions.note: Also commonly used figuratively: “we bury” (e.g., an idea, the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enterramos el tesoro en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bury the treasure in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a enterrar a su abuelo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to bury their grandfather tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it/him”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a enterrarlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to bury it tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer enterraron al perro en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they buried the dog in the yard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer enterré a mi perro en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I buried my dog in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro enterró el hueso en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog buried the bone in the garden.

definitions.note: This is from the verb “enterar” meaning “to inform.” In everyday Spanish, the reflexive form “enterarse” is very common (e.g., “me enteré” = “I found out”), but that is a different form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enteré a mi jefe del problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I informed my boss about the problem.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively with “se” (e.g., “se enteró”) to mean “found out,” but without “se” it means “informed (someone).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El secretario enteró al director de los cambios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The secretary informed the director about the changes.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "entender"; also used as the formal (usted) command: "understand".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que usted entienda la lección.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you understand the lesson.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes). Also used as an affirmative command for ustedes: “(you all) understand.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que entiendan la tarea antes de empezar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you all to understand the assignment before starting.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of "entender".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que lo entiendas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you understand it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella entiende la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She understands the question.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) form of "entender" in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entienden la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They don't understand the question.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Entiendes la pregunta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you understand the question?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entiendo la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t understand the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella entierra las llaves en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She buries the keys in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El entierro será mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The burial will be tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Primero cenamos y entonces vimos una película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: First we had dinner and then we watched a movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no puedes venir, entonces empezamos sin ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you can't come, then we'll start without you.

definitions.note: Often used to connect ideas or to continue a story (like “then…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo dinero, entonces no puedo ir al cine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have money, so I can’t go to the movies.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El entorno de la escuela es tranquilo y seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The school's environment is calm and safe.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "entrar" (also used for the "you" formal, "he/she" form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano entra en la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother goes into the house.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes a habitual action or an ongoing action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando yo entraba a la casa, el perro corría a saludarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I used to enter the house, the dog would run to greet me.

definitions.note: Vosotros (plural) command form used in Spain; equivalent to “entren” in Latin America.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, entrad y tomaos asiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, come in and take a seat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La entrada del edificio está a la derecha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The building’s entrance is on the right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré dos entradas para el cine.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two tickets for the movie theater.

definitions.note: Often used for event tickets (movies, concerts, games).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré dos entradas para el concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two tickets for the concert.

definitions.note: Used for things like diary entries, contest entries, or entries in a list.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escribí tres entradas en mi diario esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wrote three entries in my diary this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He entrado en la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have entered the house.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entramos al museo a las diez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We go into the museum at ten.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "entrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los estudiantes entran al aula a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students enter the classroom at eight.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "entrar"; often used with "estar" to talk about something happening right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy entrando al edificio ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m entering the building now.

definitions.note: Often used with things like calls, mail, or traffic (e.g., “llamada entrante”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo contestar esa llamada entrante ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't answer that incoming call right now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes entrar ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can go in now.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (past subjunctive), often used in "if" clauses and after expressions of doubt, desire, or possibility.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si él entrara ahora, me sorprendería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he came in now, I would be surprised.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros) future tense of "entrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entraremos por la puerta principal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will enter through the main door.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third person plural of "entrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entraron al museo a las diez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They went into the museum at ten.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) future tense of “entrar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato entrará en la casa cuando abras la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat will enter the house when you open the door.

definitions.native: will enter, will go in, will come in
definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) future tense of "entrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana entrarán al museo a las diez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will enter the museum at ten.

definitions.native: I will enter, I will go in
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana entraré al museo temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will go into the museum early.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense of "entrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Entras ahora o esperas un minuto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you coming in now or waiting a minute?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal "you" (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué entraste sin tocar la puerta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you go in without knocking on the door?

definitions.note: Often used figuratively to mean someone's deepest feelings or the innermost part of something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentí miedo en mis entrañas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt fear in my insides.

definitions.note: From the verb "entrar". Used for "he/she/it enters" in the present subjunctive, and also as a formal command (usted) meaning "enter".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que entre ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he/she enters now.

definitions.note: Used for position in space/time or relationships (e.g., between people or things).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El café está entre la panadería y la farmacia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The café is between the bakery and the pharmacy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La entrega llega mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The delivery arrives tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Often used in fixed phrases like “la entrega de” (the handing over of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La entrega de los documentos fue rápida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The handing over of the documents was quick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entrega el paquete mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: (He/She/You) delivers the package tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El paquete ya ha sido entregado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package has already been delivered.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a entregar el paquete mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to deliver the package tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to him, to her, to you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a entregarle el paquete al vecino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to hand the package to the neighbor.

definitions.native: to deliver it, to hand it over
definitions.note: "-lo" means "it" (masculine singular direct object) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a entregarlo mañana en la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to deliver it tomorrow at the office.

definitions.native: to surrender, to turn myself in
definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a entregarme a la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to turn myself in to the police.

definitions.native: they delivered, they handed over, they turned in
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entregaron el paquete a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They delivered the package on time.

definitions.native: to surrender, to turn yourself in
definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used for surrendering or turning oneself in to the authorities.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decidió entregarse a la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided to turn himself in to the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana el mensajero entregará el paquete.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow the courier will deliver the package.

definitions.native: I will deliver, I will hand over
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te entregaré el paquete mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will deliver the package to you tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te entrego el paquete mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll deliver the package to you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after "espero que") or as a formal (usted) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que lo entregue mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you deliver it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command for ustedes) of “entregar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que me entreguen el informe hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to hand me the report today.

definitions.note: Used with tú in the present subjunctive, often after expressions like “quiero que…” or “espero que…”. It also appears in negative tú commands (e.g., “No entregues…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no entregues el dinero todavía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t hand over the money yet.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer entregué el informe a mi jefe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I handed in the report to my boss.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular: “he/she/it delivered/handed over.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mensajero entregó el paquete ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The courier delivered the package yesterday.

definitions.note: First-person plural present subjunctive; often used to make a suggestion or invitation (“let’s…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entremos al museo antes de que cierre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go into the museum before it closes.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive or formal command (ustedes) form of "entrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que entren ahora, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to come in now, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command) form of "entrenar" for "they/you all".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que entren todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that they train every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi perro está bien entrenado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dog is well trained.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El entrenador habla con el equipo antes del partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The coach talks with the team before the game.

definitions.note: Feminine form; refers to a woman (or a female coach/trainer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La entrenadora del equipo nos explicó el plan para el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team's coach explained the plan for the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El equipo necesita más entrenamiento antes del partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team needs more training before the match.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ando): describes an action in progress ("(is) training").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy entrenando para el partido del sábado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m training for Saturday’s game.

definitions.note: Used for practicing/preparing for a sport or skill, or for training an animal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito entrenar para correr una maratón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to train to run a marathon.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo). Often used for sports or working out.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entreno tres veces por semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I train three times a week.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/it trained.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella entrenó para la carrera todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She trained for the race every day.

definitions.note: Often used for the area between the legs; can be a sensitive/intimate term depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se sentó y se lastimó la entrepierna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sat down and hurt his crotch.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "entrar"; often used after expressions like "quiero que" or "espero que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que entres en la casa con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you go into the house carefully.

definitions.note: Masculine singular form; often agrees with the noun it modifies (e.g., entretenida, entretenidos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El programa fue muy entretenido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The show was very entertaining.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco entretenimiento después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I look for entertainment after work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El payaso entretuvo a los niños durante la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The clown entertained the children during the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una entrevista de trabajo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a job interview tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a entrevistar a la candidata mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to interview the candidate tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo dos entrevistas esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two interviews this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia me entristece mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news makes me very sad.

definitions.note: Third-person singular, past (preterite): “he/she/it made (someone) sad / became sad.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia lo entristeció mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news made him very sad.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of "entrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entro en la tienda para comprar pan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go into the store to buy bread.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular of "entrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer entré en la casa sin hacer ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I entered the house without making any noise.

definitions.note: Command (tú) + indirect object pronoun “le” (“to him/her/you formal”). The thing being given is implied.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Entrégale el documento al profesor, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give the document to the teacher, please.

definitions.note: Command (tú) + "me" (to me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, entrégame el formulario hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please give me the form today.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (and formal you singular) in the simple past (pretérito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella entró en la casa sin hacer ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She entered the house without making any noise.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy entusiasmada con el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m excited about the trip.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" (e.g., "estoy entusiasmado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy entusiasmado por el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m excited about the trip.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used for a group of men or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos muy entusiasmados con el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re very excited about the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta tu entusiasmo por aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like your enthusiasm for learning Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy muy entusiasta con el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very enthusiastic about the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con el tiempo, todos vamos a envejecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With time, we are all going to age.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vino envejecido tiene un sabor más intenso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Aged wine has a more intense flavor.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of "envejecer"; used with "estar" to talk about an ongoing process.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo está envejeciendo poco a poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is aging little by little.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La comida estaba envenenada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was poisoned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro fue envenenado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog was poisoned.

definitions.note: Simple past (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Envenenaron el agua del pozo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They poisoned the well water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alguien envenenó el agua del pozo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone poisoned the water in the well.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used in passive voice or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La carta fue enviada ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The letter was sent yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El paquete ya está enviado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The package is already sent.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te he enviado un correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have sent you an email.

definitions.note: Past participle of “enviar”. It often agrees in gender/number (e.g., enviados/enviadas) when used as an adjective or in passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los documentos fueron enviados ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents were sent yesterday.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/nosotras). Can also be the preterite form: “we sent,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enviamos el paquete hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We send the package today.

definitions.note: Gerund (used like English “-ing”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy enviando un correo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sending an email now.

definitions.note: Often used for sending messages, emails, letters, or packages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enviar un correo a mi profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to send an email to my teacher.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "enviar"; often used in "si" (if) clauses or after certain expressions of doubt, emotion, or desire.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo enviara el correo hoy, llegaría mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I sent the mail today, it would arrive tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Enviaremos el paquete mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will send the package tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: The "-le" at the end is an indirect object pronoun meaning “to him,” “to her,” or “to you” (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enviarle un correo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to send him an email tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes enviarme el enlace, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you send me the link, please?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), they/you (plural, formal) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer enviaron el paquete por correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they sent the package by mail.

definitions.note: Literally “to send you” (to you = te).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a enviarte la información por correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to send you the information by email.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) future tense of “enviar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana enviará el paquete por correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she/you (formal) will send the package by mail.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ellos/ellas/ustedes) future tense of "enviar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana enviarán el paquete por correo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will send the package by mail.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te enviaré un mensaje mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will send you a message tomorrow.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) preterite form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué no me enviaste el archivo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why didn't you send me the file?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentí envidia cuando vi sus vacaciones en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt envy when I saw their vacation at the beach.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (I/he/she/you formal) of “envidiar”; often means “used to envy” or “was envying.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era joven, envidiaba la libertad de mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was young, I envied my friends' freedom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te envidio por tu paciencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I envy you for your patience.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of "enviar" for "yo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te envié un mensaje ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sent you a message yesterday.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “enviar” for he/she/it or formal you.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella me envió un mensaje ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sent me a message yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tira el envoltorio a la basura, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throw the wrapper in the trash, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella envolvió el regalo con papel de colores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She wrapped the gift with colored paper.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object (e.g., names, numbers). For “is wrong / makes a mistake,” Spanish usually uses the reflexive form: “se equivoca.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother always mixes up the names.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was a mistake to send the email to the wrong person.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu respuesta está equivocada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your answer is wrong.

definitions.note: feminine plural
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las respuestas están equivocadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The answers are wrong.

definitions.note: Often used with the verb “estar” to say someone is incorrect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo siento, estás equivocado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, you're wrong.

definitions.note: Often used with haber (e.g., "he equivocado") to mean you made a mistake. Not the same as English "equivocated."

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I got the address wrong.

definitions.note: Masculine plural adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están equivocados sobre la hora de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are wrong about the time of the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos se equivocan cuando no leen las instrucciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are wrong when they don’t read the instructions.

definitions.native: to make a mistake; to be wrong
definitions.note: Reflexive verb. Often conjugated (e.g., “me equivoqué”), but this entry’s example uses the infinitive exactly as “equivocarse.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es fácil equivocarse en esta pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s easy to make a mistake on this question.

definitions.native: you’re mistaken, you make a mistake

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re mistaken: the meeting is tomorrow, not today.

definitions.native: you were wrong, you made a mistake

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You got the address wrong and arrived late.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively: "me equivoco" = "I’m wrong / I made a mistake." (Without "me," it can also mean "I mix up" or "I confuse" something.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me equivoco a veces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wrong sometimes.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se equivocó de dirección y llegó tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was wrong about the direction and arrived late.

definitions.native: I was wrong, I made a mistake
definitions.note: First-person singular, simple past (pretérito) of “equivocar(se)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me equivoqué de número.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I dialed the wrong number.

definitions.note: A time period in history (often used with an adjective, e.g., “la era moderna”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a new era of technology.

definitions.note: often describes a state or situation in the past
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, vivía en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I lived in Madrid.

definitions.note: Nonstandard spelling without accent; standard is «éramos» (imperfect of «ser»).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we were very happy at the party.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (third-person plural) of “ser” (to be).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos eran mis mejores amigos en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were my best friends in school.

definitions.note: Imperfect form of “ser” for informal “you” (tú).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were a child, you liked dinosaurs.

definitions.note: Used with ser for identity, origin, and more permanent characteristics.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eres muy amable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are very kind.

definitions.note: Often used for eliminating something harmful (like a disease, poverty, or a problem).

definitions.note: Plural of “error”.

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That answer is wrong.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The volcano’s eruption forced people to evacuate.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) present of “ser” (to be).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is Monday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa es grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is big.

definitions.note: used before feminine singular nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa mochila es azul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That backpack is blue.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used for a woman/girl or a feminine noun)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa es mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That is my sister.

definitions.note: feminine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going to buy those flowers?

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustan esas flores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like those flowers.

definitions.note: Often used for measurements (e.g., a map scale) or proportions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este mapa tiene una escala de 1:50.000.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This map has a scale of 1:50,000.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like rock climbing.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This weekend we climb a mountain.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to climb the mountain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El conflicto puede escalar rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The conflict can escalate quickly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los ladrones escaparon por la ventana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thieves escaped through the window.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He tried to escape from the house without anyone seeing him.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a way out before it’s too late.

definitions.note: Also used for escaping from a place or situation (e.g., prison, danger).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we don’t close the door, the dog might run away.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This weekend we did an escape room with my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a water shortage in the region.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time is scarce to finish the project.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay escasos recursos en la escuela.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actor came out onto the stage and greeted the audience.

definitions.note: Often used for the place or context where something happens, especially in news or descriptions.

definitions.note: plural form of "esclavo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la antigüedad, muchos esclavos trabajaban en las minas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In ancient times, many slaves worked in the mines.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una escoba para barrer la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a broom to sweep the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Scottish.
