definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have future plans.

definitions.note: Spelling note: today it’s written “fue” (without an accent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer fué al cine con sus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she went to the movies with his/her friends.

definitions.note: Common misspelling of “fue” (modern Spanish spelling has no accent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el mensaje decía: «Ayer fué un día difícil».
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the message it said: “Yesterday was a difficult day.”

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (nosotros/nosotras) of “ir” (to go) or “ser” (to be).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si fuéramos al parque, podríamos hacer un picnic.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we went to the park, we could have a picnic.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (nosotros/nosotras) of "ser"; often used after expressions like "si" (if) or to express wishes, doubts, or hypotheticals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si fuéramos más pacientes, todo sería más fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we were more patient, everything would be easier.

definitions.note: Usually spelled "fui" (without an accent).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fuí al cine ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I went to the movie theater yesterday.

definitions.note: Used with the verb “ser” in the preterite (past) tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer fuí muy feliz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I was very happy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi madre trabaja en una fábrica de coches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My mother works in a car factory.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta ciudad hay muchas fábricas de ropa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city there are many clothing factories.

definitions.note: Often a short story with a moral lesson, sometimes with animals as characters.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La maestra leyó una fábula en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher read a fable in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este libro es fácil de leer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is easy to read.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs (e.g., “entender fácil” = “to understand easily”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella aprende fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She learns easily.

definitions.note: Plural form (used with masculine or feminine plural nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos ejercicios son fáciles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These exercises are easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo resolví fácilmente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I solved it easily.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tierra de este valle es muy fértil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soil in this valley is very fertile.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella no se fía de desconocidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She doesn’t trust strangers.

definitions.note: In some regions, this is commonly used about letting someone pay later (buying “on credit”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El dueño de la tienda le fía porque lo conoce.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The shop owner lets him buy on credit because he knows him.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). Often used with “en”: “Fíjate en …” = “Look at … / Notice …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fíjate en ese perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at that dog.

definitions.note: Command form for “you all” (ustedes). Often used with “en” (fíjense en...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fíjense en el mapa antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at the map before you leave.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). Often used as “fíjese en …” = “look at / notice …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fíjese en el mapa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please look at the map.

definitions.note: Often used with “en” (e.g., “fío en ti”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No fío en esas promesas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t trust those promises.

definitions.native: sell on credit, lend on credit
definitions.note: Common in everyday speech in some regions to mean giving someone something now and letting them pay later.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy no fío; págame primero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m not selling on credit; pay me first.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La física me parece interesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Physics seems interesting to me.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective; it agrees with a feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una actividad física todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a physical activity every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy físicamente cansado, pero mentalmente bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m physically tired, but mentally fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hicimos ejercicio físico en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We did physical exercise in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tío es físico y trabaja en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is a physicist and works at the university.

definitions.note: In many places, this is short for “fisioterapeuta.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy al físico dos veces por semana por la lesión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to the physical therapist twice a week because of the injury.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito la fórmula para calcular el área de un círculo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need the formula to calculate the area of a circle.

definitions.note: In many places, the plural “fósforos” can also mean “matches.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes un fósforo para encender la vela?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have a match to light the candle?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes fósforos para encender la vela?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have matches to light the candle?

definitions.note: In most Spanish-speaking countries, fútbol refers to soccer (association football).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A mi hermano le encanta jugar al fútbol los fines de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother loves playing soccer on the weekends.

definitions.note: In standard German spelling, nouns are capitalized ("Führer"). The word can also be associated with Adolf Hitler’s title "der Führer" in historical contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Unser führer zeigt uns den Weg.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our guide shows us the way.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me compré una gabardina para los días de lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought myself a trench coat for rainy days.

definitions.note: Often refers to the group of top government ministers (the cabinet), or to a cupboard/display cabinet in a home.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El presidente reunió a su gabinete para hablar de la crisis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The president gathered his cabinet to talk about the crisis.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural to refer to a thick, porridge-like dish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para desayunar, comimos gachas con miel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast, we ate porridge with honey.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito mis gafas para leer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need my glasses to read.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuestra galaxia se llama la Vía Láctea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our galaxy is called the Milky Way.

definitions.note: Plural of "galaxia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay miles de millones de galaxias en el universo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are billions of galaxies in the universe.

definitions.note: Often refers to an art gallery; it can also mean a balcony/upper seating area in a theater or stadium depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a visitar una galería de arte este sábado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to visit an art gallery this Saturday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay varias galerías de arte en esta calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are several art galleries on this street.

definitions.note: Used for speech or writing that is confusing or hard to understand.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo que dijo el político fue un galimatías.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What the politician said was gibberish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero una galleta con chocolate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a chocolate cookie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré unas galletas para el postre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some cookies for dessert.

definitions.note: Diminutive plural of "galleta"; often implies small, cute, or snack-sized cookies.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré unas galletitas para el café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some cookies for coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La gallina pone huevos en el corral.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hen lays eggs in the yard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las gallinas ponen huevos todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hens lay eggs every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la granja hay un gallito blanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the farm there is a little white rooster.

definitions.note: Often used to describe someone who acts brave or tries to intimidate others (e.g., “hacerse el gallito”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja de hacerte el gallito y habla con respeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop acting like a tough guy and speak respectfully.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gallo canta al amanecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rooster crows at dawn.

definitions.note: Often used for a handsome, charming man (especially in movies/TV or romance).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la serie, él es el galán que todos admiran.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the series, he is the leading man that everyone admires.

definitions.note: Noun for a Welsh person; can also be used as an adjective meaning “Welsh.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecino es galés y habla dos idiomas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Welsh and speaks two languages.

definitions.note: In Spain, "gambas" commonly refers to shrimp/prawns as food (often served as a dish).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a pedir gambas al ajillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to order garlic shrimp.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural: “ganas” (e.g., “tener ganas de…” = “to feel like…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo gana de discutir hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have the desire to argue today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella gana mucho dinero en su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She earns a lot of money at her job.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, siempre ganaba en ese juego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I always won at that game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ganado pasta en el campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The livestock grazes in the field.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es dinero ganado con mucho esfuerzo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s money earned with a lot of effort.

definitions.note: Past participle of "ganar"; often used with "haber" (e.g., "he ganado" = "I have won/earned").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He ganado el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have won the match.

definitions.note: As an adjective it means “winning”; it can also be used as a noun meaning “winner.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuestro equipo es el ganador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team is the winner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ganador recibe un premio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The winner receives a prize.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with feminine nouns or when referring to a woman).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es la ganadora del concurso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the winner of the contest.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") form of "ganar"; it can refer to winning (a game, prize) or earning (money).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy ganamos el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we win the match.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "ganar" (they/you all win/earn).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos ganan mucho dinero con ese trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They earn a lot of money with that job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tienda tuvo una ganancia grande este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store had a big profit this month.

definitions.note: Plural form of “ganancia”; often used for business profits or money earned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las ganancias de la empresa aumentaron este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company's profits increased this year.

definitions.note: Gerund/present participle of "ganar" (used for ongoing actions, often with "estar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy ganando el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am winning the game.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi equipo va a ganar el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My team is going to win the game.

definitions.note: Used especially with money, a salary, or wages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a ganar mil euros al mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to earn one thousand euros a month.

definitions.note: Used in the imperfect subjunctive (often in "if" clauses or after expressions of doubt/wishes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo ganara la lotería, compraría una casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I won the lottery, I would buy a house.

definitions.native: we will win, we will earn
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si jugamos en equipo, ganaremos el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we play as a team, we will win the match.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "ganar" with the object pronoun "me" attached ("to win me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que ganarme con tu honestidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to win me over with your honesty.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), they/you all (Spain) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos ganaron el partido ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They won the game yesterday.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; commonly used with a direct object (ganarse la vida, ganarse el respeto).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con su constancia, logró ganarse el respeto de sus compañeros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With his perseverance, he managed to earn the respect of his classmates.

definitions.native: to win someone over, to gain someone’s trust/affection
definitions.note: Often used as ganarse a alguien (to win someone over).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con paciencia, supo ganarse a la nueva jefa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With patience, he knew how to win over the new boss.

definitions.native: to make a living, to earn one’s livelihood
definitions.note: Common fixed phrase: ganarse la vida (often with an activity: ganarse la vida trabajando...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo se fue a la ciudad para ganarse la vida como carpintero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather went to the city to make a living as a carpenter.

definitions.native: to win you over, to earn you
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "te" (= you). Often used for earning someone's trust or affection ("ganarte a alguien").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero ganarte con hechos, no con palabras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to win you over with actions, not with words.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal you (usted) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si sigue así, ganará el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he keeps it up, he will win the match.

definitions.native: I will win, I will earn
definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of "ganar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si entreno más, ganaré el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I train more, I will win the match.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "ganar" (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con más práctica, ganaría el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With more practice, I would win the match.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural, often with "tener ganas de" + infinitive to mean "to feel like" doing something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo ganas de comer pizza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel like eating pizza.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si juegas bien, ganas el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you play well, you win the game.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of "ganar" for "tú" (you, informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ganaste el partido por un punto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You won the game by one point.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuelga el abrigo en el gancho, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hang the coat on the hook, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) or command form (usted) of “ganar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que gane el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope I win the match.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros), often used to make a suggestion or encouragement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Ganemos el partido!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's win the game!

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros), used after expressions of desire, purpose, or necessity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que ganemos este partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want us to win this game.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of “ganar”. Used after expressions like “espero que…”, “quiero que…”, “cuando…”, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ganes el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you win the match.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontré una ganga en la tienda y compré unos zapatos muy baratos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a bargain in the store and bought some very cheap shoes.

definitions.note: From the verb "ganar"; "gano" is the first-person singular present tense form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy gano más dinero en mi nuevo trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I earn more money at my new job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ganso camina cerca del lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The goose walks near the lake.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person singular: “I won / I earned.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer gané el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I won the match.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), third person singular (he/she/it won; you formal won).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella ganó el partido ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She won the game yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está en el garaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is in the garage.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product guarantees good results.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El éxito no está garantizado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Success is not guaranteed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedo garantizar que todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can guarantee that everything is going to turn out fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te garantizo que todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I guarantee you that everything is going to turn out fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta garantía cubre el producto por dos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This warranty covers the product for two years.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duele la garganta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My throat hurts.

definitions.note: Informal (especially in Spain); often suggests a somewhat shady or low-key place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a tomar algo a ese garito de la esquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go have a drink at that dive bar on the corner.

definitions.note: Informal; can refer to an illegal or secret place where people gamble.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police shut down an illegal gambling den.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato tiene garras muy afiladas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos una garza en el río.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a heron in the river.

definitions.note: Usually masculine in Spanish (el gas).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a gas leak in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used informally in some countries (more commonly: gasolina).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito gas para llegar a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need gas to get home.

definitions.note: Plural of "gas".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this lab we measure several gases.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito gasolina para el coche.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella gasta mucho dinero en ropa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She spends a lot of money on clothes.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something that has been used a lot and is no longer in good condition.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis zapatos están gastados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are worn out.

definitions.note: Past participle of "gastar"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he gastado").

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy gastando mucho dinero este mes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This month's spending was very high.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis gastos mensuales han aumentado este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My monthly expenses have gone up this year.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy estudiando gramática española.

definitions.note: used before a singular noun instead of grande

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a big city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivo en una casa grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live in a big house.

definitions.note: Used adverbially in expressions like “a lo grande” (on a big/grand scale).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They celebrated in a big way.

definitions.note: Plural form; used with plural nouns.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends have big ideas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La grandeza de su trabajo fue reconocida por todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The greatness of his work was recognized by everyone.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something impressive or on a large scale (events, buildings, plans, etc.).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The concert was magnificent.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That big guy doesn’t fit through the door.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That big, clumsy guy doesn’t fit in the chair.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a building where grain is stored.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The barn is full of wheat this year.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a grain of sand in my shoe.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents have a farm with chickens and cows.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The farmer works in the countryside every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me salió un grano en la nariz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got a pimple on my nose.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Add two grains of salt.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I got pimples on my face.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estas grasas no son saludables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These fats are not healthy.

definitions.note: Means “for free” (no cost).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The entrance is free.

definitions.note: Means “at no cost” (not “libre” = free as in not restricted).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Admission is free today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento mucha gratitud por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel a lot of gratitude for your help.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La entrada es gratuita hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The admission is free today.

definitions.note: Often means “free of charge,” not “gratis” as in “at no cost.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El servicio es gratuito durante el primer mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The service is free of charge during the first month.

definitions.note: Often used for serious situations like illnesses, accidents, or problems.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La situación es grave.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The situation is serious.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La gravedad hace que los objetos caigan al suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gravity makes objects fall to the ground.

definitions.note: Used to talk about how serious a situation, problem, or action is.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No entendí la gravedad del problema hasta ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t understand the seriousness of the problem until yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The man was seriously injured in the accident.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las heridas no son graves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The injuries are not serious.

definitions.note: Used for the harsh sound a crow or raven makes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cuervo grazna en el árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The crow caws in the tree.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesora es griega.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Greek.

definitions.note: Used to describe something from Greece; also used for the Greek language.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm learning Greek.

definitions.note: Often written with a capital letter in English when referring to the nationality.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecino es griego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Greek.

definitions.note: Can refer to the Greek language; in Spanish it’s not capitalized as a language name.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aprendiendo griego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Greek.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los griegos tienen una historia muy antigua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Greeks have a very ancient history.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are cracks in the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn off the tap, please.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At night you can hear many crickets in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo gripe y no voy a ir a trabajar hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the flu and I'm not going to go to work today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche es gris.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is gray.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis zapatos son grises.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are gray.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella grita cuando está enojada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She shouts when she is angry.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, gritaba mucho en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a kid, I used to shout a lot in the yard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el estadio, gritaban muy fuerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the stadium, they were shouting very loudly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He gritado tu nombre, pero no me escuchaste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shouted your name, but you didn’t hear me.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "gritar" (they/you all shout).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños gritan en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children shout in the yard.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "gritar"; often used with "estar" to mean "(to be) shouting" or to describe how something is done.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están gritando en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are shouting in the yard.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) or formal command (usted) of "gritar."

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú); used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, or in negative commands.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No grites en la biblioteca.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Oí un grito en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a shout in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escuché gritos en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard shouts in the street.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) for “yo” (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Grité tu nombre, pero no me oíste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I shouted your name, but you didn’t hear me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gritó mi nombre desde la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She shouted my name from the street.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with feminine nouns or feminine subjects).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa respuesta fue muy grosera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That answer was very rude.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas grosero con la camarera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be rude to the waitress.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (or mixed-gender plural) of "grosero".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus comentarios fueron muy groseros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His comments were very rude.

definitions.note: Often used for something impolite or offensive that someone says or does.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me digas groserías, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't say rude things to me, please.

definitions.note: Plural; often used for rude language or obscene words.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No digas groserías delante de los niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't say swear words in front of the kids.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "grueso".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wall is very thick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este libro es muy grueso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is very thick.

definitions.note: Often used for things like animals or body parts; for people, it can sound blunt.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is grumpy today because she slept little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro gruñó cuando el extraño se acercó.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a construction crane; it can also mean a tow truck in some regions.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on my gloves because it's cold.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu hermana es muy guapa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your sister is very pretty.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las chicas están muy guapas hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls look very pretty today.

definitions.note: Often used for males, but it can also describe females as “pretty” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu hermano es muy guapo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your brother is very handsome.

definitions.note: Commonly used as an adjective too (guapo/guapa = handsome/pretty), but here it’s used as a noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese guapo es mi hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That handsome guy is my brother.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used for a group of men or a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los chicos están muy guapos hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boys look very handsome today.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Estás guapísima hoy!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You look gorgeous today!

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum guard closed the door.

definitions.note: Present tense (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella guarda el dinero en una caja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She keeps the money in a box.

definitions.note: Command form (tú).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep this document, please.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bicicleta está guardada en el garaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bike is put away in the garage.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it describes something that has been kept or put away.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the document saved on my computer.

definitions.note: Past participle of "guardar"; often used with "haber" (e.g., "he guardado" = "I have saved/stored").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actor arrived with two bodyguards.

definitions.note: From "guardar"; often means keeping something for later or saving (money, files, etc.).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We save money for the vacation.

definitions.native: they keep, they store, they save
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardan la comida en el refrigerador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They keep the food in the fridge.

definitions.note: Often used with estar to talk about an action in progress (e.g., estoy guardando = “I’m saving/putting away”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy guardando dinero para el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m saving money for the trip.

definitions.note: Often used for keeping something for later or saving something (including saving a file).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a guardar este documento en mi computadora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to save this document on my computer.

definitions.note: Common when talking about putting objects somewhere they belong (e.g., food, clothes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de cenar, voy a guardar la comida en el refrigerador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After dinner, I’m going to put the food away in the refrigerator.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "guardar"; often used after expressions like "esperaba que..." (I hoped that...).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esperaba que él guardara el secreto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hoped that he would keep the secret.

definitions.native: to keep it, to save it, to store it
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a guardarlo en mi mochila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to keep it in my backpack.

definitions.native: they saved, they kept, they put away
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardaron las fotos en una carpeta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They saved the photos in a folder.

definitions.native: I will keep, I will save
definitions.note: First person singular (yo) in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardaré el dinero para el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will save the money for the trip.

definitions.note: plural of "guarda"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los guardas del museo vigilan las salas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The museum guards watch over the rooms.

definitions.note: Used with tú (informal “you”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you keep the receipt in case we need it?

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guarde el recibo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Keep the receipt, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes) and formal command (ustedes) form of "guardar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, guarden sus pasaportes en un lugar seguro.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My son goes to daycare in the mornings.

definitions.note: In some contexts, it can mean a place where plants are grown and sold.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compramos un árbol frutal en la guardería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We bought a fruit tree at the plant nursery.

definitions.note: Used with tú in the present subjunctive (often after "que") and in negative tú commands (e.g., "no guardes").

definitions.note: Often used for someone on duty providing security (e.g., at a building, event, or entrance).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two guards at the entrance.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardo las llaves en mi bolso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I keep the keys in my bag.

definitions.native: I saved, I kept, I put away
definitions.note: First-person singular preterite (completed past action).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saved the file before shutting down the computer.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/it kept/saved; you (formal) kept/saved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella guardó el dinero en su bolso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kept the money in her purse.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found the thief’s hideout.

definitions.note: Informal and insulting.

definitions.note: Used to express surprise or admiration; also used to imitate a dog's bark (“woof”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Guau, qué bonito es este lugar!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow, this place is so beautiful!

definitions.note: Informal (Spain); often used in casual speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu idea es guay.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your idea is cool.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La guerra terminó hace muchos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The war ended many years ago.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las guerras causan mucho sufrimiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wars cause a lot of suffering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El guerrero regresó al pueblo después de la batalla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warrior returned to the town after the battle.

definitions.note: Plural form of "guerrero".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los guerreros defendieron la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The warriors defended the city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La guerrilla atacó el convoy al amanecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guerrilla attacked the convoy at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El guía nos va a guiar por el museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide is going to guide us through the museum.

definitions.note: Simple future (yo) of “guiar” (to guide).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo te guiaré hasta la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will guide you to the station.

definitions.note: Often used for a movie/TV script or a written plan for what will be said.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El director está leyendo el guion de la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director is reading the movie script.

definitions.note: In Spanish, this can refer to the punctuation mark (-).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon un guion entre las dos palabras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put a hyphen between the two words.

definitions.note: Person who writes the script for a film, TV show, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana trabaja como guionista en una serie de televisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister works as a screenwriter on a TV series.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para la cena, voy a cocinar guisantes con zanahorias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For dinner, I'm going to cook peas with carrots.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy comemos guiso de pollo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re eating chicken stew.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta tocar la guitarra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to play the guitar.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las guitarras están en el estuche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guitars are in the case.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es guitarrista en una banda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a guitarist in a band.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me hizo un guiño para decirme que todo estaba bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave me a wink to tell me that everything was fine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella me guiñó un ojo antes de entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She winked at me before going in.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "guiar" (he/she/it guided; you [formal] guided).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mapa nos guió hasta el hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The map guided us to the hotel.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the written text for a film, TV show, play, or video.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy leyendo el guión de la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reading the movie script.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Encontré un gusano en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I found a worm in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el jardín hay gusanos después de la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the garden there are worms after the rain.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (me, te, le, etc.); literally means "is pleasing to."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el chocolate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like chocolate.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of “gustar” (often used with an indirect object pronoun, e.g., me/te/le).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustaba ese libro cuando era niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked that book when I was a child.

definitions.note: Used like “to be pleasing”: the thing liked is the subject, and the person who likes it is usually an indirect object (me/te/le/nos/les).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A mis amigos les gustaban mucho esas canciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends really liked those songs.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tú). Used for past habits or ongoing states in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando eras niño, te gustabas las historias de miedo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were a child, you liked scary stories.

definitions.note: Past participle of "gustar"; often used with "haber" in perfect tenses (e.g., "me ha gustado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me ha gustado mucho la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I really liked the movie.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object pronoun (e.g., “nos”) and the thing liked is usually the grammatical subject (e.g., “Nos gustan…” = “We like…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos gustamos mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We like each other a lot.

definitions.note: Used with plural subjects (the things that are liked). Often appears with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustan los perros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like dogs.

definitions.note: Usually used with estar (e.g., “me está gustando…”) to mean “(I am) liking…”; with gustar, the thing liked is the subject and the person is an indirect object (me/te/le…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me está gustando la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm liking the movie.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object (me/te/le/nos/os/les) and often followed by "(el/la/los/las)" + thing liked; literally closer to “to be pleasing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A mí me suele gustar el café por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually like coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “gustar” (often used after past-tense expressions like “quería que…”, “era importante que…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que te gustara la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted you to like the movie.

definitions.native: to please (to someone), for someone to like (something)
definitions.note: Infinitive form with an attached indirect object pronoun: gustar + le (“to him/her/you [formal]”). Often appears conjugated (gusta/gustan) in real sentences, but here it’s shown as the infinitive with -le attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Va a gustarle el café a Juan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Juan is going to like the coffee.

definitions.native: to be pleasing to me; for me to like (something)
definitions.note: Infinitive form with an indirect object pronoun attached (“gustar” + “me”). Often used after another verb (e.g., "va a gustarme", "puede gustarme"). Literally “to please me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Creo que va a gustarme esta película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I think I’m going to like this movie.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object (e.g., me/te/le/nos/les): the thing liked is the grammatical subject.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustaron mucho las películas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I liked the movies a lot.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les) to mean “(someone) will like (something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A María le gustará la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María will like the movie.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les), like: “Me gustaría…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustaría un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/os/les): e.g., “Me gustas” = “I like you.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gustas mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like you a lot.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) of "gustar"; often used in phrases like "Espero que te guste..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que te guste la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like the movie.

definitions.note: Used with the verb "gustar" in the present subjunctive (ustedes/ellos/ellas). Often appears after expressions like "Espero que..." or "Quiero que...".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que les gusten estas canciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like these songs.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "gustar" (used after expressions like "quiero que", "espero que", etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que te gustes más con este corte de pelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you like yourself more with this haircut.

definitions.note: This form is much less common than the usual structure with an indirect object (e.g., “me gusta…”). In some regions it’s used with “de”: “gusto de…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo gusto de la música clásica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like classical music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este té tiene buen gusto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This tea tastes good.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "a mi gusto" (in my opinion) or "tener gusto por" (to like).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A mi gusto, esta película es muy larga.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In my opinion, this movie is very long.

definitions.note: Plural of "gusto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cada persona tiene gustos diferentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Each person has different tastes.

definitions.note: Used with an indirect object (e.g., me/te/le) to mean that something was pleasing to someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A Juan le gustó la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Juan liked the movie.

definitions.note: Command (tú). "Lo" = "it" (masculine object pronoun, also used for unknown/neutral things).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guárdalo en tu mochila, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Save it in your backpack, please.

definitions.note: Affirmative tú command with a direct object pronoun (los = “them”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si los necesitas después, guárdalos en tu mochila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you need them later, keep them in your backpack.

definitions.note: Command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guárdame un poco de pan para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Save me a little bread for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella nos guía por la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She guides us through the city.

definitions.note: Can refer to a person (tour guide) or a guidebook/instruction guide, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El guía nos explicó la historia del museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide explained the history of the museum to us.

definitions.note: Plural of "guía".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los guías explican la historia del museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guides explain the history of the museum.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) or as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que me guíe en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you guide me in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La película trata sobre un gángster famoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is about a famous gangster.

definitions.note: Usually used in the phrase “hacer gárgaras” (to gargle).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que hacer gárgaras con agua tibia y sal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to gargle with warm water and salt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En este formulario tienes que elegir tu género.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On this form you have to choose your gender.

definitions.note: Often used to classify things like products, people, or categories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué género de música te gusta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What kind of music do you like?

definitions.note: Plural of “género.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta tienda venden muchos géneros de música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this store they sell many genres of music.

definitions.note: Plural of “género.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el formulario puedes elegir entre varios géneros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the form you can choose among several genders.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lávate las manos para no transmitir gérmenes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wash your hands so you don’t spread germs.

definitions.note: An exclamation used to show a short laugh, surprise, or triumph (often written with exclamation marks).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Ha! Ya lo sabía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ha! I knew it.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary before a past participle to form the present perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María ha terminado su tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María has finished her homework.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form compound tenses
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de haber terminado la tarea, salimos a caminar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After having finished the homework, we went out for a walk.

definitions.note: Very common as an auxiliary with a past participle (e.g., "he comido" = "I have eaten"). Also used impersonally as "hay" meaning "there is/there are."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene que haber una solución.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There has to be a solution.

definitions.native: to have her, to have it
definitions.note: Infinitive of the auxiliary verb “haber” with the direct object pronoun “la” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me alegro de haberla visto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m glad to have seen her.

definitions.note: Haber + the indirect object pronoun “le” (“to him/her/you [formal]”). Used in perfect constructions (often after another verb, e.g., “siento haberle dicho…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento haberle dicho eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sorry to have told you that.

definitions.note: Used with the auxiliary verb "haber" plus the direct object pronoun "lo" (“it”). Often appears before a past participle (e.g., "haberlo hecho" = “to have done it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debo haberlo hecho antes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must have done it before.

definitions.note: This is the auxiliary "haber" with the object/reflexive pronoun "me" attached ("me / myself"), used before a past participle (e.g., "haberme ayudado" = "to have helped me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por haberme ayudado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for having helped me.

definitions.note: Auxiliary verb form meaning “to have” with the object pronoun “nos” attached (“us”). Used with a past participle (e.g., “habernos visto” = “to have seen us” / “having seen us”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gracias por habernos ayudado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for having helped us / Thanks for helping us.

definitions.note: Infinitive of the auxiliary verb "haber" with the attached object pronoun "os" (= you all). Often used in the perfect infinitive, e.g. "haberos ayudado" = "to have helped you (all)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero haberos ayudado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope to have helped you (all).

definitions.note: Reflexive form of the auxiliary “haber”, used with infinitives to form a perfect infinitive (e.g., “haberse + participle”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lamento haberse perdido la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sorry to have missed the meeting.

definitions.note: Combination of the auxiliary verb "haber" + the object pronoun "te" (you). It’s used with an infinitive or a past participle, depending on the construction.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento haberte llamado tan tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sorry to have called you so late.

definitions.note: Past participle of “haber”, used in perfect tenses; often in “ha habido” = “there has been”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha habido muchos cambios este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There have been many changes this year.

definitions.note: Used to form the gerund/perfect constructions (e.g., "habiendo + past participle").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habiendo terminado el trabajo, nos fuimos a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having finished the work, we went home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene una gran habilidad para aprender idiomas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She has a great ability to learn languages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas habilidades de comunicación para este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need communication skills for this job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El hotel tiene muchas habitaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hotel has many rooms.

definitions.note: Often used for a bedroom in a home or a room in a hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi habitación es pequeña pero cómoda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My room is small but comfortable.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los habitantes de la ciudad quieren más parques.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The inhabitants of the city want more parks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mi lugar habitual para estudiar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s my usual place to study.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habitualmente voy al gimnasio por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I usually go to the gym in the morning.

definitions.note: Often refers to the act or manner of speaking (e.g., someone’s way of talking) as well as a speech or spoken language in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su habla es muy clara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her way of speaking is very clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella habla español con su abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks Spanish with her grandmother.

definitions.note: affirmative tú command
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habla más despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak more slowly, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted). Often describes an ongoing past action or a habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegaste, yo hablaba por teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you arrived, I was talking on the phone.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (they/you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegué, ellos hablaban de sus planes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, they were talking about their plans.

definitions.native: you were talking, you used to talk
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando eras niño, hablabas mucho en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you were a kid, you used to talk a lot in class.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (Spain); affirmative command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablad más despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak more slowly, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El español hablado en México tiene muchas expresiones propias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Spanish spoken in Mexico has many expressions of its own.

definitions.note: Past participle of "hablar"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He hablado con ella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have spoken with her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy hablador y siempre tiene una historia que contar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very talkative and always has a story to tell.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/as) form of "hablar". It can also be used for "we spoke" in the simple past, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablamos español en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We speak Spanish at home.

definitions.note: Third-person plural ("they") present tense of "hablar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos hablan español en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They speak Spanish at home.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "hablar"; used with "estar" to talk about what’s happening right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy hablando con mi profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am talking with my teacher.

definitions.note: Usually refers to people who speak a particular language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos hablantes de español en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Spanish speakers in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hablar con ella mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to talk with her tomorrow.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “hablar”; often used after expressions like “querer que…”, “pedir que…”, or in conditional-style sentences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que hablara más despacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted him to speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used in “si…” (if…) sentences and other hypothetical/uncertain contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si hablaras más despacio, te entendería mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you spoke more slowly, I would understand you better.

definitions.native: we will talk, we will speak
definitions.note: Simple future (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hablaremos con el profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will talk with the teacher after class.

definitions.native: to talk to him/her, to talk to you (formal)
definitions.note: "le" is an indirect object pronoun meaning "to him," "to her," or "to you" (formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a hablarle mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to talk to him/her tomorrow.

definitions.native: to talk to them, to speak to them
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “les” (“to them” / “to you all” in some regions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hablarles mañana después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to talk to them tomorrow after class.

definitions.native: to talk about it, to speak it
definitions.note: Infinitive form with the direct object pronoun “lo” attached (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hablarlo contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to talk about it with you.

definitions.native: talk to me, speak to me
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “me” (= to/with me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes hablarme mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you talk to me tomorrow?

definitions.native: to talk to us, to speak to us
definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached indirect object pronoun “nos” (“to us”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes hablarnos después de la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can talk to us after the meeting.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer hablaron con el profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they spoke with the teacher after class.

definitions.native: to talk to you, to speak to you
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “te” (“to you,” informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito hablarte un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to talk to you for a moment.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future tense (he/she/it will speak).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hablará con el médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he will talk with the doctor.

definitions.native: they will talk, they will speak
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hablarán con el profesor sobre el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will talk with the teacher about the exam.

definitions.native: you will speak, you will talk
definitions.note: Future tense (informal singular “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hablarás con el profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will talk with the teacher after class.

definitions.native: I will speak, I will talk
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana hablaré con mi profesora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will talk with my teacher.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "hablar" (used for hypotheticals, polite requests, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo hablaría con el profesor si tuviera tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would talk to the teacher if I had time.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablas muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You speak very fast.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “hablar”; often used in conditional or hypothetical sentences (can sound more formal/literary than “hablara”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si él hablase más despacio, lo entendería mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he spoke more slowly, I would understand him better.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular “you” (tú).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday you spoke with your teacher after class.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) of “hablar”; also used as the formal (usted) command “speak/talk” and after “que” (e.g., “que hable”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que hable con el profesor hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you speak with the teacher today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 1st person plural; often used to make a suggestion (“let’s …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablemos de tu plan para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s talk about your plan for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes) or affirmative command (ustedes) of “hablar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que hablen más despacio, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to speak more slowly, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form); often used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, “no creo que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que hables más despacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to speak more slowly.

definitions.note: Present tense, first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablo español en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I speak Spanish at home.

definitions.native: we were talking, we used to talk
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past): can describe an ongoing past action or a habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando éramos niños, hablábamos mucho en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we used to talk a lot in class.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), 1st person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer hablé con mi profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I spoke with my teacher after class.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer habló con su profesor después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she spoke with his/her teacher after class.

definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros/nosotras) future tense of the auxiliary verb “haber,” used to form the future perfect.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By tomorrow, we will have finished the project.

definitions.note: Impersonal future form of "haber" used to say that something exists or will happen (it doesn’t change for singular/plural).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there will be a meeting.

definitions.note: Impersonal form of "haber" used to say something exists/will exist; it stays singular even with plural nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana habrá una reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there will be a meeting.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the future perfect (e.g., "habrá terminado" = "will have finished").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para las cinco, ya habrá terminado el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By five o’clock, he/she will have finished the work.

definitions.note: Third-person plural, future (used to say something will exist or happen).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana habrán más asientos disponibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow there will be more seats available.

definitions.note: Used with a past participle to form the future perfect (e.g., "habrás comido" = "you will have eaten").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana a esta hora, ya habrás terminado el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow at this time, you will have already finished the work.

definitions.note: Future tense (yo). Used as an auxiliary with a past participle to form the future perfect.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para mañana, habré terminado el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: By tomorrow, I will have finished the work.

definitions.note: Conditional form of the auxiliary verb “haber”, used to form the conditional perfect tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habría llegado antes, pero había mucho tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have arrived earlier, but there was a lot of traffic.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "haber" used impersonally (often translated as "there would be").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si llegáramos más temprano, habría más tiempo para hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we arrived earlier, there would be more time to talk.

definitions.note: Conditional form of the auxiliary verb “haber”, used to form the conditional perfect (e.g., “habríamos + past participle”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habríamos llegado antes, pero había mucho tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would have arrived earlier, but there was a lot of traffic.

definitions.note: Conditional form used with a past participle to form the conditional perfect (e.g., “habrían comido” = “would have eaten”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habrían llegado antes, pero había mucho tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They would have arrived earlier, but there was a lot of traffic.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) conditional form, used to form the conditional perfect with a past participle (e.g., "habrías hecho").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you have come if I had told you earlier?

definitions.note: Used with the vosotros/vosotras form (informal plural “you” in Spain) as an auxiliary to form perfect tenses.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have you eaten already?

definitions.note: Infinitive of the auxiliary "haber" with the attached pronouns "me" (to me) + "lo" (it). Often used in phrases like "por habérmelo + past participle" (e.g., "por habérmelo dicho" = "for having told me").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Thanks for having told me.

definitions.note: Infinitive of the auxiliary “haber” with the attached pronouns “te” (to you) + “lo” (it). Often used in perfect infinitive structures like “haberte lo + past participle”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sorry to have told you that.

definitions.note: used with a past participle to form the past perfect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya había terminado la tarea antes de cenar.

definitions.note: impersonal; used for both singular and plural

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were many people in the park.

definitions.note: used as an auxiliary verb to form the past perfect

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had already eaten when you arrived.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary verb to form compound tenses (past perfect).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had already eaten when you arrived.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes) of the auxiliary verb "haber"; commonly used to form the past perfect (pluscuamperfecto) and in the impersonal form "había/habían" meaning "there was/were."

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we arrived, they had already finished the meeting.

definitions.note: Used as an auxiliary in the past perfect (pluscuamperfecto).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He does his homework after dinner.

definitions.note: used in expressions of time
