definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We lived in Madrid two years ago.

definitions.note: Command form (vosotros). Used in Spain; in most of Latin America, people usually use “hagan” instead.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Haced la tarea antes de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do the homework before dinner.

definitions.note: Plural affirmative command (vosotros) with the direct object pronoun "lo" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si ya tenéis tiempo, hacedlo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have time already, do it now.

definitions.note: Informal command using voseo (common in Argentina/Uruguay): hacé + lo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si querés terminar rápido, hacelo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want to finish quickly, do it now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy hacemos la tarea juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we do the homework together.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of "hacer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos hacen la tarea después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They do their homework after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hacer la tarea ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to do the homework now.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (“it” or “her”, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a hacerla mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to do it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to him, to her, or to you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hacerle una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ask him/her a question.

definitions.native: to do for them, to make for them
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “les” (“to them”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to make them dinner tonight.

definitions.native: to do it, to make it

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know how to do it.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “los” = “them” (typically masculine plural, or mixed group).

definitions.note: Includes the attached object pronoun “me” (= me). Often used before another word/phrase, e.g., “hacerme un favor” = “do me a favor.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you do me a favor?

definitions.native: to make us, to do to us

definitions.note: Reflexive use of "hacer": used for changes in state or becoming something (often with an adjective or noun).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over time, he is going to become more patient.

definitions.native: to make you, to do to you
definitions.note: Direct object pronoun + infinitive: hacer + te (“you”, informal singular). Often used with another verb, e.g., “hacerte reír” = “make you laugh.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero hacerte una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to ask you a question.

definitions.note: Present tense tú form (informal singular): “you do/make.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué haces hoy?

definitions.note: As a preposition, it means “toward(s)”. (With an accent: “hacía” is a verb form of hacer, “was doing/making”.)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked toward the station.

definitions.note: Used to indicate direction or movement toward a place, person, or goal.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Caminamos hacia la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked toward the station.

definitions.note: Used with time to mean “around/approximately.”

definitions.note: Often refers to a large country property (especially in Latin America).

definitions.native: doing, making (to/for him, her, you formal)

definitions.note: Gerund of “hacer” with the attached pronoun “te” (you, informal singular).

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of “hacer”; often used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, or “no creo que…”.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tormenta hizo hundir el barco cerca de la costa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm made the ship sink near the coast.

definitions.note: Commonly used in a figurative sense for causing serious damage (e.g., to a person, business, or plans).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La crisis puede hundir una pequeña empresa en pocos meses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A crisis can ruin a small business in just a few months.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), third person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El barco se hundió durante la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ship sank during the storm.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El huracán llegó anoche y dejó muchas calles inundadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hurricane arrived last night and left many streets flooded.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando ve a la policía, huye.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he sees the police, he runs away.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "huir" (they/you all run away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando ven a la policía, huyen rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they see the police, they run away quickly.

definitions.note: Gerund ("-ing" form) of "huir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ladrón está huyendo de la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief is fleeing from the police.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando escucharon la alarma, huyeron del edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they heard the alarm, they fled the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si hay peligro, huyo sin pensarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If there’s danger, I run away without thinking about it.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "huir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando vio a la policía, huyó rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the police, he ran away quickly.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective after a noun (e.g., “niño huérfano”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño huérfano vive con sus abuelos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The orphan boy lives with his grandparents.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del accidente, el niño quedó huérfano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the accident, the boy became an orphan.

definitions.note: Often used for a hotel guest.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El huésped pidió una habitación más tranquila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guest asked for a quieter room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los huéspedes llegaron temprano al hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guests arrived early at the hotel.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular of “huir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando vi al perro, huí rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I saw the dog, I ran away quickly.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando vio al perro, huía por la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he saw the dog, he was running away down the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: María es muy hábil con las manos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: María is very skilled with her hands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo el hábito de leer antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the habit of reading before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Plural of "hábito".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis hábitos han cambiado este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My habits have changed this year.

definitions.native: talk to him, talk to her
definitions.note: Affirmative tú command with the indirect object pronoun “le” (“to him/her/you (formal)”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Háblale a tu hermana ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Talk to your sister now.

definitions.native: talk to me, speak to me
definitions.note: Informal command (tú): "Speak to me."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Háblame cuando llegues a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Talk to me when you get home.

definitions.native: talk to us, speak to us
definitions.note: Command form (affirmative tú) meaning “talk/speak to us.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, háblanos de tu viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, talk to us about your trip.

definitions.native: talk to me, speak to me
definitions.note: Formal command (usted). Also written as “hábleme” with an accent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, hábleme más despacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please speak to me more slowly.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with a direct object pronoun: “lo” = “it” (masculine or neutral “it/that”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, hágalo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please do it now.

definitions.native: do (it) for me, make (it) for me
definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with an object pronoun: “me” = “for me/to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, hágame un favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, do me a favor.

definitions.note: Formal (ustedes) affirmative command: “do/make it” (to you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, háganlo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please do it now.

definitions.note: Ustedes command with the reflexive pronoun “se”; often used to tell a group to move aside or get out of the way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Háganse a un lado, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please move aside.

definitions.native: let it be done, do it
definitions.note: Formal command (usted) in the subjunctive, often used in instructions (e.g., recipes) or set phrases like “Hágase la luz” (“Let there be light”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hágase el pago antes del viernes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the payment be made before Friday.

definitions.native: do it for me, make it for me
definitions.note: Informal (tú) command with the pronouns “me” (for me) + “lo” (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, házmelo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please do it for me today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La hélice del avión gira muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plane’s propeller spins very fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es un héroe para mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a hero to me.

definitions.note: plural of "héroe"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los héroes salvaron a muchas personas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heroes saved many people.

definitions.note: Used for something made from a mix of two different things (e.g., species, styles, technologies).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este coche es un híbrido y consume menos gasolina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This car is a hybrid and uses less gasoline.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duele el hígado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My liver hurts.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ropa está húmeda porque llovió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The clothes are damp because it rained.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El aire está húmedo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The air is damp today.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la lluvia, los zapatos están húmedos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the rain, the shoes are damp.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an adjective meaning “Hungarian.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecino es húngaro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Hungarian.

definitions.note: Abbreviation for “inteligencia artificial”; often written in uppercase as “IA”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La IA puede ayudar a traducir textos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: AI can help translate texts.

definitions.note: Used with "a" + infinitive to talk about an intended action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iba a llamarte, pero se me olvidó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was going to call you, but I forgot.

definitions.note: Imperfect past form of "ir"; it describes an ongoing/habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo iba al trabajo en metro todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to go to work by subway every day.

definitions.note: Used with "a" + infinitive to talk about an intended or expected future in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iban a salir, pero empezó a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They were going to leave, but it started to rain.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "ir" (to go), used for past actions in progress or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos iban al parque todos los sábados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends used to go to the park every Saturday.

definitions.note: Often used with “a + infinitive” to mean “were going to …” (an intended future in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Ibas a llamarme ayer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Were you going to call me yesterday?

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú), imperfect tense of “ir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ibas al trabajo cuando empezó a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You were going to work when it started to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos un iceberg enorme desde el barco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a huge iceberg from the boat.

definitions.note: Plural command used with vosotros/vosotras (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Id a casa ahora mismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go home right now.

definitions.note: Usually refers to going (as opposed to returning). Common in the phrase “ida y vuelta” (“round trip”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El boleto incluye una ida y una vuelta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ticket includes an outbound trip and a return trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una idea para el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an idea for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este lugar es ideal para descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This place is ideal for resting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su ideal es ayudar a los demás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her ideal is to help others.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuestros ideales son la igualdad y la justicia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our ideals are equality and justice.

definitions.native: to come up with, to devise
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que idear un plan para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to come up with a plan for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchas ideas para el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many ideas for the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para obtener la tarjeta, necesito comprobar mi identidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To get the card, I need to verify my identity.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella identifica al sospechoso en la foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She identifies the suspect in the photo.

definitions.note: Often used for an ID card in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito tu identificación para registrarte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need your ID to register you.

definitions.note: Past participle of "identificar"; often used with "haber" (e.g., "he identificado") or with "ser/estar" (e.g., "está identificado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía ha identificado al sospechoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police have identified the suspect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía pudo identificar al sospechoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police were able to identify the suspect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su ideología política influye en sus decisiones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His political ideology influences his decisions.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of “idear” (he/she/it came up with).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella ideó un plan para ahorrar dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She came up with a plan to save money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aprendiendo un nuevo idioma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning a new language.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta escuela enseñan muchos idiomas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At this school they teach many languages.

definitions.note: Can be insulting when used about a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una idea idiota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an idiotic idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas idiota; piensa antes de hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be an idiot; think before you speak.

definitions.note: Insulting; use with care. Here it’s the plural form (can describe people or things).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esos comentarios son idiotas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those comments are idiotic.

definitions.note: Insult; can be offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hablen con ellos: son idiotas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t talk to them: they’re idiots.

definitions.note: Plural of “idiotez”; informal and often insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja de decir idioteces y ponte a trabajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stop saying stupid things and get to work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya he ido al mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve already gone to the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los dos dibujos son idénticos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two drawings are identical.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los dos documentos son idénticos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two documents are identical.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La iglesia del barrio es muy antigua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighborhood church is very old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En este pueblo hay muchas iglesias antiguas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this town there are many old churches.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él ignora mis mensajes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He ignores my messages.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used for ongoing past situations or background information.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ignoraba que la reunión era hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn't know that the meeting was today.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; suggests a repeated or ongoing habit in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella ignoraba mis mensajes durante días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She ignored my messages for days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me sentí ignorado en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I felt ignored in the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ignorancia puede causar muchos problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ignorance can cause many problems.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult (like “ignorant” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese comentario es ignorante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That comment is ignorant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes ignorar este problema para siempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can’t ignore this problem forever.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “I don’t know / I’m not aware.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ignoro la razón por la que llegó tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know the reason why he arrived late.

definitions.note: Used when you intentionally pay no attention to someone or something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando me habla así, lo ignoro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he talks to me like that, I ignore him.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella ignoró mi mensaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She ignored my message.

definitions.note: Command (tú), with the object pronoun “lo” (= it/him).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te molesta lo que dice, ignóralo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If what he says bothers you, ignore it.

definitions.note: Often used with "que" to mean "the same as" (e.g., "igual que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi camiseta es igual a la tuya.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My T-shirt is the same as yours.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it’s often used to mean “equally / the same (way)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los dos corren igual de rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They both run equally fast.

definitions.note: Common in conversation to mean “anyway / regardless”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo tiempo, pero igual voy a ir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have time, but I’m going to go anyway.

definitions.note: Used as a noun, often in phrases like “un igual” or “mi igual.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es mi igual en experiencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is my equal in experience.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Luchamos por la igualdad de oportunidades para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We fight for equal opportunities for everyone.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed gender); can also be used with feminine plural nouns depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los dos exámenes son iguales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The two exams are the same.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “igual”; often used informally for emphasis (“exactly”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu dibujo quedó igualito al mío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your drawing turned out exactly the same as mine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me gusta el café; igualmente lo tomo por las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t like coffee; I still drink it in the mornings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ilegal conducir sin licencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It is illegal to drive without a license.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esos productos son ilegales en este país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those products are illegal in this country.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La firma en el contrato es ilegible.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The signature on the contract is illegible.

definitions.note: Often used with the verb "salir" (to come out) or "quedar" (to remain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Afortunadamente, todos salieron ilesos del accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fortunately, everyone came out of the accident unharmed.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (also used for usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luna ilumina el camino por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The moon lights up the path at night.

definitions.native: was lighting, used to light, was illuminating
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past), describing an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lámpara iluminaba la habitación toda la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lamp was lighting the room all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La iluminación de esta habitación es muy buena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lighting in this room is very good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La calle está iluminada por las farolas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The street is lit by the streetlights.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lámpara puede iluminar toda la habitación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lamp can light up the whole room.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/it lit up/illuminated.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La luna iluminó el camino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The moon lit up the path.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero hacerme ilusiones, pero creo que todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to get my hopes up, but I think everything is going to turn out well.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una ilusión pensar que todo sería tan fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an illusion to think that everything would be so easy.

definitions.note: Often used for a positive feeling of anticipation (e.g., about a plan or event).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo mucha ilusión por el viaje de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m very excited about tomorrow’s trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro tiene muchas ilustraciones a color.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book has many color illustrations.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "ilustrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ejemplo ilustró la idea principal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The example illustrated the main idea.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta imagen es muy clara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This image is very clear.

definitions.note: Often used as an informal command (tú), like “imagine!” or “just imagine.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imagina cómo sería vivir en otro país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imagine what it would be like to live in another country.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for ongoing, habitual, or background actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, imaginaba que podía volar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I imagined that I could fly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La imaginación es importante para contar buenas historias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imagination is important for telling good stories.

definitions.note: past participle of “imaginar”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nunca había imaginado una ciudad tan grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had never imagined a city so big.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imaginamos un mundo mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We imagine a better world.

definitions.note: Present tense, third-person plural (they/you all imagine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos imaginan una vida mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They imagine a better life.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ando form), often used to express an action in progress (e.g., with “estar”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy imaginando cómo será tu nueva casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m imagining what your new house will be like.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta imaginar cómo será el futuro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to imagine what the future will be like.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La línea imaginaria divide el mapa en dos partes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The imaginary line divides the map into two parts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese amigo imaginario me ayudaba cuando era niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That imaginary friend helped me when I was a child.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los personajes imaginarios pueden ser muy divertidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imaginary characters can be very fun.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo imaginarlo sin ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't imagine it without you.

definitions.note: Object pronoun “te” = “you” (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedo imaginarte viviendo en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can imagine you living in Madrid.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Te imaginas vivir en otro país?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you imagine living in another country?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imagine que mañana no llueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imagine that it doesn’t rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command) form of "imaginar" for "ustedes".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imaginen que mañana no hay clases.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imagine that there are no classes tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imagino que mañana va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I imagine it's going to rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imaginé que ibas a venir hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I imagined that you were going to come today.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). Often used like “imagine!” or “just imagine!”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imagínate vivir en una isla desierta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imagine living on a deserted island.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command with object pronouns attached: te + lo.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Imagínatelo: mañana ya vivimos en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Imagine it: tomorrow we’ll already be living at the beach.

definitions.note: Plural of "imán".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los imanes se pegan a la nevera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The magnets stick to the fridge.

definitions.note: Often an insult; can be offensive.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) in the future tense of “ir”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will go to the doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana irán al museo con su clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will go to the museum with their class.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) simple future of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana irás al médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will go to the doctor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Iré a verte mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will go see you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Simple future tense (yo) of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana iré al trabajo temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will go to work early.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (used for hypotheticals, polite requests, or reported speech).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo iría contigo, pero tengo que trabajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would go with you, but I have to work.

definitions.note: Conditional tense ("would").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no lloviera, iríamos al parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it didn’t rain, we would go to the park.

definitions.note: Conditional tense, third person plural (they/you all would go).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuvieran más tiempo, irían al museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they had more time, they would go to the museum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es irónico que siempre llegue tarde al trabajo, pero odie esperar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s ironic that he always arrives late to work, but hates waiting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en una isla pequeña.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Islam is one of the most widely practiced religions in the world.

definitions.note: plural of "isla"

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The islands are very beautiful.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesora es italiana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Italian.

definitions.note: Often used for nationality or language; for the language, Spanish also uses “italiano” as a noun (el italiano).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesor es italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Italian.

definitions.note: Usually written with a lowercase letter in Spanish when referring to the language.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aprendiendo italiano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m learning Italian.

definitions.note: Can refer to a man; for a woman, use "italiana".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El italiano vive en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Italian man lives in Madrid.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form. Can also refer to a group of men or a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis vecinos son italianos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are Italian.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos italianos en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many Italians in this city.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “a la izquierda” = “to/on the left.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tienda está a la izquierda del banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store is to the left of the bank.

definitions.note: Often used with the article: a la izquierda = on the left.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tienda está a la izquierda del banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The store is to the left of the bank.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Gira a la izquierda en el semáforo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn left at the traffic light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi brazo izquierdo está cansado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My left arm is tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos un jabalí cruzar la carretera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a wild boar cross the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el bosque vimos jabalíes cerca del río.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the forest we saw wild boars near the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito jabón para lavarme las manos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need soap to wash my hands.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él jacta de sus logros en cada reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He boasts about his achievements at every meeting.

definitions.note: Gerund; used to describe someone doing the action right now (like “-ing” in English).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de correr, llegó a casa jadeando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After running, he got home panting.

definitions.note: Often means “(he/she) pulls” in the present tense; it can also be the formal command “Pull!” (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él jala la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He pulls the door.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para el desayuno, comí pan con jalea de fresa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast, I ate bread with strawberry jelly.

definitions.note: Often refers to a noisy situation or disturbance; in Spain it can also mean lively excitement/party atmosphere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se armó un jaleo en la calle por el accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a commotion in the street because of the accident.

definitions.note: More emphatic than "nunca" (often used for strong statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jamás haría algo así.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would never do something like that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para el desayuno, comí pan con jamón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast, I ate bread with ham.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesora es japonesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Japanese.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis vecinas son japonesas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are Japanese.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis vecinos son japoneses.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are Japanese.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; it can refer to a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los japoneses celebran el Año Nuevo con su familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Japanese people celebrate New Year with their family.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it agrees in gender and number with the noun it describes (e.g., japonés/japonesa/japoneses/japonesas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me encanta la comida japonesa, pero mi profesor es japonés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love Japanese food, but my teacher is Japanese.

definitions.note: Also used as an adjective meaning “Japanese” (e.g., comida japonesa).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El japonés vive en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Japanese man lives in Madrid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estudio japonés en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I study Japanese at the university.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gardening is my favorite hobby.

definitions.note: Plural of “jardín”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos jardines en esta ciudad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos un jardín pequeño detrás de la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a small garden behind the house.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put flowers in the vase on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el jazz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like jazz.

definitions.note: In Spanish, it’s usually used in the plural (los jeans).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some new jeans.

definitions.note: Often used as a masculine plural noun: «los jeans» (also «los vaqueros» in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me compré unos jeans nuevos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought some new jeans.

definitions.note: Feminine form; used for a woman who is the boss or manager.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi jefa llega a las ocho todos los días.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi jefe es muy amable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss is very kind.

definitions.note: Plural of “jefe”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los jefes están en una reunión ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bosses are in a meeting now.

definitions.note: In Spain, “jersey” commonly means a knitted sweater (not necessarily a sports jersey).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hace frío, así que me pongo un jersey.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold, so I’m putting on a sweater.

definitions.note: Often used for a sports top (e.g., soccer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré un jersey del Barcelona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a Barcelona jersey.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viajamos en jet privado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We traveled on a private jet.

definitions.note: Usually refers to someone who rides a horse (a horse rider).

definitions.note: Plural of "jinete".

definitions.note: Very informal and often vulgar/strong language; can be used as an insult or to express annoyance.

definitions.note: Vulgar/slang form of "joder"; often used in expressions like "No jodas" meaning "Don’t mess around/Don’t kid."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No jodas con eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t mess with that.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No lo jode todo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t f*ck everything up now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si perdemos este trabajo, estamos jodidas.

definitions.note: Vulgar/strong slang; commonly used to say a situation is very bad or difficult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si perdemos este trabajo, estamos jodidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we lose this job, we're screwed.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar (strong profanity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He jodido el ordenador.

definitions.note: Very informal and vulgar (strong language).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no llegamos a tiempo, estamos jodidos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están jodiendo en la habitación de al lado.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They messed everything up in five minutes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El plan se jodió en el último minuto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plan got screwed up at the last minute.

definitions.note: Very vulgar/explicit; often used to insult or to say you’re messing something up.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no me explicas bien, lo jodo todo.

definitions.note: Written laugh; often used to show a mocking or amused tone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jojo, qué gracioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ha ha, how funny.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi jornada empieza a las ocho y termina a las cinco.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The camel has a big hump.

definitions.note: Can be insulting when used to refer to a person; use with care.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el cuento, el jorobado vive cerca de la catedral.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es joven.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is young.

definitions.note: Can refer to a young person of any gender; as a noun it often means a teenager or young adult.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El joven estudia en la universidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The young man studies at the university.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “joven”; often suggests someone is quite young and can sound affectionate or slightly patronizing depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La jovencita está esperando a su mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The young girl is waiting for her mom.

definitions.note: Often a diminutive of “joven,” and can sound affectionate or slightly patronizing depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un jovencito me ayudó a llevar las bolsas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A young man helped me carry the bags.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa joya es de oro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That piece of jewelry is made of gold.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardé mis joyas en una caja fuerte.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is going to retire next year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es probable que la empresa jubile a Pedro este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s likely that the company will retire Pedro this year.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): he/she/you (formal) retired.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi padre se jubiló el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father retired last year.

definitions.note: In standard Spanish, this word is usually spelled with an accent: “judío”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecino es judio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Jewish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy vamos a comer judías con patatas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we’re going to eat green beans with potatoes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Añade judías a la sopa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Add beans to the soup, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las mujeres judías celebran Janucá con sus familias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Jewish women celebrate Hanukkah with their families.

definitions.note: Can also be used as a noun meaning “Jew” (male), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecino es judío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor is Jewish.

definitions.note: Noun for a male Jewish person; feminine is "judía".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él es judío y celebra Janucá con su familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Jewish and celebrates Hanukkah with his family.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta ciudad viven muchos judíos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many Jews live in this city.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "jugar" (for "he/she/you (formal) plays").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana juega al tenis los sábados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister plays tennis on Saturdays.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “jugar” (used for “they” or “you all” in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños juegan en el parque después de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids play in the park after school.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Juegas al fútbol los sábados?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you play soccer on Saturdays?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este juego es muy divertido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This game is very fun.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "juego de llaves" (set of keys) or "juego de sábanas" (set of sheets).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré un juego de sábanas nuevas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a new set of sheets.

definitions.note: Present tense, 1st person singular (yo) of "jugar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo juego al fútbol los sábados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play soccer on Saturdays.

definitions.note: Plural of “juego”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los juegos empiezan a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The games start at six.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) or formal affirmative command (usted) of «jugar».

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you play with us tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal commands) for ustedes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que jueguen en el parque después de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to play in the park after school.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "jugar" (used after expressions like "quiero que", "espero que", etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que juegues con nosotros mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you play with us tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often suggests a lively night out (sometimes with drinking).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoche tuvimos una juerga con mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night we had a party with my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jueves tengo una reunión.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge listened to the witnesses before making a decision.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted): used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, jugaba al fútbol todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I played soccer every day.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all in Spain). Used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando eran niños, jugaban en el parque todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When they were kids, they played in the park every day.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That play changed the game.

definitions.note: Past participle of "jugar"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es jugador del equipo de fútbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a player on the soccer team.

definitions.note: plural of "jugador"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los jugadores entrenan todos los días.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/nosotras).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los sábados jugamos al fútbol en el parque.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are playing in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My kids like to play soccer after school.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural (they).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer jugaron al fútbol en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday they played soccer in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana jugará al fútbol con sus amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will play soccer with his/her friends.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana jugarán al fútbol en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will play soccer in the park.

definitions.note: Often used as “(it) hurts” (3rd person singular). Not to be confused with the noun “lástima” (with an accent), meaning “pity/shame.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to hurt myself playing soccer.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to hurt you.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm studying Latin at the university.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have washed the car today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lavadora está llena de ropa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The washing machine is full of clothes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sink is next to the mirror.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "lavar" (they/you all wash).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos lavan los platos después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wash the dishes after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to the laundromat to wash the clothes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a lavarlo después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to wash it after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a lavarme las manos antes de comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to wash my hands before eating.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que lavarnos las manos antes de comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to wash our hands before eating.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the clothes in the washing machine and turned it on.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana lavaré la ropa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will wash the clothes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wash the dishes after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are loyal.
