definitions.native: to get up, to stand up
definitions.note: Reflexive form with "me" (myself). Often used for getting out of bed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que levantarme temprano mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get up early tomorrow.

definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning “to get ourselves up” (we).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que levantarnos temprano mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to get up early tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se levantaron temprano para ir al aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They got up early to go to the airport.

definitions.native: to get up; to stand up
definitions.note: Reflexive verb (uses reflexive pronouns: me/te/se/nos/os/se). In the infinitive, it appears as “levantarse.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que levantarme temprano, pero hoy me cuesta levantarse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get up early, but today it’s hard to get up.

definitions.native: to get up, to stand up
definitions.note: Reflexive form with the object pronoun "te" ("yourself"). Often used for getting out of bed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito levantarte temprano mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need you to get up early tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular future (he/she/it will, you-formal will).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella levantará la caja con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will lift the box carefully.

definitions.native: I will lift, I will raise
definitions.note: Future tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Levantaré la caja con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will lift the box carefully.

definitions.note: Future tense (yo). Often used reflexively: «me levantaré».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana levantaré temprano para ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will get up early to go to work.

definitions.native: you lift, you raise, you pick up
definitions.note: Present tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué no levantas la caja?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you lift the box?

definitions.native: you got up, you lifted, you raised
definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te levantaste temprano para ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You got up early to go to work.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted) or in the present subjunctive of “levantar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Levante la mano, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Raise your hand, please.

definitions.note: Often used as a command to more than one person (or formal “you”), meaning “(you all) stand up/get up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Niños, levanten la mano si tienen una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Kids, raise your hand if you have a question.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "levantar"; often used after expressions like "quiero que" or "espero que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que levantes la mano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to raise your hand.

definitions.note: Affirmative command (tú) of "levantar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Levantes las cajas con cuidado!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lift the boxes carefully!

definitions.native: I get up, I lift, I raise
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me levanto a las siete todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I get up at seven every day.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun “me” (me levanté) to mean “got up.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Levanté la caja con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I lifted the box carefully.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), third-person singular: “he/she/it got up” or “you (formal) got up,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se levantó temprano para ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He got up early to go to work.

definitions.note: Often used for mild intensity (e.g., pain, symptoms, damage).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un dolor leve en la espalda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a slight pain in my back.

definitions.note: Affirmative informal command (tú) with a reflexive pronoun (“-te”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Levántate ahora mismo!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get up right now!

definitions.note: Command (ustedes). It’s a reflexive form: “stand up / get up (yourselves).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, levántense y formen una fila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stand up and form a line.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). Often used with "de" (e.g., "Levántese de la silla").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señor, por favor, levántese.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, please stand up.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta ley protege a los trabajadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This law protects workers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa leyenda cuenta la historia de un dragón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That legend tells the story of a dragon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En este pueblo hay muchas leyendas sobre el castillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this town there are many legends about the castle.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "leer"; used with "estar" to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy leyendo un libro interesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am reading an interesting book.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted form) of "leer"; often used after "si" (if) or to express wishes/doubt about a past or hypothetical situation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo leyera más, aprendería más español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I read more, I would learn more Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las leyes cambian con el tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Laws change over time.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular: “he/she/you (formal) read.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella leyó el libro en una semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She read the book in a week.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of “leer” for “yo” (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer leí un libro muy interesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I read a very interesting book.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegaste, yo leía en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you arrived, I was reading on the sofa.

definitions.note: Past participle of "leer"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect (he leído = I have read).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He leído ese libro dos veces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have read that book twice.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Leíste el libro que te presté?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you read the book I lent you?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos comprar leña para la chimenea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to buy firewood for the fireplace.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El leñador cortó un árbol en el bosque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lumberjack cut down a tree in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El león duerme bajo el árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lion sleeps under the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gobierno libera a los prisioneros.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government frees the prisoners.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La liberación de los rehenes fue ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The release of the hostages was yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "liberar"; often used with "estar" or "ser" (e.g., "está liberado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pájaro fue liberado después de la revisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bird was released after the checkup.

definitions.note: Past participle plural; often used with "ser/estar" or in the passive voice.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los rehenes fueron liberados ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hostages were freed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía va a liberar a los rehenes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police are going to free the hostages.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los bomberos liberaron al perro atrapado en el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The firefighters freed the dog trapped in the car.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted) or formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que libere a los rehenes pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he releases the hostages soon.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command) form of “liberar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que liberen a los rehenes pronto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they free the hostages soon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La libertad es un derecho fundamental.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Freedom is a fundamental right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En muchos países, la gente lucha por sus libertades.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In many countries, people fight for their freedoms.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular: “he/she/it freed/released.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía lo liberó después de la investigación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police released him after the investigation.

definitions.note: Can mean the unit of weight or the British currency (often specified as “libra esterlina”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré dos libras de manzanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two pounds of apples.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" to mean "we free (someone) from" something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te libramos de ese problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We free you from that problem.

definitions.native: to free, to get rid of
definitions.note: Often used with “de” (to free someone from something). Also commonly used reflexively: “librarse de” = to get rid of / to avoid.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero librar a mi hermano de esta deuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to free my brother from this debt.

definitions.native: to free myself, to get rid of (me)
definitions.note: Reflexive form: "me" = myself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero librarme de esta preocupación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to free myself from this worry.

definitions.native: free us, get rid of us
definitions.note: Infinitive with an object pronoun: “to free/get rid of us.” Often appears after another verb (e.g., querer, poder) or after a preposition (e.g., para).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos librarnos de este problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to get rid of this problem.

definitions.native: to get rid of; to free oneself; to escape
definitions.note: Reflexive verb. Commonly used with “de” (librarse de algo/alguien) meaning “to get rid of” or “to be free from.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero librarse de este problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to get rid of this problem.

definitions.note: Plural of "libra"; can refer to the unit of weight (lb) or a pound of currency (e.g., British pounds), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Manzanas: dos libras, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Apples: two pounds, please.

definitions.note: Often means “available” (not busy) or “vacant” (not occupied), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Estás libre esta tarde?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you free this afternoon?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes hablar libremente aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can speak freely here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay una librería cerca de mi casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s a bookstore near my house.

definitions.note: Plural form of "libre".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los estudiantes están libres hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are free today.

definitions.note: Plural form of "libre"; often used for seats, rooms, times, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Hay mesas libres?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are there any tables available?

definitions.note: Often refers to a small notebook or notepad used for notes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una libreta para tomar apuntes en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a notebook to take notes in class.

definitions.note: Diminutive of "libro"; often expresses small size or affection.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré dos libritos para leer en el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two little books to read on the trip.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este libro es muy interesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This book is very interesting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchos libros en mi mochila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many books in my backpack.

definitions.note: Often used with "de" ("librar de" = to free someone from something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El medicamento lo libró del dolor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The medicine got rid of his pain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una licencia para conducir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a license to drive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el licor de café después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like coffee liqueur after dinner.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it/you formal) present of "liderar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lidera el equipo con calma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She leads the team calmly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella va a liderar el equipo este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is going to lead the team this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su liderazgo ayudó al equipo a ganar el partido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His leadership helped the team win the game.

definitions.note: Often used with “con” (e.g., “lidiando con…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy lidiando con mucho estrés esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dealing with a lot of stress this week.

definitions.note: Often used with “con”: “lidiar con” = “to deal with.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que lidiar con muchos correos hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to deal with a lot of emails today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos una liebre cruzar el camino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw a hare cross the road.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos dos liebres corriendo por el campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw two hares running through the countryside.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pintor preparó el lienzo antes de empezar el retrato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The painter prepared the canvas before starting the portrait.

definitions.note: Common in parts of Latin America; in Spain, this meaning is usually expressed with “llamar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te voy a ligar más tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll call you later.

definitions.note: Common in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la fiesta, Marta intentó ligar con alguien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the party, Marta tried to hook up with someone.

definitions.note: Often used in some Latin American regions; “encender” is also common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes ligar la computadora, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you turn on the computer, please?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta maleta es ligera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This suitcase is light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy ligeramente cansado hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m slightly tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este bolso es ligero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bag is light.

definitions.note: Often used for meals that aren’t heavy or filling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero un almuerzo ligero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a light lunch.

definitions.note: Often used with verbs like "comer" or "dormir" to mean doing something in a light way (not much, not heavily).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy comí ligero porque no tenía mucha hambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I ate lightly because I wasn't very hungry.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos zapatos son ligeros y cómodos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These shoes are light and comfortable.

definitions.note: Plural of “lila” (the color).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prefiero los lilas porque son colores suaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer lilacs because they are soft colors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este acuerdo limita el número de participantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This agreement limits the number of participants.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tiempo es limitado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Time is limited.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; used for a group of men or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los recursos son limitados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Resources are limited.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En verano, me gusta beber limonada fría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer, I like to drink cold lemonade.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré limones para hacer limonada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought lemons to make lemonade.

definitions.note: Usually refers to money given to a poor person (often as charity).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le dio una limosna al hombre que pedía en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave a handout to the man who was begging on the street.

definitions.note: Can also be used as an informal command (tú): “clean!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana limpia la cocina todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister cleans the kitchen every day.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cocina está limpia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is clean.

definitions.note: Feminine form (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cocina está limpia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kitchen is clean.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegaste, yo limpiaba la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you arrived, I was cleaning the kitchen.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros): “we clean.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los sábados limpiamos la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Saturdays we clean the house.

definitions.note: Preterite past tense (nosotros): “we cleaned.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer limpiamos la cocina después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we cleaned the kitchen after dinner.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form; used with estar to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy limpiando la cocina ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m cleaning the kitchen now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito limpiar la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to clean the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used in the imperfect subjunctive in hypothetical or dependent clauses (e.g., after “si” meaning “if”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo limpiara mi cuarto, me sentiría mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I cleaned my room, I would feel better.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “te” (“yourself” / informal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas limpiarte las manos antes de comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to clean your hands before eating.

definitions.note: First-person singular future tense ("I will clean").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana limpiaré la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will clean the kitchen.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “limpio.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las habitaciones están limpias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rooms are clean.

definitions.note: Used for the present subjunctive (e.g., “que yo/él/ella limpie”) or the formal command “(usted) limpie”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que limpie la cocina hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you clean the kitchen today.

definitions.note: Used for the present subjunctive (they/you all clean) and also as a formal command for ustedes (“clean!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que limpien la cocina hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they clean the kitchen today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La limpieza de la casa me tomó toda la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cleaning the house took me all morning.

definitions.note: Verb form of "limpiar". (It can also be an adjective meaning "clean" in other contexts.)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo limpio la cocina todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I clean the kitchen every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El baño está limpio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bathroom is clean.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El baño está limpio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bathroom is clean.

definitions.note: Used mainly in set phrases like “hablar limpio” (“to speak plainly / frankly”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablemos limpio: no tengo tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's speak plainly: I don't have time.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los platos están limpios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dishes are clean.

definitions.note: simple past (preterite)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer limpié la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I cleaned the kitchen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer limpió la cocina después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday, he/she cleaned the kitchen after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos a la boda en una limusina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived at the wedding in a limousine.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú). Often used as “limítate a + infinitive” (“just stick to…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Limítate a escuchar y aprender.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Just listen and learn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero un té con limón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a tea with lemon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viene de un linaje noble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He comes from a noble lineage.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu casa es linda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your house is pretty.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las flores están lindas hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flowers are pretty today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Qué lindo es tu perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How cute your dog is.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños son muy lindos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are very cute.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco la linterna porque no hay luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for the flashlight because there’s no light.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos dos linternas para caminar de noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need two flashlights to walk at night.

definitions.note: Often used for settling debts/accounts or paying what is owed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa va a liquidar la deuda este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company is going to pay off the debt this month.

definitions.note: In some contexts, it refers to dismissing employees, often in large numbers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a liquidar a varios empleados por falta de presupuesto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to lay off several employees because of a lack of budget.

definitions.note: Plural of the currency name (e.g., Turkish lira).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambié dólares por liras en el aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I exchanged dollars for liras at the airport.

definitions.note: Plural of the musical instrument "lira".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el museo vimos liras antiguas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the museum we saw ancient lyres.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El piso está liso y resbala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floor is smooth and slippery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hice una lista de cosas para comprar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a list of things to buy.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What were you carrying in your backpack?

definitions.note: Plural informal command (vosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevad estas sillas al comedor, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take these chairs to the dining room, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He llevado a mi hermana a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have taken my sister to school.

definitions.note: Used with a gerund (-ando/-iendo) to say how long an action has been going on (e.g., "llevamos + gerundio").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevamos esperando una hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ve been waiting for an hour.

definitions.native: we carry, we wear, we take
definitions.note: Can mean “we have been (doing something)” with a time expression (e.g., “Llevamos dos horas aquí.”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevamos agua y comida para el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We carry water and food for the trip.

definitions.note: Used with a time expression + gerund to say how long someone has been doing something (e.g., “llevan dos horas esperando” = “they have been waiting for two hours”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevan dos horas esperando el autobús.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have been waiting for the bus for two hours.

definitions.native: they carry, they wear, they take
definitions.note: Present tense form used with ellos/ellas/ustedes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos llevan mochilas a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They carry backpacks to school.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "llevar"; often used with "estar" to form the progressive ("is/are ...-ing").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy llevando una chaqueta porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wearing a jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Often used for having something on you or with you (e.g., carrying a bag, taking an umbrella).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre voy a llevar mi teléfono conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m always going to carry my phone with me.

definitions.note: Used for wearing clothes or accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy voy a llevar una chaqueta porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m going to wear a jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era importante que ella llevara el pasaporte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was important that she carry the passport.

definitions.note: Past subjunctive form (used in sentences like “it was important that they…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Era importante que llevaran agua al viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was important that they carry water on the trip.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used after "si" (if) to talk about hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si llevaras el paraguas, no te mojarías.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you carried the umbrella, you wouldn’t get wet.

definitions.native: we will take, we will bring
definitions.note: Future tense (nosotros) of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana llevaremos a los niños a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will take the kids to school.

definitions.native: to take it, to carry it
definitions.note: "-la" is a direct object pronoun meaning "it" (feminine noun) or "her."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes llevarla a casa?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you take her/it home?

definitions.native: to take (something) to him/her, to bring him/her (something)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to him, to her, or to you [formal]).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a llevarle el libro a Marta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take the book to Marta.

definitions.native: to take it, to carry it, to wear it
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it/him”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a llevarlo al aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take it to the airport.

definitions.native: to take them, to carry them
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que llevarlos al aeropuerto mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take them to the airport tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used for clothing or accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero llevarlos puestos a la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to wear them to the party.

definitions.note: "-me" means "me" (object pronoun) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes llevarme a casa, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you take me home, please?

definitions.native: take us, carry us, bring us
definitions.note: This is the infinitive "llevar" with the pronoun "nos" (us) attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes llevarnos al aeropuerto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you take us to the airport?

definitions.native: they took, they carried, they wore
definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), 3rd person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevaron las cajas al coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They carried the boxes to the car.

definitions.note: Often used with “bien/mal”: “llevarse bien/mal”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para llevarse bien, es importante respetarse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: To get along, it’s important to respect each other.

definitions.native: to take (something) with you, to take away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es fácil llevarse algo por error si no prestas atención.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s easy to take something by mistake if you don’t pay attention.

definitions.native: to take you, to carry you
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "te" = "you" (informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedo llevarte al aeropuerto mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can take you to the airport tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) future tense of “llevar” (also used with “usted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella llevará el paquete a la oficina mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will take the package to the office tomorrow.

definitions.native: will take, will carry, will wear
definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) future tense of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana llevarán las cajas al almacén.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will take the boxes to the warehouse.

definitions.native: you will take, you will carry, you will wear
definitions.note: Future tense (tú form). Often used to mean ‘you will wear’ (clothes) or ‘you will take/bring’ (something with you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana llevarás tu abrigo porque hará frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will wear your coat because it will be cold.

definitions.native: I will take, I will carry
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana llevaré el libro a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will take the book to school.

definitions.note: Used for clothing or accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy hace frío; llevaré un abrigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold today; I will wear a coat.

definitions.native: would take, would carry, would wear
definitions.note: Conditional form of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo llevaría una chaqueta si hiciera frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would wear a jacket if it were cold.

definitions.native: you wear, you carry, you take
definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Llevas abrigo hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you wearing a coat today?

definitions.native: you took, you carried, you wore
definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) preterite (simple past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué no llevaste el paraguas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why didn’t you take the umbrella?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (yo) or formal command (usted) of "llevar"; it can also be the present subjunctive of "llevar" for other persons depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que lleve su chaqueta porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you wear your jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.native: let’s take, let’s bring, let’s carry
definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros); often used to make a suggestion (“let’s …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevemos agua y comida para el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s take water and food for the trip.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command) form of “llevar” for “ustedes” (and also present subjunctive for “ellos/ellas”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que lleven sus pasaportes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you bring your passports.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "llevar"; also used as the affirmative informal command when preceded by "no" (negative tú command).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que lleves tu chaqueta porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you bring your jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.note: Often used with a gerund (-ando/-iendo) to say how long something has been happening (llevar + gerund).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevo estudiando dos horas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I've been studying for two hours.

definitions.native: I carry, I wear, I take
definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of "llevar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevo una chaqueta porque hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m wearing a jacket because it’s cold.

definitions.native: we were taking, we were carrying
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (we). Often used for ongoing or habitual actions in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevábamos las maletas al coche cuando empezó a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were carrying the suitcases to the car when it started to rain.

definitions.native: you (all) carry, you (all) wear, you (all) take
definitions.note: Present tense, vosotros form (used mainly in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Lleváis paraguas o no?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you (all) carrying umbrellas or not?

definitions.native: to take it away, to take it with you
definitions.note: Pronominal form of "llevar" with attached pronouns: "se" (to oneself/for oneself) + "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo quedarme con esto; tengo que llevárselo a mi hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t keep this; I have to take it to my brother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevé el libro a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took the book to school.

definitions.note: Used for wearing clothes or accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer llevé una camisa azul.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I wore a blue shirt.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite) form meaning a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella llevó el libro a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She took the book to school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi bebé llora mucho por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My baby cries a lot at night.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, lloraba mucho por las noches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to cry a lot at night.

definitions.note: Past participle of "llorar"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He llorado mucho hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have cried a lot today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lloramos cuando vemos una película triste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We cry when we watch a sad movie.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "llorar" (they cry).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los bebés lloran cuando tienen hambre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Babies cry when they are hungry.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "llorar"; used with "estar" or to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy llorando porque extraño a mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am crying because I miss my family.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella empieza a llorar cuando ve la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She starts to cry when she watches the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si ve esa película, llorará al final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he/she watches that movie, he/she will cry at the end.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú, informal singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué lloras?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you crying?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "llorar" (yo/usted/él/ella). Often after expressions of doubt, emotion, desire, or commands.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que llore de alegría cuando lo sepa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he/she cries with joy when he/she finds out.

definitions.note: Formal command (imperative) for "usted" from "llorar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, no llore; todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t cry; everything is going to be fine.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) or negative imperative (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No llores, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t cry, please.

definitions.note: Often used to imply complaining in an annoying or childish way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está lloriqueando porque no quiere irse a dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s whining because he doesn’t want to go to sleep.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces lloro cuando veo películas tristes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I cry when I watch sad movies.

definitions.note: Commonly used as an informal command (“cry!”) in voseo regions (e.g., Argentina, Uruguay).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dale, llorá si lo necesitás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go on, cry if you need to.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lloré cuando vi la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cried when I saw the movie.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular (he/she/it/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lloró cuando vio la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She cried when she saw the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s going to rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana lloverá por la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow it will rain in the afternoon.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "llover"; it’s an impersonal verb, so it’s usually used with "it" in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Según el pronóstico, llovería por la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the forecast, it would rain in the afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ha llovido mucho hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It has rained a lot today.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "llover"; used with "estar" (e.g., "está lloviendo") or to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está lloviendo mucho hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining a lot today.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "llover"; often used after "si" (if) and in hypothetical or dependent clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lloviera mañana, cancelaríamos el picnic.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it rained tomorrow, we would cancel the picnic.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer llovió todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday it rained all day.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of "llover"; describes ongoing or habitual rain in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer por la tarde llovía y hacía frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday afternoon it was raining and it was cold.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “llover”; often used after expressions like “Espero que…”, “Ojalá…”, or “Es posible que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no llueva mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it doesn’t rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to talk about the weather; it doesn’t refer to a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy llueve mucho en la ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s raining a lot in the city today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La lluvia no para desde ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rain hasn’t stopped since yesterday.

definitions.note: Plural of "lluvia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las lluvias de esta semana causaron inundaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This week's rains caused flooding.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy está muy lluvioso y hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today it’s very rainy and it’s cold.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los días lluviosos me hacen querer quedarme en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rainy days make me want to stay at home.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with a direct object pronoun attached (-la = “her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tienes tiempo, llámala esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have time, call her tonight.

definitions.native: call him, call her, call it
definitions.note: Informal affirmative command (tú). "-le" is an indirect object pronoun (to him/her/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si necesitas ayuda, llámale ahora mismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you need help, call him/her right now.

definitions.note: Command (tú) form with a direct object pronoun (-lo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no contesta, llámalo otra vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he doesn't answer, call him again.

definitions.note: Affirmative informal (tú) command + object pronoun “me”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llámame mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Call me tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with an attached object pronoun (nos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tienes preguntas, llámanos mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have questions, call us tomorrow.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with the attached object pronoun “lo” (him/it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tiene preguntas, llámelo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have questions, call him tomorrow.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, llámeme mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please call me tomorrow morning.

definitions.note: Command form (ustedes); used to address more than one person or as a formal command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tienen preguntas, llámenme mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you have questions, call me tomorrow.

definitions.note: Affirmative command (tú): “Fill it.” The “lo” means “it” (masculine direct object) and attaches to the end of the command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llénalo con agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fill it with water, please.

definitions.note: Command (tú) form with attached object pronoun "la".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévala al médico, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take her to the doctor, please.

definitions.native: take (it) to him/her, take (it) to you (formal)
definitions.note: Command form of “llevar” with the indirect object pronoun “le” attached (“to him/her/you formal”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévale el libro a Ana, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take the book to Ana.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú): "Take it."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te gusta, llévalo contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you like it, take it with you.

definitions.note: Command (tú) + "me" (to me). Often "bring me" when the destination is where the speaker is going; "take me" when focusing on going somewhere else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévame a casa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take me home, please.

definitions.note: Command form (tú) with the object pronoun “nos” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, llévanos al hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take us to the hotel.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) with “se” (often used like “take it with you” / “go ahead and take it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévate el paraguas; va a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take the umbrella with you; it’s going to rain.

definitions.native: take it away, take it with you
definitions.note: Informal (tú) affirmative command. Includes attached pronouns: -te (“to/for you”) + -la (“it/her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no la vas a usar, llévatela a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you’re not going to use it, take it home with you.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) with the pronouns "te" (to yourself) and "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te gusta, llévatelo a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you like it, take it home with you.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with the pronouns “se” + “los” attached (meaning “take them away/with you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no los vas a usar, llévatelos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you’re not going to use them, take them.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). The ending "-lo" means "it."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévelo a la oficina, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take it to the office, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with the object pronoun "me" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, lléveme al hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take me to the hotel.

definitions.note: Command form used for ustedes (you all) or formal you (plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévenlo a casa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take it home, please.

definitions.note: Command to “you” (plural: ustedes). Used to tell a group to take/bring you somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, llévenme al hospital.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take me to the hospital.

definitions.note: Command (ustedes) with the reflexive pronoun: “take yourselves off / leave” or “take [something] with you” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si ya terminaron, llévense sus cosas y vámonos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you’re already finished, take your things with you and let’s go.

definitions.note: Formal (usted) command; often used with "se" to mean taking something with you/for yourself.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llévese este paraguas, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please take this umbrella with you.

definitions.note: Used before an adjective/adverb in sentences like “lo + adjective/adverb + que …” to emphasize degree (often translated as “how”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sabes lo cansado que estoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t know how tired I am.

definitions.note: Neuter definite article used before an adjective (or similar) to refer to an abstract idea or “the … thing/part” (e.g., lo bueno = “the good part”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo importante es descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The important thing is to rest.

definitions.note: direct object pronoun; often refers to a masculine singular noun, but it can also refer to an idea or situation
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No lo entiendo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't understand it.

definitions.note: Often used in Spanish the same way as in English, especially for a hotel or building entrance area.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos vemos en el lobby del hotel a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you in the hotel lobby at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El lobo vive en el bosque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wolf lives in the forest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el bosque viven lobos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wolves live in the forest.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana está loca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is crazy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco un restaurante local para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm looking for a local restaurant for dinner.

definitions.note: Often refers to a business location or venue (a physical space).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El restaurante cambió de local el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The restaurant changed premises last year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Miran la película en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They watch the movie at home.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "mirar"; often used with "estar" to talk about what someone is doing right now.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am watching TV.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I look at the sea from the window.

definitions.native: I will look, I will watch

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense of “mirar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué miras?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you looking at?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you watch the movie last night?

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted): “Mire …” = “Look …”. It can also be the present subjunctive form of “mirar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mire por la ventana, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look out the window, please.

definitions.note: Usually the ustedes command (imperative) of “mirar”; it can also be the present subjunctive (ustedes) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Miren la pizarra, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at the board, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú). Often used after phrases like "quiero que" or "es importante que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que mires esta foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to look at this photo.

definitions.note: Negative informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No mires el teléfono mientras conduces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't look at your phone while you're driving.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo). Often means “I look at” or “I watch.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Miro la televisión por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I watch TV at night.

definitions.note: Used in voseo (e.g., Argentina, Uruguay): informal command form for “vos”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mirá esa foto, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at that photo, please.

definitions.note: Gerund of "mirar" with the object pronoun "me" attached ("me").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estás mirándome y no dices nada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re looking at me and you’re not saying anything.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of “mirar” for “yo” (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Miré por la ventana y vi a mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I looked out the window and saw my friends.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of "mirar" (he/she/it looked; you [formal] looked).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She looked out the window and saw the rain.

definitions.note: used before plural nouns

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are under the bed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a la misa del domingo por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to Sunday morning Mass.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone feels very unhappy or is having a bad time (not just “poor”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy miserable desde que me fui de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve been miserable since I left home.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sin trabajo, vivían en condiciones miserables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without a job, they lived in miserable conditions.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Muchas familias viven en la miseria.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many families live in misery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten misericordia de mí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have mercy on me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez fue misericordioso con el acusado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge was merciful to the defendant.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ejército lanzó un misil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army launched a missile.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El país probó dos misiles esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country tested two missiles this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuestra misión es ayudar a las familias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our mission is to help families.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "mismo"; it agrees with a feminine singular noun or pronoun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella vive en la misma casa que yo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lives in the same house as I do.

definitions.note: feminine singular form of “mismo”; used to agree with a feminine singular noun or pronoun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero la misma camiseta que tú.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want the same T-shirt as you.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “mismo”. Often used for emphasis (like “the very same”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es la misma persona que vimos ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the same person we saw yesterday.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; agrees with a feminine plural noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en las mismas calles desde hace años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ve lived on the same streets for years.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form, used to emphasize identity or exact sameness (e.g., “the same ones” / “the very same”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellas mismas lo hicieron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They themselves did it.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis meaning “the very/same (one),” and also in the phrase “lo mismo” = “the same (thing).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en el mismo edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in the same building.

definitions.note: Used after a noun or pronoun for emphasis: e.g., “yo mismo” = “I myself,” “el presidente mismo” = “the president himself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo mismo lo hice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did it myself.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis ("the very same") or to mean "right now" depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella vive en el mismo edificio que yo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lives in the same building as me.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis, meaning “exact/same very one” (e.g., “ahora mismo” = “right now”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en el mismo edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in the same building.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis to mean “myself/yourself/himself/etc.” (e.g., yo mismo = myself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo el mismo problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the same problem.

definitions.native: (myself, yourself, himself, herself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves)
definitions.note: Used after a pronoun or noun for emphasis (e.g., él mismo = he himself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo mismo lo hice.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I did it myself.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos los mismos problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have the same problems.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used with masculine plural nouns or mixed groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en los mismos edificios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in the same buildings.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of “mismo”; it agrees with a masculine plural noun or refers to a group of males/mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos mismos lo dijeron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They themselves said it.

definitions.note: An emphatic form of «mismo» meaning “the very/exact same.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the very same book I lent you last week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos misterios en este caso.

definitions.note: feminine singular form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mysterious messages arrived at night.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cut the apple in half.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mito explica cómo se creó el mundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The myth explains how the world was created.

definitions.note: Often used for a famous person who is admired a lot (informal).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For many people, Messi is a football legend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En clase hablamos de la mitología griega.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In class we talked about Greek mythology.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El miércoles tengo una cita con el médico.

definitions.note: Used to show thinking, hesitation, or mild agreement; meaning depends on tone and context.

definitions.note: Used to show you are thinking, unsure, or that something tastes/smells good; meaning depends on context and tone.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hmm... I'm not sure.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mmmm… no estoy seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hmm… I’m not sure.

definitions.note: Often used in formal contexts (e.g., a motion/proposal in a meeting or parliament).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They presented a motion to change the rules.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El niño tiene mocos y necesita un pañuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The child has snot and needs a tissue.

definitions.note: Informal and usually insulting.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No le hagas caso a ese mocoso.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural (los modales).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important to have good manners at the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este coche es el modelo nuevo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos modelos son muy populares este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These models are very popular this year.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La moderación es importante cuando comes postre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Moderation is important when you eat dessert.

definitions.note: feminine form of "moderno"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ciudad tiene una arquitectura moderna.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The city has modern architecture.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré dos lámparas modernas para la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two modern lamps for the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este edificio es moderno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This building is modern.

definitions.note: plural masculine form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These buildings are modern.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is modest and he never brags about his achievements.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like your way of speaking.

definitions.note: Often used for settings or operating states (e.g., on a device).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon el teléfono en modo avión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the phone in airplane mode.

definitions.note: Plural of "modo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos modos de resolver este problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many ways to solve this problem.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo la camisa mojada por la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shirt is wet from the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las toallas están mojadas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The towels are wet.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The floor is wet.

definitions.note: masculine plural form

definitions.note: From the verb "molestar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese ruido me molesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise bothers me.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa música es muy molesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That music is very annoying.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective (past participle of "molestar"). It looks like English "molested," but it usually just means "bothered" or "annoyed."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy molestado por el ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed by the noise.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "molestar" (they bother/annoy).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me molestan los ruidos fuertes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Loud noises bother me.

definitions.note: Often used for annoying someone; it can also mean physically harassing in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdón, ¿te estoy molestando?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, am I bothering you?

definitions.note: Often used in polite questions like “¿Te molesta si…?” (“Do you mind if…?”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero molestarte, pero necesito ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to bother you, but I need help.

definitions.native: to bother him, to annoy him
definitions.note: In Spanish, molestar usually means “to bother/annoy,” not “to molest” in the sexual sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero molestarlo, pero necesito hacerle una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to bother him, but I need to ask him a question.

definitions.note: Often a false friend with English “molest,” which usually means “sexually assault” in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quieres molestarme, ¿verdad?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You don’t want to bother me, right?

definitions.note: Often means “to bother/annoy,” not necessarily the same as English “to molest” (which usually has a sexual meaning).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los vecinos me molestaron toda la noche con música alta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighbors bothered me all night with loud music.

definitions.native: to get annoyed, to get upset
definitions.note: Reflexive: means becoming annoyed/upset (often about something). Not the same as English “to molest.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero molestarse por eso; no es importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to get upset about that; it’s not important.

definitions.native: to bother you, to annoy you
definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “te” (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdón por molestarte tan tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for bothering you so late.

definitions.note: Often means “to bother/annoy.” It can also mean “to disturb” (e.g., with noise). It does not usually mean “to molest” in the English sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ruido te molestará si intentas dormir aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise will bother you if you try to sleep here.

definitions.note: Conditional tense; often used to ask politely or hypothetically.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Te molestaría cerrar la ventana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you mind closing the window?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué molestas a tu hermana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why do you bother your sister?

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tus preguntas son molestas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your questions are annoying.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted). Not the same as English “molest” (which usually means sexual abuse).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, no me moleste ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don’t bother me right now.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command) form of “molestar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, no molesten a los demás.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, don’t bother the others.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "molestar"; also negative imperative (tú): "don’t bother/annoy".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me molestes ahora, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t bother me right now, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdón por la molestia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for the bother.

definitions.note: Often used for a mild physical problem (e.g., a stomach or back discomfort).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una molestia en la espalda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have some discomfort in my back.

definitions.note: Plural of "molestia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo molestias en la garganta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have discomfort in my throat.

definitions.note: False friend: it looks like English “molest,” but in Spanish it usually means “to bother/annoy,” not sexual abuse.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No molesto a nadie; solo hago una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not bothering anyone; I’m just asking a question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese ruido es muy molesto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That noise is very annoying.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy molesto porque llegaste tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m annoyed because you arrived late.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form (used with masculine plural nouns or mixed groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los vecinos son muy molestos por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The neighbors are very annoying at night.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): first-person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdón, molesté a mis vecinos con la música anoche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I bothered my neighbors with the music last night.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past): describes a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ruido me molestó toda la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The noise bothered me all night.

definitions.note: Common in Spain; informal.

definitions.note: Very common in Spain; informal and often used to describe someone/something as adorable or very nice.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She offered me help with the homework.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I offered my help to my neighbors.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te ofrezco ayuda con la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I offer you help with the homework.

definitions.note: Often written with an accent as “ojalá”. Used to express a wish or hope.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hopefully it won’t rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to express a strong wish about the future (often followed by the subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ojalá mañana no llueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Hopefully it won’t rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My eye hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has green eyes.

definitions.note: Very common in informal speech and writing; also used in Spanish just like in English.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “See you at six?” “OK, perfect.”

definitions.note: Common informal interjection; also used in Spanish as a loanword.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Nos vemos a las seis? —Okay.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —See you at six? —Okay.

definitions.note: Informal; also commonly spelled «ok» or «okay» in Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Vienes mañana? —Okey, nos vemos a las diez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —Are you coming tomorrow? —OK, see you at ten.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a wave in the sea/ocean.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Una ola grande golpeó la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A big wave hit the beach.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las olas son muy grandes hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The waves are very big today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can smell the coffee from here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a olerlo antes de comprarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to smell it before buying it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo buen olfato para encontrar flores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a good sense of smell for finding flowers.

definitions.note: Gerund of "oler" (used for ongoing actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy oliendo las flores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am smelling the flowers.

definitions.note: Usually a cooking pot (often with a lid).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse la sopa en una olla grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the soup in a big pot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un olor extraño en la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a strange smell in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "olvidar".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always forgets his keys at home.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre olvidaba las llaves en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always used to forget the keys at home.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This number is already forgotten.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have forgotten your name.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) with the object pronoun "lo" (it).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it hurt you, forget it and move on.
