definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escribe un párrafo sobre tu familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write a paragraph about your family.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command of "pasar" with the direct object pronoun "lo" (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pásalo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pass it, please.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú): “pass/give it to me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pásame la sal, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pass me the salt, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pásate por mi casa esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come by my house this afternoon.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) with the pronoun “me” attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Páseme la sal, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pass me the salt, please.

definitions.note: Command (tú). Can also mean "stick/glue it to me" depending on context, but "hit me" is common and clear.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si quieres pelear, pégame primero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want to fight, hit me first.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command with the pronoun “te” attached; often used with “a” (pégate a…).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pégate a mí para que no te pierdas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay close to me so you don’t get lost.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); reflexive form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Péinate antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Comb your hair before you go out.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pérdida de mi teléfono fue un problema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The loss of my phone was a problem.

definitions.note: Plural of "pérdida".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa tuvo grandes pérdidas este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company had big losses this year.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “mi pésame” (“my condolences”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi pésame por tu pérdida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My condolences for your loss.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La comida estuvo pésima.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The food was terrible.

definitions.note: Stronger than "malo" (very bad).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El servicio fue pésimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The service was awful.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los pétalos de esta flor son muy suaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The petals of this flower are very soft.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). Also means “ask him/her (to)” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pídale ayuda al profesor, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask the teacher for help, please.

definitions.native: ask him, ask her, ask (to) him, ask (to) her
definitions.note: Command (tú) of “pedir” with the indirect object pronoun “le” (to him/to her).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pídele ayuda a tu profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ask your teacher for help.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me tomo una píldora con un vaso de agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take a pill with a glass of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomo dos píldoras al día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take two pills a day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los viernes por la noche jugamos al póker con unos amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On Friday nights we play poker with some friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una póliza de seguro para el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have an insurance policy for the car.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). The "-lo" means "it" (masculine object or "that").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, póngalo en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please put it on the table.

definitions.note: Formal (usted) command with the object pronoun “me” attached; often used when ordering/requesting something (e.g., food or drinks).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Póngame un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Give me a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Formal/plural command (ustedes) with the direct object pronoun “lo” = “it.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pónganlo en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put it on the table, please.

definitions.note: Command (ustedes): used to tell a group to put something on or to place themselves somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pónganse los abrigos, hace frío afuera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put on your coats; it’s cold outside.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). Often used reflexively as a polite instruction (e.g., to put on clothing).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Póngase el abrigo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put on your coat, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted), used with "de pie" to mean "stand up".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Póngase de pie, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stand up, please.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command with object pronouns (te + lo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hace frío; póntelo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s cold; put it on now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Jugamos al póquer los viernes por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We play poker on Friday nights.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pórtate bien en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Behave well at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un póster de mi banda favorita en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a poster of my favorite band on the wall.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta información es pública.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This information is public.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las escuelas públicas cierran en verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Public schools close in the summer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un lugar público, así que no hagas ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a public place, so don’t make noise.

definitions.note: As a noun, it usually refers to an audience or the public in general.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El público aplaudió al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The audience applauded at the end of the concert.

definitions.note: Often used as an invariable color adjective (same form for masculine/feminine and singular/plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el color púrpura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the color purple.

definitions.note: Used in comparisons (e.g., “más… que”, “menos… que”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi coche es más rápido que el tuyo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My car is faster than yours.

definitions.note: Used in comparisons (e.g., más/menos... que).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi casa es más grande que la tuya.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My house is bigger than yours.

definitions.note: Often used to introduce a relative clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro que compré es interesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book that I bought is interesting.

definitions.note: Used in comparisons after "más" or "menos".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es más alta que yo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is taller than I am.

definitions.note: used to refer back to a person or thing already mentioned
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La película que vimos anoche fue excelente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie that we saw last night was excellent.

definitions.note: Often omitted in natural English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vengas mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope that you come tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vaso está quebrado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is broken.

definitions.note: Often used about a business or finances (e.g., un negocio quebrado).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El negocio está quebrado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The business is bankrupt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten cuidado para no quebrar el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful not to break the glass.

definitions.note: Often used when talking about a business or company.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La empresa podría quebrar este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company could go bankrupt this year.

definitions.note: Future tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo aprietas demasiado, lo quebraré.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you squeeze it too hard, I will break it.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer quebré el vaso sin querer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I broke the glass by accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer se quebró el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday the glass broke.

definitions.note: Can refer to the Quechua language or a person from the Quechua people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella habla quechua en casa con su abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She speaks Quechua at home with her grandmother.

definitions.note: Often used to say how something is located or ends up after a change (e.g., clothing, hair, a place).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chaqueta te queda bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jacket fits you well.

definitions.native: is left, remains (as in time/quantity remaining)
definitions.note: Common in phrases like "queda" + time/amount (e.g., "Queda poco tiempo").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solo queda una semana para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There’s only one week left until the exam.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used to describe what remained/was left at that time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solo quedaba un asiento libre en el tren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Only one seat was left on the train.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or repeated past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la fiesta, quedaban en casa para descansar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the party, they stayed at home to rest.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He quedado en casa hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have stayed at home today.

definitions.note: Often used to set plans: “Quedamos a las…” = “Let’s meet at…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedamos a las seis en la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet up at six at the station.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present of "quedar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todavía quedan dos sillas libres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are still two free chairs left.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "quedar"; often used with "estar" to describe something that is in the process of remaining or being left.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se está quedando en casa esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She is staying at home tonight.

definitions.note: Affirmative command for “vosotros” (informal “you all,” mainly used in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedaos aquí y no os mováis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay here and don’t move.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes quedar aquí esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can stay here tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Solo puede quedar dos asientos disponibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Only two seats can be left available.

definitions.native: to meet (up), to arrange to meet
definitions.note: Often used as “quedar con” someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a quedar mañana a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to meet tomorrow at six.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of "quedar" (yo/él/ella/usted). Often used after "si" (if) or in more formal contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si yo quedara en casa, vería una película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I stayed at home, I would watch a movie.

definitions.note: Often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., after "si" = "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si quedaras aquí, te ayudaría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you stayed here, I would help you.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “we’ll meet up / we’ll arrange to meet,” usually with a time or place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedaremos mañana a las seis en la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll meet tomorrow at six at the station.

definitions.note: Often used to mean “to stay (somewhere)” or “to remain,” with the pronoun “me” = “myself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a quedarme en casa hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to stay at home today.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the pronoun «nos» (“us/ourselves”), often used for making plans: «Vamos a quedarnos…» = “We’re going to stay…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a quedarnos en casa esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to stay at home tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al final, quedaron en casa viendo una película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, they stayed home watching a movie.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; used for staying in a place or remaining in a particular state.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero quedarme aquí, pero mi amigo prefiere irse.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to stay here, but my friend prefers to leave.

definitions.native: to keep (something), to hold on to (something)
definitions.note: Used when you keep something instead of returning/giving it back.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes quedarte con este libro hasta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can keep this book until tomorrow.

definitions.native: to be left (without), to run out of
definitions.note: Often used with “sin” to express being left without something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me voy a quedar sin dinero si sigo gastando así, así que prefiero quedarme en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to be left without money if I keep spending like that, so I’d rather stay home.

definitions.native: to end up (in a state), to be stuck (feeling)
definitions.note: Common with adjectives: “quedarse + adj.” (e.g., sorprendido, tranquilo, en silencio).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me quedé sorprendido y no supe qué decir; después, decidí quedarme en silencio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was surprised and didn’t know what to say; afterward, I decided to stay silent.

definitions.native: to miss (a scheduled event), to fail to catch
definitions.note: Common with transport: “quedarse sin el tren / el vuelo.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llegamos tarde y nos quedamos sin el tren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We arrived late and missed the train.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “te” (“you”), meaning “for you to stay.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes quedarte aquí si quieres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can stay here if you want.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) future tense of “quedar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro quedará en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book will stay on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la fiesta, quedarán dos pizzas en la nevera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the party, two pizzas will remain in the fridge.

definitions.native: you will stay, you will remain
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te sientes cansado, quedarás en casa hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you feel tired, you will stay at home today.

definitions.note: Used with “con” to talk about meeting someone (often by arrangement).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana quedarás con tus amigos después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will meet your friends after class.

definitions.native: I will stay, I will meet up
definitions.note: Future tense of "quedar". Depending on context, it can mean staying somewhere or agreeing to meet (e.g., "quedar con alguien").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedaré en casa esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will stay at home tonight.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “quedar”. It can also mean “would be (located/situated)” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si llegamos tarde, me quedaría en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we arrive late, I would stay at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tú quedas aquí mientras yo voy a la tienda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You stay here while I go to the store.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “quedar,” used in hypothetical or uncertain situations (often with “si,” “como si,” etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si el libro quedase en la mesa, lo verías.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the book were to remain on the table, you would see it.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of "quedar" for "tú".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te quedaste en casa toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You stayed at home all afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used with "quedar (con ...)" to talk about arranging to meet.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿A qué hora quedaste con Ana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time did you meet up with Ana?

definitions.note: Often used with "quedar" meaning "to be left" (something remaining).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la fiesta, quedaste sin comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the party, you were left without food.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command meaning “stay (here/there)”; it includes the attached pronoun “te”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedate aquí conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay here with me.

definitions.note: Often used after "que" to express a wish, possibility, or requirement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que él quede aquí esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope he stays here tonight.

definitions.note: Commonly used to make a plan with someone (from "quedar" = to arrange to meet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿A qué hora quedemos mañana para estudiar?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What time should we meet tomorrow to study?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes/ellos/ellas) of "quedar"; often used after expressions like "espero que" or "para que".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que queden en casa esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they stay at home tonight.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "quedar"; often used after expressions like "Espero que..." or with negative commands ("No quedes...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que te quedes en casa hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you stay at home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me quedo en casa hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m staying at home today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me quedé en casa toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I stayed at home all afternoon.

definitions.note: Often used with "con" + person to mean you agreed on a plan (for example, a time to meet).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedé con Ana a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I arranged to meet Ana at six.

definitions.note: A “let’s …” command (nosotros imperative) with the reflexive pronoun “nos”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quedémonos aquí un rato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s stay here for a while.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of "quedar" (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se quedó en casa toda la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She stayed at home all afternoon.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of "quedar" (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al final, quedó claro que tenías razón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, it turned out clear that you were right.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse una queja en recepción porque la habitación estaba sucia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filed a complaint at the front desk because the room was dirty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano siempre se queja del calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother always complains about the heat.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or habitual action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre se quejaba del ruido en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always complained about the noise in the street.

definitions.note: Used with “se”: “se quejan” = “they complain.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos se quejan del ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They complain about the noise.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: “quejándose” = “complaining.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre estás quejando del ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You’re always complaining about the noise.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with “me” (to complain about something / to complain to someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a quejarme con el gerente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to complain to the manager.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached pronoun “os” (reflexive “you all,” informal in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Podéis quejaros si algo no os gusta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can complain if you don’t like something.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb: used as "quejarse de" (to complain about) or "quejarse" + clause.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre dice que va a quejarse del ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He always says he’s going to complain about the noise.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the pronoun “te” (informal “you”): “to complain (yourself)”. Often used after another verb (e.g., dejar de, deberías).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deberías dejar de quejarte todo el tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You should stop complaining all the time.

definitions.note: Often used with a reflexive pronoun: me quejaré (“I will complain”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si el servicio es malo, me quejaré con el gerente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the service is bad, I will complain to the manager.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos muchas quejas sobre el servicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have many complaints about the service.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿De qué te quejas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What are you complaining about?

definitions.note: Reflexive: “quejarse de” = “to complain about.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está quejándose del ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is complaining about the noise.

definitions.note: Usually used with the reflexive pronoun: quejarse (to complain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se quejó del ruido toda la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He complained about the noise all night.

definitions.note: Verb form of "quemar" (not the noun "quema").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El fuego quema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fire burns.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tostada está quemada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The toast is burned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El pan está quemado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bread is burnt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He quemado la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I burned the dinner.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; often used after a noun (e.g., "los panes quemados").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los panes están quemados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The breads are burned.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene quemaduras en los brazos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has burns on his arms.

definitions.note: Present tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las hojas se queman en el otoño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The leaves burn in the fall.

definitions.note: Gerund/progressive form (used like “burning” in “is burning”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La casa está quemando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is burning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten cuidado: puedes quemar la comida si dejas la olla en el fuego.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful: you can burn the food if you leave the pot on the heat.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) of “quemar.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quemaron las cartas en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They burned the letters in the yard.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo dejas en el sol, se quemará.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you leave it in the sun, it will burn.

definitions.note: Used with «ustedes» (formal plural) in the present subjunctive or as an affirmative command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no quemen la comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don't burn the food.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of “quemar” for “yo” (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me quemé la mano con la sartén caliente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I burned my hand on the hot pan.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sopa se quemó en la estufa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soup burned on the stove.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "caber".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que quepa todo en la mochila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope everything fits in the backpack.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 1st person plural (nosotros/nosotras) of “querer”. Often used after expressions like “es importante que…”, “quiero que…”, or to express wishes/uncertainty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que queramos aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that we want to learn Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queremos aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We want to learn Spanish.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo digo que voy a querer un café, pero ahora prefiero té; en todo caso, puedo querer un café más tarde, y siempre puedo querer otro después.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I say I'm going to want a coffee, but right now I prefer tea; in any case, I might want a coffee later, and I can always want another after that.

definitions.note: Often used to express affection (e.g., family, friends).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre voy a querer a mi familia, y también voy a querer a mis amigos en los momentos difíciles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will always love my family, and I will also love my friends in difficult times.

definitions.native: to want it, to want him
definitions.note: Infinitive + direct object pronoun “lo” (“it/him”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito quererlo para poder cuidarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to want it (to want him) in order to be able to take care of it (of him).

definitions.note: Often used for loving a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sé que es difícil, pero intento quererlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know it’s hard, but I try to love him.

definitions.native: to love you, to want you
definitions.note: "te" refers to "you" (informal, singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a quererte siempre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to love you always.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used as a warm way to address a woman (e.g., in letters: “Querida Ana,” = “Dear Ana,”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela es una persona muy querida en el barrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother is a very beloved person in the neighborhood.

definitions.note: Often used as an affectionate way to address a woman (like “dear” or “darling”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Querida, ¿cómo estuvo tu día?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear, how was your day?

definitions.note: Often used as a friendly way to address someone in letters, emails, or speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Querido amigo, gracias por tu ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear friend, thank you for your help.

definitions.note: Past participle of "querer"; used with "haber" to form perfect tenses (e.g., "he querido").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He querido llamarte, pero no he tenido tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have wanted to call you, but I haven't had time.

definitions.note: Used as a term of endearment for someone you love (often with "mi").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi querido, ¿cómo estuvo tu día?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My darling, how was your day?

definitions.note: Often used as a greeting (e.g., in letters or speeches).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Queridos amigos, gracias por venir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Dear friends, thank you for coming.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "querer"; often used with "estar" to mean "to be wanting".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy queriendo aprender español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am wanting to learn Spanish.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/you formal) future tense of "querer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella querrá hablar contigo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will want to talk to you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ellos/ellas/ustedes) future tense of “querer”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana querrán visitar el museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will want to visit the museum.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú), simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana querrás descansar después del viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will want to rest after the trip.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) future tense of "querer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana querré descansar un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will want to rest a little.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "querer"; often used to make polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Querría un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Conditional ("we" form) of "querer"; often used to make polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Querríamos una mesa para dos, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like a table for two, please.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dijeron que querrían ayudar, pero no pudieron.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They said they would want to help, but they couldn’t.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (used for polite requests or hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Querrías ayudarme con la tarea?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you want to help me with the homework?

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vosotros/vosotras) present subjunctive of “querer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que queráis venir mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you want to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (Spain); present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Queréis comer ahora o más tarde?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to eat now or later?

definitions.note: Used with vosotros/vosotras (Spain); present tense. Often used with “querer a” for people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Os quiero, pero ¿queréis venir mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love you all, but do you want to come tomorrow?

definitions.note: Common in voseo (e.g., Argentina, Uruguay) as the form for “vos”; equivalent to “quieres” with “tú”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Querés un café?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want a coffee?

definitions.note: Also often used politely to soften requests, like 'would like' in English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo quería un helado, pero la tienda estaba cerrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted an ice cream, but the shop was closed.

definitions.note: With people or animals, querer often means 'to love' rather than 'to want'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, quería mucho a mi abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I loved my grandmother very much.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past, ongoing or habitual).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando éramos niños, queríamos un perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we wanted a dog.

definitions.note: Imperfect (they/you all wanted; also used for habitual actions in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Querían comprar una casa, pero no tenían suficiente dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They wanted to buy a house, but they didn’t have enough money.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tú form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Querías ir al cine, pero estabas cansado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You wanted to go to the movies, but you were tired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el queso en el sándwich.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like cheese in the sandwich.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta tienda venden muchos quesos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sell many cheeses in this store.

definitions.note: Usually used in fixed expressions like “sacar de quicio” (to drive someone crazy / make someone lose their temper).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La puerta se salió del quicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The door came off its hinge.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo fuerzas, se quiebra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you force it, it breaks.

definitions.note: Used when a person or company cannot pay their debts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si la empresa no consigue inversión, quiebra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If the company doesn't get investment, it goes bankrupt.

definitions.note: Used for people; often appears with an accent as “quién” in questions and exclamations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chica quien llamó es mi hermana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl who called is my sister.

definitions.note: Plural form of “quién/quien”; used for multiple people, in questions or relative clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿quienes son tus amigos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who are your friends?

definitions.note: Often used in fixed expressions like «quienquiera que sea» (“whoever it is”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quienquiera puede aprender español con práctica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Whoever can learn Spanish with practice.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "querer" (used after expressions of desire, doubt, or to make polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que quiera venir mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you want to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "querer" (can mean "to love" in some contexts).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No creo que ella lo quiera de verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't think she really loves him.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive, 3rd person plural (ustedes/ellos/ellas). Often used after expressions of desire, doubt, or requests (e.g., "Espero que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que quieran venir mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they want to come tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "querer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No creo que quieras ir ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't think you want to go now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiere aprender español este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She wants to learn Spanish this year.

definitions.note: when talking about affection for a person
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela quiere mucho a sus nietos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother loves her grandchildren very much.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) form of "querer" in the present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos quieren ir al cine esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They want to go to the movies tonight.

definitions.note: used with tú
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres venir conmigo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want to come with me?

definitions.note: used with tú
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sé que me quieres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know you love me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero aprender español este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to learn Spanish this year.

definitions.note: often used for affection toward people; usually less intense than amar
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te quiero mucho, mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I love you very much, Mom.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La niña está quieta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girl is still.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las niñas están quietas en la biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are being quiet in the library.

definitions.note: Often used to tell someone (or something) to stop moving.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quédate quieto, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay still, please.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están quietos en la biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children are quiet in the library.

definitions.note: Plural of “kilo”; commonly used to talk about weight (especially kilograms).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito dos quilos de manzanas, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two kilos of apples, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo quince años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am fifteen years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo quinientos euros en el banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have five hundred euros in the bank.

definitions.note: feminine form (used with feminine nouns)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy es la quinta vez que lo intento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today is the fifth time I try it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivo en el quinto piso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I live on the fifth floor.

definitions.note: Often a small street stand where you buy newspapers, snacks, or drinks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré una revista en el quiosco de la esquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a magazine at the newsstand on the corner.

definitions.note: Used in hospitals; also called "sala de operaciones".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El paciente ya está en el quirófano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient is already in the operating room.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "querer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quise llamarte ayer, pero no tuve tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted to call you yesterday, but I didn’t have time.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite way to ask for something; it’s also the imperfect subjunctive form of “querer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quisiera un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would like a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (tú form) of "querer"; commonly used in polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quisieras venir conmigo al cine?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Would you like to come with me to the movies?

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of "querer" for "tú".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué quisiste irte tan temprano?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you want to leave so early?

definitions.note: Often used to make polite requests or suggestions; it can also mean “we wanted” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quisiéramos una mesa para dos, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We would like a table for two, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "querer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiso llamarte anoche, pero se quedó sin batería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/she wanted to call you last night, but his/her phone ran out of battery.

definitions.note: Used for someone who makes a fuss over small details or minor faults.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi jefe es muy quisquilloso con los detalles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss is very picky about details.

definitions.note: Can be the present tense form (he/she/it removes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella quita la etiqueta de la botella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She removes the label from the bottle.

definitions.note: Can be an informal command (tú): “Remove it / Take it off.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quita tu chaqueta, hace calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take off your jacket, it’s hot.

definitions.note: Past participle of "quitar"; often used like an adjective (e.g., something already removed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cartel ya está quitado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sign has already been removed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quitamos la tapa para ver qué hay dentro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We take off the lid to see what’s inside.

definitions.note: Often used with a direct object: quitan algo (they remove something / take something away).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre quitan las sillas del pasillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They always remove the chairs from the hallway.

definitions.note: Often used in the construction “quitando + noun” to mean “removing/taking away (something)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy quitando la etiqueta de la botella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am removing the label from the bottle.

definitions.native: move away, get out of the way
definitions.note: Informal plural command (vosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Quitaos de ahí, por favor!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Move away from there, please!

definitions.note: Often used for removing something from somewhere/someone, or taking something off (like clothes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a quitar el vaso de la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to remove the glass from the table.

definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” = “from him/her/you (formal)” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a quitarle el teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take the phone away from him/her.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “me” (“from me / myself”), often used for taking off clothes or accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a quitarme los zapatos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take off my shoes.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “nos” (“us”) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a quitarnos el teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to take the phone away from us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quitaron el cartel de la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They removed the sign from the wall.

definitions.native: to take off (clothes), to remove (something) from yourself
definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive: used for taking something off oneself (e.g., clothing). In conjugated form it appears as "quitar" + reflexive pronoun (me/te/se/nos/os/se), but here the example includes the exact infinitive "quitarse".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a quitarse la chaqueta porque tengo calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take off my jacket because I’m hot.

definitions.native: to get out of the way, to move aside
definitions.note: Often used as a command (more naturally: "¡Quítate!"), but this example includes the exact infinitive "quitarse".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que quitarse de ahí, por favor, que no puedo pasar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to move out of there, please, I can’t get through.

definitions.note: Includes the attached pronoun “te” (“you” informal): “to take off/remove … from you” or “to take off/remove … yourself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a quitarte el abrigo porque hace calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take off your coat because it’s hot.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué no quitas el abrigo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why don’t you take off your coat?

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué quitaste la etiqueta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you take off the label?

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted): “Quite…”. It can also be the present subjunctive form of “quitar”. Not related to English “quite”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quite la mano de ahí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take your hand away from there, please.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command: ustedes) form of "quitar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es importante que quiten los zapatos antes de entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s important that you take off your shoes before coming in.

definitions.note: Often used with «no» as a negative command to one person (tú). Not the same as English “quit.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quites el abrigo, hace frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t take off your coat; it’s cold.

definitions.note: From "quitar". Not the same as English "quit" (to stop).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me quito los zapatos en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I take off my shoes at home.

definitions.native: take it away from me, remove it from me
definitions.note: Infinitive with attached pronouns: me (from me) + lo (it).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes quitármelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't take it away from me.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form meaning “I removed / I took off.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me quité los zapatos al entrar en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took off my shoes when I came into the house.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite): “he/she/you (formal) removed/took off.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quitó la tapa de la botella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She took the cap off the bottle.

definitions.note: Often used interchangeably with “quizás.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quizá mañana llueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maybe it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quizás mañana llueva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Maybe it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: used in direct and indirect questions, and in exclamations
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quién llamó ayer por la noche?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who called last night?

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations to refer to more than one person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quiénes son tus amigos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who are your friends?

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations; has an accent to distinguish it from unaccented “que” (often meaning “that”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué quieres comer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you want to eat?

definitions.note: Used in questions and exclamations; it carries a written accent to distinguish it from que (“that/which”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué quieres comer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What do you want to eat?

definitions.note: used before a noun in questions or exclamations
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué película quieres ver esta noche?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What movie do you want to watch tonight?

definitions.note: Used to ask for repetition/clarification or to express surprise; in questions it’s written with an accent (qué).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué? No te escuché bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What? I didn’t hear you well.

definitions.note: used in questions and exclamations; written with an accent mark to distinguish it from que
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué es eso?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is that?

definitions.note: Used to introduce an indirect question (e.g., after verbs like saber, decir, preguntar).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé qué quieres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know what you want.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quédate aquí conmigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay here with me.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te gusta, quédatelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you like it, keep it.

definitions.note: Affirmative command for ustedes (you all).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quédense aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Stay here, please.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, quédese aquí un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please stay here for a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La química es mi materia favorita.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Chemistry is my favorite subject.

definitions.note: As an adjective meaning 'chemical'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este producto es químico y debe usarse con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This product is chemical and must be used with care.

definitions.note: As a noun referring to a professional who works in chemistry.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El químico analizó la muestra en el laboratorio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The chemist analyzed the sample in the laboratory.

definitions.note: As a noun meaning a chemical substance; often plural in English ('chemicals').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No mezcles este químico con otros limpiadores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t mix this chemical with other cleaners.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form of the adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos productos químicos para el laboratorio.
