definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del trabajo, me gusta relajarme en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I like to relax at home.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form (yo/él/ella/usted) of “relajar”; often used after “si” (if) or in hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si él se relajara, dormiría mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If he relaxed, he would sleep better.

definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning "to relax myself" or "to relax" (about oneself).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito relajarme después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to relax after work.

definitions.note: Includes "us" (reflexive/object pronoun): "relax ourselves / relax".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del trabajo, vamos a relajarnos en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, we’re going to relax at home.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb meaning to relax (oneself) or to become relaxed; commonly used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/se/nos/os/se).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de trabajar, necesito relajararse un rato en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After working, I need to relax for a while at home.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with "te" (you, informal): "to relax (yourself)".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas relajarte un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need to relax a bit.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del trabajo, me relajo en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I relax at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este examen fue relativamente fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This exam was relatively easy.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like “de manera relativa” (relatively) or “en términos relativos” (in relative terms).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su éxito es relativo, porque todavía tiene mucho que aprender.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His success is relative, because he still has a lot to learn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El periodista escribió un relato de lo que ocurrió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist wrote an account of what happened.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Leí varios relatos sobre el viaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I read several stories about the trip.

definitions.note: Plural of "religión".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la clase hablamos de diferentes religiones del mundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In class we talked about different religions of the world.

definitions.note: Feminine form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela es muy religiosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother is very religious.

definitions.note: Adjective (masculine singular form). Feminine: religiosa; plural: religiosos/religiosas.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo es muy religioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is very religious.

definitions.native: religious (person); religious man (member of a religious order)
definitions.note: Noun (masculine). Often used for a male member of a religious order; feminine: religiosa.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El religioso vive en el monasterio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The religious man (member of a religious order) lives in the monastery.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi familia practica una religión diferente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My family practices a different religion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el museo hay una reliquia antigua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the museum there is an ancient relic.

definitions.note: Plural form of "reliquia".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el museo hay reliquias de la época romana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the museum there are relics from the Roman era.

definitions.note: From the verb “rellenar.” In many contexts it means “fills in” (for a form) or “fills” (a container, a gap).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella rellena el formulario con sus datos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She fills in the form with her information.

definitions.native: to fill in, to fill out
definitions.note: Often used for completing forms or filling an empty space/container.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que rellenar este formulario antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to fill out this form before sending it.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) or present subjunctive form of “rellenar.” Often used for forms/documents.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, rellene este formulario con sus datos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please fill out this form with your information.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi reloj está en la mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My watch is on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la tienda venden relojes baratos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sell cheap watches in the store.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú); also reflexive: “relájate” = “relax (yourself).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Relájate, todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Relax, everything is going to be fine.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). Also used as a polite suggestion: “please relax.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, relájese y espere un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please relax and wait a moment.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Un relámpago iluminó el cielo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: A lightning flash lit up the sky.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vimos relámpagos en el cielo durante la tormenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We saw lightning flashes in the sky during the storm.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "remar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos remando hacia la orilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are rowing toward the shore.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana vamos a remar en el lago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we’re going to row on the lake.

definitions.note: Often used for medicine (including home remedies) and also for a solution to a problem.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico me recetó un remedio para la tos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed me a medicine for my cough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos remedios caseros me ayudaron con la tos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These home remedies helped me with my cough.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que tomar estos remedios dos veces al día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to take these medicines twice a day.

definitions.note: Common in Argentina and Uruguay; in Spain you’re more likely to hear “camiseta”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me compré una remera azul para el verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a blue T-shirt for the summer.

definitions.note: Often used for the person or address that sends a letter or package (on mail, shipping labels, or emails).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El remitente no escribió su dirección en el sobre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sender didn’t write their address on the envelope.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche lleva un remolque para transportar las bicicletas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is pulling a trailer to transport the bicycles.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sintió un gran remordimiento después de mentirle a su amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He felt great remorse after lying to his friend.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento remordimientos por lo que dije ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel remorse about what I said yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los remos están en el bote.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The oars are in the boat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en un pueblo remoto en las montañas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a remote town in the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él remueve la mancha con jabón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He removes the stain with soap.

definitions.note: In many contexts, especially in Spain, this means “stirs” (not “removes”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella remueve el café con una cuchara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She stirs the coffee with a spoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para mí, mudarme a otra ciudad fue un renacimiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For me, moving to another city was a rebirth.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siente rencor desde aquella discusión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He feels resentment since that argument.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La rendición del ejército fue inevitable.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army’s surrender was inevitable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ejército se ha rendido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The army has surrendered.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del trabajo, estoy rendido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After work, I’m exhausted.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos rendimos porque no podemos ganar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We give up because we can't win.

definitions.note: Often used with objects like results or profits: "rendir frutos/beneficios/resultados".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este trabajo puede rendir buenos resultados si lo haces con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This work can yield good results if you do it carefully.

definitions.note: Often used as "rendirse"; with the exact form "rendir" it can appear after verbs like "decidir" or "ordenar": "decidieron rendir las armas".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decidieron rendir las armas al ver que era imposible ganar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They decided to lay down their arms when they saw it was impossible to win.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an indirect object pronoun: "rendirme" = "to surrender/give up" + "to me" (often used as "not to give up").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No voy a rendirme ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not going to give up now.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “nos” (“us/ourselves”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor rendirnos ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better to give up now.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; used for surrendering in a conflict or giving up after effort/resistance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No voy a rendirse aunque sea difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m not going to give up even if it’s difficult.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the object pronoun "te" attached ("to give yourself up").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que rendirte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to give up.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite) of "rendir"; often used with "cuentas" (give an account) or for producing results.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rendí cuentas al jefe al final del día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I gave an account to the boss at the end of the day.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite) of "rendirse" (reflexive form).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me rendí porque ya no podía seguir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I surrendered because I couldn’t continue anymore.

definitions.note: Often used for renewing something like a passport, subscription, or contract; also for renovating a place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que renovar mi pasaporte esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to renew my passport this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pago la renta el primer día de cada mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I pay the rent on the first day of every month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su renta anual es bastante alta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His annual income is quite high.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of “rentar” (he/she/you formal rented).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano rentó un coche para el fin de semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother rented a car for the weekend.

definitions.note: Often used for resigning from a job or position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Presentó su renuncia ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She submitted his/her resignation yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella renuncia a su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She resigns from her job.

definitions.note: Often used with a form of "haber" (e.g., "ha renunciado") to mean someone has resigned.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El director ha renunciado por motivos personales.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director has resigned for personal reasons.

definitions.note: Used for having given up a right, claim, or opportunity (e.g., "ha renunciado a..."), or as an adjective (e.g., "un derecho renunciado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya ha renunciado a su derecho a reclamar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has already renounced his right to make a claim.

definitions.note: Often used with “a” (renunciar a algo) meaning “to give up/renounce something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decidió renunciar a su trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She decided to resign from his/her job.

definitions.note: Conditional form of “renunciar” (used for hypothetical situations or polite statements).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo renunciaría a mi trabajo si tuviera otra oferta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would quit my job if I had another offer.

definitions.native: would give up, would give up on
definitions.note: Often used with “a” (renunciar a algo) to mean giving something up or waiving a right.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Renunciaría a ese derecho para evitar problemas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would give up that right to avoid problems.

definitions.note: Often used with “a”: “renuncio a …” = “I give up …”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Renuncio a mi puesto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I resign from my position.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Renuncié a mi trabajo la semana pasada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I quit my job last week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Renunció a su trabajo la semana pasada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She quit his/her job last week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El reo fue trasladado a otra prisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The convict was transferred to another prison.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las reparaciones del coche costaron mucho dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car repairs cost a lot of money.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La reparación del coche fue rápida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car repair was quick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche ya está reparado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is already repaired.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ando form), often used with “estar” to mean “(is/are) fixing/repairing.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy reparando la bicicleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m fixing the bicycle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que reparar la bicicleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to repair the bicycle.

definitions.note: Common in phrases like “reparar en” (to notice, to pay attention to).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quise reparar en el detalle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t want to notice the detail.

definitions.native: to repair it, to fix it
definitions.note: Direct object pronoun "lo" = "it" (or sometimes "him").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a repararlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to fix it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present tense (él/ella/usted) of "repartir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor reparte las hojas a los estudiantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher hands out the sheets to the students.

definitions.native: they handed out, they distributed, they shared out
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third-person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Repartieron folletos en la plaza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They handed out flyers in the plaza.

definitions.native: we hand out, we distribute, we share out
definitions.note: Usually refers to distributing things (like flyers, food, cards, tasks) among people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy repartimos folletos en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we hand out flyers in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a repartir folletos en la plaza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are going to hand out flyers in the square.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "reparar" for "I".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer reparé la bicicleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I fixed the bike.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she repaired; you (formal) repaired.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mecánico reparó el coche en una hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mechanic repaired the car in an hour.

definitions.note: Often used for reviewing material (like for a test) or going over something again.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy repasando para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm reviewing for the exam.

definitions.note: Often used for reviewing notes, a lesson, or material before an exam.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a repasar mis apuntes antes del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to review my notes before the exam.

definitions.note: Feminine form of the adjective (used with feminine nouns).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tormenta fue repentina y nos sorprendió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm was sudden and surprised us.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tormenta empezó repentinamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The storm started suddenly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cambio fue repentino y nos sorprendió a todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The change was sudden and surprised us all.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La repetición de la palabra me ayudó a recordarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The repetition of the word helped me remember it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes repetir la pregunta, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you repeat the question, please?

definitions.note: "-lo" is an object pronoun meaning "it" (masculine; or a neutral "it" for an idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes repetirlo, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you repeat it, please?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo repetiré mañana en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will repeat it tomorrow in class.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), first-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Repetí la pregunta porque nadie me escuchó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I repeated the question because nobody listened to me.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted); it often describes an ongoing or habitual past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre repetía la misma pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She always repeated the same question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puse los libros en la repisa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the books on the shelf.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). Also used for a present subjunctive form (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, repita la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please repeat the question.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) form of «repetir». Often used after expressions like «no» (don’t), «quiero que» (I want you to), «es importante que» (it’s important that).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No repitas la pregunta, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t repeat the question, please.

definitions.note: Also commonly used as a command: “Repeat.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, repite la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please repeat the question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy repitiendo la pregunta porque no me escuchaste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m repeating the question because you didn’t hear me.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/it repeated” or “you (formal) repeated.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Repitió la pregunta dos veces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She repeated the question twice.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo siento, repito la pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry, I repeat the question.

definitions.note: Used when practicing lines, a speech, music, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta tarde repito mi presentación para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This afternoon I rehearse my presentation for tomorrow.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "repleto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La sala está repleta de gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The room is full of people.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” (repleto de + noun) to mean “full of.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El autobús está repleto de gente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus is full of people.

definitions.note: Often used for a news story with more detail than a short news item (e.g., on TV, radio, or in a newspaper).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vi un reportaje sobre el cambio climático en la televisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I saw a report about climate change on TV.

definitions.note: Often used for reporting information (e.g., in news, to the police, or to a company).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito reportar el problema a soporte técnico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to report the problem to technical support.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase “reportar beneficios” (“to bring/yield benefits”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este cambio puede reportar muchos beneficios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This change can bring many benefits.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito el reporte para la reunión de mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need the report for tomorrow's meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El reportero habló con los vecinos después del accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The reporter spoke with the neighbors after the accident.

definitions.note: Plural of "reporte".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los reportes indican que las ventas subieron este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The reports indicate that sales went up this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La periodista reportó los hechos desde el lugar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist reported the events from the scene.

definitions.note: Often used for letting someone/something rest or settle (for example, food, dough, or wine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja reposar la masa durante una hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let the dough rest for an hour.

definitions.note: Can be used as a formal command (usted) or as present subjunctive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Repose un momento, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rest for a moment, please.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like “en reposo” (at rest) or “guardar reposo” (to rest, often due to illness).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico me recomendó reposo por dos días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor recommended rest for two days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este gráfico representa las ventas del año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This chart represents last year's sales.

definitions.note: Used for acting or portraying a character.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la película, ella representa a una detective.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the movie, she plays a detective.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La representación de la obra empieza a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The performance of the play starts at eight.

definitions.note: third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “representar”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos representan a su país en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They represent their country at the meeting.

definitions.note: Used for a person who speaks or acts for someone else (e.g., a company or organization).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El representante de la empresa habló con los clientes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The company's representative spoke with the customers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este dibujo puede representar un árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This drawing can represent a tree.

definitions.native: to perform, to put on (a play)
definitions.note: Used especially for theater (a play) or similar performances.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a representar una obra de teatro esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to put on a play tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo represento a mi empresa en la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I represent my company at the meeting.

definitions.note: Most commonly used for failing an exam or a class.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Reprobaron el examen de matemáticas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They failed the math exam.

definitions.note: Usually used for failing an exam/class; also used for ‘disapproved’ (did not approve) in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Reprobó el examen de matemáticas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She failed the math exam.

definitions.note: Present tense, third person plural (they/you all reproduce).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los conejos se reproducen rápidamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rabbits reproduce quickly.

definitions.note: Often used for playing media (music, videos) on a device.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes reproducir la canción otra vez.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it turns out to be easy.

definitions.note: Simple past (él/ella/usted). Often used to say how something ended up being.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Al final, la solución resultó más simple de lo que pensábamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the end, the solution turned out to be simpler than we thought.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un resumen del capítulo para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a summary of the chapter for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La resurrección de Jesús es una creencia central en el cristianismo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The resurrection of Jesus is a central belief in Christianity.

definitions.note: Often used in military contexts; also used more generally as “support” or “back-up” behind the front line.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El comandante se quedó en la retaguardia para coordinar la defensa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The commander stayed in the rear to coordinate the defense.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retamos a nuestros amigos a una carrera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We challenge our friends to a race.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él retira el dinero del cajero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He withdraws the money from the ATM.

definitions.note: Used for someone who has stopped working (e.g., after a career).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo está retirado y pasa mucho tiempo con sus nietos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is retired and spends a lot of time with his grandchildren.

definitions.note: Used for a place that is quiet or far from others.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vivimos en un pueblo retirado en las montañas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live in a secluded town in the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He retirado dinero del banco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have withdrawn money from the bank.

definitions.note: Often used to say someone has stopped working (retired).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo está retirado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is retired.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, puede retirar los zapatos antes de entrar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please remove your shoes before coming in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a retirar dinero del cajero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to withdraw money from the ATM.

definitions.native: to withdraw (a proposal/candidacy), to pull back
definitions.note: Often used reflexively: "retirarse" = to leave/withdraw.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la reunión, decidió retirar su candidatura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the meeting, he decided to withdraw his candidacy.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “me” (“myself”), so it refers to the speaker leaving/withdrawing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito retirarme temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to leave early.

definitions.note: Reflexive/with pronoun “nos”: it means “for us to leave/withdraw” or “to withdraw (something) for ourselves,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos que retirarnos ya porque es tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have to leave now because it’s late.

definitions.native: they removed, they withdrew, they took away
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retiraron el coche de la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They removed the car from the street.

definitions.note: Often used to mean leaving a place or stepping away (sometimes politely); also used for withdrawing (from an activity, discussion, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a retirarse un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to step out for a moment.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an attached object pronoun: retirar + te (“yourself/you”). Often used for leaving or moving away (e.g., from a place or situation).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor retirarte ahora antes de que empiece la discusión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better to step away now before the argument starts.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted) or in the present subjunctive of "retirar". Not related to English "retire" (= stop working).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, retire la tarjeta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please remove the card.

definitions.note: Often used for withdrawing money (e.g., from an ATM).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retiro dinero del cajero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I withdraw money from the ATM.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi padre está en retiro desde el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My father has been in retirement since last year.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "retirar" (I).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retiré el dinero del cajero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I withdrew the money from the ATM.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form: “he/she/it removed” or “you (formal) removed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico retiró la venda con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor removed the bandage carefully.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) of “retar”; also used as a noun meaning “challenge,” but this entry is for the verb form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te reto a correr conmigo hasta la esquina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I challenge you to run with me to the corner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprender un nuevo idioma es un reto, pero vale la pena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Learning a new language is a challenge, but it’s worth it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El retorno a casa fue más tarde de lo esperado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The return home was later than expected.

definitions.note: Common in signs and store policies (e.g., “No se aceptan retornos”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No aceptamos retorno de productos abiertos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We don’t accept returns for opened products.

definitions.note: Plural of "reto".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tenemos muchos retos este semestre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have many challenges this semester.

definitions.note: Can mean causing something to happen later (delay) or arriving later than expected (be late), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tráfico retrasa el autobús.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Traffic delays the bus.

definitions.note: Often used for schedules or things that are behind time (e.g., trains, flights, deliveries).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren va retrasado hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train is running late today.

definitions.note: Commonly used for things like flights, deliveries, or schedules. Avoid using it to describe a person; it can be offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vuelo está retrasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The flight is delayed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El mal tiempo puede retrasar el vuelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bad weather can delay the flight.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, no se retrase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don't be late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo un retraso de veinte minutos en el tren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a twenty-minute delay on the train.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tráfico retrasó el autobús.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Traffic delayed the bus.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El retrato de mi abuela está en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandmother's portrait is in the living room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el museo hay retratos de muchos artistas famosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the museum there are portraits of many famous artists.

definitions.note: Often used as a command to a group (or to you formal plural): “(you all) back up / move back.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, retrocedan un paso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, back up one step.

definitions.note: Also used figuratively (e.g., a situation or progress goes backward).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando ve el coche, retrocede un paso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he sees the car, he steps back one step.

definitions.native: to move back, to back up, to go back
definitions.note: Often used for physical movement (people/vehicles) or for retreating in a more general sense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche tuvo que retroceder porque la calle estaba cerrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car had to back up because the street was closed.

definitions.note: Command (tú): telling one person informally to move away/withdraw.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Retírate de la puerta, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Step away from the door, please.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular (he/she/it) of “retar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lo retó a una carrera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She challenged him to a race.

definitions.note: Often used like a past participle to describe people or things that are together in one place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando llegué, el grupo ya estaba reunido en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I arrived, the group was already gathered in the room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hemos reunido toda la información.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have gathered all the information.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "reunir"; often used with "estar" to form the present continuous.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos reuniendo a todos en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are gathering everyone in the room.

definitions.note: Third person plural, simple past (pretérito).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se reunieron en el parque para hablar del proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gathered in the park to talk about the project.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/as) of "reunir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos reunimos en el parque para hablar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We meet up in the park to talk.

definitions.note: Plural of "reunión".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo tres reuniones hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have three meetings today.

definitions.note: Often used for gathering people or collecting things into one place.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a reunir a todos en la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to gather everyone in the room.

definitions.native: we will gather, we will bring together
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana reuniremos a todos los estudiantes en el aula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will gather all the students in the classroom.

definitions.native: to meet up (with someone) / to get together (with someone)
definitions.note: Infinitive with a reflexive pronoun attached ("me"): "reunirme" = "to meet (up)" with "me" as the person meeting (often used after another verb or preposition).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes reunirme con Ana mañana por la tarde?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you meet up with Ana tomorrow afternoon?

definitions.native: to meet with me (formal/explicitly "me" as the person being met)
definitions.note: Can be used when another person is asked/expected to arrange a meeting that includes you; in many contexts Spanish more commonly uses "reunirte conmigo" to mean "meet with me," but this entry keeps the exact form "reunirme" as requested.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El director quiere reunirme con el equipo antes de la presentación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director wants to have me meet with the team before the presentation.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “nos” (“us”), meaning the action is done with/for “us” (e.g., “to meet up”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a reunirnos mañana por la tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to meet up tomorrow afternoon.

definitions.note: Reflexive form; often used for people meeting (e.g., friends, a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es difícil reunirse con todos a la vez.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to meet with everyone at the same time.

definitions.note: Infinitive + "te" (informal "you" as an object). Often used when talking about arranging a meeting with someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito reunirte con mi jefe esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to set up a meeting between you and my boss this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El guía reunirá al grupo en la entrada del museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guide will gather the group at the entrance of the museum.

definitions.note: Often used with things like information, documents, money, or evidence.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella reunirá la información necesaria para el informe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will collect the necessary information for the report.

definitions.native: I will gather, I will collect
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana reuniré todos los documentos necesarios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will gather all the necessary documents.

definitions.note: Often used for bringing people together in one place (like gathering a group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El director reunió al equipo para hablar del proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The manager brought the team together to talk about the project.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo una reunión a las tres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a meeting at three.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El informe revela datos importantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report reveals important data.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La revelación de la verdad sorprendió a todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The revelation of the truth surprised everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El secreto fue revelado ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The secret was revealed yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los documentos revelan la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The documents reveal the truth.

definitions.note: Used for developing film or photos.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta tienda revelan fotos en una hora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this shop they develop photos in one hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo revelar el secreto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't reveal the secret.

definitions.note: Used for processing photographic film or photos.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a revelar las fotos esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to develop the photos this afternoon.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “he/she/you (formal) revealed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El periodista reveló la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The journalist revealed the truth.

definitions.note: Commonly used for things like balloons, tires, pipes, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El globo va a reventar si lo inflas más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon is going to pop if you blow it up more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El globo reventó de repente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The balloon burst suddenly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuvimos un reventón en la autopista y tuvimos que parar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a blowout on the highway and had to stop.

definitions.note: Common in some Latin American countries as informal slang.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoche hubo un reventón en casa de Laura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night there was a big party at Laura’s house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hizo una reverencia al final del concierto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He made a bow at the end of the concert.

definitions.note: Often used for showing respect in a formal or religious context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mostró reverencia en la iglesia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She showed reverence in the church.

definitions.note: Title used for a male member of the clergy; often used as a form of address.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El reverendo habló con la familia después de la misa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Reverend spoke with the family after Mass.

definitions.note: Often used for checking something to make sure it’s correct or OK.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella revisa el correo todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She checks her email every morning.

definitions.note: Past participle of "revisar"; often used like an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El informe ya está revisado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The report is already checked.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “revisar”; often used with “estar” to talk about an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy revisando el informe ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m reviewing the report now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a revisar mi correo antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to check my email before leaving.

definitions.native: to check it, to review it
definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito revisarlo antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to check it before sending it.

definitions.native: I will check, I will review
definitions.note: First-person singular (yo), simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revisaré el correo esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will check the email this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo revise el informe antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I reviewed the report before sending it.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive or affirmative command (ustedes) of "revisar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revisen la tarea antes de entregarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Check the homework before turning it in.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hicimos una revisión del documento antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We did a review of the document before sending it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Reviso el correo antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I check my email before leaving.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro una revista en el quiosco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy a magazine at the newsstand.

definitions.note: Plural of “revista”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compro revistas en el aeropuerto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I buy magazines at the airport.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revisé el informe antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I checked the report before sending it.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): “(he/she/you formal) checked/reviewed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La profesora revisó mi tarea ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher checked my homework yesterday.

definitions.native: to revive, to bring back to life
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los médicos lograron revivir al paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctors managed to revive the patient.

definitions.note: Often used with memories or experiences (e.g., “revivir un momento”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces logro revivir ese día en mi mente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes I manage to relive that day in my mind.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El paciente revivió después de unos minutos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient came back to life after a few minutes.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tiene una idea revolucionaria para la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a revolutionary idea for the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su idea fue revolucionario para la época.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her idea was revolutionary for the time.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La revolución cambió la historia del país.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The revolution changed the country's history.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Revolvió el café con una cuchara.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He stirred the coffee with a spoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El viento revolvió las hojas en el patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The wind messed up the leaves in the yard.

definitions.native: the opposite side, the wrong way around
definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “al revés” = “the other way around / in reverse.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo pusiste al revés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You put it in the wrong way around.

definitions.note: Often used as “un revés” meaning an unexpected bad event.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perder el trabajo fue un revés para ella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Losing her job was a setback for her.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía encontró un revólver en el coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police found a revolver in the car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El rey vive en el palacio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The king lives in the palace.

definitions.note: Plural of "rey".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los Reyes Magos traen regalos a los niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Three Wise Men bring gifts to the children.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella reza todas las noches.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She prays every night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rezamos antes de comer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We pray before eating.

definitions.note: Gerund of "rezar"; often used with "estar" to mean "to be praying."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy rezando por mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am praying for my family.

definitions.note: Often used for religious prayer; can also mean to say a prayer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas las noches voy a rezar antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every night I am going to pray before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Simple future (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana rezaré por ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will pray for you.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo) form of "rezar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cada noche rezo antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every night I pray before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "rezar" for él/ella/usted.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoche rezó antes de dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night he/she prayed before going to sleep.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of "reír".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer reí mucho con esa película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I laughed a lot at that movie.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella reía con sus amigas en el café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was laughing with her friends at the café.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (third person plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando contabas esa historia, todos reían.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When you told that story, everyone laughed.

definitions.note: Past participle of "reír" (to laugh).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nunca he reído tanto en mi vida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve never laughed so much in my life.

definitions.note: Present tense of "reír" (also used as the preterite: "we laughed").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre reímos con sus chistes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We always laugh at his jokes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me hace reír ese chiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That joke makes me laugh.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an indirect object pronoun: “me” = “(to) me” (as in “it makes me laugh”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa película siempre logra reírme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That movie always manages to make me laugh.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb; can also be used with “de” (reírse de alguien/algo) meaning “to laugh at someone/something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No pude evitar reírse durante la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I couldn't help laughing during the movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella reúne a todos en la sala para empezar la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She gathers everyone in the room to start the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi jefe se reúne con los clientes los lunes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss meets with the clients on Mondays.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “reunir” (used for “they” or “you all” in Latin America).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se reúnen en el parque todos los domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They meet in the park every Sunday.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) affirmative command; used reflexively (“meet up” / “get together”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Reúnete con nosotros en el café a las seis.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Meet up with us at the café at six.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “rico.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tía es rica y vive en una casa grande.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My aunt is rich and lives in a big house.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "rico"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las familias ricas viven en esa zona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rich families live in that area.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "rico"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las galletas están muy ricas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cookies are very tasty.

definitions.note: Masculine singular form; agrees with a masculine singular noun (e.g., hombre, país).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su padre es muy rico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His father is very rich.

definitions.note: Commonly used to talk about food and drinks; masculine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este postre está muy rico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This dessert is very delicious.

definitions.note: Often used with an article, especially in plural: “los ricos” = “the rich (people)”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El rico no quiere pagar más impuestos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rich person doesn't want to pay more taxes.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group); can also be used after a verb like "ser"/"estar" to describe people or things.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis abuelos son ricos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandparents are rich.

definitions.note: Often used for food.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos tacos están ricos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These tacos are tasty.

definitions.note: Plural form; refers to people who are rich.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los ricos a veces pagan menos impuestos que la clase media.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Rich people sometimes pay fewer taxes than the middle class.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa idea es ridícula.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That idea is ridiculous.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es ridículo pagar tanto por una botella de agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s ridiculous to pay so much for a bottle of water.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the phrase “hacer el ridículo” (“to make a fool of yourself”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hiciste el ridículo delante de todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You made a fool of yourself in front of everyone.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tus comentarios son ridículos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your comments are ridiculous.

definitions.note: Present tense form of “regar” (to water).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She waters the plants every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jinete agarró las riendas del caballo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rider grabbed the horse's reins.

definitions.note: Present participle (gerund) of "reír".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy riendo con tus chistes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am laughing at your jokes.

definitions.note: Third-person plural preterite (they/you all laughed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos rieron mucho en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They laughed a lot at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un riesgo de lluvia esta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a risk of rain this afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos riesgos en este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many risks in this job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es muy riesgoso conducir tan rápido en la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s very risky to drive so fast in the rain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El policía lleva un rifle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police officer carries a rifle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor es muy riguroso con las fechas de entrega.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher is very strict about the due dates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos un análisis riguroso antes de tomar una decisión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need a thorough analysis before making a decision.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato duerme en el rincón de la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat sleeps in the corner of the living room.

definitions.note: Often used with the reflexive pronoun: «se rinda» = “gives up / surrenders.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que ella no se rinda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope she doesn’t give up.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "rendir"; often used after expressions like "No quiero que..." or "Es importante que..."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero que te rindas ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want you to give up now.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about results (e.g., a plan or effort yields results) or about something going a long way (e.g., money).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este esfuerzo rinde buenos resultados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This effort yields good results.

definitions.note: Often used for things like investments, work, or studying that give results (e.g., “rendir frutos” = “to bear fruit”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estas inversiones rinden mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These investments yield a lot.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te rindes ahora, nunca sabrás si podías lograrlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you give up now, you’ll never know if you could have achieved it.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito) form of "rendir" meaning to produce or provide a result (e.g., money, effort, a harvest).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El negocio rindió mucho dinero este año.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The business made a lot of money this year.

definitions.note: Past tense (pretérito) form of "rendir" used as "rendirse" (to surrender).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El soldado se rindió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The soldier surrendered.

definitions.note: From "rendirse" (to surrender/give up).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me rindo; es demasiado difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I give up; it's too difficult.

definitions.note: From "rendir" meaning to yield or hand over (often used with "cuentas" or "un informe").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rindo cuentas al final del mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I submit my accounts at the end of the month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre rio cuando veo esa película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always laugh when I watch that movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La riqueza no siempre trae felicidad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wealth doesn’t always bring happiness.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las riquezas del país no se distribuyen de manera justa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The country's wealth is not distributed fairly.

definitions.note: Superlative of "rico" (delicious).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este pastel está riquísimo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This cake is really tasty.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su risa llenó toda la sala.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her laughter filled the whole room.

definitions.note: Plural of "risa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se oían risas en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You could hear laughter in the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos sentamos cerca del risco para ver el valle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sat near the cliff to see the valley.

definitions.note: Diminutive of “risa”; often used for a small or cute laugh.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Soltó una risita cuando vio el perro con sombrero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She let out a little giggle when she saw the dog wearing a hat.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ritmo de la canción es muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rhythm of the song is very fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ritual empieza al amanecer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ritual begins at dawn.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuestro equipo tiene un rival muy fuerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our team has a very strong rival.

definitions.note: Often used for hair (pelo/cabello).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiene el pelo rizado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He has curly hair.

definitions.note: Gerund form of “reírse” (to laugh). Often used with “se” in Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está riéndose de ese chiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He’s laughing at that joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duelen los riñones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My kidneys hurt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duele el riñón derecho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right kidney hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él rió cuando escuchó el chiste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He laughed when he heard the joke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él roba mi bicicleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He steals my bike.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense; often implies a repeated or ongoing action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era joven, robaba comida para sobrevivir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was young, I was stealing food to survive.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle (often used like an adjective or in the passive voice).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bicicleta fue robada anoche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bicycle was stolen last night.

definitions.note: Often used as an adjective (from the past participle of "robar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi teléfono fue robado ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My phone was stolen yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me han robado el móvil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They've stolen my phone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los cuadros robados aparecieron en el mercado negro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The stolen paintings showed up on the black market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Robamos comida porque no teníamos dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We stole food because we didn’t have money.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “robar” (they/you all steal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A veces roban bicicletas en esta calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sometimes they steal bicycles on this street.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "robar"; used with "estar" for actions in progress or as "while/by stealing."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están robando en la tienda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are stealing in the store.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alguien va a robar mi bicicleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone is going to steal my bike.

definitions.native: to steal from him, to steal from her
definitions.note: "le" means "to him" or "to her" (and can also mean "to you" formal, depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Intentaron robarle el bolso a María en el metro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tried to steal María’s purse from her on the subway.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third-person plural (“they”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Anoche robaron mi bicicleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last night they stole my bike.

definitions.native: to rob you, to steal from you
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ten cuidado; pueden robarte el teléfono.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Be careful; they can steal your phone from you.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense of “robar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si robas otra vez, llamaré a la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you steal again, I’ll call the police.

definitions.note: Simple past (tú) form of "robar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué robaste mi cartera?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you steal my wallet?

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for commands with ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no roben nada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they don't steal anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El roble del parque es muy viejo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The oak tree in the park is very old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No robo nada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t steal anything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo un robo en la tienda anoche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a robbery at the store last night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo varios robos en el barrio esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were several thefts in the neighborhood this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El robot limpia la casa todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The robot cleans the house every day.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la fábrica, los robots trabajan todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the factory, the robots work all day.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of "robar" for "yo".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I stole a bicycle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Alguien robó mi bicicleta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Someone stole my bike.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay una roca grande en el camino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a big rock on the path.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay rocas grandes en la playa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are big rocks on the beach.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the music genre in Spanish; for “rock” as a stone, Spanish commonly uses “roca”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta el rock, pero prefiero el pop.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like rock, but I prefer pop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por la mañana, el rocío cubre el césped.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the morning, dew covers the grass.

definitions.note: Used for making a movie/TV show (the period when scenes are filmed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El rodaje de la película empieza mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The filming of the movie starts tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for cars or machines when they are new (engine break-in).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Durante el rodaje del coche, no conduces muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: During the car’s break-in period, you don’t drive very fast.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "rodar"; often used with "estar" to mean "to be rolling/going around".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pelota está rodando por el suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball is rolling on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pelota empezó a rodar cuesta abajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball started to roll downhill.

definitions.note: Often used for filming a movie, video, or scene.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a rodar una escena en el centro esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to shoot a scene downtown tonight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cerca rodea el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The fence surrounds the garden.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (an ongoing or repeated action in the past).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The garden was surrounding the house.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The house is surrounded by trees.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The town is surrounded by mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El castillo está rodeado por un foso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The castle is surrounded by a moat.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We live surrounded by mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los árboles rodean la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The trees surround the house.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me straight, please.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My right knee hurts.

definitions.note: plural of "rodilla"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duelen las rodillas cuando corro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My knees hurt when I run.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La pelota rodó hasta la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ball rolled to the door.

definitions.note: Often used in formal or emphatic contexts; commonly with “rogar (a alguien) que …” or “rogar por …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te ruego que me perdones; te rogaré hasta que lo hagas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I beg you to forgive me; I will plead with you until you do.

definitions.note: Past tense (preterite), first person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rogué que me perdonaras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I begged you to forgive me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella rogó por ayuda, pero nadie respondió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She begged for help, but nobody answered.

definitions.note: feminine singular form (used with feminine nouns)
