definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The apple is red.

definitions.note: feminine plural form of "rojo"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo dos manzanas rojas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two red apples.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi coche es rojo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My car is red.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to the color red.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El rojo es mi color favorito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Red is my favorite color.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis zapatos son rojos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are red.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi rol en el proyecto es coordinar al equipo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My role in the project is to coordinate the team.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré un rollo de papel higiénico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought a roll of toilet paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La película es un romance entre dos estudiantes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is a romance between two students.

definitions.note: Usually refers to Rome or the ancient Roman civilization (can also mean “from Rome”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este puente es de origen romano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This bridge is of Roman origin.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los romanos construyeron muchas carreteras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Romans built many roads.

definitions.note: Used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “espero que…”) or as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no se rompa el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope the glass doesn’t break.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) or negative imperative (tú) of "romper".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No rompas el vaso, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t break the glass, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él rompe el vaso sin querer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He breaks the glass without meaning to.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este rompecabezas tiene mil piezas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This puzzle has a thousand pieces.

definitions.note: Present tense (they/you plural) form of "romper".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no tienen cuidado, rompen el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If they aren't careful, they break the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero romper el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to break the glass.

definitions.native: to break (oneself); to break; to get broken
definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive; used for something that breaks on its own or ends up broken (often translated as “to break” / “to get broken”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es fácil romperse si lo doblas demasiado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s easy for it to break if you bend it too much.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo fuerzas, se romperá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you force it, it will break.

definitions.note: Simple future (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si no tienes cuidado, romperé el vaso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you're not careful, I will break the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si lo tiro al suelo, se rompería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I throw it on the floor, it would break.

definitions.note: Gerund (-ing form) of "romper".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy rompiendo el hielo con una broma.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m breaking the ice with a joke.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): “they broke” / “you (plural, Spain) broke.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se les rompieron las gafas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Their glasses broke.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) informal “you” (tú).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you break my glass?

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he/she broke the glass by accident.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Rompí el vaso sin querer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I broke the glass by accident.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La cena fue muy romántica.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dinner was very romantic.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compró flores para sus citas románticas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He bought flowers for his romantic dates.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él es muy romántico con su pareja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is very romantic with his partner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prefiero el ron con cola.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer rum with cola.

definitions.note: Present participle / gerund of "roncar"; often used with "estar" to talk about something happening right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano está roncando en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is snoring on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi papá dice que a veces empieza a roncar antes de dormirse por completo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dad says that sometimes he starts to snore before fully falling asleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando duermo boca arriba, ronco mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I sleep on my back, I snore a lot.

definitions.note: Used for a voice or sound that is rough because of irritation, tiredness, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy ronco y me duele la garganta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m hoarse and my throat hurts.

definitions.note: Often used for a police/security patrol or a round someone makes to check an area.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El guardia hace una ronda cada noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The guard makes a round every night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta ronda la pago yo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This round is on me.

definitions.note: Commonly used for cats (and sometimes other animals).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato ronronea cuando lo acaricio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat purrs when I pet him.

definitions.note: Gerund ("-ing" form), often used with "estar" to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gato está ronroneando en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat is purring on the couch.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar ropa para el invierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy clothes for the winter.

definitions.note: Plural of “ropa.” In Spanish, “ropa” is usually used as an uncountable noun (like “clothing”), but the plural “ropas” can be used to mean items/sets of clothes.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put the clean clothes in the closet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta la camiseta rosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the pink T-shirt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Le regaló una rosa a su mamá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He gave his mom a rose.

definitions.note: Often used for pale/light pink; can also describe something that has turned slightly pink (e.g., skin).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the pink dress.

definitions.note: As a color adjective, it can describe things that are pink.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguid las instrucciones, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow the instructions, please.

definitions.note: Used after a time expression or number to mean consecutive (e.g., “tres días seguidos/seguidas”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He trabajado tres días seguidas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve worked three days in a row.

definitions.note: Command (vosotros form) + “me” (object pronoun). Used in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguidme, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow me, please.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase "a menudo" or "muy seguido" (especially in Latin America) to mean "often."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy al gimnasio muy seguido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I go to the gym very often.

definitions.note: Often used after a time word (e.g., “días/horas/veces seguidas”) to mean “in a row.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He trabajado tres días seguidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve worked three days in a row.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ladrón fue seguido por la policía.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was followed by the police.

definitions.note: Often used for followers on social media.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchos seguidores en Instagram.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have many followers on Instagram.

definitions.note: Used to talk about things happening one after another (often with time expressions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trabajé tres días seguidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I worked three days in a row.

definitions.note: Often used for monitoring progress or continuing attention after something (e.g., a visit, a case, a request).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos hacer un seguimiento del proyecto esta semana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to follow up on the project this week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguimos estudiando después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We keep studying after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguimos al guía por el museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We follow the guide through the museum.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El perro va a seguir a su dueña por todas partes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The dog is going to follow its owner everywhere.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a seguir estudiando mañana, pero también quiero seguir practicando la pronunciación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to continue studying tomorrow, but I also want to keep practicing pronunciation.

definitions.native: we will continue, we will follow
definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros/as) future tense of "seguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguiremos trabajando hasta terminar el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We will keep working until we finish the project.

definitions.native: to follow it, to follow her
definitions.note: Includes the attached direct object pronoun “la” (“it/her”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que seguirla en el mapa para llegar al hotel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to follow it on the map to get to the hotel.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “las” = “them” (feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo verlas bien, pero voy a seguirlas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't see them well, but I'm going to follow them.

definitions.native: to follow him/her/it, to keep up with him/her/it
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (to him/her/it; also formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo seguirle el ritmo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't keep up with him.

definitions.note: "-los" means "them" (direct object, usually masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a seguirlos hasta la estación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to follow them to the station.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun "me" is attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes seguirme, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you follow me, please?

definitions.note: Can also mean "to continue following me," depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si te pierdes, intenta seguirme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you get lost, try to keep following me.

definitions.note: Can be literal (go after you) or figurative (understand you).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo seguirte tan rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't follow you that fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana seguirá el mismo camino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will follow the same path.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ellos/ellas/ustedes) future tense of "seguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguirán trabajando hasta terminar el proyecto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will keep working until they finish the project.

definitions.native: I will continue, I will keep going, I will follow
definitions.note: Simple future tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguiré estudiando español mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will continue studying Spanish tomorrow.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "seguir"; often used for hypothetical situations or polite statements.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuviera más tiempo, seguiría estudiando español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I had more time, I would continue studying Spanish.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella vive en la segunda casa a la derecha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She lives in the second house on the right.

definitions.note: Used with feminine plural nouns (e.g., segundas oportunidades).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos dieron segundas oportunidades.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They gave us second chances.

definitions.note: Often used in time expressions (e.g., “un segundo” = “a second”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es la segunda vez que lo intento, pero esta es la primera vez que lo logro en menos de un segundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s the second time I’m trying, but this is the first time I manage to do it in less than a second.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it’s used in time expressions meaning “a second” (a moment).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vuelvo en un segundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll be back in a second.

definitions.note: Unit of time; also used for ordinal numbers (e.g., “el segundo” = “the second”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espera un segundo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a second, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "segundo" (a unit of time).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Faltan diez segundos para empezar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are ten seconds left to start.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta zona es segura por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This area is safe at night.

definitions.note: feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy segura de que él viene mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sure that he’s coming tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used to express a strong likelihood ("probably") rather than absolute certainty.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguramente vamos a llegar tarde por el tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ll probably arrive late because of the traffic.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estas calles son seguras por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These streets are safe at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La seguridad de los niños es lo más importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children's safety is the most important thing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este barrio es seguro por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This neighborhood is safe at night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy seguro de que tienes razón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm sure you’re right.

definitions.note: Often used to express confidence or reassurance (similar to “sure”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguro que mañana llueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Surely it will rain tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used as an interjection to agree or confirm something (like “sure” or “okay”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Puedes ayudarme mañana? —Seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —Can you help me tomorrow? —Sure.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un seguro de coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need car insurance.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "seguro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos barrios son seguros por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These neighborhoods are safe at night.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "seguro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estamos seguros de la respuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We are sure of the answer.

definitions.note: Plural form; often refers to insurance policies or types of insurance.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comparar seguros antes de elegir uno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to compare insurance policies before choosing one.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first-person singular of "seguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer seguí las instrucciones del profesor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I followed the teacher’s instructions.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past), first-person singular of "seguir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aunque estaba cansado, seguí trabajando hasta tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even though I was tired, I continued working until late.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of “seguir”; it describes an ongoing or habitual action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo seguía a mi hermana en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was following my sister in the park.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños seguían al maestro por el pasillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children were following the teacher down the hallway.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes). Often used with another verb (e.g., "seguían trabajando").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aunque llovía, seguían jugando en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Even though it was raining, they kept playing in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Según el profesor, el examen será fácil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the teacher, the exam will be easy.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Según el médico, debo descansar más.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: According to the doctor, I should rest more.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo seis hermanos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have six siblings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay seiscientos estudiantes en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are six hundred students in the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay una buena selección de libros en esta biblioteca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a good selection of books in this library.

definitions.note: Commonly used for sealing something (e.g., an envelope) or stamping/validating an official document.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito sellar este sobre antes de enviarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to seal this envelope before sending it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un sello para enviar esta carta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a stamp to send this letter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré sellos en la oficina de correos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought stamps at the post office.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Exploramos la selva durante dos días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We explored the jungle for two days.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La próxima semana tengo un examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Next week I have an exam.

definitions.note: plural of "semana"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a estar de viaje por dos semanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to be traveling for two weeks.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a sembrar semillas de tomate en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to sow tomato seeds in the garden.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third-person singular (he/she/you formal) of "sembrar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo sembró maíz en el campo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather planted corn in the field.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buscamos una solución semejante a la que usamos el año pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re looking for a solution similar to the one we used last year.

definitions.note: Often used for emphasis to mean “such a” + noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo creer que dijera semejante cosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t believe he said such a thing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La prueba detectó semen en la ropa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The test detected semen on the clothing.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este semestre tengo clases de historia y matemáticas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This semester I have history and math classes.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Planté una semilla en el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I planted a seed in the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos comprar semillas para el jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to buy seeds for the garden.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un seminario mañana por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a seminar tomorrow morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El semáforo está en rojo, así que tenemos que parar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traffic light is red, so we have to stop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta ciudad hay muchos semáforos en el centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this city there are many traffic lights downtown.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the upper house of a country's legislature (e.g., el Senado de España).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El senado aprobó la nueva ley.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senate approved the new law.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El senador dio un discurso en el Congreso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senator gave a speech in Congress.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los senadores votaron a favor de la nueva ley.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The senators voted in favor of the new law.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of "sencillo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La explicación fue sencilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The explanation was simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sencillamente no tengo tiempo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I simply don’t have time today.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las instrucciones son sencillas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The instructions are simple.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta la sencillez de este diseño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like the simplicity of this design.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un plato sencillo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s a simple dish.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los ejercicios son sencillos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The exercises are simple.

definitions.note: Often refers to a narrow path, especially in the countryside or mountains.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Seguimos la senda hasta el río.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We followed the path to the river.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Caminamos por un sendero en el bosque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We walked along a trail in the forest.

definitions.note: Often used to describe loss of mental abilities due to old age; it can sound insulting when used about a person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El abuelo ya está un poco senil y a veces se olvida de los nombres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Grandpa is a bit senile now and sometimes he forgets names.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡La película estuvo sensacional!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was sensational!

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tuve la sensación de que alguien me miraba.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had the feeling that someone was watching me.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos tomar un camino sensato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need to take a sensible path.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo sensibilidad en los dientes al comer algo frío.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have sensitivity in my teeth when I eat something cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su sensibilidad la hace notar cuando alguien está triste.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her sensitivity makes her notice when someone is sad.

definitions.note: Often refers to being emotionally sensitive or easily affected.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es muy sensible a las críticas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is very sensitive to criticism.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis ojos son muy sensibles a la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My eyes are very sensitive to light.

definitions.note: Plural form. Often used to mean 'reasonable' in Spanish (not 'sensitive').
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tus argumentos son muy sensibles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your arguments are very sensible / reasonable.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sensor detecta movimiento en la entrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sensor detects movement at the entrance.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense of “sentar”; often describes a habitual or ongoing past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas las tardes, mi abuelo se sentaba en el patio a leer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every afternoon, my grandpa would sit down in the patio to read.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy sentada en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sitting on the sofa.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy sentado en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sitting on the couch.

definitions.note: Often used with estar (e.g., "estar sentado") to describe someone’s position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy sentado en el sofá.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m sitting on the couch.

definitions.note: Masculine plural; used for a group of men or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los estudiantes están sentados en el suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The students are sitting on the floor.

definitions.note: Most commonly used as “we sit down” (present tense). It can also be “we sat down” (preterite) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos sentamos en la primera fila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sit down in the front row.

definitions.note: Plural command (vosotros) used in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Niños, sentaos en el suelo y escuchad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Kids, sit down on the floor and listen.

definitions.note: Often used reflexively as "sentarse" (to sit down). Non-reflexive "sentar" usually means to seat someone (to make someone sit).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a sentar al niño en la silla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to sit the child on the chair.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form of “sentar”, often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., after “si” = “if”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si me sentara aquí, podría ver mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I sat here, I could see better.

definitions.note: From "sentar"; in this form it usually means to sit down (not to seat someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después de la película, nos sentaremos en el café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the movie, we will sit down in the café.

definitions.note: Reflexive form: "me" = "myself" (I sit down).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a sentarme aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to sit down here.

definitions.note: reflexive + us: “sit down” (ourselves).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a sentarnos aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's sit down here.

definitions.note: Third-person plural simple past (pretérito) of "sentar". Often used reflexively as "se sentaron" = "they sat down."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños se sentaron en el suelo para escuchar el cuento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children sat down on the floor to listen to the story.

definitions.note: Reflexive verb meaning “to sit down.” In conjugation it appears as a form of *sentar* plus a reflexive pronoun (me/te/se/nos/os/se).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a sentarse aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to sit down here.

definitions.note: Includes the pronoun “te” (“yourself/you,” informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es mejor sentarte un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s better to sit down for a moment.

definitions.note: Future tense (he/she/you formal). It can mean ‘will sit down’ (reflexive: sentarse) or ‘will seat’ (to seat someone).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana sentará al bebé en la silla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow, he/she will seat the baby in the chair.

definitions.note: Future tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me sentaré aquí un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will sit down here for a moment.

definitions.note: Informal command used with vos (common in Argentina/Uruguay); equivalent to "siéntate" (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sentate acá, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sit down here, please.

definitions.note: Often used in legal contexts to mean a judge’s ruling or verdict.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El juez dictó sentencia ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The judge issued the ruling yesterday.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El ladrón fue sentenciado a cinco años de cárcel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The thief was sentenced to five years in prison.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "tener sentido" (to make sense) or "en el sentido de" (in the sense of).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta frase no tiene sentido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This sentence doesn't make sense.

definitions.note: Often used like an adjective meaning something was deeply felt. Not the same as English “scented.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El golpe fue muy sentido por todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The blow was deeply felt by everyone.

definitions.note: Past participle of "sentir"; often used with "haber" to form the present perfect (e.g., "he sentido").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He sentido mucho frío hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have felt very cold today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo los cinco sentidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have the five senses.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta palabra tiene dos sentidos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This word has two meanings.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo se pone sentimental cuando ve fotos antiguas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather gets sentimental when he sees old photos.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo un sentimiento extraño sobre esto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a strange feeling about this.

definitions.note: Often used for emotions or attitudes (for example, "sentimientos" can mean "feelings").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus palabras reflejan un sentimiento de esperanza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His words reflect a feeling of hope.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchos sentimientos encontrados sobre ese tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of mixed feelings about that topic.

definitions.native: we feel, we regret, we are sorry
definitions.note: From "sentir". Often used to express apologies or sympathy (e.g., "Lo sentimos" = "We’re sorry").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo sentimos mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re very sorry.

definitions.note: Often used for emotions or physical sensations; also used in expressions like “sentir + noun” for “to smell/hear” in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo sentir la mano derecha.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't feel my right hand.

definitions.note: Used to apologize or express sympathy, often in “lo siento”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debo sentir mucho lo que pasó.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must be very sorry about what happened.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “la” (= it/her, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedo sentirla cerca.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can feel her nearby.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” = “it” (for something masculine or an idea).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedo sentirlo en el aire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can feel it in the air.

definitions.note: Reflexive form with an attached object pronoun (“me” = myself). Often used to talk about how you feel physically or emotionally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy voy a sentirme mejor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I'm going to feel better.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive used to talk about how someone feels physically or emotionally; conjugated forms include me siento, te sientes, etc.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señores, por favor, tomen asiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Gentlemen, please take a seat.

definitions.note: Often used as a polite form of address for a young woman; in some contexts it can feel old-fashioned or imply marital status.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Disculpe, señorita, ¿me puede ayudar?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Excuse me, miss, can you help me?

definitions.note: Plural of “señorita”; often used as a polite way to address or refer to young women (sometimes like “ladies”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Buenas tardes, señoritas, ¿en qué puedo ayudarles?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Good afternoon, young ladies, how can I help you?

definitions.note: Used as a formal form of address for a judge (in court).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con la venia de su señoría, quisiera hacer una pregunta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With your honor's permission, I would like to ask a question.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El cazador dejó un señuelo para atraer a los patos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The hunter left a decoy to attract the ducks.

definitions.note: Used mainly in the US context; it refers to an elected county law enforcement officer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sheriff habló con los vecinos después del robo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sheriff spoke with the neighbors after the robbery.

definitions.note: Often used in Spanish in medical contexts (e.g., "shock" or "estado de shock").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El paciente está en shock después del accidente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient is in shock after the accident.

definitions.note: Often used for live entertainment; a common loanword from English.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El show empieza a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The show starts at eight.

definitions.note: Conditional conjunction meaning “if” (written without an accent: si).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si llueve, no salimos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it rains, we’re not going out.

definitions.note: Used to introduce an indirect yes/no question (without accent: si).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé si viene hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know whether he’s coming today.

definitions.note: In some contexts, si (without accent) can appear in an embedded clause where English would use “yes,” though Spanish also commonly uses “sí” as a standalone reply.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dijo que si, que quería venir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He said yes, that he wanted to come.

definitions.note: Used to agree or confirm; it can also be written with an accent (sí) when it means “yes.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Vienes mañana? —Si.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: “Are you coming tomorrow?” “Yes.”

definitions.note: In fixed-do solfège, “si” is the note B.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Canta la nota si antes de do.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sing the note B before C.

definitions.note: reflexive pronoun used after prepositions (e.g., after “para”, “de”, “a”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo hizo para si.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did it for himself.

definitions.note: Without an accent; unlike sí, this does not mean 'yes'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé si Marta viene hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't know whether Marta is coming today.

definitions.note: Conditional conjunction meaning “if.” (Without an accent: “si.” With an accent: “sí” = “yes.”)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si quieres, vamos al parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you want, we’ll go to the park.

definitions.note: Used in indirect questions to mean “whether.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé si viene hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know whether he’s coming today.

definitions.note: Often used with the subjunctive (e.g., “por si”) to mean “in case.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llevo un paraguas por si llueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m taking an umbrella in case it rains.

definitions.note: Introduces a condition; sometimes translated as “whether” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si llueve mañana, nos quedamos en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If it rains tomorrow, we’ll stay at home.

definitions.note: Used in indirect questions; often followed by “o no” (or not).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sé si va a venir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t know whether he/she is going to come.

definitions.note: Sets a requirement or condition that must be met.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes salir si terminas la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can go out as long as you finish your homework.

definitions.note: As a reflexive pronoun after a preposition, it is normally written with an accent: “sí” (e.g., “para sí”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo hizo para si.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He did it for himself.

definitions.note: Medical term; acronym from Spanish “síndrome de inmunodeficiencia adquirida”. Usually written in all caps in English (AIDS).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He was diagnosed with AIDS five years ago.

definitions.note: Past participle of "ser", used with "haber" in perfect tenses.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been very patient with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He sido muy paciente contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have been very patient with you.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo form) of "sembrar".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Every spring, he/she sows (plants) tomatoes in the garden.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú form).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre desayuno antes de salir de casa.

definitions.note: Gerund of "ser" (to be); used to form progressive constructions or as a linking word meaning "being".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is being very kind to me.

definitions.note: Gerund of “ser” (“to be”), used in progressive forms and after prepositions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sigo siendo tu amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I keep being your friend.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) from "sentar".

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "sentir"; also used as a formal command (usted) meaning "feel".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you feel better soon.

definitions.note: Usually used with "que" (present subjunctive), often for "they" or "you" (ustedes).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siento frío en las manos.

definitions.note: Often refers to someone in a dependent, subservient position (historically, a serf).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The servant worked the lord’s lands.

definitions.note: Often refers to a short rest or sleep in the early afternoon.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After eating, I like to take a nap.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo siete años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am seven years old.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive of "seguir"; also used for the formal command (usted): "(you) continue/follow".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, siga recto hasta el semáforo.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "seguir" used with "nosotros"; commonly used to make a suggestion ("let's...").

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s continue with the lesson.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes). Often used for giving instructions or encouragement.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sigan por este camino hasta la plaza.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “seguir” (used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “es importante que…”, or in negative commands: “No sigas…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que sigas estudiando español todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to keep studying Spanish every day.

definitions.note: Often implies moving or acting so as not to be noticed.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The cat entered the room stealthily.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This castle is from the 15th century.

definitions.note: Plural of "siglo".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Many centuries have passed since then.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué significa esta palabra?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What does this word mean?

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (used for habitual actions or ongoing states in the past).

definitions.note: Plural of "significado".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That word meant a lot to me.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for polite commands with usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que esto signifique algo para ti.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope this means something to you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese signo significa peligro.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The signs of the illness appeared quickly.

definitions.native: I continue, I go on, I follow
definitions.note: Present tense, first person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sigo estudiando español todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I continue studying Spanish every day.

definitions.note: This form can also be used as the affirmative tú command: continue!, keep going!
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La música sigue después de un momento de silencio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The music continues after a moment of silence.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sigue las instrucciones con mucho cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She follows the instructions very carefully.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present (they/you all follow/continue).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos siguen las instrucciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They follow the instructions.

definitions.note: Present tense of “seguir” for “tú” (informal “you”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you still studying Spanish?

definitions.native: to hold, to fasten, to secure
definitions.note: Often used for physically holding something in place (e.g., with your hand, a clip, a strap, etc.).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You must hold the box tightly so it doesn't fall.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am subject to the rules of the contract.

definitions.note: Often used in grammar (the subject of a sentence) or in general to mean a person under discussion.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella sujetó la bolsa con fuerza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She held the bag tightly.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy superando mis miedos poco a poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m overcoming my fears little by little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito superar este problema.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sé que es difícil, pero vas a superarlo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I know it’s hard, but you’re going to get over it.

definitions.native: you will overcome, you will get over

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Superarás este problema con paciencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will overcome this problem with patience.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to someone higher in rank (e.g., at work or in the military).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to talk to my superior before making a decision.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los pisos superiores tienen una mejor vista.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My superiors approved the project.

definitions.note: plural

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The survivors of the accident were taken to the hospital.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): first-person singular (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Superé el miedo a hablar en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I overcame my fear of speaking in public.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella superó el miedo y habló en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She overcame her fear and spoke in public.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted form) of "saber"; often used after expressions like "quería que..." or in "si" (if) clauses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que supiera la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted him/her to know the truth.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (ellos/ellas/ustedes) of “saber”; often used after expressions like “quería que…”, “dudaba que…”, etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que supieran la verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I wanted them to know the truth.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (tú form); often used after expressions like “si…” (if…) or to express doubt, wishes, or hypotheticals.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si supieras la verdad, no dirías eso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you knew the truth, you wouldn’t say that.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of "saber" for "we".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supimos la verdad ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We found out the truth yesterday.

definitions.native: you found out, you learned, you knew
definitions.note: Preterite (completed past), informal singular “tú” form of “saber”.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How did you find out the truth?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we knew the truth, we would tell you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te suplico que me ayudes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I beg you to help me.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of “saber”; often used for finding out or learning information.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he found out, he got very angry.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eso supone que todos están de acuerdo.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cambiar de ciudad supone empezar de nuevo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Changing cities means starting over.

definitions.note: Often used to express an assumption or something taken for granted. The example uses the infinitive form exactly: “suponer”.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tu suposición no es correcta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Your assumption is not correct.

definitions.note: Used to indicate that something is said to be true but is not confirmed (and sometimes the speaker doubts it).

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form meaning a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supuse que ya habías llegado a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I assumed that you had already gotten home.

definitions.note: Informal command form (tú) of “suponer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Supón que mañana llueve: ¿qué hacemos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Suppose it rains tomorrow—what do we do?

definitions.note: Often used with nouns to mean “southern” (e.g., viento sur = south wind).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The south wind is warm.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The south of Spain is very warm in summer.

definitions.note: From the verb "surgir" (to arise/come up).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: An unexpected problem has arisen.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De repente, surgieron varios problemas.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si puede surgir un problema, te llamo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If a problem can arise, I’ll call you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De repente surgió un problema.

definitions.note: used before plural nouns

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El proyecto está suspendido hasta nuevo aviso.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El partido está suspendido por la lluvia.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I failed the math exam.
