definitions.note: Written with an accent to distinguish it from si (“if”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Tienes hambre? —Sí, un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —Are you hungry? —Yes, a little.

definitions.note: With an accent mark; without it, si usually means "if".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: —¿Quieres más café? —Sí, gracias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: —Do you want more coffee? —Yes, thanks.

definitions.note: Used as a noun (often with an article), meaning the word “yes” or an affirmative answer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su respuesta fue un sí rotundo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His/Her answer was a firm yes.

definitions.note: Reflexive pronoun used after a preposition (e.g., "para sí", "de sí").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lo guardó para sí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She kept it to herself.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, sígame al mostrador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please follow me to the counter.

definitions.note: Formal command to more than one person (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Síganme, por favor; los llevo a su mesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow me, please; I'll take you to your table.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú): it tells one person to follow the speaker.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sígueme, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Follow me, please.

definitions.note: Plural of “sílaba”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta palabra tiene tres sílabas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This word has three syllables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este símbolo significa paz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This symbol means peace.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la puerta hay símbolos que indican que no se puede fumar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: On the door there are symbols that indicate you can't smoke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La fiebre es un síntoma común de la gripe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Fever is a common symptom of the flu.

definitions.note: Plural of “síntoma”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo síntomas de gripe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have flu symptoms.

definitions.note: Formal command (ustedes). Often used when inviting guests to take food or drink; reflexive "-se" implies serving yourselves.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sírvanse café y galletas, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help yourselves to coffee and cookies, please.

definitions.note: Formal command used to politely tell someone to do something; common in very polite requests (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sírvase pasar a la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please go ahead and come into the office.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with an indirect object pronoun (me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, sírveme un vaso de agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please serve me a glass of water.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command + reflexive pronoun; often used to invite someone to take food or drink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sírvete un poco más de sopa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Help yourself to a little more soup, please.

definitions.note: Likely a misspelling of “sólo/solo” in Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero sóio una cosa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want only one thing.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La mesa es sólida y no se mueve.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The table is solid and doesn't move.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este material es sólido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This material is solid.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos muebles son sólidos y duraderos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These pieces of furniture are solid and durable.

definitions.note: Also used as an adverb meaning “only/just.” In modern Spanish it’s often written without the accent (solo) unless needed to avoid ambiguity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sólo quiero un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only want a coffee.

definitions.note: Traditionally written with an accent to distinguish it from the adjective solo; today it is often written without the accent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sólo quiero un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I just want a coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Guardamos las cajas en el sótano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We keep the boxes in the basement.

definitions.note: Often used in historical or monarchy contexts; it refers to people under the rule of a king/queen.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los súbditos obedecían las leyes del rey.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The subjects obeyed the king’s laws.

definitions.note: Affirmative tú command of "subir" with the indirect object pronoun "le" (often used with volume: "Súbele a la música").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Súbele a la música, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Turn up the music, please.

definitions.native: get on, get in, get up
definitions.note: Command form (tú) meaning “get yourself up/on/in.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Súbete al coche y nos vamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Get in the car and we’ll leave.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche frenó súbitamente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car braked suddenly.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech to mean something is very good or excellent.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡La película estuvo súper!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie was super!

definitions.note: Informal; used to emphasize adjectives and adverbs.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy súper cansado hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm super tired today.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tabaco es malo para la salud.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tobacco is bad for your health.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos encontramos en una taberna del centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We met at a tavern downtown.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon la tabla en el suelo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the board on the floor, please.

definitions.note: Used for information arranged in rows and columns (not a piece of furniture).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mira la tabla de precios.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Look at the price table.

definitions.note: Often used for a board you write on (like a chalkboard/whiteboard) or a board used for games.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor escribe en el tablero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher writes on the board.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me senté en un taburete para desayunar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I sat on a stool to eat breakfast.

definitions.note: Describes someone who hates spending money or sharing.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tío es muy tacaño y nunca invita a nadie.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My uncle is very stingy and never treats anyone.

definitions.note: Used mainly in soccer to refer to a tackle, often a sliding one.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El defensa hizo un tacle para quitarle el balón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The defender made a tackle to win the ball.

definitions.note: In Spanish it can also mean a "plug" or "cork" in some contexts, but the food meaning is the most common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a pedir dos tacos de pollo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to order two chicken tacos.

definitions.note: Usually refers to the heels of shoes (high heels).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me duelen los pies por llevar tacones todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My feet hurt from wearing heels all day.

definitions.note: Plural of "taco".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pedimos tacos para cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered tacos for dinner.

definitions.note: Often used in phrases like "sentido del tacto" (the sense of touch) and "tener tacto" (to have tact).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El sentido del tacto nos ayuda a sentir el frío y el calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sense of touch helps us feel cold and heat.

definitions.note: Refers to sensitivity or diplomacy when dealing with people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitas tacto para hablar con ella sobre ese tema.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You need tact to talk with her about that topic.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi profesora es tailandesa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My teacher is Thai.

definitions.note: Can refer to a man from Thailand; for a woman, use “tailandesa”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él es tailandés y vive en Bangkok.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is Thai and lives in Bangkok.

definitions.note: Often used before a noun: "tal cosa" = "such a thing".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero hablar de tal tema ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to talk about such a topic now.

definitions.note: Used before a singular noun to mean "a certain" or "that kind of".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nunca había visto a tal persona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had never seen such a person.

definitions.note: usually used in the expression ¿qué tal...? to ask how someone or something is, or how something went
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué tal estás hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you today?

definitions.note: Used to refer to a person or thing that has been mentioned or is known in the context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo tal información.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't have such information.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to something or someone unspecified or previously mentioned (e.g., “tal persona” = “such a person”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero vivir en un lugar tal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to live in such a place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un taladro para hacer un agujero en la pared.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a drill to make a hole in the wall.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tiene mucho talento para la música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has a lot of talent for music.

definitions.note: Plural of "talento".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esta empresa valoramos tus talentos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At this company, we value your talents.

definitions.note: feminine form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es muy talentosa para la música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is very talented at music.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es muy talentoso para la música.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is very talented at music.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also refer to a mixed-gender group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis compañeros son muy talentosos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My classmates are very talented.

definitions.note: Plural form; often used before a plural noun (e.g., “tales cosas” = “such things”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero oír tales excusas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to hear such excuses.

definitions.note: Commonly used for clothing and shoe sizes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué talla usas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What size do you wear?

definitions.note: Commonly refers to long noodles (like spaghetti); in some countries it’s a general word for pasta noodles.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy voy a cocinar tallarines con salsa de tomate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m going to cook noodles with tomato sauce.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me inscribí en un taller de escritura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I signed up for a writing workshop.

definitions.note: Often used for places where things are repaired, especially cars: "taller mecánico".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El coche está en el taller.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The car is at the repair shop.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El leñador taló el árbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lumberjack cut down the tree.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué tamaño necesitas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What size do you need?

definitions.note: Often written with an accent: “también”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo tambien quiero ir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I also want to go.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo también quiero ir al parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I also want to go to the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tambor suena muy fuerte en el desfile.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drum sounds very loud in the parade.

definitions.note: Used with negative statements to mean “neither” or “either” (e.g., “I don’t… either”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me gusta el café, y a ella tampoco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like coffee, and she doesn't either.

definitions.note: Used before adjectives and adverbs; in comparisons, it often appears in tan... como for 'as... as'.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hables tan rápido, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please don't speak so fast.

definitions.note: Used to express degree or comparison, often with adjectives/adverbs (tan alto...) or in patterns like “tan... como...”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No es tan difícil como parece.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s not as difficult as it seems.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Bailamos tango toda la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We danced tango all night.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tanque está lleno de agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tank is full of water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tanque avanzó por la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tank moved forward down the street.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay dos tanques estacionados cerca del puente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are two tanks parked near the bridge.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used with feminine singular nouns or as a pronoun referring to something feminine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No necesito tanta ayuda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't need so much help.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of "tanto"; used with feminine plural nouns (e.g., "tantas cosas").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sabía que tenías tantas ideas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t know you had so many ideas.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No sabía que tenías tantas amigas aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I didn’t know you had so many friends here.

definitions.note: Common in Latin American Spanish; often used informally.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espera tantito, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wait a little bit, please.

definitions.note: Used to express a large degree or quantity; often appears in comparisons or with expressions like “no... tanto” (“not so much”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No comas tanto; te va a doler el estómago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t eat so much; your stomach will hurt.

definitions.note: Often used in the pattern “tanto... como” (“as much/many... as”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero tanto café como tú.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want as much coffee as you.

definitions.note: Often used in comparisons (e.g., “no tanto como…” = “not as much as…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me gusta tanto como antes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't like it as much as before.

definitions.note: Used to introduce a result or consequence in the pattern “tanto…, que …” (“so much…, that …”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trabaja tanto que siempre está cansado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He works so much that he's always tired.

definitions.note: Used before a noun; agrees in gender/number (tanto, tanta, tantos, tantas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tengo tanto tiempo hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t have so much time today.

definitions.note: Often used in comparisons with "como" ("tanto como" = "as much as").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero tanto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want so much.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used with plural masculine nouns (or mixed-gender groups) to indicate quantity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No comas tantos dulces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't eat so many sweets.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form of "tanto"; used with masculine plural nouns or as a pronoun referring to a masculine/mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo creer que haya tantos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can’t believe there are so many.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon la tapa en la olla, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the lid on the pot, please.

definitions.note: Common in Spain: a small appetizer served with a drink or as a snack.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a pedir una tapa de tortilla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's order a tapa of Spanish omelet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tapa la olla para que no se enfríe.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She covers the pot so it doesn’t get cold.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bote está tapado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The container is covered.

definitions.note: Often used for covering something (with a lid, cloth, etc.) or blocking an opening (like a drain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, voy a tapar la olla para que no se enfríe la sopa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, I’m going to cover the pot so the soup doesn’t get cold.

definitions.note: In Spain, this often refers to small portions served with drinks or shared as snacks.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pedimos unas tapas y una bebida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ordered some tapas and a drink.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las tapas de los recipientes no cierran bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The lids of the containers don’t close well.

definitions.note: Plural form of "tapón".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito dos tapones para las botellas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need two stoppers for the bottles.

definitions.note: Common in Spain: "un tapón" in traffic means a jam.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay tapones en la autopista esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are traffic jams on the highway this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon el tapón en la botella, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the stopper in the bottle, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré las entradas en la taquilla del teatro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought the tickets at the theater box office.

definitions.note: Common in Spain for a locker in places like gyms, pools, or schools.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Deja tu mochila en la taquilla del gimnasio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Leave your backpack in the gym locker.

definitions.note: Offensive/insulting; avoid in polite conversation.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No le hagas caso; es un tarado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t pay attention to him; he’s an idiot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El autobús tarda veinte minutos en llegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus takes twenty minutes to arrive.

definitions.note: Past participle of "tardar"; commonly used with "haber" in the present perfect, often with time expressions (e.g., "He tardado mucho").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tardado mucho en llegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ve taken a long time to arrive.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about how long something takes to do or how long it takes to arrive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tardamos veinte minutos en llegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took twenty minutes to get there.

definitions.note: Present tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos tardan mucho en llegar a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends take a long time to get home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lamento la tardanza; había mucho tráfico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for the delay; there was a lot of traffic.

definitions.note: Often used with an amount of time (e.g., “Tardo diez minutos”) or with “en” to say how long something takes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tren suele tardar una hora en llegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The train usually takes an hour to arrive.

definitions.note: Commonly used in the negative (“No tardes”) to tell someone not to be late.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Perdón por tardar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sorry for being late.

definitions.note: Preterite; used to say something took a certain amount of time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tardaron dos horas en llegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took two hours to arrive.

definitions.note: Refers to how long something will take.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El autobús tardará treinta minutos en llegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus will take thirty minutes to arrive.

definitions.note: Refers to how long something will take; often used with "en" + time period (e.g., "tardar en llegar").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tardaré diez minutos en llegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll take ten minutes to get there.

definitions.note: Present tense (tú). Often used with a time expression (e.g., “tardas mucho”) or with “en” + infinitive (“tardas en llegar”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué tardas tanto en responder?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you taking so long to reply?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no tarde mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope it doesn’t take long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre llego tarde a clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always arrive late to class.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “por la tarde” (in the afternoon).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por la tarde estudio en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In the afternoon I study at home.

definitions.note: Often used with “en” + infinitive: “tardar en hacer algo” = “to take a long time to do something.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que no tardes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you don’t take long.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trabajo por las tardes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I work in the afternoons.

definitions.native: I take (a long time), I’m late
definitions.note: From the verb "tardar": often used to mean "to take a long time" (tardar en + infinitive) or "to be late".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre tardo en contestar los mensajes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always take a long time to reply to messages.

definitions.native: I took a long time, I was late
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): first person singular of "tardar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tardé mucho en llegar a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I took a long time to get home.

definitions.note: Third-person singular in the past (preterite): “he/she/it took… / was late.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El autobús tardó mucho en llegar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bus took a long time to arrive.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo mucha tarea para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of homework for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo muchas tareas para mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a lot of homework to do for tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tarifa incluye el desayuno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The rate includes breakfast.

definitions.note: Often used for things like credit/debit cards, ID cards, or gift cards.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes pagar con tarjeta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you pay by card?

definitions.note: Plural of "tarjeta".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo dos tarjetas en mi billetera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have two cards in my wallet.

definitions.note: Usually used in expressions like “cartas del tarot” (tarot cards).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella lee las cartas del tarot.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She reads tarot cards.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon las galletas en el tarro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put the cookies in the jar.

definitions.note: In Spain, “tarta” usually refers to a cake (often with layers or frosting).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para mi cumpleaños, quiero una tarta de chocolate.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For my birthday, I want a chocolate cake.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando está nervioso, tartamudea un poco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When he is nervous, he stutters a little.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré dos tartas para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought two cakes for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos tienen dos clases hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They have two classes today.

definitions.note: used with que + infinitive to express obligation
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tienes que estudiar para el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You have to study for the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tienes tiempo ahora?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you have time now?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuela es muy tierna con los niños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandma is very affectionate with the children.

definitions.note: Often used for people, animals, or gestures that make you feel affection.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El bebé es muy tierno.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The baby is very sweet.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tierra está mojada por la lluvia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ground is wet from the rain.

definitions.note: Plural of “tierra.” Often used for areas of land or types of soil/terrain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estas tierras son muy fértiles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These lands are very fertile.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tifón llegó anoche y causó muchos daños.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The typhoon arrived last night and caused a lot of damage.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tigre vive en la selva.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The tiger lives in the jungle.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En este zoológico hay dos tigres.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In this zoo there are two tigers.

definitions.note: Usually used in the plural in Spanish.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito unas tijeras para cortar el papel.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need some scissors to cut the paper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un timbre para enviar esta carta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a stamp to send this letter.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su timidez le impide hablar en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His shyness keeps him from speaking in public.

definitions.note: Often refers to a boat’s rudder; it can also mean a vehicle’s steering wheel in some contexts.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El capitán agarró el timón y giró el barco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The captain grabbed the helm and turned the boat.

definitions.note: Often refers to a large container (like a washtub or vat).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Llené la tina con agua caliente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I filled the tub with hot water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito más tinta para la impresora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need more ink for the printer.

definitions.note: Informal slang; can sound disrespectful depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa tipa siempre llega tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That woman always arrives late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué tipo de música te gusta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What kind of music do you like?

definitions.note: informal
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ese tipo siempre llega tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That guy is always late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos tipos de pan en esta tienda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many types of bread in this store.

definitions.note: Common in informal speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esos tipos son muy simpáticos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those guys are very nice.

definitions.note: Often used for “he/she/you (formal) throws”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tira la pelota.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She throws the ball.

definitions.note: Can also be used as a tú command: “pull!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tira de la cuerda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Pull the rope.

definitions.note: Feminine form; often used with "estar" to mean something is left/thrown somewhere (not neatly placed).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La chaqueta está tirada en la silla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jacket is thrown on the chair.

definitions.note: Often used to describe something (or someone) left on the ground or abandoned somewhere.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Había ropa tirado en el suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There were clothes lying on the floor.

definitions.note: Common in the phrase “tirado de precio”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este teléfono está tirado de precio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This phone is really cheap.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El papel está tirado en el suelo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The paper is thrown on the floor.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó al tirador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested the shooter.

definitions.note: Common for furniture (like a drawer).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El tirador del cajón está roto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drawer pull is broken.

definitions.note: Commonly refers to the handles on drawers, cabinets, or doors.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los tiradores de la cómoda están rotos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The drawer handles on the dresser are broken.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó a dos tiradores.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested two shooters.

definitions.native: we throw, we pull, we take off
definitions.note: From the verb "tirar"; can mean throwing something, pulling something, or taking something off (like clothing) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Después del partido, tiramos la camiseta sudada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the game, we take off the sweaty shirt.

definitions.note: Often used with "la basura" to mean "throwing away the trash."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tirando la basura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m throwing away the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se me rompieron los tirantes del pantalón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My suspenders broke.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debes tirar la basura en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn’t throw the trash in the street.

definitions.note: Commonly used for removing clothing or accessories.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tirar la chaqueta porque hace calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take off my jacket because it’s hot.

definitions.native: to throw it, to pull it, to take it off
definitions.note: Direct-object pronoun “lo” = “it” attached to the infinitive “tirar.” Meaning depends on context (throw vs. pull vs. remove).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero tirarlo a la basura.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to throw it in the trash.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No vayas a tirarme la pelota tan fuerte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t throw me the ball so hard.

definitions.note: Often used with places like “al agua” (into the water) to mean jumping in.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tirarme al agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to jump into the water.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiraron la pelota al patio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They threw the ball into the yard.

definitions.native: to throw oneself, to jump (into/on), to lie down
definitions.note: Reflexive form of "tirar"; often used for throwing/jumping oneself somewhere ("tirarse al agua") or for lying down ("tirarse en la cama").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Decidió tirarse al agua para salvar al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He decided to throw himself into the water to save the dog.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiraré la pelota al aire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I will throw the ball into the air.

definitions.note: Plural of “tira”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Corta el papel en tiras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Cut the paper into strips.

definitions.note: Can also mean "you take off" (e.g., clothes) depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué tiras la basura al suelo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you throwing the trash on the ground?

definitions.native: you threw, you pulled, you tossed
definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of "tirar" for informal "you" (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué tiraste la pelota tan lejos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why did you throw the ball so far?

definitions.note: Commonly used with "la basura" (take out/throw away the trash) or "fotos" (take photos), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tire la pelota al aire.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She throws the ball into the air.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also used for formal command with ustedes) of "tirar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero que tiren la comida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want you to throw away the food.

definitions.note: Can mean either “you throw” (to throw) or “you pull” (to pull), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tires la cuerda, se abre la puerta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you pull the rope, the door opens.

definitions.note: Verb form of "tirar". Not related to the English word "tire".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Siempre tiro la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I always throw the ball to the dog.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escuché un tiro en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard a shot in the street.

definitions.note: Often used for a throw (for example, in sports).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su tiro fue muy preciso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His throw was very accurate.

definitions.note: Plural of "tiro".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escuché tiros en la calle.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I heard shots in the street.

definitions.note: Usually refers to an incident where shots are fired; “shootout” often implies an exchange of gunfire.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hubo un tiroteo cerca de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There was a shooting near the school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tiré la pelota al jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I threw the ball into the yard.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person singular of "tirar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él tiró la pelota al perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He threw the ball to the dog.

definitions.note: Often used for the person whose name is officially on an account, document, or position.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La titular de la cuenta vive en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The account holder lives in Madrid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor escribió en la pizarra con tiza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher wrote on the board with chalk.

definitions.note: Plural of "tiza".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito tizas de colores para la pizarra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need colored chalk for the board.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "teñir"; often used with "estar" to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tiñendo mi cabello en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m dyeing my hair at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito una toalla limpia después de ducharme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a clean towel after showering.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más toallas para el baño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more towels for the bathroom.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me torcí el tobillo jugando al fútbol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I twisted my ankle playing soccer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No toca eso, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t touch that, please.

definitions.note: Used with musical instruments (e.g., tocar la guitarra).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano toca el piano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother plays the piano.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used for ongoing or habitual past actions (e.g., playing an instrument).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocaba el piano cuando era niño.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to play the piano when I was a child.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often used for ongoing or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocaba la pared para ver si estaba fría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was touching the wall to see if it was cold.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando éramos niños, tocaban la guitarra en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, they played the guitar in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tocado el botón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have touched the button.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tocado la guitarra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have played the guitar.

definitions.note: Can mean either “we play” (music/instrument) or “we touch,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocamos la guitarra después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We play the guitar after dinner.

definitions.note: Present tense (ellos/ellas/ustedes). Often used with instruments (play) or physical contact (touch).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocan la guitarra en una banda.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They play the guitar in a band.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "tocar"; often used with "estar" to describe an action in progress.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tocando la guitarra en mi cuarto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am playing the guitar in my room.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, no tocar el vidrio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, do not touch the glass.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Sabes tocar la guitarra?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you know how to play the guitar?

definitions.note: Used especially for bells, doorbells, or phones.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Van a tocar el timbre en un momento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re going to ring the doorbell in a moment.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of “tocar”; often used after “si” to talk about hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tocara el piano, practicaría todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I played the piano, I would practice every day.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive of “tocar”; often used after “si” to talk about hypothetical situations.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tocara esa olla, me quemaría.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I touched that pot, I would burn myself.

definitions.native: to touch it, to touch her
definitions.note: The ending “-la” is a direct object pronoun meaning “it” (feminine noun) or “her.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debes tocarla; está muy caliente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn't touch it; it's very hot.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” = “it” (for a masculine noun or a general/neutral “it”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No debes tocarlo; está caliente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You shouldn't touch it; it's hot.

definitions.note: Often used for playing a song/piece or an instrument; “lo” = “it”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero tocarlo en la guitarra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to play it on the guitar.

definitions.note: Includes the attached object pronoun “me” = “me.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedes tocarme.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You can't touch me.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "tocar" for "they/you all" (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tocaron la puerta y nadie abrió.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They knocked on the door and nobody opened.

definitions.note: Infinitive with the attached object pronoun “te” (“you,” informal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero tocarte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to touch you.

definitions.note: From the verb "tocar". Often means "will play" when talking about a musical instrument.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tocará el piano mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will play the piano tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used for playing a musical instrument.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tocaré la guitarra en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will play the guitar at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tocaré nada sin permiso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I won't touch anything without permission.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "tocar" (used for hypotheticals or polite requests).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo tocaría el piano si tuviera tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would play the piano if I had time.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué tocas mi teléfono?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why are you touching my phone?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) of "tocar" for "tú".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tocaste el piano ayer?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you play the piano yesterday?

definitions.note: In some regions it can also refer to pork fat/lard, but the most common meaning is bacon.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Para el desayuno, quiero huevos con tocino.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: For breakfast, I want eggs with bacon.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No toco la pantalla con las manos sucias.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t touch the screen with dirty hands.

definitions.note: Used with musical instruments (e.g., tocar la guitarra).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Toco la guitarra todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I play the guitar every day.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "tocar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tocó el piano en la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She played the piano at the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Toda la familia vino a la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The whole family came to the party.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used to refer back to a feminine noun already mentioned (e.g., la pizza, la casa).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres la pizza? Toda es tuya.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want the pizza? It's all yours.

definitions.note: used before feminine plural nouns
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas las ventanas están abiertas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the windows are open.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form; used for groups of women/girls or feminine nouns.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todas están listas para salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone is ready to go out.

definitions.note: Often means 'yet' in negative sentences.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todavía no he terminado la tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I haven't finished the homework yet.

definitions.note: As an adverb, it can emphasize “completely/entirely” (e.g., “todo listo” = “all ready”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya lo sé todo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I already know everything.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estudié todo el día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I studied all day.

definitions.note: As a pronoun, it usually means "everything" or "all of it," not the adjective "every".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todo salió bien al final.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everything turned out well in the end.

definitions.note: Often used to refer to God (e.g., "Dios todopoderoso").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dios es todopoderoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: God is almighty.

definitions.note: used before a plural masculine noun
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos los estudiantes llegaron temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: All the students arrived early.

definitions.note: refers to a masculine or mixed-gender group
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Todos llegaron temprano a la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Everyone arrived early to the meeting.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy vamos a cocinar tofu con verduras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we're going to cook tofu with vegetables.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesitamos más tolerancia en la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We need more tolerance at school.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis padres son muy tolerantes con mis ideas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My parents are very tolerant of my ideas.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis vecinos son muy tolerantes con el ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are very tolerant about the noise.

definitions.native: I tolerate, I put up with
definitions.note: First-person singular present of "tolerar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo tolero el ruido por la noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I tolerate the noise at night.

definitions.note: Often used in set phrases like “toma de control” (takeover of control) or “toma de rehenes” (hostage-taking).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía evitó la toma del edificio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police prevented the takeover of the building.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella toma el autobús todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She takes the bus every day.

definitions.note: Often used with beverages (e.g., café, agua) to mean “drink.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él toma café por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He drinks coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, tomaba el autobús a la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to take the bus to school.

definitions.note: Used to address a group informally (vosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomad una foto aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a photo here, please.

definitions.note: Often used to say a seat/table/spot is already occupied or reserved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta mesa está tomada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This table is taken.

definitions.note: Feminine singular past participle of "tomar"; used with passive voice or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La foto fue tomada ayer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The photo was taken yesterday.

definitions.note: Past participle of "tomar"; often used with "haber" to form perfect tenses (e.g., "he tomado").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tomado un café esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I had a coffee this morning.

definitions.note: Most commonly: “we take” in general; “we drink” when talking about beverages.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos un café después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We have a coffee after class.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "tomar" (they/you all take/drink).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos toman café todas las mañanas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They drink coffee every morning.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of “tomar”; commonly used with “estar” to mean “(to be) taking/having” something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy tomando un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m having a coffee.

definitions.note: Often used with food/drink to mean “to have” (e.g., tomar un café = to have a coffee).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomar el autobús a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take the bus at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero tomar agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to drink water, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive form, often used in hypothetical situations (e.g., with "si" = "if").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tomara el autobús, llegaría más temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If I took the bus, I would arrive earlier.

definitions.native: we will take, we will have (food/drink)
definitions.note: Future tense (nosotros). Often used for having food or drinks in context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tomaremos el tren a Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will take the train to Madrid.

definitions.native: to take (something) from/for him, her, you (formal)
definitions.note: Includes the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to/for him, her, or you formal). Often used with “una foto” to mean “take a photo of him/her.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomarle una foto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take a photo of him/her.

definitions.note: Object pronoun “lo” = “it” (masculine singular) attached to the verb.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomarlo ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to take it now.

definitions.native: to take (for myself), to have (for myself)
definitions.note: Reflexive/indirect object form: literally “to take me” / “to take for myself,” often used with drinks or medicine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomarme un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to have a coffee.

definitions.note: Reflexive with an indirect object pronoun: “tomarnos” often means “to have/drink (something)” and “nos” indicates it’s for/among us (e.g., “let’s have a coffee”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a tomarnos un café después de clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s have a coffee after class.

definitions.note: Third-person plural preterite (they/you all took).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos tomaron el autobús a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They took the bus at eight.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive; very common with food/drinks (e.g., tomarse un café = to have a coffee).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomarse un café por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to have a coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Used (especially in some regional usages) to express how long something takes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puede tomarse dos horas llegar en coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It can take two hours to get there by car.

definitions.native: to have (something to drink), to take (something)
definitions.note: Often used with drinks (e.g., “tomarte un café” = “to have a coffee”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomarte un café antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to have a coffee before leaving.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) future tense of “tomar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tomará el autobús mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will take the bus tomorrow.

definitions.native: you will take, you will have
definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana tomarás el autobús a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you will take the bus at eight.

definitions.native: I will take, I will have (drink)
definitions.note: First-person singular future tense of “tomar”. Often used for choosing a drink (“I’ll have…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomaré un café, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'll have a coffee, please.

definitions.note: Conditional form of "tomar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo tomaría un café, pero ya es muy tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would have a coffee, but it’s already very late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tomas el autobús todos los días?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you take the bus every day?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), informal singular (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Tomaste el café esta mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Did you drink the coffee this morning?

definitions.note: Informal command (tú) of “tomar” with the attached pronoun “te” (= yourself). Often used to tell someone to have/eat/drink something.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomate un café y seguimos hablando.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Have a coffee and we’ll keep talking.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito un tomate para la ensalada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need a tomato for the salad.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré tomates para la ensalada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought tomatoes for the salad.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted): “tome” = “take”. It can also be present subjunctive (e.g., “Espero que tome…”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tome este medicamento dos veces al día.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take this medicine twice a day.

definitions.note: Used to suggest doing something together (nosotros command / present subjunctive). Often used as an invitation, e.g., to have a drink.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomemos un café después de la clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let's have a coffee after class.

definitions.note: Command form used for “you” (ustedes), and also the present subjunctive for “you” (ustedes).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, tomen asiento.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, have a seat.

definitions.note: Often used after expressions like “no” (negative command) or “que…” (subjunctive).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No tomes esto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t take this.

definitions.note: From the verb "tomar". Often used for taking something (like medicine) or drinking (especially beverages).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomo un café por la mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have a coffee in the morning.

definitions.note: Informal command form used with voseo (common in Argentina, Uruguay, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomá este libro, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take this book, please.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) form of "tomar". It often means "I took" (took something) or "I had" (food/drink).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer tomé un café antes de ir al trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I had a coffee before going to work.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (preterite) of “tomar”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él tomó un café esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He took (had) a coffee this morning.

definitions.note: metric ton (1,000 kilograms)

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truck carries a ton of sand.

definitions.note: Plural of “tonelada” (metric tons in most Spanish-speaking contexts).

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No me gustó el tono de tu mensaje.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La canción tiene tonos suaves.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas tonta; ya hiciste tu parte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't be silly; you already did your part.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be a fool; check the date again.

definitions.note: feminine plural form

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t say silly things.

definitions.note: Plural; often used to dismiss something as unimportant or stupid.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No digas tonterías; eso no es verdad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't say nonsense; that's not true.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person or behavior; can be insulting depending on tone and context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas tonto; mira por dónde caminas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be silly; watch where you’re walking.

definitions.note: Often used as an insult; can also be used more lightly (like “silly”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No seas tonto, ponte el abrigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t be an idiot, put on your coat.

definitions.note: Plural form (masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No digas cosas tontos, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don't say silly things, please.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can also be used for mixed-gender groups.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No hagas caso a esos tontos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t pay attention to those fools.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He topado con Ana en el supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I ran into Ana at the supermarket.

definitions.native: we run into, we bump into

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We ran into Ana at the supermarket.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El topo vive bajo tierra.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The mole lives underground.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday he ran into me at the supermarket and said hi.

definitions.note: Often used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “espero que…”).
