definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La novela fue traducida al inglés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The novel was translated into English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El documento ya está traducido al inglés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The document is already translated into English.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of “traducir”; used with “estar” or to describe an ongoing action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy traduciendo este texto al inglés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am translating this text into English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes traducir este texto al inglés?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you translate this text into English?

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) in the simple future.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella traducirá el documento mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She will translate the document tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El traductor trabaja con documentos en inglés y español.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The translator works with documents in English and Spanish.

definitions.note: feminine form (a female translator)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es traductora y trabaja desde casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is a translator and works from home.

definitions.note: plural form of "traductor"
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los traductores trabajan con textos en muchos idiomas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The translators work with texts in many languages.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "traducir" for "I".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer traduje el documento al inglés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I translated the document into English.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "traducir" (to translate).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella tradujo el documento al inglés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She translated the document into English.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted) and also present subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, traduzca este documento al inglés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please translate this document into English.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes). Also used for affirmative commands with ustedes: “Translate!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que traduzcan este texto al inglés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you translate this text into English.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "traducir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo traduzco el artículo al inglés.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I translate the article into English.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano trae pan a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother brings bread home.

definitions.note: Command form used with vosotros (Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Traed agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Bring water, please.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, traeme un vaso de agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please, bring me a glass of water.

definitions.note: Present tense (nosotros/nosotras) of "traer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy traemos comida para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today we bring food for the party.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of "traer" (they/you all bring).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos traen comida para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They bring food for the party.

definitions.note: Often used with an indirect object pronoun (me/te/le/nos/les), e.g. “Tráeme…” = “Bring me…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes traerme un vaso de agua?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring me a glass of water?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana traeremos comida para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will bring food for everyone.

definitions.note: Often used when bringing something to a place or to someone; English may use “take” depending on perspective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te preocupes: traeremos los documentos a la reunión.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry: we’ll bring the documents to the meeting.

definitions.native: to bring her, to bring it
definitions.note: Direct object pronoun “la” = “her” (for a female person) or “it” (for a feminine noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a traerla mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to bring her/it tomorrow.

definitions.native: bring to him, bring to her, bring to you (formal)
definitions.note: Contains the indirect object pronoun “le” (= to him/her/you formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a traerle un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to bring him/her a coffee.

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun “lo” (“it/him”) is attached to the infinitive “traer.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a traerlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to bring it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "traer" with the direct object pronoun "los" attached ("them," usually masculine or mixed group).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a traerlos mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to bring them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun "me" (to/for me).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes traerme un vaso de agua?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring me a glass of water?

definitions.note: Object pronoun order: traer + nos (to us) combined as traernos.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Puedes traernos el menú, por favor?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you bring us the menu, please?

definitions.note: Direct object pronoun: te (you) attached to the infinitive traer.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a traerte un café.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to bring you a coffee.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana traerá los documentos a la oficina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will bring the documents to the office.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ellos/ellas/ustedes) future tense of "traer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana traerán la comida para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow they will bring the food for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana traeré el libro a clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow I will bring the book to class.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo traería comida, pero no tengo tiempo de cocinar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would bring food, but I don't have time to cook.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "traer" used with "tú" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Traes tu libro a clase?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you bringing your book to class?

definitions.note: Often refers to someone who traffics illegal goods (especially drugs or people).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó a un traficante de drogas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested a drug trafficker.

definitions.note: Usually refers to people who illegally traffic drugs, weapons, or people; often used with “de” (e.g., “traficantes de drogas”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La policía arrestó a varios traficantes de drogas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The police arrested several drug traffickers.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi perro traga muy rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My dog swallows very fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He tragado la pastilla con agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I swallowed the pill with water.

definitions.note: Often implies swallowing quickly or with difficulty; it can also be used figuratively (e.g., to accept something unpleasant).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No puedo tragar esta pastilla sin agua.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I can't swallow this pill without water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La muerte del actor fue una tragedia para su familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The actor’s death was a tragedy for his family.

definitions.note: Commonly refers to an alcoholic drink in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Me invitas un trago?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Will you buy me a drink?

definitions.note: Commonly used for alcoholic drinks in Latin America.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos unos tragos después de cenar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We had a few drinks after dinner.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Se atragantó porque tragó demasiado rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He choked because he swallowed too fast.

definitions.note: Often used as a past participle functioning as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me siento traicionado por mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel betrayed by my friends.

definitions.note: Past participle of "traicionar"; often used with "haber" (e.g., "he traicionado") or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me he sentido traicionado por mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have felt betrayed by my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero traicionar tu confianza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want to betray your trust.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me traicionaron y me dolió mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They betrayed me, and it hurt a lot.

definitions.note: Conditional form (used for hypothetical situations).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nunca traicionaría a mis amigos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would never betray my friends.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me traicionaste cuando contaste mi secreto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You betrayed me when you told my secret.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él traicionó a su mejor amigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He betrayed his best friend.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su traición me dolió mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His betrayal hurt me a lot.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Lo consideraron un traidor por contar el secreto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They considered him a traitor for telling the secret.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los traidores fueron castigados por el rey.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traitors were punished by the king.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (also formal command: “bring”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que traiga el documento mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you bring the document tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (or formal command) form of “traer” used with ustedes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que traigan los documentos mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you bring the documents tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "traer"; used after expressions like "quiero que", "espero que", "no creo que", etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que traigas tu libro mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you bring your book tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "traer" (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Traigo pan y leche del supermercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m bringing bread and milk from the supermarket.

definitions.note: Preterite form of “traer” (used for completed past actions).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer traje pan a la casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I brought bread home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me puse un traje para la entrevista.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I put on a suit for the interview.

definitions.note: Imperfect subjunctive (yo/él/ella/usted form) of “traer”; often used after expressions like “quería que…” or “si…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quería que yo trajera el libro a clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted me to bring the book to class.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite), third person plural.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos trajeron comida para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They brought food for everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la boda, muchos invitados llevaban trajes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: At the wedding, many guests were wearing suits.

definitions.note: Preterite (simple past) of "traer" for "nosotros/nosotras".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer trajimos comida para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday we brought food for everyone.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú), simple past (preterite).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué trajiste para la fiesta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What did you bring for the party?

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "traer".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella trajo pan para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She brought bread for everyone.

definitions.note: Used for the plot of a story (a book, movie, series, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La trama de la película es muy interesante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The plot of the movie is very interesting.

definitions.note: Often implies making secret or dishonest plans.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están tramando algo contra él.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They’re plotting something against him.

definitions.note: Often used for a section of a road, route, or period of time.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este tramo de la carretera está en obras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This stretch of the road is under construction.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pusieron una trampa para atrapar al ratón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They set a trap to catch the mouse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eso fue una trampa en el examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That was cheating on the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pusieron trampas para ratones en la cocina.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put mouse traps in the kitchen.

definitions.note: Often used for dishonest behavior (like cheating) or a trick meant to deceive someone.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En ese juego hay muchas trampas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that game there are lots of cheats.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está tranquila ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is calm now.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hablamos tranquilamente en el parque.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We talked calmly in the park.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las niñas están tranquilas en clase.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The girls are calm in class.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Busco tranquilidad después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m looking for calm after work.

definitions.note: Present tense (él/ella/usted) of “tranquilizar” or an affirmative command (tú): “calm down / reassure (someone)” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta música me tranquiliza.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This music calms me down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico me recetó un tranquilizante para dormir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed me a tranquilizer to sleep.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico me recetó tranquilizantes para la ansiedad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor prescribed me tranquilizers for anxiety.

definitions.note: Includes the object pronoun “te” (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy aquí para tranquilizarte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m here to calm you down.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La noticia tranquilizó a mi madre.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The news calmed my mother.

definitions.note: Often used to describe a person or situation that is relaxed or not stressful.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hoy estoy tranquilo porque terminé mi tarea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Today I’m calm because I finished my homework.

definitions.note: Often used informally as an adjective used like an adverb (e.g., “Habla tranquilo” = “Speak calmly”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Habla tranquilo; todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Speak calmly; everything is going to be fine.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form; used for a group of men or a mixed group.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están tranquilos ahora.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are calm now.

definitions.note: Plural command used with ustedes; the -se means it’s reflexive (calm yourselves).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, tranquilícense; todo está bajo control.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please calm down; everything is under control.

definitions.note: Formal command (usted). With “se,” it’s a reflexive command meaning “calm yourself down.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Señor, tranquilícese, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sir, calm down, please.

definitions.note: Informal command (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tranquilízate, todo va a salir bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Calm down, everything is going to be okay.

definitions.note: Often used as an invariable adjective; it can also be used as a prefix meaning “trans-” (e.g., transatlántico).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi primo es trans y lo apoyamos mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My cousin is trans and we support him a lot.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrase “en el transcurso de …” = “in the course of … / over the course of …”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En el transcurso del año, visitamos a nuestros abuelos varias veces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Over the course of the year, we visited our grandparents several times.

definitions.note: Often used for bank transfers and other financial transfers.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hice una transferencia al banco esta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I made a transfer to the bank this morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El dinero ya ha sido transferido a tu cuenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The money has already been transferred to your account.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a transferir dinero a tu cuenta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to transfer money to your account.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La transformación de la ciudad fue rápida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The transformation of the city was fast.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tecnología puede transformar nuestra forma de trabajar.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Technology can transform the way we work.

definitions.note: Future tense (él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tecnología transformará la educación en los próximos años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Technology will transform education in the coming years.

definitions.note: Simple past (preterite): used for a completed action in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La tecnología transformó la manera en que trabajamos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Technology transformed the way we work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La transición a la universidad puede ser difícil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The transition to university can be difficult.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La transmisión del partido fue en vivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The broadcast of the match was live.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El transmisor envía la señal a la antena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The transmitter sends the signal to the antenna.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of “transmitir” (also used for “usted”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La radio transmite las noticias cada mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The radio broadcasts the news every morning.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (they/you all) present tense of “transmitir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los canales transmiten las noticias en vivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The channels broadcast the news live.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund form of "transmitir"; often used with "estar" to talk about what is happening right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Están transmitiendo el partido en vivo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are broadcasting the game live.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vidrio es transparente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The glass is transparent.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present (he/she/it transports).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella transporta las cajas en su camioneta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She transports the boxes in her van.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vamos a transportar las cajas al almacén.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re going to transport the boxes to the warehouse.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El transporte público es barato en esta ciudad.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Public transportation is cheap in this city.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tomamos el tranvía para ir al centro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We took the tram to go downtown.

definitions.note: Often refers to an old or dirty piece of cloth used for cleaning.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Limpié la mesa con un trapo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I cleaned the table with a rag.

definitions.note: Often used in the phrases “detrás de” (behind) and “tras” (after) in expressions like “uno tras otro” (one after another).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños corrieron tras el perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The children ran after the dog.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La puerta trasera está abierta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The back door is open.

definitions.note: Refers to the back/rear part of an object or area; for doors, the more common adjective is “trasera,” but this example uses “trasero” as a noun to keep the exact word form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El trasero del coche está dañado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The back of the car is damaged.

definitions.note: Informal; can be mildly rude depending on context. Also appears as “trasero/trasera” as an adjective in some uses, but here it’s the noun “trasero.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me caí y me golpeé el trasero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fell and hurt my butt.

definitions.note: Common, informal in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me caí y me duele el trasero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I fell and my butt hurts.

definitions.note: Often used to mean someone/something has been moved from one place (or position) to another; not the same as English “translated.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El paciente fue trasladado al hospital en ambulancia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The patient was transferred to the hospital by ambulance.

definitions.native: we will move, we will transfer
definitions.note: First-person plural (nosotros) future tense of "trasladar".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana trasladaremos las cajas al garaje.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will move the boxes to the garage.

definitions.note: Third-person plural simple past (pretérito): “they moved/transferred.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los trasladaron al hospital en ambulancia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They transferred them to the hospital by ambulance.

definitions.note: Often used for moving someone/something from one place to another (e.g., a transfer to a different location).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El traslado al nuevo hospital fue rápido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The transfer to the new hospital was quick.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): he/she/it moved; you (formal) moved.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El gobierno trasladó a las familias a un lugar más seguro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The government moved the families to a safer place.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El director traspasó la empresa a su hija.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The director transferred the company to his daughter.

definitions.note: Often used with “de” + infinitive: “trata de hacer…” = “tries to do…”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella trata de aprender español todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She tries to learn Spanish every day.

definitions.note: Used when talking about how someone treats another person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi jefe me trata muy bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My boss treats me very well.

definitions.note: Used to talk about the topic of a book, movie, etc., often with “de”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La película trata de una familia en Madrid.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The movie is about a family in Madrid.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; often describes an ongoing or repeated past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Trataba de llamar, pero no había señal.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I was trying to call, but there was no signal.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense; used when "tratar" means "to deal with" (a topic).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El libro trataba de la historia de México.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The book was about the history of Mexico.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (ongoing or repeated action in the past).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos trataban de abrir la puerta, pero estaba cerrada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They tried to open the door, but it was closed.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella fue tratada con respeto.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She was treated with respect.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana tiene varicela y no puede ir a la escuela.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Prices vary depending on the season.

definitions.note: Often used as a noun meaning “man,” but it can also be used as an adjective meaning “male,” especially when talking about a child.

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense of “ir.” Commonly used with “a” + infinitive to talk about the near future.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going to study today?

definitions.note: Second-person singular (tú) present tense of "ir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Vas a la escuela hoy?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going to school today?

definitions.note: Often used for a pot or container, especially made of clay or ceramic.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The clay pot is on the table.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero un vaso de agua, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want a glass of water, please.

definitions.note: Plural of "vaso".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pon dos vasos en la mesa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Put two glasses on the table, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El desierto es vasto y silencioso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The desert is vast and silent.

definitions.note: Form of “ir” used in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”). It can also be used as a formal command (usted): “Go.”

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you go to the doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted): “Vaya…”. It can also be the present subjunctive form of “ir” (e.g., “Espero que vaya…” = “I hope he/she goes…”).

definitions.note: Used as an exclamatory determiner to show surprise or emphasis (often with nouns).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What a problem we have!

definitions.note: Common interjection to show surprise, emphasis, or mild annoyance; meaning depends on tone and context.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Wow! I didn’t expect to see you here.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of "ir"; commonly used as an affirmative command with "nosotros" (let’s...).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s go to the park after class.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (they/you all). Also used for affirmative ustedes command: “Go!”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vayan al médico hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope they go to the doctor today.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive form of “ir” (used after expressions like “quiero que…”, “espero que…”, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vayas a la fiesta mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you go to the party tomorrow.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vosotros/vosotras) present subjunctive of "ir"; used mainly in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vayáis mañana al médico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you go to the doctor tomorrow.

definitions.note: Used to suggest leaving/going somewhere; literally “let’s go (ourselves).”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ya es tarde; vayámonos a casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s late; let’s go home.

definitions.note: Abbreviation of “usted” (formal “you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cómo está vd, señora?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: How are you, ma’am?

definitions.note: Informal command (tú imperative) of “ir”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ve a casa, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go home, please.

definitions.note: From the verb "ver" (to see).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Él ve la película.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He sees the movie.

definitions.note: Used with the subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like “I hope that…”) or as a formal command (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vea la película mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you see the movie tomorrow.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (nosotros) often used to suggest something or to mean “let’s see.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veamos qué podemos hacer.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Let’s see what we can do.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (ustedes / ellos / ellas). Also used as a polite command for ustedes.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero que vean este video.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want you to see this video.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú form) of “ver”; often used after expressions like “espero que…”, “quiero que…”, “no creo que…”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que veas la diferencia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you see the difference.

definitions.note: Plural of "vez" (used for counting how many times something happens).

definitions.note: Feminine form; refers to a woman who lives nearby.

definitions.note: Feminine form of "vecino".

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My (female) neighbor is very kind.

definitions.note: Plural, feminine.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis vecinas son muy amables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My (female) neighbors are very kind.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta este vecindario porque es tranquilo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like this neighborhood because it's quiet.

definitions.note: As an adjective, it describes something that is next to or near something else.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay un parque vecino a mi casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a park next to my house.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi vecino vive al lado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbor lives next door.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis vecinos son muy amables.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My neighbors are very kind.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This plant needs a lot of light and water.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar vegetales para la ensalada.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy vegetables for the salad.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used to describe a woman or a feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana es vegetariana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister is vegetarian.

definitions.note: describes a male person or a masculine noun (feminine: vegetariana)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermano es vegetariano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is vegetarian.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My brother is a vegetarian.

definitions.note: masculine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos son vegetarianos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends are vegetarian.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay muchos vehículos en la calle durante la hora pico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There are many vehicles on the street during rush hour.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo veintisiete años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am twenty-seven years old.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo veintiséis años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am twenty-six years old.

definitions.note: Used before a masculine singular noun (short form of “veintiuno”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo veintiún años.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I am twenty-one years old.

definitions.note: Second-person plural (vosotros) present tense of "ver"; mainly used in Spain.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Veis la montaña desde aquí?

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In old age, it’s important to take good care of yourself.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My bladder hurts.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vela del barco es blanca.

definitions.note: Used for things like deadlines, bills, and documents.

definitions.note: Often used for things like documents, cards, or bills that are no longer valid or past their due date.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi tarjeta de crédito está vencida.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: After the match, the team was defeated.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team is defeated.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este yogur está vencido.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sellers offer fresh fruit at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vendemos pan todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We sell bread every day.

definitions.note: Third-person plural present tense of “vender” (used for “they sell” and also “you (plural, Spain) sell”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos venden frutas en el mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sell fruit at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero vender mi coche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sell my car.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero venderla mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sell it tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (= “it”).

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sell it today.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to sell you my car.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (he/she/it) or formal you (usted) in the simple future.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito): third person plural.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She sold her car last week.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vendo mi coche porque necesito dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m selling my car because I need money.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (él/ella/usted) future tense of “venir”.

definitions.note: Third-person plural (ellos/ellas/ustedes) in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vendrán mañana por la tarde.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I sold my car.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to avenge my brother's death.

definitions.note: Reflexive form meaning “to take revenge (for myself)” or “to get revenge.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero vengarme de él por lo que hizo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to take revenge on him for what he did.

definitions.note: Reflexive form (vengarse de alguien/algo = to get revenge on someone/for something).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiso vengarse de su vecino por el ruido.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He wanted to get revenge on his neighbor for the noise.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (tú) of "venir"; used after expressions like "quiero que", "espero que", "dudo que", etc.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que vengas mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you come tomorrow.

definitions.note: First-person singular present tense of "venir" (to come).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vengo a tu casa después del trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I come to your house after work.

definitions.note: Imperative (vosotros) form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Venid aquí, por favor!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come here, please!

definitions.note: Past participle of "venir"; used with "haber" to form perfect tenses.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He venido temprano hoy.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have come early today.

definitions.note: First-person plural ("we") present tense of "venir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Venimos a cenar a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’re coming for dinner at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes venir mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you come tomorrow?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La venta de la casa fue rápida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The sale of the house was quick.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tener experiencia es una gran ventaja para este trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Having experience is a big advantage for this job.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las ventajas de este plan son claras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The advantages of this plan are clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abre la ventana, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Open the window, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Abre las ventanas, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Open the windows, please.

definitions.note: Often refers to a small window at a counter (e.g., in a bank, station, or office) where you are attended.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Saque un número y espere su turno en la ventanilla 3.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Take a number and wait for your turn at window 3.

definitions.note: Common in Latin America for the side window of a car.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Baja la ventanilla, por favor; hace mucho calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Roll down the window, please; it’s very hot.

definitions.note: Plural of “venta”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Las ventas subieron este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Sales went up this month.

definitions.note: Present subjunctive (usted/él/ella) form of "venir".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Espero que usted vente temprano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I hope you come early.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ventilación de esta habitación es muy buena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The ventilation in this room is very good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hace calor, enciende el ventilador.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hot; turn on the fan.

definitions.note: Often used for letting fresh air in (a room, clothes, etc.).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a ventilar la habitación porque hace calor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to air out the room because it's hot.

definitions.native: to discuss, to bring up (an issue)
definitions.note: Common in phrases like “ventilar un tema/asunto” (to discuss/raise an issue), often in a public or open way.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero ventilar este tema en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don't want to discuss this topic in public.

definitions.note: Common in Rioplatense Spanish (Argentina/Uruguay) as the informal singular imperative (vos).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vení conmigo, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Come with me, please.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo venía a casa todos los días después de la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I used to come home every day after school.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (nosotros). Often implies an ongoing or habitual past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veníamos a casa cuando empezó a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were coming home when it started to rain.

definitions.native: you were coming, you used to come
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Por qué venías tan tarde?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Why were you coming so late?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desde aquí veo las montañas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From here I can see the mountains.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero ver una película esta noche.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to watch a movie tonight.

definitions.note: This form is normally written with an accent: “verá” (future tense of “ver”). Without the accent, “vera” is a common misspelling.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana vera a su abuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow he/she will see his/her grandmother.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En verano hace mucho calor aquí.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In summer it’s very hot here.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis veranos en España fueron increíbles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My summers in Spain were incredible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te lo explicaré verbalmente para que quede claro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll explain it to you verbally so that it’s clear.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La verdad siempre sale a la luz.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The truth always comes to light.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella contó la verdadera historia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She told the true story.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verdaderamente no entiendo por qué estás tan enojado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I truly don't understand why you're so angry.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sus historias son verdaderas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Her stories are true.

definitions.note: Adjective; agrees in gender/number (verdadero, verdadera, verdaderos, verdaderas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este documento es verdadero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This document is true/genuine.

definitions.note: Often used with "ser" to describe someone’s honesty or sincerity.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero ser verdadero contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to be truthful with you.

definitions.native: the real/true one (in contrast to an imitation)
definitions.note: Can imply authenticity or the "right"/"correct" version.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este es el verdadero original.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the true/original one.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esos documentos son verdaderos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Those documents are true.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dime las verdades, aunque duelan.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tell me the truths, even if they hurt.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi coche es verde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My car is green.

definitions.note: As a noun, it refers to the color.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El verde es mi color favorito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Green is my favorite color.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis zapatos son verdes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My shoes are green.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Necesito comprar verdura para la cena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I need to buy vegetables for dinner.

definitions.note: Plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Compré verduras frescas en el mercado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought fresh vegetables at the market.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jurado anunció su veredicto al final del juicio.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The jury announced its verdict at the end of the trial.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana veremos la película en casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow we will see the movie at home.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Pusieron una verga de metal para sostener la lona.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They put a metal pole up to hold the tarp.

definitions.note: Vulgar slang in many Spanish-speaking countries; often considered offensive.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No digas "verga" en la escuela; es una grosería.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t say “verga” at school; it’s a swear word.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue una situación vergonzosa para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an embarrassing situation for everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Fue un momento vergonzoso para todos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It was an embarrassing moment for everyone.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me da vergüenza hablar en público.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I feel embarrassed to speak in public.

definitions.note: Present tense (él/ella/usted) or an affirmative tú command, depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella verifica la información antes de enviarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She checks the information before sending it.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a verificar la información antes de enviarla.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I'm going to verify the information before sending it.

definitions.note: Often used as a formal command (usted) or in the present subjunctive (e.g., after expressions like "es importante que...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Por favor, verifique su correo electrónico.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Please verify/check your email.

definitions.note: Usually a metal barrier, often with bars (e.g., around a yard, garden, or window).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Hay una verja alta alrededor del jardín.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: There is a tall fence around the garden.

definitions.native: to see her, to see it
definitions.note: Infinitive with the direct object pronoun “la” attached (her/it, feminine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero verla mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see her tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “las” (= them, feminine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero verlas mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Literally “to see + le”. Here, “le” commonly refers to a male person (“him”) or to “you” in the formal sense (usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero verle mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see him tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “lo” (“it” or “him,” masculine).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero verlo mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see him tomorrow.

definitions.note: Includes the direct object pronoun “los” (“them”) attached to the verb “ver”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero verlos mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see them tomorrow.

definitions.note: Infinitive "ver" with the object pronoun "me" attached (often after another verb, like "poder").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Puedes verme mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can you see me tomorrow?

definitions.note: Infinitive of “ver” with the pronoun “nos” attached; often used to mean “for us to see each other” (or “to see us/ourselves,” depending on context).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Podemos vernos mañana?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Can we see each other tomorrow?

definitions.note: Used with the object pronoun "os" (you all, informal; used mainly in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero veros mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see you tomorrow.

definitions.note: Reflexive form of "ver"; often used for seeing yourself (e.g., in a mirror).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es difícil verse sin un espejo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s hard to see yourself without a mirror.

definitions.note: Commonly used to describe how someone/something looks (often with an adverb like "bien" or "mal").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Con esa chaqueta vas a verse muy bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: With that jacket, you’re going to look really good.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta es la última versión de la aplicación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the latest version of the app.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El primer verso del poema es muy famoso.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The first verse of the poem is very famous.

definitions.note: Used in print contexts, as in “anverso y reverso” (front and back).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Escribe tu nombre en el verso de la hoja.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Write your name on the back of the sheet.

definitions.note: Usually refers to lines of a poem or song lyrics.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Aprendí los versos de la canción.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I learned the verses of the song.

definitions.note: Infinitive of "ver" with the object pronoun "te" attached.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero verte mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to see you tomorrow.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La línea es vertical.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The line is vertical.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vertió el agua en el vaso con cuidado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He/She poured the water into the glass carefully.

definitions.note: Third-person singular (also formal usted) of "ver" in the future tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mañana verá el resultado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tomorrow you/he/she will see the result.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Verán la película mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They will see the movie tomorrow.

definitions.note: Usually used to tell someone that something will become clear or that a prediction will come true.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No te preocupes; verás que todo saldrá bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Don’t worry; you’ll see that everything will turn out fine.

definitions.note: First-person singular (yo) future tense of "ver".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Te llamaré cuando veré los resultados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’ll call you when I see the results.

definitions.note: Future tense, vosotros form (used mainly in Spain).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Veréis que todo saldrá bien.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You will see that everything will turn out fine.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (yo/él/ella/usted form), often used for hypotheticals or polite requests.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Yo vería esa película contigo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I would see that movie with you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si tuviéramos tiempo, veríamos la ciudad juntos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If we had time, we would see the city together.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (ustedes/ellos/ellas).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Sin sus gafas, no verían bien el pizarrón.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Without their glasses, they wouldn't see the board well.

definitions.note: Conditional tense (tú).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Si vinieras conmigo, verías el museo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: If you came with me, you would see the museum.

definitions.note: Present tense form of "ir" used with "tú" (informal "you").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Ves al cine esta noche?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Are you going to the movies tonight?

definitions.note: Present tense (tú): “you see.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Ves esa casa blanca?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you see that white house?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; used to describe a woman/girl or a feminine noun.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella está vestida para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is dressed for the party.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me compré un vestido para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I bought myself a dress for the party.

definitions.note: Often used with "estar" and "de" (e.g., "estar vestido de...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Está vestido de negro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is dressed in black.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En la tienda venden vestidos muy bonitos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They sell very pretty dresses in the store.

definitions.note: Plural masculine adjective (also used for mixed-gender groups).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Los niños están vestidos para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The kids are dressed for the party.

definitions.note: Often used for clothing in a more formal or general sense than "ropa".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La vestimenta tradicional de esta región es muy colorida.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traditional clothing of this region is very colorful.

definitions.note: Base verb form; often used reflexively as “vestirse” = “to get dressed.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Debo vestir antes de salir de casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I must dress before leaving the house.

definitions.note: Can mean putting clothes on another person.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a vestir al bebé con una chaqueta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to dress the baby in a jacket.

definitions.note: Reflexive form: it means “to dress myself.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Tengo que vestirme antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have to get dressed before leaving.

definitions.note: Reflexive infinitive: it means to dress yourself / to get dressed.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a vestirse antes de salir.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to get dressed before leaving.

definitions.note: Often used with reflexive meaning (vestirse) referring to “you” (tú), e.g. “Es hora de vestirte.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es hora de vestirte.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It’s time to get dressed.

definitions.note: Can also mean someone dresses another person (“you”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Quiero vestirte para la fiesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I want to dress you for the party.

definitions.note: Often used for clothing used in a specific context (e.g., uniforms, costumes, sports kit) or for the set of clothes someone has.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El vestuario del equipo es azul y blanco.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The team's uniform is blue and white.

definitions.note: Preterite (past simple), first-person singular.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta mañana me vestí rápido para llegar a tiempo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This morning I got dressed quickly to arrive on time.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (yo/él/ella/usted).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, vestía un uniforme todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I wore a uniform every day.

definitions.note: Often refers to the main entrance area of a building (like a hotel, theater, or office).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nos vemos en el vestíbulo del hotel a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: See you in the hotel lobby at eight.

definitions.note: Informal (tú) command; often used with "de aquí" = "go away from here."
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Vete de aquí, por favor.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Go away from here, please.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi abuelo es veterano del ejército.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My grandfather is an army veteran.

definitions.note: Feminine form; also commonly used to mean a (vet) clinic depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La veterinaria le dio una vacuna a mi perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The veterinarian gave my dog a vaccine.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El veterinario examinó a mi perro.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The veterinarian examined my dog.

definitions.note: used for an occurrence or instance, not for clock time
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es la primera vez que como paella.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: It's the first time I've eaten paella.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense (yo/él/ella/usted). Often translates as “was seeing” or “used to see,” depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, veía dibujos animados todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to watch cartoons every day.

definitions.native: we used to see, we were seeing
definitions.note: Imperfect tense (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: De niños, veíamos esa película todos los veranos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: As kids, we used to watch that movie every summer.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (they/you all) of “ver.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Desde la ventana, veían el mar cada mañana.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: From the window, they saw the sea every morning.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ayer vi una película muy buena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Yesterday I saw a very good movie.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esa idea es viable si conseguimos más dinero.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: That idea is viable if we get more money.

definitions.note: Third-person singular present tense of “viajar” (he/she/it travels; you travel—formal).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mi hermana viaja mucho por trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My sister travels a lot for work.

definitions.note: Imperfect past tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando era niño, viajaba con mi familia todos los veranos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When I was a child, I used to travel with my family every summer.

definitions.note: Past participle of "viajar". Used with "haber" to form the present perfect, or as an adjective.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: He viajado a México dos veces.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I have traveled to Mexico twice.

definitions.note: Can also mean “we traveled” in the simple past (preterite), depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este verano viajamos a México con mis abuelos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This summer we travel to Mexico with my grandparents.

definitions.note: present tense, they/you (plural)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis amigos viajan a México cada verano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My friends travel to Mexico every summer.

definitions.note: Present participle/gerund of "viajar"; often used with "estar" to talk about what someone is doing right now.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estoy viajando por España este mes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m traveling around Spain this month.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Me gusta viajar en tren.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I like to travel by train.

definitions.note: Simple future (nosotros).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este verano viajaremos a México.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This summer we will travel to Mexico.

definitions.note: Informal singular (tú) present tense.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Viajas mucho por trabajo?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you travel a lot for work?

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Nuestro viaje a México fue increíble.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Our trip to Mexico was incredible.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El viajero llegó al hotel muy tarde.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The traveler arrived at the hotel very late.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Mis viajes de trabajo son muy frecuentes.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: My work trips are very frequent.

definitions.note: Present tense (yo).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viajo a México todos los veranos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I travel to Mexico every summer.

definitions.native: we were traveling, we used to travel
definitions.note: Imperfect (past) form; describes an ongoing past action or a habitual past action.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando éramos niños, viajábamos a la playa todos los veranos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we used to travel to the beach every summer.

definitions.native: I traveled, I went (on a trip)
definitions.note: Simple past (preterite) form of "viajar" for "yo".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Viajé a México el verano pasado.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I traveled to Mexico last summer.

definitions.note: Simple past (pretérito) form of “viajar” (he/she/you formal)
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El año pasado viajó a México por trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Last year, he traveled to Mexico for work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Dejó el vicio de fumar hace un año.

definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He lives in Madrid.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El profesor puso énfasis en la pronunciación.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The teacher put emphasis on pronunciation.

definitions.note: Often used to talk about a historical time period.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: En esa época, no había internet.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: In that era, there was no internet.

definitions.note: Plural of "época".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: A lo largo de distintas épocas, la ciudad ha cambiado mucho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Throughout different eras, the city has changed a lot.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense (past). Used for ongoing states/background description in the past.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando éramos niños, jugábamos en el parque todos los días.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we played in the park every day.

definitions.note: feminine singular form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres ésa o ésta?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want that one or this one?

definitions.note: Feminine plural form of “ese” used to point out specific things or people.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quieres ésas o éstas?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Do you want those or these?

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun (masculine singular).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: No quiero este; quiero ése.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I don’t want this one; I want that one.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun (masculine plural).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Quiénes son ésos?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Who are those?

definitions.note: Feminine singular form; with an accent it’s normally used as a pronoun (meaning “this one”), though in some contexts you may also see it used as a determiner.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ésta es mi casa.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my house.

definitions.note: feminine singular pronoun (used to refer to a female thing; often contrasted with "esa" / "aquella")
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ésta es mi mochila.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This one is my backpack.

definitions.note: feminine plural demonstrative pronoun; used to refer to specific items/people. It carries a written accent to distinguish it from the adjective “estas”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Éstas son mis llaves.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are my keys.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun meaning “this one/this”; it refers to a person or thing directly (not followed by a noun).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Éste es mi hermano.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is my brother.

definitions.note: Demonstrative pronoun; used to refer to something already mentioned or understood. Often written without an accent in modern Spanish (este).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Cuál prefieres: éste o aquél?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Which do you prefer: this one or that one?

definitions.note: Neuter demonstrative pronoun meaning “this (thing/idea)”. In modern spelling it’s usually written without an accent: “esto”.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¿Qué es ésto?
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: What is this?

definitions.note: Masculine plural demonstrative pronoun; it replaces a noun (often with an implied “ones”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Prefiero éstos porque son más baratos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I prefer these ones because they are cheaper.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La ética es importante en el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Ethics is important at work.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Su proyecto fue un éxito.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: His project was a success.

definitions.note: Plural of «éxito».
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Celebramos nuestros éxitos en el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We celebrate our successes at work.

definitions.note: Imperfect past (nosotros/nosotras) of "ir"; can also be used to form the past progressive ("we were going to...").
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Íbamos al mercado cuando empezó a llover.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We were going to the market when it started to rain.

definitions.note: Imperfect tense of "ir" (to go), used for ongoing or habitual past actions.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Cuando éramos niños, íbamos al parque todos los domingos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: When we were kids, we used to go to the park every Sunday.

definitions.note: Often used for a sports, music, or public figure that people admire a lot.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Messi es el ídolo de muchos aficionados.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Messi is the idol of many fans.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form of “íntimo.”
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es mi amiga íntima desde la infancia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She has been my close friend since childhood.

definitions.note: Often used for close personal relationships or for something very personal/private.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Es un amigo íntimo de mi familia.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: He is a close friend of my family.

definitions.note: Plural masculine form; can refer to close relationships or private/personal matters.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Somos amigos íntimos desde la escuela.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: We’ve been close friends since school.

definitions.note: Common in Latin America; in Spain, "autobús" is more common.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Voy a tomar el ómnibus a las ocho.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I’m going to take the bus at eight.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta noche vamos a la ópera.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Tonight we’re going to the opera.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La Tierra está en órbita alrededor del Sol.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The Earth is in orbit around the Sun.

definitions.note: In anatomy, it refers to the bony cavity where the eye sits.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico examinó la órbita del paciente.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor examined the patient’s eye socket.

definitions.note: Plural form of "orden".
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El jefe dio órdenes claras.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The boss gave clear orders.

definitions.note: Usually refers to a body organ; it can also mean a musical organ depending on context.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El corazón es un órgano muy importante.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The heart is a very important organ.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico revisó los órganos internos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor checked the internal organs.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El óxido de hierro se usa para hacer pigmentos.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Iron oxide is used to make pigments.

definitions.note: Commonly used to refer specifically to rust on iron or steel in everyday speech.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: La bicicleta tiene óxido en la cadena.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The bicycle has rust on the chain.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: El médico dijo que tengo una úlcera en el estómago.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: The doctor said I have an ulcer in my stomach.

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Esta es la última vez que te lo digo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the last time I’m telling you.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Últimamente he estado muy ocupado con el trabajo.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Lately I've been very busy with work.

definitions.note: feminine plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estas son las últimas preguntas del examen.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are the last questions on the exam.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este es el último día de clases.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This is the last day of classes.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos son los últimos días de vacaciones.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These are the last days of vacation.

definitions.note: Command (tú) with the reflexive pronoun “te”; often used as an invitation (e.g., “Join us!”).
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: ¡Únete a nosotros para cenar!
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: Join us for dinner!

definitions.note: Feminine singular form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ella es la única persona que conoce la respuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: She is the only person who knows the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Únicamente quiero descansar un rato.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: I only want to rest for a while.

definitions.note: Feminine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Son unas oportunidades únicas.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are unique opportunities.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Eres el único que entiende esta idea.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: You are the only one who understands this idea.

definitions.note: Masculine plural form.
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Ellos son los únicos que conocen la respuesta.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: They are the only ones who know the answer.

definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Este consejo es muy útil.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: This advice is very useful.

definitions.note: plural form
definitions.example_sentence_target_language: Estos consejos son muy útiles.
definitions.example_sentence_native_language: These tips are very useful.
